original_description: Dairy is the largest organic commodity in the United States, with 1.6 billion in annual sales, yet organic milk represents just 2 % of the nations dairy production and is declining. USDA’s Organic Dairy Market News reports that year-to-date sales of organic milk products are down 1.6 % from the prior year. As organic dairy production costs have increased in recent years, the price premium of fluid organic milk over conventional milk has eroded, leaving organic dairy producers, most of them small family farms, with shrinking on-farm profits that threaten their livelihood. To address this challenging issue, Rumiano Cheese Company, seeks to expand in-house processing capacity to make and market innovative, high-demand organic dairy products in channels that offer a higher price premium over fluid. Activities to be performed will include 1) installing a state-of-the-art processing line to upcycle organic cheese trim into value-added sauces, dips and spreads; 2) acquiring additional equipment to create artisanal specialty cheese wheels inhouse; and 3) expanding marketing, sales, and innovation to gain retail access and build consumer demand for the expanded volume produced through this project. This venture’s goals are to process an additional 32,372,700 pounds of fluid milk and cheese trim, generating approximately $31.5 million in sales revenue and benefiting 27 Northern California pasture-based organic dairy producers during the project period.
updated_description: Rumiano Cheese Company is undertaking a strategic project to expand its in-house processing capabilities and market a range of innovative organic dairy products, addressing a critical need within the organic dairy sector. The core of this venture involves installing a state-of-the-art processing line specifically designed to upcycle organic cheese trim into high-demand sauces, dips, and spreads, alongside the acquisition of additional equipment to facilitate the creation of artisanal specialty cheese wheels entirely within the company’s operations. This initiative aims to process an additional 32,372,700 pounds of fluid milk and cheese trim, generating an anticipated $31.5 million in sales revenue. The project will directly benefit 27 Northern California pasture-based organic dairy producers, providing a new sales channel for their existing production. Furthermore, the expanded product line will target consumer markets, capitalizing on the premium pricing potential of these value-added organic offerings. The success of this project hinges on establishing retail access and fostering increased consumer demand for the increased volume of products produced. Ultimately, Rumiano Cheese Company’s efforts will strengthen the market position for these farmers and processors, representing a significant opportunity for the stakeholders involved.

original_description: The Schmitt’s Farm converted to 100% organic in 2018. The farm grows spring wheat, hulless oats, lentils, yellow peas, chickpeas, hemp grain, canola, alfalfa, and flax. It has a crop rotation of 25% cereal grains (wheat, oats, etc), 25% Legume (peas, chickpeas, alfalfa), 25% oil seeds (flax, hemp seed, canola) and 25 % fallow with cover crop. A number of innovative practices are being tested continuously to get closer to notill or minimum tilling using cover crops, interseeding multiple crops together and relay seeding crops together. The purpose of this project is to help address a current bottleneck in the organic marketplace: which is a lack of organic grain processing infrastructure. Goals include: 1) strengthening and expanding farm capacity 2) Providing grain cleaning services to other organic growers, and 3) increasing access to organic grains. The purchase of this equipment will allow Schmitt’s Farm to increase its annual gross income, increase storage capacity by 13,500 bushels, decrease annual miles traveled by 60,000 miles per year, and increase processing capacity of organic grains by 800,000 bushels per year. The main equipment beneficiaries will include Schmitt Organic Farms and other farms in the region that will now have local or more regionalized access to organic grain processing. This will have a trickle-down effect leading to greater access to organic grain throughout the entire North west region. This will also positively impact buyers as 3 Schmitt’s Farm will be able to more reliably provide them with products. In turn, consumers, bakeries, and restaurants will also have greater access to organic grains.
updated_description: Schmitt’s Farm has initiated a project focused on addressing a critical need within the organic marketplace: the lack of sufficient grain processing infrastructure. This project involves the purchase of equipment designed to strengthen and expand farm capacity, providing grain cleaning services to other organic growers, and increasing access to organic grains throughout the Northwest region. Specifically, the investment will result in a significant increase in processing capacity – 800,000 bushels per year – alongside expanded storage capabilities, adding 13,500 bushels. Furthermore, the equipment will reduce annual miles traveled by 60,000 miles, representing a substantial logistical improvement. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative include Schmitt’s Farm and other regional organic growers, processors, and ultimately, consumers who will gain more reliable access to organic grains. This project anticipates a positive ripple effect, allowing Schmitt’s Farm to more consistently supply buyers with high-quality organic grains, benefiting farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders in the organic supply chain. The anticipated outcomes will contribute to enhanced market access for organic grains, supporting the growth of the organic sector and improving the supply of this commodity to a broader range of consumers and businesses, such as bakeries and restaurants.

original_description: This project increases output and lowers the costs of a small organic dairy processing plant serving underserved producers in economically distressed areas. By supporting a full-time sales position, it expands market access both for existing organic dairy producers and for dairy producers transitioning to organic. It does this through co-packing, two processor-affiliated brands, and other marketing channels it has developed and will continue to expand. Plant upgrades include adding packaging options optimized for food service and food product manufacturers that represent over a third of the national demand for dairy products. The desire central outcome of these activities is to develop product market matches that successfully generate sustained income for organic dairy producers by meeting the needs of existing sales outlets more efficiently and completely.
updated_description: This project aims to substantially increase output and reduce costs within a small organic dairy processing plant, specifically designed to support farmers and processors in economically distressed areas. The core of this initiative involves the creation of a full-time sales position, significantly expanding market access for both existing organic dairy producers and those transitioning to organic certification, through co-packing operations and the development of two processor-affiliated brands. Furthermore, the plant will undergo upgrades, notably the addition of packaging options optimized for food service and food product manufacturers, representing over a third of the national demand for dairy products. The anticipated outcome of these activities is the successful development of product market matches that will reliably generate sustained income for organic dairy producers by more efficiently and completely fulfilling the needs of established sales outlets. This project will support farmers and processors, ultimately benefiting consumers who seek organic dairy products. The enhanced capacity of the plant and expanded market reach will allow for greater volume production, reducing operational costs and improving profitability for the involved stakeholders. This project seeks to create a stronger, more resilient organic dairy supply chain, addressing a critical need for expanded market pathways for organic agricultural commodities.

original_description: Agoge, a sustainable organic product-focused company, has spent 2 years and significant funds researching developing a foundational set of products with organic ingredients to support improved health outcomes. The ingredients in its products are isolated hempseed proteins, certified Organic by the USDA. In short, Agoge is introducing the USA’s first Organic Hemp Protein Isolate (OHPI). The project aims to open the OHPI market and drive the expansion of the upstream (supply) and downstream (demand) supply chain for this organic, sustainable rotational crop through education, marketing, and consumer buyer outreach. The objectives include: 1) Opening the OHPI market by providing the food ingredient sector with the USA’s very first Organic Hemp Protein Isolate products a deeply researched foundational ingredient and its first 3 formulated finished goods. 2) Targeting and educating 8,000 consumers a month using traditional and digital marketing campaigns through education events targeting dietitians, nutritionists, doctors, etc., and 3) Hosting a 20x20 exhibitor booth at 10 of the USA’s biggest ingredient and food conferences. The project will include OHPI industry connector events twice a year for 2 years across 4 different cities.
updated_description: Agoge is undertaking a project to establish and expand the market for the USA’s first Organic Hemp Protein Isolate (OHPI), a product developed after two years of research and significant investment. The core of this initiative involves the creation of a foundational set of products, beginning with the OHPI itself and three formulated finished goods, all utilizing certified organic hempseed proteins. This project anticipates driving expansion throughout the supply chain, encompassing farmers cultivating rotational crops, processors involved in manufacturing, and consumers seeking organic ingredients. A key objective is to reach 8,000 consumers monthly through targeted marketing campaigns, including education events directed toward dietitians, nutritionists, and medical professionals, alongside the establishment of a substantial presence at ten major ingredient and food conferences, each hosting a 20x20 exhibitor booth. Furthermore, Agoge will host twice-yearly industry connector events across four different cities over a two-year period, fostering connections between stakeholders. The project aims to solidify OHPI’s position as a readily available organic ingredient within the food sector, ultimately benefiting both the farmers supplying the raw materials and the consumers seeking high-quality, organic products. The anticipated outcome is a significantly broadened market for this novel organic ingredient, supported by a robust network of supply chain partners.

original_description: This project paves the way to making regenerative kelp farming a viable industry for rural seaside farming communities that rely on volatile wild-caught seafood. Historically, kelp farming within the US has not been considered a lucrative industry because of perceived competition from Asian markets and a lack of profitable end markets for US-grown kelp products. As a result, 95% of seaweed products sold in the US are imported from Asia. Consumers are already proving they are ready for kelp-based snacks, so now is the time to invest in scaling up the kelp industry, spurring demand for more kelp farmers to grow a regenerative and ocean-friendly crop. The major limitation for kelp farmers is a lack of processing and product manufacturing capacity to transform kelp into high-value products. By providing a profitable end market for kelp 12 Tides solves this issue. This project scales up the production of a highly sought-after product line that provides high quality, consistent revenue to rural kelp farmers. Kelp is easy to grow, produces low CO2-equivalent emissions than corn, and can be reliably harvested year after year while mitigating ocean acidification and increasing marine biodiversity. This provides economic stability for farmers in communities historically reliant on increasingly volatile seafood industries as well as a healthy snack product for consumers. This grant allows 12 Tides to scale its processing capacity, support a nationwide launch, and expand the supply chain by purchasing from 27 new organic farms, while employing 144 staff, and supporting 275 kelp farming jobs in the U.S.
updated_description: 12 Tides is undertaking a project to establish a viable industry for regenerative kelp farming within rural seaside farming communities reliant on volatile wild-caught seafood. The core purpose of this initiative is to scale up the production of a highly sought-after product line, providing high-quality, consistent revenue streams to these farmers. Specifically, the project involves purchasing and building processing and manufacturing capacity to transform kelp into valuable products, addressing a key limitation within the current industry. This expansion will support a nationwide launch and enable the acquisition of kelp from 27 new organic farms, resulting in the employment of 144 staff and the support of 275 kelp farming jobs across the United States. The anticipated outcome is the creation of a stable and reliable market for kelp, bolstering economic stability for these farming communities. Ultimately, the project will benefit both farmers and consumers by offering a healthy snack product. These stakeholders will gain access to a domestically produced product, while the project supports the expansion of kelp farming operations. This represents a significant step in developing a sustainable and profitable agricultural sector reliant on a naturally regenerative crop.

original_description: Heal the Earth at Wild Acres Farm, a San Diego County nonprofit and avocado farm, will improve and grow the long-term viability of the domestic organic avocado market by coordinating a direct to consumer valuechain and launching a comprehensive regional marketing campaign. This project will facilitate the flow of avocados into regional markets by leveraging the expertise of, and building on the work done in partnership with, the Avocado Growers of California, the City of Escondido, and other stakeholders. Collaborative efforts will include marketing and outreach to buyers and consumers, promoting opportunities to sell and buy US-grown avocados at a local food hub, a feasibility study, and resulting strategic promotional efforts tailored to the needs of domestic organic avocado growers and US consumers. Heal the Earth will expand staff capacity, build and maintain relationships with certified organic growers, establish new and expanded markets for organic avocados, and develop and execute a marketing plan that differentiates the organic, US-grown product to both buyers and end consumers. Heal the Earth will 1) build relationships between organic avocado producers and consumers, 2) create alternative market channels for organic avocados and ancillary organic farm products, 3) increase consumer awareness of the benefits of locally-grown, 7 California-produced avocados. There is a growing demand for avocados, and organic fruit both supports local farmers and climate-smart growing practices.
updated_description: Heal the Earth at Wild Acres Farm is undertaking a project to improve and grow the long-term viability of the domestic organic avocado market by coordinating a direct-to-consumer value chain and launching a comprehensive regional marketing campaign. This initiative will facilitate the flow of avocados into regional markets through collaborative efforts with key stakeholders, including the Avocado Growers of California, the City of Escondido, and other relevant parties. The project will focus on building relationships between organic avocado producers and consumers, creating alternative market channels for organic avocados and ancillary organic farm products, and increasing consumer awareness of the benefits of locally-grown California-produced avocados. Specifically, Heal the Earth will expand staff capacity, build and maintain relationships with certified organic growers, and develop and execute a marketing plan to differentiate the organic, US-grown product to both buyers and end consumers. The anticipated outcomes include the establishment of a local food hub for the sale and purchase of organic avocados, and the creation of new and expanded markets for organic avocados. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the avocado industry. The project will support the growth of the domestic organic avocado market, and the increased availability of locally-sourced organic agricultural products. Ultimately, this project aims to strengthen the avocado industry and provide enhanced market opportunities for organic avocado growers.

awardee_name: Wehah Farm, Inc dba Lundberg Family Farms
original_description: In 2022, US farmers produced more than 16 billion pounds of rice to serve domestic and international consumers (USDA Economic Research Service). Still, less than 1% of the rice produced in the United States is organic, despite strong and consistent growth in US demand for organic food. With more than 82% of US households buying organic products regularly, the Organic Center notes demand in the US for organic rice exceeds domestic supply, encouraging significant competition from imports. In fact, US imports of rice have steadily increased over the past five years, growing more than 36% from the 2017/2018 crop year to the 2021/2022 crop year. This is primarily due to the major barriers that exist to producing, processing, and marketing organic rice, namely higher costs of production, and lack of processing and marketing infrastructure. To meet current US consumer demand and expand opportunities to build the US organic rice 8 market (project purpose), Lundberg Family Farms, the nation’s largest organic rice producer and processor, will launch a comprehensive effort to support current and transitioning organic producers in increasing organic rice production. Project activities toward removing barriers to entry for producers include grower outreach and technology adaptation expanding processing capacity to create more and better markets for organic producers and executing marketing and promotional activities that will help to build commercial markets for US organic rice products. This project’s goals (deliverables and expected outcomes) include achieving 3,000 new acres of organic rice processing and a $17 million increase in domestic regenerative organic rice sales by the end of the project period.
updated_description: Lundberg Family Farms will launch a comprehensive project to support the growth of organic rice production within the United States, driven by the significant and sustained demand for organic food among US consumers. This initiative will focus on removing barriers to entry for farmers seeking to produce organic rice, encompassing grower outreach and the adaptation of technological advancements to improve production methods. A key component of the project involves expanding processing capacity to create increased and improved markets for organic rice producers, alongside the execution of targeted marketing and promotional activities designed to build commercial markets for US organic rice products. The anticipated outcomes of this project include achieving 3,000 new acres dedicated to organic rice processing, ultimately leading to a $17 million increase in domestic sales of regenerative organic rice. This effort will directly benefit farmers and rice processors by establishing new commercial pathways for their products, and consequently provide consumers with greater access to domestically produced organic rice. The success of this project will strengthen the overall organic rice supply chain and contribute to meeting the growing demand for this product within the United States.

original_description: ZEGO is a woman-owned B Corp-certified brand focusing on supply-chain transparency and purity testing using Montana Gluten Free’s hull-less, high-protein, organic oats. ZEGO sells products in 1500+ stores nationwide. The project will increase processing and consumption of organic, gluten-free, high-protein oats and rotational crop millet in Montana and the surrounding growing region by creating a collaborative integrated value chain (CVIC). The goals are to 1) expand organic processing capacity at Montana Gluten Free (MGF) to alleviate a regional grain processing bottleneck that forces farmers to sell premium crops for bird and animal feed at 50% of full value; 2) develop more products from organic specialty grains for people with medically restricted diets due to allergies or gluten intolerance, toxin and pesticide concerns, or diabetes or to increase dietary plant protein; 3) increase special-diet consumer pull (demand) of organic grains by expanding product trials, adding sales channels, building consumer trust in organic food; and 4) benefit the environment by decreasing transportation miles and promotion of hulless oats, which produce 50% less carbon emissions, and drought-tolerant millet, which uses 1/3rd less water than other grains. In addition to the project goals Zego predicts that the project will 1) increase organic finished goods capacity 5 by integrating operations at MGF with faster and more efficient equipment for bag filling and improved processing efficiency; 2) upgrade food safety certification level; 3) establish a millet value chain by purchasing and installing equipment to dehull millet. It will also help setting up procurement contracts with regional farmer and developing 3-5 new organic specialty grain products, in collaboration with Snacktivist, targeting markets such as food service accounts and big box stores, and build B2B ingredient sales. The project will allow for the implementation of marketing strategies led by a specialized marketing director to increase awareness and adoption of organic specialty grains among special-diet and non-toxic living consumers; and collaborate with technology partner Food Vision to enhance ZEGO’s purity transparency system, making product information accessible and expanding the scope of information to include links to farmers.
updated_description: ZEGO’s project aims to increase the processing and consumption of organic, gluten-free, high-protein oats and rotational crop millet in Montana and the surrounding growing region by establishing a collaborative integrated value chain (CVIC). This initiative will address a regional grain processing bottleneck, currently forcing farmers to sell premium crops for bird and animal feed at reduced values, and simultaneously develop new organic specialty grain products for consumers with medically restricted diets due to allergies, intolerances, or specific health concerns, such as diabetes. The project will encompass the purchase and installation of equipment to dehull millet, alongside upgrades to processing efficiency through faster bag filling and improved operational workflows at Montana Gluten Free (MGF). Anticipated outcomes include an increase in organic finished goods capacity, a higher level of food safety certification, and the creation of a robust millet value chain. Stakeholders, including farmers, processors, and consumers, will benefit from enhanced market access for organic grains and increased availability of specialty dietary products. Furthermore, the project will support the development of 3-5 new organic specialty grain products in collaboration with Snacktivist, targeting food service accounts and big box stores, and facilitating B2B ingredient sales. The initiative will leverage technology through Food Vision to improve ZEGO’s purity transparency system, expanding product information to include links to farmers. This project anticipates a reduction in transportation miles and the promotion of hulless oats, which generate 50% less carbon emissions, and drought-tolerant millet, which utilizes 1/3rd less water than other grains, ultimately benefiting both the environment and ZEGO’s operational efficiency.

awardee_name: Vista Livestock Co. dba Burroughs Family Orchards
original_description: Burroughs Family Orchards (BFO) is a certified organic and regenerative family farm committed to fostering a sustainable food system. This project is designed to increase consumption of BFO's organic almond and olive products, drive market interest, and meet the growing demand for high-quality organic products. BFO plans to broaden its market reach by expanding into new geographic regions, specifically in the Central and Southern U.S. territories. This strategic expansion will be facilitated through hiring a marketing contractor and a broker, who will work to increase the visibility and availability of BFO's organic almond and olive products. Additionally, BFO will invest in developing new and improved organic products, partnering with experienced consultants to expand their product range and drive market interest and demand for organic products. To meet the growing demand for organic almonds, BFO plans to enhance its storage and distribution capacity by investing in temperature and weatherproofing its existing warehouse storage space to ensure optimal freshness and shelf life of their products year-round. These enhancements will enable BFO to scale its operations in tandem with the rising demand for organic almonds. The project is expected to significantly improve BFO's ability to compete in the organic sector. It will advance their mission of promoting a sustainable food system, contributing to the growth of the organic market, and delivering high-quality, innovative almond and olive products to consumers across the nation.
updated_description: Burroughs Family Orchards is undertaking a strategic project designed to significantly increase the consumption of its certified organic almond and olive products, driving market interest, and meeting the growing consumer demand for high-quality organic offerings across the nation. This initiative will involve several key elements, including the engagement of a marketing contractor and a broker to expand the visibility and availability of BFO’s products, alongside a substantial investment in developing new and improved organic product lines through collaboration with experienced consultants. To support this growth, Burroughs Family Orchards plans to enhance its storage and distribution capacity by implementing temperature and weatherproofing measures within its existing warehouse, ensuring year-round optimal freshness and shelf life of its almond products. The anticipated outcome of this project is a considerable improvement in BFO’s competitive position within the organic sector, directly benefiting farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the supply chain. Ultimately, this project aims to deliver high-quality, innovative almond and olive products to consumers nationwide, fostering broader market access for these organic commodities. By scaling operations to meet rising demand, Burroughs Family Orchards intends to solidify its role as a key contributor to the organic market, positively impacting the businesses of farmers and processors and providing consumers with a premium product choice.

original_description: The Rock Front Ranch’s (RFR) project goal is to increase market access to organic products by improving the efficiency of transporting organic fruit to organic minded consumers and generating employment opportunities in a community with persistent poverty. Rock Front Ranch (RFR) has provided organic jujube fruit to 29 Whole Foods in Southern California since 2017. Recently, the ranch has endeavored to serve Whole Foods and other organic stores in the Northern California region. Those efforts have been curtailed by lack of sufficient transportation capabilities and the prohibitive expense of contracting for 3rd party delivery. The addition of two delivery trailers would allow RFR to provide both fresh and dried organic jujube fruit to the entire network of Whole Foods in Northern California, an additional 39 stores, as well as other organic stores. Two trailers will provide the capacity to deliver fresh and dried organic jujube fruit to both Northern and Southern California markets simultaneously, increasing efficiency as well as creating two 4 to-four new employment opportunities for residents of the Cuyama Valley, a community with persistent poverty.
updated_description: The Rock Front Ranch’s (RFR) project aims to enhance market access for organic jujube fruit, a key component of its operations since 2017, by improving transportation efficiency and generating employment opportunities within the Cuyama Valley community. This project will involve the acquisition of two specialized delivery trailers designed to facilitate the simultaneous distribution of both fresh and dried organic jujube fruit to a broader network of retail outlets. Specifically, RFR intends to serve an additional 39 Whole Foods stores located throughout Northern California, alongside its existing 29 partners in Southern California, as well as numerous other organic stores. The anticipated outcome is a significant expansion of market reach for RFR’s product, directly benefiting farmers and processors involved in the jujube supply chain. The project will create two new, full-time employment positions for residents of the Cuyama Valley, addressing the community’s persistent economic challenges. RFR’s expanded operations will provide a reliable supply of organic jujubes to retailers and consumers seeking this fruit, increasing the availability of domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. The success of this project will be measured by the volume of jujube fruit delivered to market and the number of new jobs created, ultimately supporting the economic viability of the ranch and contributing to the prosperity of the Cuyama Valley community.

awardee_name: California Craft Maltings, LLC dba Admiral Maltings
original_description: The purpose of this project is to purchase and install milling equipment to allow for new product offerings and expanded organic capacity for milled raw grains. It is a natural extension of what Admiral Maltings already does to mill and package organic flour for bakeries and grist (raw grains) for distillers. Milling organic flour for bakers and distillers’ grist uses similar agricultural ingredients to what California Craft Maltings already sources. But it is a different process from malting organic grain and requires new equipment. This equipment purchase will allow Admiral Maltings to increase the contracted acreage of organically grown grain, increase land under organic certification, and create a more resilient, local agricultural economy to supply bakers and distillers. It will lead to aggregate efficiencies for growing, storing, and processing organic grains. There is increased consumer demand to know who grows their food, where it is grown, where it is processed, and who mills it.
updated_description: Admiral Maltings’ project centers on the strategic purchase and installation of milling equipment to facilitate new product offerings and expand organic capacity for milled raw grains, representing a natural progression from the company’s existing operations of producing and packaging organic flour for bakeries and grist for distillers. This equipment acquisition will enable Admiral Maltings to increase the contracted acreage of organically grown grain, bolster the overall volume of land certified as organic, and foster a more resilient, localized agricultural economy to supply bakers and distillers with high-quality ingredients. The anticipated outcomes include aggregate efficiencies throughout the entire process – from the cultivation of grains to their storage and subsequent processing – ultimately benefiting farmers and processors involved in the organic grain supply chain. By expanding its capabilities, Admiral Maltings will contribute to meeting increased consumer demand for traceability and transparency regarding food production, ensuring that stakeholders have confidence in the origin and processing of their ingredients. This project will support the scaling of organic grain production, thereby enhancing the availability of these commodities to a growing base of consumers and processors who prioritize locally sourced and certified organic products. The increased production capacity will positively impact the economic viability of farms engaged in organic grain cultivation and strengthen the position of processors utilizing these grains in their manufacturing operations.

original_description: California Certified Organic Farmers (CCOF), Inc. has over fifty years of experience working with organic producers and is now the largest member-based organic agriculture organization in California, and owns the largest organic certification company in the U.S. The purpose of this grant is to improve and expand market access for small and underserved organic farmers. The three goals for this grant are: 1) to address two key obstacles restricting growth in organic sales: which are the lack of consumer clarity on what “organic” means and a perceived lack of consumer confidence in the seal; 2) to create market paths for small and underserved organic producers by linking them with buyers actively looking to source their products; and 3) to educate and provide farmers with tools to talk to consumers and buyers about organic. These goals will be achieved by launching a multi-channel marketing campaign, creating a marketing toolkit, marketing trainings for farmers, and updating and disseminating an organic sourcing directory to school and retail buyers. The expected outcomes of this project are that consumers and buyers will gain knowledge about organic products and that small and underserved producers will increase organic production to meet the increased demand through direct-market channels and buyer business transactions.
updated_description: California Certified Organic Farmers (CCOF), Inc. is undertaking a project focused on enhancing market access for small organic producers across California. The primary purpose of this initiative is to address two significant barriers to organic sales growth: a lack of consumer understanding regarding the meaning of “organic” and a resulting lack of consumer confidence in the certification seal, alongside creating direct market pathways for small producers. CCOF will achieve this by launching a multi-channel marketing campaign, developing a comprehensive marketing toolkit, and updating a directory of organic sourcing opportunities available to school and retail buyers. The anticipated outcomes of this project include increased knowledge among consumers and buyers about organic products, and a corresponding rise in organic production by small producers through direct market channels and business transactions with buyers. This will support farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in organic agriculture. Ultimately, CCOF seeks to bolster the availability of domestically produced organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients. The project will benefit stakeholders involved in the organic supply chain, working to expand market opportunities for these producers and increase the overall volume of organically produced goods.

original_description: Straus Family Creamery, Inc. has over twenty-five years of experience processing raw organic dairy sourced from a network of farms in the Northern Bay Area region of California into value-added products. The goals of this grant proposal are to 1) Expand local dairy processing capacity and increase revenues for organic dairy farmers in the Northern Bay Area region of California 2) Help producers find solutions to rising expenses and improve their overall climate resiliency, 3) Support continued growth opportunity for organic dairy producers, and 4) Ensure opportunity for the next generation of organic dairy producers and, thereby, the future local organic dairy supply. To achieve these goals Straus Family Creamery will install new processing equipment, increasing yogurt and ice cream-making capacity by 200%. This expanded capacity will allow Straus Family Creamery to increase fluid milk purchases by over three million gallons per year at a 12.5% organic premium price to farmers. Straus Family Creamery will pursue national distribution for these products through existing key retail partnerships, increasing the value of organic yogurt and organic ice cream supply by $10.4 million. To further address the crisis facing regional organic dairy producers the business will offset the cost of creating Carbon Farm Plans for up to ten dairies in its network, contributing to a reduction of feed costs and a strengthening of climate resiliency for these farms. Straus Family Creamery will also work with Chico State University to provide education and technical assistance to dairy students interested in transitioning their family dairy to organic and or pursuing a job in organic dairy.
updated_description: Straus Family Creamery, Inc. proposes a project designed to expand local dairy processing capacity and bolster the organic dairy supply chain within the Northern Bay Area region of California. This initiative will involve the installation of new processing equipment, dramatically increasing yogurt and ice cream-making capabilities by 200%, allowing for the purchase of over three million gallons of fluid milk annually from organic dairy farmers at a 12.5% premium. The expanded production will be utilized to create and distribute organic yogurt and organic ice cream products through existing retail partnerships, with an anticipated increase in the value of these products by $10.4 million. Straus Family Creamery will also create Carbon Farm Plans for up to ten dairies within its network, directly offsetting the cost of these plans and contributing to reduced feed expenses for the farmers. This project anticipates supporting the continued growth of organic dairy producers and creating opportunities for the next generation of organic dairy producers, securing the future local organic dairy supply. The project aims to strengthen the overall organic dairy supply chain and ensure greater resilience for the stakeholders involved. By increasing production and establishing new distribution channels, Straus Family Creamery intends to benefit farmers, processors, and ultimately, consumers seeking organic dairy products. The expanded capacity will create more market opportunities for organic dairy products, improving access for consumers and bolstering the economic viability of organic dairy operations within the region.

original_description: Despite having a high density of small farms, Southern California significantly lacks certified organic processing facilities, an issue that negatively affects small and underserved farms that rely on timeconsuming, costly hand labor to process and add value to their organic commodities. To address this 9 bottleneck, The Ecology Center (TEC) proposes to expand its processing and distribution capacity for valueadded products (VAP) made from organic corn, legumes, and fruit, by providing a shared processing service to facilitate market access for small organic farms. Project activities include 1) renovating its processing warehouse to accommodate new equipment for high-demand VAP including jams, tortillas, dried beans, and sauces, 2) expanding partnerships to benefit at least 15 organic farms, and 3) expanding TEC’s current DTC sales model that reaches 70,000 consumers to larger channels, by leveraging partners’ channels and relationships with regional groceries. This project will increase processing by 80,000 lbs. of organic corn, legumes, and fruit processed into 372,000 units of organic VAP. It will reach at least 40,000 more repeat consumers, influencing up to 400,000 new consumers by the addition of 10 or more sales channels. This project will facilitate market access for 15 or more Southern Californian organic producers (at least 10 of which are small, beginner, or underserved farms). It will also increase their profitability with access to processing equipment and increase consumption of locally made organic products–inducing approximately $2.2 million in sales by the project’s third year.
updated_description: The Ecology Center (TEC) proposes a project to significantly increase value-added processing capacity for organic agricultural commodities in Southern California, addressing a critical gap in market access for small farms. This project will involve renovating TEC’s processing warehouse to accommodate new equipment specifically designed for the production of high-demand value-added products, including jams, tortillas, dried beans, and sauces. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in processing volume, with the aim of processing 80,000 pounds of organic corn, legumes, and fruit into 372,000 units of organic value-added products. The project seeks to benefit at least fifteen Southern Californian organic producers, with a priority on supporting small and beginning farms, ultimately reaching an estimated 40,000 more repeat consumers and potentially influencing up to 400,000 new consumers through the leveraging of expanded sales channels. This initiative is expected to generate approximately $2.2 million in sales across the project’s third year. The project’s success will be measured by increased market access for these farmers, bolstering their profitability through access to processing equipment. This project will ultimately enhance the availability of locally produced organic goods, and support processors and stakeholders involved in the organic supply chain.

original_description: Turning Green continues integrating local, organic food into California’s K-12 school meal programs. This project will leverage the massive purchasing scale of the school food sector to grow the organic supply chain by bringing together school food networks, small disadvantaged organic farmers, and local agricultural support organizations. The project will provide added training and technical support to school food service teams and organic farmers to align planning, implementation, logistics, and metrics to grow the sale of organic products to schools in California. Given that much of the current food purchased and served in schools is not organic, this segment is an attractive and burgeoning opportunity to expand the organic marketplace. Turning Green has facilitated and supported procurement and has served fresh, local, organic, nutritious food in K-12 schools. In 2020/21, during the pandemic, they worked with a local school district of 28,000 students to transition its entire meal program to 100% organic with 41 new vendors, resulting in over $17 million that flowed into the organic supply chain. Since then, Turning Green has partnered with seven more school districts to spur demand and enlist support from many small organic farmers to grow supply. Working with producers and school districts, Turning Green identifies gaps and market barriers while creating innovative systemic solutions for crop planning, delivering, and consuming high-quality goods. An experienced team is equipped to expand their work in building the organic market with school food programs. Leveraging local agricultural support organizations and school food networks, the project will provide added training and technical support to school food service teams and small disadvantaged farmers to align planning, implementation, logistics, and metrics to meet school requirements.
updated_description: Turning Green is undertaking a project to integrate more local, organic food into California’s K-12 school meal programs, leveraging the substantial purchasing power of the school food sector to cultivate a robust organic supply chain. The project aims to connect school food networks with small, disadvantaged organic farmers and associated agricultural support organizations, focusing on the acquisition of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients currently unavailable in organic form. This initiative anticipates a significant expansion of the organic marketplace, driven by increased demand from schools across California. The project will directly benefit farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic agricultural commodities. Specifically, Turning Green has successfully partnered with seven more school districts since 2020/21, building upon a prior effort where they collaborated with a district of 28,000 students, transitioning their entire meal program to 100% organic through 41 new vendors, resulting in over $17 million flowing into the organic supply chain. By working to identify gaps and market barriers, Turning Green will create systemic solutions for the planning, delivery, and consumption of high-quality organic goods within school food programs, ultimately enhancing the availability of these products for consumers.

original_description: Ferreira & Son Dairy has been certified organic since 2007 and became certified grass fed in 2016. Historic drought and increasing feed costs in recent years have forced local dairies to make decisions about the future of their generational businesses. In response to these industry and climate -based challenges, Ferreira & Son Dairy has embarked on a five-year plan to remain self-sufficient by expanding and diversifying production, taking over their own distribution thereby cutting the costs of middle distributors. During the first year, 2021-2022, Ferriera & Son Dairy completed the first phase of this expansion, building Humboldt County’s first truly local milk processing and bottling plant. The milk is processed right from the tank, bottled into glass bottles, then distributed directly to local stores. The next phase of the project is the 11 acquisition of equipment to expand production. The funds from this opportunity will enable the dairy to purchase equipment that will quadruple production from 300 to 2000 gallons per week of milk with diversified fats percentages that can be used to develop, produce and distribute other products that will generate more income for the dairy and increase growth of the market for organic products overall in the local economy.
updated_description: Ferreira & Son Dairy has embarked on a five-year plan to ensure the continued viability of its generational business, responding to significant industry and environmental challenges. This project’s primary purpose is to establish a self-sufficient dairy operation through expansion and direct market distribution, ultimately cutting reliance on middle distributors and reducing costs. During the initial phase, Ferreira & Son Dairy completed the construction of Humboldt County’s first local milk processing and bottling plant, which allows for the immediate processing of milk directly from the tank, followed by bottling into glass bottles. The funds secured through this opportunity will enable the purchase of equipment designed to dramatically increase production capacity, projecting a quadrupling of output from 300 to 2000 gallons per week. This expanded capacity will also facilitate the production of milk with varied fat percentages, allowing for the development and distribution of new products, thereby generating additional revenue streams for the dairy. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened market position for Ferreira & Son Dairy and an increased supply of organic agricultural commodities within the local economy. The beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and consumers who will have access to locally produced organic milk and potentially other organic dairy products. The project aims to bolster the local economy by supporting a significant increase in the availability of organic agricultural commodities, contributing to a more robust market for these goods and offering economic support to stakeholders involved in the dairy industry.

original_description: Alexandre Dairy (the “Dairy”), is the 1st Certified “Regenerative” US organic dairy, producing 100% A2/A2, grass-based milk, and organic hay and silage, is seeking funding to replace antiquated milk collection, cooling, and storage equipment and to purchase post-harvest hay collection equipment to increase domestic supply chain capacity and facilitate expanded market development. As a vertically integrated company, the Dairy supplies organic milk to Alexandre Family Creamery (“AFC”) for processing into Alexandre Family Farm (“AFF”) branded, as well as co-packaged, products. Nationwide demand for organic, A2/A2 grass-based, certified regenerative milk has significantly increased but the outdated raw dairy milk collection equipment cannot keep up with weekly demand and projected brand growth, and the Dairy’s ailing harvest equipment curtails its ability to collect and store feeds within a short harvest season. The Dairy currently produces 55% of its organic livestock forage annually and can increase production by 10- 15% simply by upgrading equipment, helping to reduce regional pressure on organic livestock forages. Investment in new equipment supporting milk collection/storage, post-harvest hay/silage processing, and transport to provide on-farm resiliency, will support the Dairy’s investment in national market penetration of its organic farm-gate products. The project would benefit Pavel’s Yogurt Company and Kefir Lab, which AFC co-packs for and the Farm sells organic raw dairy, Rumiano Cheese, which the Dairy supplies with 25% of its weekly organic milk volume, and Humboldt Creamery which also uses 22% of the Dairy’s production to make organic fluid milk, ice cream and milk powder. In addition, the West Coast’s organic, pasture based dairy producers which support 85% of California’s organic fluid production will benefit from the Dairy’s brand penetration into new and expanded regions educating consumers about the importance of California climate friendly milk, innovative on farm certifications that add margin, and models for small organic family farm expansion and innovation focused on genetics, grass-fed and flash grazing practices.
updated_description: Alexandre Dairy is seeking funding to modernize its raw dairy collection, cooling, and storage infrastructure, alongside purchasing new post-harvest hay collection equipment, to substantially increase domestic supply chain capacity and facilitate expanded market development. This project encompasses the acquisition of upgraded equipment crucial for handling 55% of its annual organic livestock forage, ultimately allowing for a 10-15% production increase. The anticipated outcomes of this investment include increased capacity to supply organic milk to Alexandre Family Creamery, Pavel’s Yogurt Company, Kefir Lab, Rumiano Cheese, and Humboldt Creamery, all of whom utilize the Dairy’s production for their respective products. Specifically, the modernized operation will bolster the availability of organic milk to processors and retailers, thereby benefiting farmers and consumers alike. The Dairy’s enhanced capabilities will support its strategy for national market penetration of its organic, farm-gate products, while also positively impacting organic milk producers across the West Coast, particularly those focused on California’s fluid organic dairy production. Ultimately, this project aims to increase the supply of high-quality organic milk, strengthening the market position for the Dairy and supporting related stakeholders throughout the organic food supply chain.

original_description: The project proposes a planning and implementation process for the development of a permanent certified organic, dry bean processing facility located in Olathe, Colorado. The facility will provide a certified organic process for the cleaning of dry beans received directly from field harvesting and enable versatile packaging of dry beans. The planning process will consist of completing Technical and Economic Feasibility analyses and Marketing and Business Plans for such a facility. The first goal is to optimize the technical aspects of processing to ensure efficiency and increase capacity in a certified organic dry bean cleaning and packaging facility. This will provide a finished product, packaged in various weights, which accommodate market needs and consumer demand. The project will develop a Marketing and Business plan to optimize economic benefits and purchase of equipment to implement a facility. Project is expected to improve access for producers in the Western Slope to sell products into regional and national organic dry bean markets, provide incentives to expand the volume and varieties of organic dry beans grown in these regions, and increase regional organic dry bean sourcing accessibility for buyers and consumers.
updated_description: The Olathe Organic Dry Bean Facility project proposes the development of a permanent, certified organic dry bean processing facility located in Olathe, Colorado, with the primary purpose of establishing a streamlined and efficient process for cleaning and packaging dry beans directly from field harvesting. This facility will be built to optimize technical aspects of processing, ensuring capacity is increased to accommodate market needs and consumer demand, and will be equipped with the necessary machinery for versatile packaging options in various weights. The anticipated outcomes of this project include improved access for farmers in the Western Slope to sell their products into regional and national organic dry bean markets, creating incentives for expanding the volume and varieties of organic dry beans grown in these regions, and greater regional organic dry bean sourcing accessibility for buyers and consumers. Specifically, the project will support the processing of dry beans, ultimately benefiting farmers, processors, and consumers alike. The facility’s operation will address a critical need for expanded market pathways for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. By creating a dedicated processing facility, the project aims to bolster the organic dry bean supply chain and make these products more readily available to a wider range of buyers. The project’s success will translate into increased volumes of organic dry beans moving through the market, ultimately supporting the economic viability of organic farming operations and expanding consumer choice.

original_description: In 2022, a farm partner company received a grant to purchase equipment to turn organic peaches into puree that could be used in food service and production of beverages and value-added foods. The goal was 12 to make Colorado’s celebrated peaches available year-round. An additional goal was to upcycle waste peaches. Tons of peaches go to waste each year because of minor imperfections or because they are too ripe to travel through traditional distribution channels. This summer, that company began puree production for restaurants, breweries, and other food producers. This project includes two goals; 1) to market this local resource year-round in ways that honor the goodness and flavor of the fruit and 2) to celebrate this local resource within the community, in ways that can nourish ALL community members. One solution is to package the puree in squeeze popsicles that are shelf-stable, to be frozen on-demand. The joy of a squeeze popsicle is a true celebration of local flavors. The plan is to keep the fruit content near 100 percent. This means that these organic popsicles will be healthful for everyone. This equipment grant will allow Honey Rock to purchase a popsicle machine, and supporting equipment, to make delicious, safely-produced servings of fruit. This will help keep costs down and make these items affordable for distribution to community schools, hospitals, and the food bank. This product is in line with the farm’s initiatives to reduce food waste by upcycling peaches to 1) adopt the most earth-friendly practices, 2) level the farm’s working hours by adding off-season work to solve local production and storage problems that keep local institutions from serving more local fruit, and 3) bring greater awareness to and appreciation of local agricultural resources.
updated_description: Honey Rock Farm initiated a project in 2022, receiving a grant to establish a system for transforming organic peaches into puree, with the primary purpose of making Colorado’s celebrated peaches available year-round and upcycling waste peaches. This project involves the purchase of a popsicle machine and supporting equipment, enabling the farm to produce shelf-stable, fruit-based servings for distribution. The anticipated outcome is to create a consistent supply of organic peach puree, catering to the needs of restaurants, breweries, and other food producers, while simultaneously addressing significant quantities of fruit waste. The beneficiaries of this project include farmers, processors, and consumers seeking high-quality, local fruit products. Specifically, the farm intends to make this resource available to community schools, hospitals, and the food bank, ensuring affordable access to healthful peach puree. This initiative represents a practical solution to reduce waste and address challenges related to seasonal fruit availability, supporting stakeholders involved in food production and distribution. The farm’s goal is to increase the supply of local fruit and reduce the challenges related to off-season storage and production, thereby contributing to a more reliable and accessible local food system.

original_description: By working with several high-influence partners in the organic food space, the Colorado Grain Chain (CGC) will enhance market opportunities for producers, processors, and value-added product makers of organic grain for human consumption. Although grains make up an average of 30-50% of dietary intake, the organic grain market for human consumption is relatively limited, with little emphasis on local sourcing. Since the inception of the Colorado Grain Chain in 2019, the non-profit organization's mission has been to grow and connect a community-centered grain economy in the state of Colorado. This work involves connecting the membership base of 50+ Business and Consumer Members to educational and marketing resources, partners, and technical assistance. CGC’s membership base ranges from farmers, processors (millers and maltsters), to artisanal makers (bakers, brewers, distillers, chefs), food hubs, and institutions. The Organic Market Development Grant (OMDG) will allow Colorado Grain Chain to support stakeholders in the grain supply chain through the promotion of organic grains in value-added marketplaces in alignment with the Colorado Grown Grains marketing initiative, while building off and expanding current program models to organic grains. Specifically, the project seeks to support connections through the grain supply chain that a) incentivize the cultivation of diverse organic grains through Microgrants for small businesses/farms, b) enhance distribution of organic grains through increased visibility in value-added market channels, and c) increase market awareness and demand for locally sourced, food-grade, organic grain through event coordination and the continuation of the Colorado Grown Grains co-brand strategy.
updated_description: Colorado Grain Chain will undertake a project to enhance market opportunities for farmers, processors, and value-added product makers involved in the production of organic grains for human consumption within Colorado. This initiative, supported by the Organic Market Development Grant, aims to stimulate the cultivation of a broader range of organic grains through the provision of microgrants to small businesses and farms, thereby increasing the availability of these commodities. The project will also focus on improving the distribution of organic grains by increasing their visibility in value-added market channels, aligning with the Colorado Grown Grains marketing strategy and building upon existing program models. A key element of the effort will be to improve market awareness and demand for locally sourced food grade grains. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened grain supply chain that supports the engagement of stakeholders throughout the supply chain and increased market awareness and demand for locally sourced organic grains. The beneficiaries of this project include farmers, processors like millers and maltsters, and artisanal makers such as bakers, brewers, and distillers, along with food hubs and institutions. By providing financial support and promotional initiatives, the Colorado Grain Chain intends to connect these stakeholders and stimulate a robust, locally-focused organic grain economy in Colorado, bolstering the production and consumption of these valuable agricultural commodities.

original_description: Hobbs Meyer, LLC DBA Pueblo Seed Food Co (Pueblo Seed) is a family farm located in Southwestern Colorado. The farm has been certified organic since 2001 by the Colorado Department of Agriculture and specializes in open pollinated vegetable seeds, varietal garlic, and heritage grains and legumes on 30 acres. This project will allow Pueblo Seed to purchase equipment to increase capacity in its facility to scale up processing and develop new products from these crops for seed feed and food markets. During the COVID19 pandemic, the farm began producing a line of 7 value-added grain products and working towards opening a seed and bakehouse. In 2021, the farm purchased a 5300-square foot commercial building in downtown Cortez. In 2022-2023, the farm purchased a food grade seed cleaning line and other grain processing equipment for making products and providing seed cleaning services to partner growers. During 2023, the farm increased the seed of 10 species of drought and heat tolerant grains and legumes. Organic drought hardy heritage grains and cover crops, in particular, are in extremely short supply in the U.S. (Hubbard et al., 2022). Pueblo Seed’s goal is to become a central organic supplier of cowpeas, tepary beans, finger millets, pearl millets, amaranths, grain sorghums, culinary ryes, culinary barleys, select wheat, and flour maize. The business will utilize its existing seed customer list and long-term relationships with national seed companies to increase the seed market and work through food hubs, food pantries, and institutions to increase food market share.
updated_description: Hobbs Meyer, LLC DBA Pueblo Seed Food Co (Pueblo Seed) is undertaking a project to significantly expand its processing capabilities and product offerings, driven by a strategic investment in new equipment and a recently acquired facility. The core of this expansion involves the purchase of a food-grade seed cleaning line, alongside other grain processing equipment, all aimed at increasing production capacity within the 5300-square foot commercial building located in downtown Cortez. Pueblo Seed’s objective is to establish itself as a central supplier of a range of organic grains and legumes, specifically focusing on 10 species of drought and heat-tolerant varieties including cowpeas, tepary beans, finger millets, pearl millets, amaranths, grain sorghums, culinary ryes, culinary barleys, select wheat, and flour maize. This expansion will allow the farm to fulfill increasing market demands for these specialized crops, capitalizing on an existing customer list and relationships with national seed companies while also distributing products through food hubs, food pantries, and institutional channels. The anticipated outcome is an increased supply of organic grains and legumes to various stakeholders, including farmers, processors, and consumers. By bolstering its production and distribution network, Pueblo Seed intends to meet the growing need for these crops, particularly those exhibiting resilience to challenging growing conditions. This project supports the development of new market pathways for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities, contributing to a more robust supply chain for these specific grain varieties.

original_description: Consumer awareness about Connecticut’s certified organic producers and handlers is largely unknown. The Connecticut Department of Agriculture will use these grant funds to increase market access for certified organic producers, producers transitioning to organic farming, and certified organic handlers in Connecticut by coordinating with Transition to Organic Partnership (TOPP) partners, including the University of Connecticut (UConn) Extension and the Connecticut Northeast Organic Farming Association (CT NOFA). The goal of this project is to strengthen new and emerging markets, strengthen farm to institution market channels, increase producer and handler knowledge and skills to market their organic products, and foster consumer education to increase demand for organic products. Proposed goals will be accomplished by 1) evaluating the current market for CT Grown organic products in CT to understand consumers’ perceptions and understanding and to evaluate areas for growth and improved market access; 2) examining 14 opportunities for CT Grown organic product sales specifically for farm-to-institution; 3) implementing new communication strategies to reach consumers in the state to increase awareness and highlight CT Grown organic products and producers (which considers the information gained through the market evaluation), and 4) developing and conducting a workshop series for transitioning and certified organic producers and handlers to implement new marketing strategies and capitalize on areas for improvement identified by the results of marketing research.
updated_description: Connecticut Department of Agriculture will undertake a project to bolster market access for certified organic producers and handlers within the state, focusing on increasing consumer awareness and demand for Connecticut Grown organic products. The project will achieve this through a four-pronged approach: initially, a comprehensive evaluation of the current market for Connecticut Grown organic products will be conducted to understand consumer perceptions and identify opportunities for improvement; second, the project will examine fourteen specific avenues for farm-to-institution sales of these products; third, new communication strategies will be implemented to raise awareness of these products and producers among consumers; and fourth, a workshop series will be developed for transitioning and certified organic producers and handlers to facilitate the adoption of enhanced marketing approaches based on market research findings. The anticipated outcomes include strengthened market channels for organic products, increased producer and handler knowledge and skills related to marketing, and ultimately, greater consumer demand for Connecticut Grown organic goods. The primary beneficiaries of this project are Connecticut farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in organic production and handling, alongside the stakeholders who represent the broader consumer base. This project aims to support the growth of the organic sector within Connecticut by providing resources and strategies to effectively connect producers with markets and build consumer understanding of the value proposition of Connecticut’s organic offerings.

original_description: The Latino Farmers Association’s (LFA) project aims to foster equitable participation in the organic marketplace for historically underserved and socially disadvantaged farmers and ranchers, veterans, and beginning farmers, with a concerted effort to combat food deserts in the District of Columbia, Maryland, and Virginia. To do so, LFA will pursue four key objectives. First, LFA will expand the organic vendor capacity of the Van Ness Farmers Market, in the District of Columbia, by facilitating a transition to an exclusively organic market and obtaining organic certifications for vendors via partnerships with the Transition to Organic Partnership Program (TOPP) Regional Lead, Pennsylvania Certified Organic, and the Organic Trade Association. Second, LFA will open three new organic farmers markets in healthy food priority areas in the District of Columbia and one in Southwest Virginia. Third, the association will develop a scalable Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) producer-to-consumer system supported by a Virtual Marketplace, which will connect market vendors with individual and institutional consumers. LFA will develop a diversified marketing strategy to build robust relationships with institutional buyers, distributors, grocery stores, and food co-ops. Finally, LFA will enhance market accessibility for producers by acquiring one box truck, one mobile market, and one delivery van. This will enable LFA to increase the scale and variety of product offerings that are now limited by transport and storage constraints. By providing an enhanced distribution process that reduces the cost of transport to market and includes eggs, meat, dairy and value-added products, LFA will diversify the producers’ income streams and cash flow, while lowering the collective carbon footprint.
updated_description: The Latino Farmers Association’s project aims to expand organic market opportunities for farmers and ranchers, with a focus on addressing food access challenges in the District of Columbia, Maryland, and Virginia. This initiative will achieve this by implementing several key strategies, including the complete transition of the Van Ness Farmers Market in the District of Columbia to an exclusively organic market, facilitated through partnerships with organizations like the Transition to Organic Partnership Program (TOPP) Regional Lead, Pennsylvania Certified Organic, and the Organic Trade Association. Furthermore, LFA will establish three new organic farmers markets in designated priority areas within the District of Columbia and one in Southwest Virginia, significantly increasing access to fresh produce. To support these markets and the associated producers, LFA will develop a scalable Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) producer-to-consumer system utilizing a Virtual Marketplace, attracting both market vendors and individual and institutional consumers. The organization will also acquire one box truck, one mobile market, and one delivery van to improve the distribution of goods, allowing for the inclusion of a wider range of products, such as eggs, meat, and dairy, thereby diversifying revenue streams for participating stakeholders. Ultimately, this project anticipates increasing the availability of organic agricultural commodities and bolstering the capacity of farmers and ranchers to reach consumers through enhanced distribution processes. This will positively impact the communities served by these markets and the producers involved, promoting greater access to fresh, organic food options.

original_description: Little Sesame will expand the domestic certified organic chickpea market by increasing aggregation, processing, and distribution of its consumer-packaged line of hummus while simultaneously growing consumer demand through enhanced sales and marketing capacity. Over the past several years, droughts, flooding, and war in top chickpea-producing countries have led to an increased market demand for domestically grown chickpeas. That, paired with a growing interest in plant-based foods that rely on chickpeas and other legumes, creates a unique opportunity for organic chickpea producers in the United States. Yet, the market remains underdeveloped. Northern Plains farmers in the U.S. have difficulty finding direct sales relationships for chickpeas, a crop abundantly grown in rotation with wheat due to its soilbuilding properties. By achieving SQF certification, investing in manufacturing improvements, and implementing a shopper, trade, and field marketing program, Little Sesame will leverage market demand and create a much-needed direct market for 10 domestic chickpea farmers, purchasing 800,000 pounds of chickpeas annually across 2,000 production acres. Marketing efforts targeted at distributors, retailers, grocery stores, and household consumers will highlight the value of choosing products sourced from domestically grown certified organic chickpea growers and bring increased opportunities for certified organic producers for years to come.
updated_description: Little Sesame will expand the domestic certified organic chickpea market by increasing aggregation, processing, and distribution of its consumer-packaged line of hummus, capitalizing on heightened market demand resulting from droughts, flooding, and geopolitical instability impacting top chickpea-producing nations. The project will purchase 800,000 pounds of chickpeas annually from 10 domestic chickpea farmers, sourced from approximately 2,000 production acres, and involve investments in achieving SQF certification and improvements to manufacturing processes. This initiative is designed to create a much-needed direct market for these farmers and, through enhanced sales and marketing capacity, stimulate increased consumer interest in plant-based foods reliant on chickpeas and other legumes. The anticipated outcomes include the establishment of a robust domestic supply chain for certified organic chickpeas and the promotion of domestically grown products to consumers, distributors, retailers, and grocery stores. Ultimately, Little Sesame seeks to benefit farmers by providing a stable outlet for their crops and to deliver a valued product to consumers. The project will support processors and other stakeholders within the food industry involved in the production and distribution of hummus and related products. By focusing on the availability of certified organic chickpeas, Little Sesame aims to strengthen the position of these farmers and bolster the overall organic agricultural sector within the United States.

original_description: The project will stimulate the demand for and increase the sales of organic products by promoting the science-backed benefits of USDA certified organic products and farming to consumers. Organic is an umbrella term that addresses several individual product claims; however, consumers remain confused about the wholistic requirements of the USDA organic label and how they translate to benefits for people and the planet. By providing consumers with access to more credible information about what organic production and processing means and the benefits it provides, consumption of organic will increase. This joint project by The Organic Center and the Organic Trade Association (OTA owns the TOC) will be done in collaboration with Organic Voices and an Industry Advisory Committee (including TOPP regional leads) to develop fresh creative content on the regulatory and science-based environmental, animal, and human benefits of organic. Targeted content that motivates consumers to purchase pinpointed products like organic dairy, grain, and fiber will be prioritized. The creative content will be promoted through a full-scale integrated marketing campaign leveraging TOC and Organic Voices' existing consumer networks and paid advertising. Targeted efforts will ensure that promotion reaches beyond the mainstream organic markets into regions and communities where organic production is not already thriving. The Industry Advisory Committee will include partners from underserved communities and pinpointed markets to ensure the 16 creative and promotional campaign meets industry needs and expectations. The project will culminate by sharing learnings and successes in the creation of effective organic consumer marketing strategies, content, and messaging with the organic industry at large to increase their return on investment for future marketing opportunities. Printed copies of the final report will be disseminated to all addresses listed in the Organic Integrity Database (approximately 27,400 addresses), which includes around 19,000 producers (livestock and crop scopes) and 8,400 buyers (handler scopes).
updated_description: The Organic Center, in collaboration with the Organic Trade Association, Organic Voices, and an Industry Advisory Committee, will stimulate demand and increase sales of certified organic products by providing consumers with credible information regarding the science-backed benefits of organic production and processing. This project will develop fresh, creative content focused on the regulatory and environmental, animal, and human benefits of organic farming, prioritizing targeted promotion of specific products such as organic dairy, grains, and fibers. The anticipated outcome is an increased consumption of organic commodities, benefiting farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the organic industry. The project’s activities will concentrate on reaching consumers in regions and communities where organic production is not currently prominent, maximizing the impact of a full-scale integrated marketing campaign leveraging existing consumer networks and paid advertising. The Industry Advisory Committee, comprised of partners from various markets, will ensure the campaign’s relevance and effectiveness, culminating in the dissemination of learning and successful strategies to the organic industry at large. Approximately 27,400 addresses within the Organic Integrity Database, including roughly 19,000 producers and 8,400 buyers, will receive the final report, reflecting a commitment to broadening access to organic products and driving increased sales within the organic sector.

original_description: The goal of this project is to create a new market and enhance the value of certified organic peanuts produced and processed in Georgia. The project will forge a new partnership between the Georgia Organic Peanut Association, a farmer-owned marketing cooperative, and Oliver Oil Company, a small family-owned processor of cold-pressed culinary oil. Together, they will acquire parallel processing equipment that will enable, for the first time in the Southeast, the production of Certified Organic peanut oil by expanding processing capacity and preventing commingling of organic and non-organic products. This new enterprise 17 will be supported by a joint marketing campaign to stimulate demand. As a result of the project, one processing facility and one storage facility will obtain organic certification for the first time, fostering a new local supply chain for Certified Organic commodities. Marketing through the Georgia Organic Peanut Association, farmers will increase the production, processing, and sales of Certified Organic peanuts grown in the region by 50%. The project will have a beneficial financial effect on no fewer than 15 farmers in the Southeast, including two beginning farmers and two socially disadvantaged producers, and create one new job.
