updated_description: The Georgia Organic Peanut Association, in partnership with Oliver Oil Company, is undertaking a project to establish a new market for certified organic peanuts produced and processed in Georgia, aiming to significantly enhance the value of these commodities. This initiative will involve the acquisition of parallel processing equipment, specifically designed to enable the first production of certified organic peanut oil in the Southeast, thereby expanding processing capacity and preventing the commingling of organic and non-organic products. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a 50% increase in the production, processing, and sales of certified organic peanuts grown in the region, as driven by a joint marketing campaign managed by the Georgia Organic Peanut Association. Furthermore, at least fifteen farmers across the Southeast will experience a beneficial financial effect, with two beginning farmers and two socially disadvantaged producers receiving particular support. The project will result in one processing facility and one storage facility obtaining organic certification for the first time, establishing a new local supply chain for certified organic commodities. The stakeholders involved – including farmers, processors, and consumers – will benefit from increased availability of organic peanuts and peanut oil. This project is expected to generate a positive financial impact for the participating farmers and establish a stronger market for organically produced agricultural goods within the region.

original_description: The Organic Grain Gateway of Iowa (OGGI) project will help stabilize the organic grains and livestock feed supply chain. It will offer new market access for Iowa’s organic grain farmers, reduce reliance on imports for the coastal organic livestock markets, and ultimately increase organic grain production in Iowa. This will be achieved by assembling a dedicated organic grain aggregation and marketing terminal in central Iowa 24 with existing direct access to Norfolk Southern, BNSF and Union Pacific railroads the only site in Iowa with this connectivity. By the end of the project, Iowa’s organic corn and soybean farmers will see an increased demand for organic products, specifically on the East and West Coasts which currently rely on imports to meet regional demand for these products. By connecting these three critical railways in one location, centrally located in the largest producing state of organic corn and soybeans, organic farmers in the state of Iowa will have direct access to new markets. Together, with the support of Iowa organic farmers, USDA NOP TOPP Partners, the Iowa Department of Agriculture, and The Organic Trade Association, the project will be a crucial step in sustaining the growth of domestic organic production by providing the infrastructure and market access needed.

original_description: Fresh aronia berries are the flagship of Levi Lyle’s business. Blueberry, cranberry, and cherry fruit industries operate under a business model that has not served the infant aronia berry industry well. Iowa farmers have had to export aronia to Michigan where processing infrastructure exists. These locations require consolidation of produce into 100,000 pounds to conduct a “small run” of concentrate juice or consolidation of 1,000,000 pounds to gain access to cleaning and freezing facilities. Further challenges in aggregation and financial risks larger startups undertake exacerbate these challenges. The success of this 1- acre organic certified aronia crop develops out of a strong identity in place-based food. The business has expanded from farmers markets into health-food stores. For this project, Levi Lyle is partnering with a 10- acre organic certified grower to expand his Aronia Berry Organic Purée. The goal for this Aronia business is to successfully market a shelf-stable product created from the whole fruit ingredient, currently unavailable. Unique purée will be bottled in 16 ounces for retail. The Aronia Berry Organic Puree Project will bottle 4,000 gallons of whole berry puree for retailers partnered with this Aronia business. Market feasibility studies demonstrate the products currently available use highly processed concentrated juice, which requires a greater cost to produce in small batches, separates the juice from the fiber, and minimizes aronia’s health benefits located in the fiber and polyphenols. This project will benefit the 100+ aronia producers in the region who are without a market by growing to serve the needs of a struggling aronia industry.
updated_description: Levi Lyle’s Aronia Berry Organic Purée Project aims to create a shelf-stable product from whole aronia berries, addressing a critical need in the market. The project will involve the production of 4,000 gallons of whole berry puree, to be bottled in 16-ounce containers for retail distribution. This initiative seeks to capitalize on the increasing consumer interest in natural food products and the unique nutritional profile of aronia berries, specifically focusing on the fiber and polyphenols found within the fruit. The anticipated outcome of this project is to establish a viable market for a new product, currently unavailable, utilizing a consistent supply chain from a 10-acre organic certified grower. This will directly benefit over 100 aronia producers in the region who currently lack established market channels. The project will support farmers and processors involved in the aronia berry industry, creating a pathway to commercialize their harvest and increase their revenue streams. The resulting product offers a distinct alternative to existing offerings that rely on highly processed concentrated juice, and will ultimately satisfy consumer demand for a product that preserves the inherent health benefits of the aronia berry. By developing and distributing this purée, Levi Lyle’s business anticipates expanding its reach to health-food stores and other retail outlets, thereby strengthening the overall aronia berry industry.

original_description: The purpose of this project is to create a marketplace to sell organic feeds. Currently, a gap exists in the Idaho supply chain between organic commodities that are being grown in the area and the organic feed being consumed. Specialized machines and equipment are used to turn various organic commodities into 20 precise rations and mixtures for feeds. Farmers grow organic crops intended for animal feed but are unable to sell locally because the ability and/or capacity to process the organic commodity into animal feed is unavailable. Thus, the farmer resorts to selling crops to feed processors out of the area, causing the organic feed consumer to buy out of the area as well. This creates significant added costs for both buyer and seller. This project would address the supply chain issue directly. The activities to be performed are the purchase and installation of various machinery and equipment to be used to convert organic crops efficiently and accurately into precise animal feeds. This would enable to create a marketplace for organic animal feeds. The marketplace would create deliverable organic feed products that would include formulated pellets, total mixed rations, and processed commodities that could be used individually or incorporated into the customer's mixed ration for their feeding operation. The expected outcomes would be an increased processing capacity in the area for organic crop farmers and increased consumption of local organic feeds.
updated_description: The Organic Market Development Grant project aims to establish a marketplace for organic animal feeds, directly addressing a critical gap in the Idaho supply chain. This initiative will involve the purchase and installation of specialized machinery and equipment designed to efficiently and accurately convert various organic crops into 20 precise rations and mixtures for feeds. These machines will facilitate the production of deliverable organic feed products, including formulated pellets, total mixed rations, and processed commodities, suitable for use individually or incorporated into customer mixed rations for their feeding operations. The anticipated outcomes of this project include an increased processing capacity within the region for organic crop farmers and a corresponding increase in the consumption of locally produced organic feeds by consumers and ranchers. This marketplace will benefit farmers by providing a viable local outlet for their organically grown crops, eliminating the need to sell to out-of-area processors and thereby reducing transportation costs and logistical challenges. Furthermore, the project will supply organic feed to processors and ranchers, providing a valuable source of locally-sourced ingredients. Ultimately, this marketplace will support a more efficient and localized supply chain, benefiting stakeholders throughout the organic animal feed sector.

original_description: The project goal is to increase farmstead creamery processing capacity and, in doing so, to create a milk market for other organic producers to sell their milk to the North Sky Farm creamery. With the increased processing volume, North Sky Farm will be able to meet the expectations of a wholesale distributor allowing them to sell organic cheese to many more people. The project will increase cheesemaking capacity so they are able to buy milk from another dairy farm in addition to processing milk from their own farm. The project team will rearrange creamery space to accommodate larger equipment, update the wastewater system to accommodate a larger volume, increase personnel to process the larger volume of cheese, and work with a consultant to sell the increased volume of cheese through a distributor. In addition, North Sky Farm is creating a milk market for another producer. Increasing processing will allow them to reach the minimum volume needed to work with wholesale cheese distributors which will bring organic cheese to a much broader customer base. This project would double processing capacity. There are three main expected outcomes: 1) milk contracts offered to two organic dairy farms, North Sky Farm’s own dairy and one other organic dairy thus creating a milk market, 2) processing will expand to a level to be able to sell through a wholesale distributor so their cheese will be able to be sold in mainstream grocery stores over a wide geographic area, and 3) an increase in sales volume to a level where the organic creamery is economically sustainable and is able to continue to employ at least four, and likely more fulltime employees beyond the end of the project period. North Sky Farm will achieve these goals by making some key changes to increase production capacity to remove processing facility equipment bottlenecks that curtail manufacturing capacity.
updated_description: North Sky Farm’s project aims to significantly increase its creamery processing capacity to establish a robust milk market for organic producers and itself. Moon Valley Farm is a certified organic, year-round, diversified produce farm that grows legumes and grains on a small-scale and aggregates legume, grains, fruits, mushrooms, eggs and more from partner farms. The Farm wants to increase processing and aggregation of these crops to benefit its crop rotation plan, whole-farm planning, and to meet customers demand. However, the business lacks the equipment required to increase production, storage, and delivery of these specialty crops. Moon Valley Farm’s goals with this project are to expand capacity to process, aggregate, store and deliver high quality legumes and grains to meet regional customer demand with key pieces of equipment. This project will strengthen the community of farms, impact hundreds of acres, and increase the region’s food security and climate resilience.
updated_description: Moon Valley Farm’s project aims to significantly expand its capacity for processing, aggregating, storing, and delivering high-quality legumes and grains to meet growing regional demand across Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Virginia. This expansion will be achieved through the acquisition of essential equipment, and will directly benefit farmers, processors, and consumers within these states. The project anticipates a substantial increase in the volume of organic grains and legumes handled, supporting the Farm’s crop rotation plan and overall whole-farm planning strategies. By increasing production and storage capabilities, Moon Valley Farm intends to supply a greater volume of goods to its existing subscriber base, direct market channels, and wholesale customers. This increased supply will bolster the Farm’s ability to support its 40+ regional partner farms, strengthening the collective agricultural network. The anticipated outcomes include a substantial impact on hundreds of acres of farmland and a strengthening of the region’s food security. Ultimately, this project will benefit farmers by providing a larger market for their products, and consumers by increasing the availability of organic grains and legumes. The project’s success will contribute to a more resilient agricultural system and support the growth of a robust regional food supply chain.

original_description: Soybeans have been historically grown in the central United States, however, climate change is causing droughts in these areas and affecting yield. Maine is warming and has ample water supply, creating an increasingly ideal climate for soybeans. As a nitrogen-fixing crop, soybeans are an ideal rotation crop for other grains, providing nitrogen for the next year's crop and reducing the need for synthetic and manure fertilizers. Although Maine farmers want to produce more soybeans, they lack access to processing infrastructure to enable them to take advantage of the premium, food grade, organic soybean markets. Aurora Mills Farm (Aurora) is one of the leading organic small grains and legume growers in Maine. Aurora is also a value-added producer that processes and mills organic grains and legumes, providing flour, rolled oats, soybeans and field peas to numerous New England based institutions and food producers. Adding bean polishing, destoning and a second cleaner to create a gluten free cleaning line to the existing processing infrastructure will open up new market opportunities for Maine growers. They will be able to grow and access the organic soybean market by using Auroras processing infrastructure. Soybeans, the easiest legume to market, require a stain free, stone free bean. Increased weeds, inherent in organic production, contribute to more staining in the combining harvesting process. Aurora currently has the ability to remove the weeds in the cleaning process, but stained beans are still left. Polishing and destoning will provide Maine’s small grain and legume producers to access new gluten-free markets
updated_description: Aurora Mills Farm (Aurora) is undertaking a project to facilitate the expansion of organic soybean production and processing within Maine, aligning with the state’s agricultural goals. The core of this project involves the acquisition and implementation of new processing equipment, specifically a bean polishing system, destoner, and secondary cleaning apparatus, to be integrated into Aurora’s existing infrastructure. This investment will enable Maine farmers to produce soybeans meeting the stringent requirements of food-grade, organic markets, addressing a critical gap in the state’s agricultural supply chain. The anticipated outcome is the creation of a new market channel for Maine-grown soybeans, allowing processors to supply premium, stain-free, stone-free beans to consumers and food producers throughout New England. Maine farmers will be able to capitalize on the increased demand for organic soybeans, benefiting from access to established distribution networks. This project directly supports the economic viability of Maine’s small grain and legume producers, expanding their market opportunities and bolstering the state’s agricultural sector. The project’s beneficiaries include Maine farmers, processors, and ultimately, consumers seeking high-quality, organic soybean products. By addressing the need for specialized processing capabilities, Aurora Mills Farm will play a key role in connecting producers with market demands and fostering a more robust and reliable supply chain for organic soybeans in Maine.

original_description: The economic viability of this farm is made stronger by the synergy of growing and marketing a legume such as edamame with two distinctive benefits: 1) the creation of a niche market for value-added fresh and frozen edamame, generating an additional diversified income benefit for the farm and 2) Utilizing the nitrogen-fixing ability of soybeans to fix and incorporate between 30 to 50 lbs. of nitrogen per acre into the soil. The project fulfills the need to purchase processing equipment and a transport van which plays a critical role in the storage and delivery of fresh and frozen edamame, ensuring the end product maintains the proper quality, safety, and shelf life throughout its final distribution channels such as long-established Farmers Markets and the numerous retail outlets the farm serves throughout the state of Maine
updated_description: The Organic Market Development Grant project strengthens the economic viability of the farm by establishing a specialized market for edamame, providing a new revenue stream for farmers and ranchers. This initiative centers on the cultivation of soybeans, leveraging their natural ability to fix nitrogen in the soil, aiming to incorporate between 30 and 50 pounds of nitrogen per acre, thereby improving soil health and reducing the need for synthetic fertilizers. To facilitate the production and distribution of this value-added product, the farm will purchase essential processing equipment and a transport van. These items are critical to maintaining the quality, safety, and shelf life of the fresh and frozen edamame throughout its journey from the farm to established Farmers Markets and numerous retail outlets across the state of Maine. The anticipated outcome is the increased availability of a high-demand organic product, benefiting both farmers and consumers. The project directly supports stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural commodities. This initiative seeks to provide fresh and frozen edamame to a wider range of consumers, bolstering the farm’s market reach and overall profitability. By creating a dedicated channel for this organic legume, the project contributes to a more robust and resilient agricultural system within the state.

original_description: This project's goal is to expand on-farm processing capacity to increase consumption of organic cheeses. To address the lack of availability of organic milk for purchase, Balfour Farm is expanding on-farm milk production to increase the farm’s on site processing. Proposed equipment purchases will replace existing equipment with larger capacity cheesemaking equipment to accommodate the planned 175% increase in milk production. The farm will increase the capacity for milk production from 12 cows to 20 cows by the end of 2025. The farm will replace the current oil-fired system, which is approximately 25 years old, with high efficiency propane system. This increases the volume of milk processed and reduces the time required per batch. A cleaner burning, efficient system will modernize process controls and be more a sustainable energy source.The automatic curd mill will solve two problems - workflow and employee fatigue. As more milk is processed, larger batches of cheese will take longer to mill the curds. The EBR curd mill will reduce curd cutting time. This will also reduce worker fatigue. The current hand operated mill places significant stress on the shoulder and arm joints while using. Replacing the mechanical cheese press with higher capacity pneumatic modelwill increase volume and provide for consistent process control, having a positive effect on product appearance, flavor, and texture.The farm’s increased organic milk processing will result in an annual cheese production increase of 7,745 lbs.
updated_description: Balfour Farm’s project aims to expand on-farm processing capacity to increase consumption of organic cheeses, directly addressing the current lack of organic milk availability. The farm will significantly increase its production capabilities through strategic equipment purchases, including a high-efficiency propane system to replace the existing 25-year-old oil-fired system, a robotic curd mill to streamline curds cutting and reduce worker fatigue, and a higher capacity pneumatic cheese press to improve product quality and consistency. These upgrades will facilitate a substantial increase in milk processing volume, projected to yield an annual cheese production increase of 7,745 pounds. The enhanced operation will bolster the ability of farmers and processors to meet market demand for organic dairy products. The project will positively impact consumers by offering greater access to domestically produced organic cheeses and supporting the farm’s efforts to scale its operations. This project directly supports the economic viability of Balfour Farm, enabling it to efficiently process increased milk volumes and expand its market reach. Ultimately, the increased production will benefit a range of stakeholders within the agricultural sector.

original_description: This project will increase access for local organic products to large scale Northeast grocery chains by providing industry standard, cost effective, custom packaging of produce for small organic farms. Organic products in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic regions are significantly underrepresented in large scale grocery markets where the vast majority of organic food products are sold. Small organic farms in the region do not have access to automated packaging machinery that can portion and pack bulk produce into retail size, industry standard UPC labelled units for large scale retail sale. Currently, small organic farms are packaging by hand into expensive small run packages. Reducing packaging costs will allow these farms to increase production volume and sales revenue. This project will allow the purchased, installed and calibration of equipment to provide custom packaging for four farms with the following goals 1)to increase the market share of organic products in large scale grocery stores throughout the Northeast, 2) to decrease 27 unit cost of small organic farm product packaging for retail grocery sales making these products more competitive while increasing sales volume, 3) to increase labor efficiency by reducing or eliminating low skill packaging tasks, and providing higher skill and ultimately higher value tasks for workers on organic farms, and 4) to foster and strengthen connections between small organic farms to develop shared pathways towards expanded markets.
updated_description: This project aims to significantly improve access for local organic producers to large-scale grocery chains within the Northeast region by providing industry-standard, cost-effective, custom packaging solutions for produce from small organic farms. The project will involve the purchase, installation, and calibration of specialized equipment designed to produce retail-sized, UPC-labelled units from bulk produce, addressing a critical gap in the market. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in the market share of organic products within Northeast grocery stores, alongside a reduction of 27 units in the cost of packaging for these farm products, which will facilitate increased sales volume for the participating farms. This initiative will directly benefit farmers and processors by enabling them to more competitively offer their organic goods to a broader consumer base. Furthermore, the project seeks to improve labor efficiency on organic farms by minimizing the need for low-skill packaging tasks, allowing farm workers to concentrate on higher-value operations. The overall goal is to foster and strengthen connections between these small organic farms, developing shared pathways towards expanded markets and creating a more robust supply chain for organic agricultural commodities. The project is expected to positively impact both farmers and consumers seeking access to fresh, organic produce.

original_description: Almar Orchards is a 4th and 5th generation, family-owned organic apple orchard in Michigan, where organic markets are limited. A washing and sorting line would enable Almar to access a new commodity market through baby and kid food company, Once Upon a Farm (OFarm). This partnership would result in increased domestic sourcing by companies like OFarm and serve as an aggregator for other growers in the region. With the ability to clean and sort apples for the commodity market, Almar projects its sales volumes of organic apples could increase by 3 times the current rate over the next 5 years. This increase is driven by other apple growers in the region, who would also benefit from the grant. Nearby growers would be able to aggregate their crop through this wash line, thereby gaining access to new commodity markets. The increased capacity provided by the wash line would also enable Almar to expand organic apple production onto 100 additional acres that are currently fallow or being leased by annual crop growers. This development would result in a future production increase beyond the 5 year projections. Given that Michigan is the third largest apple producer in the country, there is significant opportunity to expand organic production in the state if access to a viable market is present.
updated_description: Almar Orchards is undertaking a project to establish a washing and sorting line, a critical investment designed to significantly expand its access to commodity markets and bolster the organic apple industry within Michigan. This initiative will involve the construction of a specialized processing line, enabling the orchard to meet the stringent requirements of companies like Once Upon a Farm (OFarm) for the production of baby and kid food. The anticipated outcome of this project is a threefold increase – approximately three times the current rate – in Almar Orchards’ sales volumes of organic apples over the next five years, driven not only by Almar’s own expansion but also by the aggregation of crops from neighboring growers. This aggregation will facilitate access to new markets, particularly for processors and stakeholders involved in the broader organic apple industry. Furthermore, the enhanced capacity provided by the wash line will allow Almar to dedicate 100 additional acres to organic apple production, currently fallow or leased for annual crops, representing a substantial increase in overall production potential. Consequently, this project will benefit farmers and ranchers throughout the region, increasing market opportunities for their organic apple harvests. The expanded production capacity is expected to contribute to greater availability of organic apples for consumers and drive overall economic activity within the agricultural sector, supporting the growth of organic food production and strengthening the position of Michigan as a leading apple producer.

original_description: This project aims to strengthen consumer and institutional demand for local, organic dairy products produced in the Northeast (NE) US which face challenges such as contract cancellations and rising production costs. The project seeks to address this crisis by expanding the farm-to-institution market for organic dairy, increasing the number of retail outlets promoting organic dairy, and implementing targeted consumer marketing efforts to boost demand for products made with NE dairy. The first main activity is to increase grocery retail partners by onboarding food co-ops, independent grocers, and large-chain supermarkets committed to promoting and selling organic dairy from the Northeast. The Northeast Organic Family Farm Partnership (NOFFP) will develop compelling program pitch materials, increase staff support to onboard and retain Retail Partners, and establish a retail peer group to share best practices in promoting organic dairy. The second main goal is to facilitate product innovation for bulk organic dairy. For this goal, NOFFP will collaborate with regional farm-to-institution partners to increase the number of participating colleges, K-12s, and hospitals buying NE organic dairy. Strengthening relationships between buyers, distributors, and processors will enable market developments, including the introduction of bulk formats for organic yogurt, cheese, and fluid milk, in response to institutional buyer demands. The final goal is to develop a marketing campaign through the development of new marketing strategies to engage consumers and educate them about the benefits of NE organic dairy. This includes creating brand awareness and loyalty for local organic dairy brands through Point of Sale (POS) marketing, consumer food demos, social media, and targeted messaging. The project is expected to benefit more than 286 organic family farms and 30 value-added organic processors.
updated_description: The Organic Market Development Grant (OMDG) project aims to bolster consumer and institutional demand for local, organic dairy products originating from the Northeast (NE) US, addressing challenges such as contract cancellations and rising production costs. This initiative will accomplish this by expanding the farm-to-institution market for organic dairy, increasing the number of retail outlets committed to promoting and selling organic dairy from the Northeast, and implementing targeted consumer marketing efforts to elevate demand for products crafted with NE dairy. A primary component of the project involves onboarding food co-ops, independent grocers, and large-chain supermarkets, facilitated by the Northeast Organic Family Farm Partnership (NOFFP) which will develop compelling program pitch materials and build a retail peer group to share best practices. Simultaneously, the project seeks to foster product innovation through collaboration with regional farm-to-institution partners to increase the number of participating colleges, K-12s, and hospitals purchasing NE organic dairy. This includes facilitating the development of bulk formats for organic yogurt, cheese, and fluid milk, responding directly to institutional buyer demands. Finally, the project will develop a marketing campaign encompassing Point of Sale (POS) marketing, consumer food demonstrations, social media, and targeted messaging to cultivate brand awareness and consumer loyalty for local organic dairy brands. The anticipated outcomes of this project include benefitting more than 286 organic family farms and 30 value-added organic processors, as well as supplying organic dairy products to institutions and retailers across the region. The project will support farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic dairy. By stimulating market growth, this project intends to create viable pathways for the economic success of these businesses and ensure a sustainable supply of local, organic dairy products for consumers.

original_description: Northern Michigan is home to many organic producers, yet no capability exists for organic producers to develop organic packaged products with the raw organic commodities they produce. The purpose of this project is to expand market access for new organic packaged products by establishing aggregation and comanufacturing services serving multiple organic producers in Northern Michigan initially, with continued growth throughout the Midwest. As a USDA Organic certified organic handler and processing facility, Cultured Ferments is well-positioned to introduce these services and transform a singular product line facility into one with the ability to package almost any viscous product in an organic format. This project will enable product development of organic kombucha made available in cans, along with existing glass bottle formats. The project includes the following activities: installation of a canning line to produce organic kombucha in canned format, partnering with area organic producers to provide co-manufacturing services, expanding delivery networks and maximizing efficiency, and serving area organic producers including small and underserved organic producers with access to new markets.The project is expected to expand networks for organic producers, particularly those in historically underserved areas, to develop and deliver organic packaged products, and provide them access new markets.
updated_description: Cultured Ferments is undertaking a project to expand market access for new organic packaged products originating from Northern Michigan’s organic producers. The core objective of this initiative is to establish aggregation and comanufacturing services, initially serving multiple organic producers across the region with the potential for growth throughout the Midwest. This project involves the installation of a canning line specifically designed to produce organic kombucha in both canned and existing glass bottle formats, alongside partnerships with local organic producers to provide co-manufacturing services. The anticipated outcome is the creation of new channels for organic products to reach consumers and processors, significantly increasing the availability of domestically produced organic commodities. Specifically, the project will support farmers and ranchers in Northern Michigan who produce organic raw materials and processors seeking to expand their offerings. The expanded networks will provide these stakeholders with the means to develop and deliver organic packaged products, ultimately increasing the volume of organic goods available to the market. The project’s success will be measured by the increased capacity to produce and distribute organic products, benefiting both producers and consumers seeking organic options. Cultured Ferments’ existing USDA Organic certification positions them as a critical facilitator in this endeavor, solidifying their role as a key component in the expansion of the organic market within the region.

original_description: The primary goal of the project is to enhance current manufacturing capacity for USDA Organic Tomato Paste in tubes, thereby meeting the increasing demand for organic products. As the sole domestic producers of this unique product, under the Giovanni’s brand label, Giovanni’s is committed to providing consumers with a high-quality, organic, and locally sourced option using only domestically grown ingredients. The equipment upgrade aims to streamline the production process and increase efficiency to meet the rising demand for organic tomato paste in tubes. By investing in the tube filling equipment, Giovanni’s aims to achieve three objectives, which align with the purpose of the program: 1) Promoting sustainable agriculture through exclusive use of domestically grown organic tomatoes emphasizing the company’s commitment to promoting sustainable agricultural practices within the United States. By supporting this project, the program can encourage and endorse responsible farming methods that minimize environmental impact and conserve natural resources. 2) Strengthening domestic manufacturing by enhancing domestic manufacturing capabilities and reducing reliance on imports. As the only US manufacturer of USDA Organic Tomato Paste, this project directly aligns with this goal, of contributing to the growth and resilience of the domestic manufacturing sector. 3) Meeting consumer demand for organic 31 products: With an increasing number of consumers seeking organic and locally sourced food options, this project addresses this demand by providing a unique and certified organic tomato paste in user-friendly tubes. This helps to foster healthier eating choices and supports the program's aim of promoting organic products in the market.
updated_description: Giovanni’s is undertaking a significant project to enhance its manufacturing capacity for USDA Organic Tomato Paste in tubes, directly responding to the growing demand for organic products within the market. This initiative focuses on upgrading equipment to streamline the production process and increase operational efficiency, ensuring Giovanni’s can meet this rising consumer interest. The core objective of this project is to bolster domestic manufacturing capabilities and support the availability of certified organic tomato paste, a product currently supplied exclusively by Giovanni’s under the brand label. By investing in new tube filling equipment, Giovanni’s aims to achieve three key outcomes: firstly, to promote sustainable agricultural practices through the exclusive use of domestically grown organic tomatoes, thereby supporting responsible farming methods; secondly, to strengthen the domestic manufacturing sector by reducing reliance on imported products; and thirdly, to satisfy consumer demand for convenient, certified organic tomato paste packaging. The anticipated beneficiaries of this project include farmers who supply the organic tomatoes, processors involved in the paste production, and ultimately, consumers seeking high-quality, locally sourced organic food options. Giovanni’s anticipates that this expanded capacity will result in increased availability of this particular organic product, facilitating healthier eating choices for a wider range of stakeholders. The success of this project will be measured by the ability to increase production volumes and maintain the highest standards of organic certification, further solidifying Giovanni’s position as a leading producer of this specialized product.

original_description: The goal of this project is to enhance Granor Farm's capacity to handle, package, and distribute identitypreserved organic grains to various end-users. Granor Farm is seeking to meet the substantial demand from 29 its partners such as maltsters, millers, distillers, bakers, brewers, and other end users for certified organic rotational crops, with a focus on barley, wheat, and cereal rye. The project will purchase equipment allowing Granor Farm to weigh and batch identity-preserved grain with utmost care and cleanliness, ensuring precise filling of supersack totes. The built-in belt conveyor will eliminate lot contamination between crops and enable filling of multiple supersacks with high accuracy. The mobile design also allows for indoor filling during winter, enhanced operational safety and flexibility, and reduced weather-related delays. The implementation of the Brandt conveyor will eliminate excessive grain damage and contamination during packaging and post-harvest handling. By replacing traditional steel augers, the belt conveyor ensures the retention of no grain byproducts or extra kernels after operation, eliminating the need for grain purges while maintaining clean and contaminant-free grain lots. The improved capacity and safety measures will enable Granor Farm to meet growing market demands for organic products in Michigan and throughout the upper Midwest.
updated_description: Granor Farm is undertaking a project to significantly enhance its capacity for the handling, packaging, and distribution of identity-preserved organic grains, specifically focusing on barley, wheat, and cereal rye to meet substantial demand from 29 partners including maltsters, millers, distillers, bakers, and brewers. This project involves the purchase of critical equipment designed to ensure the precise weighing and batching of these crops with utmost care and cleanliness, utilizing a built-in belt conveyor to eliminate lot contamination between crops and facilitate the high-accuracy filling of supersack totes. The mobile design of this system allows for indoor filling during winter months, offering enhanced operational safety and flexibility while minimizing delays caused by weather conditions. The implementation of this equipment, particularly the Brandt conveyor, will remove excessive grain damage and contamination during packaging and post-harvest handling, guaranteeing the retention of no grain byproducts or extra kernels. By improving capacity and safety measures, Granor Farm anticipates a substantial increase in its ability to serve the growing market for organic products within Michigan and the upper Midwest. This project will ultimately benefit farmers, processors, and stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic grains, supporting their efforts to meet consumer demand for high-quality, identity-preserved agricultural commodities. The increased operational efficiency and reduced risk of contamination will allow Granor Farm to confidently supply its partners with consistent and reliable organic grain supplies, bolstering the availability of these valuable agricultural products to the marketplace.

original_description: There is no certified organic hay and forage available for purchase within 200 miles of Weinrich Farm, and very little available anywhere in Michigan. Consequently, producing organic beef, lamb, or goat is currently not an option for farms in the area. This project will upgrade and expand the hay and forage making capacity of the Weinrich Farm, LLC, creating the only large-scale organic producer of hay and forage in northern Michigan. Newer and better hay and forage equipment will enable them to rapidly cut, bale and transport, making the business more efficient with existing organic transition pasture. It will also allow them to bring hundreds more acres into organic production over three years. This equipment will kick-start a supply chain for organic, grass-fed ruminants in this region. The project will allow Weinrich Farm to transition their own ruminants to organic feed, eventually enabling them to produce organic grass-fed beef. It will remove a barrier to organic certification for other local small farms who cannot currently access organic hay and forage. This project will create new revenue streams for several existing organic vegetable farms in northern Michigan that have under-utilized pastures which could be used for organic hay, forage, and straw. The project will also support the expansion of organic wheat in the area by enabling the production of forages as a profitable complement in a crop rotation.
updated_description: Weinrich Farm, LLC, is undertaking a project to establish the only large-scale organic hay and forage producer in northern Michigan, addressing a critical market need within a 200-mile radius where no certified organic hay or forage is currently available for purchase. This initiative will involve the purchase and installation of new and improved hay and forage equipment, enabling rapid cutting, baling, and transport processes, designed to maximize efficiency within the farm’s existing organic transition pasture operations and to facilitate the immediate integration of hundreds more acres into organic production over a three-year timeframe. The anticipated outcome of this project is the creation of a robust supply chain for organic, grass-fed ruminants in the region, directly benefiting ranchers and processors who require access to certified organic feed. Furthermore, Weinrich Farm intends to transition its own ruminants to organic feed, paving the way for the eventual production of organic grass-fed beef. This project will also positively impact existing organic vegetable farms in northern Michigan by unlocking the potential of their under-utilized pastures for the production of organic hay, forage, and straw, creating new revenue streams. Finally, the project will support the expansion of organic wheat production in the area, promoting the incorporation of forages as a profitable component of crop rotations, serving a wider range of stakeholders involved in the agricultural sector.

original_description: Great Lakes Garlic Farm is a USDA Certified Organic garlic, grains, and vegetable farm in Grand Traverse County, in Northern Michigan. The operation includes a state-inspected commercial processing facility where it currently dehydrates, grinds, and hand-fills spice jars to create value-added products. The community has a lack of available dehydrated and shelf stable local organic products. By expanding processing capacity of organic ingredients, producing, and storing organic livestock feed, and establishing end-user markets for rotational crops, this project will ease existing bottlenecks and increase supply of several organic ingredients and products. Additional processing equipment will facilitate new product development of value-added products including additional dehydrated vegetable powders, cubed and minced shelf-stable products, and alternative flours. It will also introduce production and storage of organic livestock feed, enabling area farms to produce more organic animal protein to be made available for consumers in the community. This project will enable access to new markets through increased processing and these new product offerings, which can include developing value-added products for other organic farms in the community. Furthermore, establishing an end-user market for organic rotational crops strengthens Great Lakes Garlic Farm’s organizational capacity and ability to process organic ingredients from other organic farms in the community and further diversifies the local food system
updated_description: Great Lakes Garlic Farm’s project aims to significantly increase the supply of organic ingredients and value-added products within Grand Traverse County, Michigan, addressing a critical gap in the local market. The project will involve the purchase and installation of expanded processing equipment to facilitate the production of dehydrated vegetable powders, cubed and minced shelf-stable products, and alternative flours, alongside the creation of a dedicated facility for the storage of organic livestock feed. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in the availability of domestically produced organic grains, legumes, and animal protein, directly benefiting farmers, ranchers, and processors within the region. This expanded capacity will allow Great Lakes Garlic Farm to strengthen its organizational capabilities and serve as a central hub for processing organic ingredients from multiple farms, effectively creating a more robust local food system. The project will also establish end-user markets for organic rotational crops, further supporting the economic viability of local organic production. Ultimately, this initiative will provide greater access to organic ingredients for consumers and contribute to the overall growth of the organic agricultural sector, offering a reliable source of locally produced goods and strengthening the connections between producers and consumers within the community.

original_description: The goal of the project is to purchase equipment to increase the capacity of Maple Drive Farms’ gluten-free, certified organic cleaning facility. The most pressing need is to increase the capacity to clean, dehull, and separate organic buckwheat, e.g., to separate the hull from the edible groat (much like separating the meat of a nut from its shell). The funds will be used to acquire grain cleaning and processing equipment, specifically a second dehuller, a separator, new cleaning screens, a bucket elevator, ten bottom bins, a welded steel aerated grain bin, and upgraded downspouts and grain valves. The increased processing capacity and improved down spouting and valves should allow Maple Drive Farms to increase organic 32 dehulling capacity from around 50,000 pounds per year to at least 100,000 pounds per year, creating a higher product yield without compromising quality. The new storage and conveyance equipment will also substantially increase capacity to clean other organic gluten free grains, such as organic oats, soybeans, corn, and popcorn.
updated_description: Maple Drive Farms is undertaking a project to significantly increase the capacity of its certified organic cleaning facility, addressing a critical need to enhance the processing of organic grains. The project’s core objective is to acquire essential equipment to expand operations, including a second dehuller, a separator, new cleaning screens, a bucket elevator, ten bottom bins, and a welded steel aerated grain bin, alongside upgraded downspouts and grain valves. These additions are designed to elevate the facility’s dehulled buckwheat processing capacity from approximately 50,000 pounds annually to a minimum of 100,000 pounds, substantially improving the yield of this valuable organic product without compromising quality. Furthermore, the expanded infrastructure will substantially increase the facility’s ability to clean other organic gluten-free grains such as organic oats, soybeans, corn, and popcorn, providing greater flexibility in processing a wider range of commodities. The anticipated outcome is a marked increase in the volume of organic grains produced and prepared for market, directly benefiting farmers and processors involved in the organic grain supply chain. This enhanced capacity will facilitate the creation of a stronger domestic market for organic grains, ultimately supporting the production and distribution of these commodities to consumers. The project’s success will positively impact the farmers who cultivate these grains and the processors who transform them into marketable products, strengthening the overall organic grain sector.

original_description: The poject goal is to create a robust organic soybean market tailored to organic growers, crushers, and manufacturers in the Great Lakes Region. This initiative aims to improve market accessibility and encourage higher consumer consumption of domestic food grade organic vegetable oil. To achieve this goal, Quality Roasting (QR) plans to develop an organic soybean oil refining line with the capacity to process over 18 million pounds of organic oil per year. The refining process of soybean oil involves degumming, bleaching, and deodorization to remove impurities and enhance the oil’s quality, taste, and stability. This refining line will be an expansion of the existing soybean crush process, establishing a more extensive organic soybean market for over 1,400 growers in the region. Moreover, this project will expand the market opportunities for crude organic soybean oil by establishing a local market for the five existing soybean crush plants within the Great Lakes Region. Furthermore, the supply of refined organic vegetable oil will increase, benefiting 22 manufacturers who package the oil for consumers. QR initiated its organic program in July 2020, and there has been a remarkable increase in the production of organic soybean meal and oil. From a first- ear output of a few hundred tons, the company has scaled up to produce over 17,000 tons of organic soybean meal and oil in 2022.
updated_description: Quality Roasting is undertaking a significant project to establish a robust organic soybean market within the Great Lakes Region, focused on increasing consumer demand for domestic organic vegetable oil. This initiative involves the development of a new organic soybean oil refining line with a capacity to process over 18 million pounds of organic oil annually, representing an expansion of the company’s existing soybean crush process. The refining line will implement standard processes, including degumming, bleaching, and deodorization, to elevate the quality, taste, and stability of the oil. The project anticipates a positive outcome for over 1,400 soybean farmers in the region, supporting their production of organic soybeans and benefiting five existing soybean crush plants within the Great Lakes Region. Furthermore, the project will positively impact 22 manufacturers who package and distribute refined organic vegetable oil to consumers. Since initiating its organic program in July 2020, Quality Roasting has experienced substantial growth, scaling production from a few hundred tons to over 17,000 tons of organic soybean meal and oil in 2022. This expansion directly supports stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic agricultural commodities. The project’s success will be measured by increased market access for farmers, enhanced processing capabilities for crushers, and expanded market opportunities for oil packaging manufacturers.

original_description: The project will add additional processing capacity for creating milled organic field pea fiber. Field peas are legumes used in organic rotational cropping systems. The organic market for field peas is being developed and expanded through uses of their components including milled flours, low and high protein content proteins, starches, and fibers. Organic pea fibers are primarily used in value-added markets in a milled, flour format. When peas are processed, the outer fibrous layer is removed and separated from the inside of the pea. This outer fibrous layer is called the pea hull and is very light, taking up a lot of space for storage and is only marketable to livestock at little to no value. The proposed project will add a fiber milling line to an 33 existing organically certified pea handling facility that produces pea hulls but does not have the ability to mill the hulls into a marketable product. The proposed pea milling project will be added to an existing building footprint and be ready to process 2023 crop organic peas into organic pea fiber.
updated_description: The proposed project aims to establish additional processing capacity for creating milled organic field pea fiber, addressing a specific market need within the organic agricultural sector. original_description: Cold Springs Organics, LLC is requesting funds to install a pelleting line at their facility near Bozeman, MT. Certified organic livestock feed has been identified as a critical barrier to growing the organic livestock market. Organic livestock farmers looking to transition to organic have been faced with record high feed prices over the past three years while organic crop producers have experienced whiplash prices for their certified organic crops. Cold Springs Organics is looking to bridge this disconnect through the expansion of its grain handling operation by purchasing, installing and operating an alfalfa and complete feed pelleting facility. This project will work to both increase the overall supply of organic feed available across Montana and the Northwest Region. It will also allow Cold Springs Organics to expand market access for both crop growers and livestock raisers. By pelletizing perennial legumes like alfalfa, and offering consistent prices to farmers year over year, they will expand the overall organic feed processing capacity in the region, offering more options to livestock producers and crop growers. Cold Springs Organics will increase market access by shipping the pelletized feed via rail. They will expand the opportunities for crop growers to sell a wide variety of leguminous and cereal feed crops that maximize the soil health of the farm all while producing livestock feed at a price point that is commercially viable for broiler, layer, hog, and dairy producers.
updated_description: Cold Springs Organics, LLC is requesting funding to establish a critical component of Montana’s organic livestock feed supply chain: a pelleting facility near Bozeman, MT. original_description: Amaltheia Organic Dairy, LLC is seeking funding to provide wholesome, organic pasteurized goat milk to the public in this health-conscious community. original_description: The goal of this project is to mitigate the risk of sprout damage to vulnerable organic grain crops grown for a food-grade and seed market by providing infrastructure for an on-farm grain drying system, thus enabling Horton Farm to choose a harvest window and help avoid crop loss due to pre-harvest sprouting which damages the quality of grain for food-grade application and for viable seed germination. Specifically, Horton Farm has been growing Appalachian White Wheat, a regionally adapted hard white winter wheat variety for Carolina Ground flour mill since 2018. This variety came out of the USDA-Agricultural Research Service Uniform Bread Wheat trials and has respectable yields, a good disease package, and a strong market, but as a white wheat, it lacks the dormancy period at maturity that red wheats contain, so the crop is at a higher risk of pre-harvest sprouting. To build a resilient food-grade grain-based value chain in the South, Horton Farm needs this critical infrastructure to minimize the risk of relying solely on good weather during the harvest window of June - July. Since 2012, Horton Farm in relationship with Carolina Ground, has been producing high quality stone-ground flour made from certified organic grains grown predominantly in North Carolina and surrounding southern states, and serving bakeries throughout the southeast.
updated_description: Horton Farm’s project aims to mitigate the risk of sprout damage to Appalachian White Wheat, a regionally adapted hard white winter wheat variety grown for a food-grade and seed market, by constructing an on-farm grain drying system. This system will enable Horton Farm to establish a harvest window and minimize crop loss due to pre-harvest sprouting, which negatively impacts the quality of the grain for Carolina Ground’s flour milling operations and the viability of seed germination. The project involves the purchase and installation of necessary equipment to facilitate on-site grain drying, supporting Horton Farm’s continued production of high-quality stone-ground flour from certified organic grains. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened food-grade grain-based value chain, allowing Horton Farm to reliably supply Carolina Ground with premium wheat for flour production and ensuring a consistent supply of viable seed. Farmers and processors involved in the supply chain will benefit from reduced losses and improved grain quality. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers who cultivate Appalachian White Wheat and the processors, specifically Carolina Ground, who utilize the grain to produce flour for distribution throughout the Southeast. Ultimately, this project supports a robust and reliable supply of certified organic grains, benefiting the farmers, processors, and consumers who rely on these products.

original_description: The purpose of Anchor’s processing improvement project is to increase the market for US producers by expanding organic storage and processing capabilities across Anchor Ingredients Co., LLC’s ( Anchor) supply chain through improvement of current processes and installation of new equipment. This will be done through three activities. The first is to improve the product drags at internally owned facilities. This will allow for increased efficiency in moving organic products through value-add processing, storage, and inbound/outbound transit. Anchor’s current product drags cannot be operated in certain weather conditions which causes significant downtime. Additionally, these old/malfunctioning drags leak/spill product, causing additional work to re-clean spilled product as well as unnecessary loss of product. This goal will be completed over a two-week span at Hillsboro and Buffalo, ND locations in which the old drags will be disassembled, and the new clean product drags will be re-installed. The second activity is to install and update processing equipment, over six months. The new processing equipment will expand the channel for value-added organic products and increase organic storage capacity. Prior to Anchor acquiring the facility, it was not certified organic and didn’t have processing capabilities. The third activity is to create a new organic value-added product, by installing pelletizing processing equipment. Pelletizing hulls compresses the hulls into small, dense pellets. These pellets take up less space compared to loose hulls, allowing for more efficient storage and transportation. Pelletizing will increase Anchor’s storage capacity, and decrease the number of truck shipments to customers, as trailers are able to hold more pelletized product than non-pelletized product. It also allows customers to store these pelletized hulls more efficiently, thus creating additional capacity.
updated_description: Anchor’s processing improvement project is designed to significantly expand the market for US producers by enhancing organic storage and processing capabilities throughout its supply chain. This initiative will be implemented through three key activities: first, the complete overhaul of existing product drags at Anchor’s Hillsboro and Buffalo, ND facilities, a two-week endeavor that involves dismantling the outdated equipment and installing new, clean product drags. These improvements are essential to address the current operational limitations of the old drags, which cannot function in certain weather conditions and frequently leak or spill product, necessitating substantial re-cleaning efforts and product loss. Second, over a six-month period, Anchor will install and update processing equipment to broaden the channel for value-added organic products and increase organic storage capacity, a critical step considering the facility’s previous lack of organic certification and processing capabilities. Finally, Anchor will establish a new organic value-added product by installing pelletizing processing equipment. This equipment will compress hulls into dense pellets, reducing storage volume and transportation needs for both Anchor and its customers. The anticipated outcome is an increase in the availability of organic ingredients for farmers, ranchers, and processors, alongside improved storage efficiencies for consumers. This project directly benefits stakeholders involved in the organic agricultural supply chain, ultimately supporting the movement of domestically produced organic commodities and bolstering market access for US producers.

original_description: Healthy Oilseeds is a small family-owned business that processes flaxseed, hempseed, borage, and other minor oilseeds. They cold press expel, mill, sift, and clean oilseeds. There is great demand for Healthy Oilseeds organic flaxseed and hempseed oil products grown and processed in the United States and they can supply these products that are certified USDA Organic and Primus Food Safety Certified. The project will help supply the consumer demand and create a clear market channel for organic production of oilseeds to be processed close to where the seeds are grown.

original_description: North Country Smokehouse (NCS) is a vertically integrated organic meat producer committed to sustainable agriculture. A century of breeding has delivered hybrid trees well-suited for commercial organic production, which can yield 1,500-3,500 lbs./acre of a nutrient-dense, gluten-free perennial starch crop. Given growing consumer interest in grain alternatives, gluten-free 43 ingredients, and local/sustainable foods, Savanna Institute identifies a present-day market opportunity for a +50,000% increase over current production. A growing number of Northeast farmers (particularly historically underserved farmers) see organic chestnut agroforestry systems as a key strategy for diversifying agricultural landscapes and enterprises. The project will conduct a feasibility/technical development study for a best-in-class, global organic chestnut processing facility and complete key improvements to a Breadtree-owned, on-farm facility to deliver processing capacity for organic chestnuts. The project will allow the purchase and installation of specialized processing, handling, storage, and distribution equipment. Also, conducting outreach at buyer-engagement events, regional local food events festivals markets, product demonstration days targeted at handlers, organic consumar package goods, food advocacy marketing professionals-Increase regional producer coordination best practices through technical workshops, farm consultation visits, webinars, focused on best practices for product consistency, marketing, post-harvest processing coordination. Through this project, Breadtree and a national coalition of partners will address: the lack of existing in-region commercial processing capacity; demand for product development and strengthened supply-chain connections between buyers, consumers, handlers and producers; the need for improved supply-chain coordination between producers by building enhanced processing capacity, developing new paths-to-market, and engaging producers, while building relationships with consumers, handlers, and culinary professionals to increase market access and consumption. These interventions would transform the Northeast’s organic chestnut industry and contribute to important strategic growth of organic chestnut industries in other U.S. regions.

original_description: The goal is to purchase wool equiment to create a market for wool in the horticultural industry to replace products currently used with more sustainable, certifiable organic products that will benefit both sheep and crop farmers. The only regional aggregator of wool from shearing has stopped buying wool. Sheep farming in Ohio is increasing, and with it, wool production. Coarse and low-grade wool can substitute soil amendments and weed suppression materials used in horticulture. Wool stores up to 33% of its weight in water and slowly releases water once the surrounding environment drops below 65% relative humidity, is fully degradable, contains Nitrogen, Calcium, Magnesium, Iron, Sulfur, and other Micro Nutrients. Felted wool mats can replace plastic weed barriers. They can regulate soil temperatures, prevent moisture loss, add fertilizer, act as a pest barrier to slugs and snails, and provide excellent weed prevention. Shredded wool can be mixed with seed to be a delivery method for habitat restoration, landscaping, and crop establishment. Soil and potting mixes are currently amended with peat, vermiculite, and perlite to increase the water-holding capacity and provide aeration. Adverse ecological impacts resulting from to these soil amendments include the depletion of peat bogs and the high carbon footprint of vermiculite and perlite from transportation and overseas mining operations. Wool pellets can provide aeration, hold moisture, and are naturally high in nitrogen making them the perfect slow-release, all-natural fertilizer.
updated_description: the goal of this project is to establish a market for wool within the horticultural industry, replacing conventional soil amendments and weed control products with a sustainable, certifiable organic alternative. Driven by the cessation of regional wool aggregation and the rising sheep farming industry in Ohio, coarse wool offers a viable substitute for peat, vermiculite, and perlite, mitigating their adverse ecological impacts. Wool’s unique properties – water retention (up to 33%), slow-release humidity regulation, and nutrient content (Nitrogen, Calcium, Magnesium, etc.) – make it ideal for felted mats as weed barriers, shredded wool for habitat restoration, and wool pellets as a slow-release, natural fertilizer.  This aligns with the Organic Market Development Grant (OMDG) program’s mission to expand domestic organic agricultural markets and support certified organic production.

original_description: In 2022, U.S. farmers produced more than 2.35 billion tons of grain feed to serve domestic and international livestock producers (USDA Economic Research Service). Still, less than 1% of the grain feed produced in the United States is organic, despite strong and consistent growth in U.S. demand for organic food. With more than 82% of U.S. households buying organic products regularly (Organic Trade Association), the Organic Center notes that driven by growth in demand for U.S. organic livestock feed the U.S. has become a substantial net importer of organic products. In fact, U.S. imports of grain feed have steadily increased over the past decade, growing from 40% in the 2011/2012 crop year to 60% in the 2021/2022 crop year. This is primarily due to the major barriers that exist to producing, processing, and marketing organic grain feed, namely higher costs of production and lack of processing and marketing infrastructure. To meet current U.S. consumer demand and expand opportunities to build the U.S. organic grain feed market, Grange Cooperative will perform the following activities: 1) expand its processing capacity to create more and better markets for organic producers and 2) execute marketing and promotional activities that will help to build commercial markets for U.S. organic grain feed products. This project’s goals (deliverables and expected outcomes) include achieving 2,000 additional tons of organic grain feed processed and a $1,655,000 increase in domestic organic grain feed sales by the end of the project period.

original_description: The PA Flax Project (PAFP) is a woman-owned cooperative business whose mission is to reestablish the fiber flax industry in Pennsylvania by initiating new organic production and processing capacity. This initiative focuses on supporting small, beginning, and disadvantaged farmers, particularly those within a region characterized by low per capita income and a significant population base, to stimulate economic growth and enhance agricultural production. The project will facilitate direct market channels for specialty crops such as beans, peppers, and herbs, connecting farmers directly with purchasers and increasing the availability of domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. Anticipated outcomes include increased market access for these farmers and enhanced sales of locally grown organic products. By fostering collaboration and providing access to resources, this project seeks to create a lasting positive impact on the agricultural landscape of Southeastern North Carolina.

original_description: Plants to Food is a manufacturing service partner for plant-based food brands. They bring over 25 years of manufacturing expertise and excellence in the areas of product formulation, testing, labeling, packaging, distribution, and more. Plants to Food has been cooking, blending, infusing, and packaging premium food products for over 25 years. In addition to product and packaging capabilities, they also offer R&D, labels, and nutritional software that creates nutrition fax panels per FDA guidelines. Plants to Food’s temperaturecontrolled production facility is state-of-the-art with an innovative warehouse management process. This includes a dedicated pick and pack fulfillment line for direct-to-consumer and a separate pallet racking system for storage and carrier pallet loads. As the company continues to expand, they are constantly looking for new ways to accommodate growing demands. This project will include the purchase of a Rotary Fill and Seal Machine for Premade Doypack as well as a Piston Filler for Liquids and Pastes. This machine will increase processing by roughly 12,000 units per month. It will allow Plants to Food to take on seven new customers and supply four new jobs at its factory. Overall, Plants to Food will see a 10% increase in processing with this new machinery. With this purchase, its factory will see an increase in processing capacity by 4,500 pounds a month. As Plants to Food continues to grow, it receives an influx of orders beyond what the facility can currently produce. As a co-manufacturing business, this new equipment will not only help expand Plants to Food processing but also the processing of the various organic food companies they are partnered with.
updated_description: Plants to Food is undertaking a project to significantly expand its manufacturing capabilities, primarily to support the increasing demands of its plant-based food brand partners. original_description: Berrybrook Organics, LLC (Berrybrook) is a certified organic farm and value-added processing company. Throughout their 24 years producing and marketing organic value-added grains, meats, and eggs, their reputation for product quality and consistency has earned them a loyal customer base, extensive marketing experience, and valuable relationships with wholesale clients. The equipment requested addresses two needs: supply chain management/improvement through the purchase of a delivery vehicle, and processing efficiency through the purchase of an Egg Grader machine for organic egg processing. Berrybrook currently supplies Grade A organic eggs to two local grocery stores and nine Sioux Falls wholesale and retail customers. Last year, about 95% of total eggs produced were sold to these outlets. In addressing these two areas of need, Berrybrook will reach new organic markets, increase processing efficiency for their organic goods, and ensure a quality, safe organic product to consumers.
updated_description: Berrybrook Organics, LLC is undertaking a project focused on enhancing its operations to expand market reach and improve processing capabilities, directly supported by the acquisition of key assets. This investment will allow Berrybrook to significantly increase its capacity for fulfilling existing contracts with two local grocery stores and nine wholesale and retail customers, currently accounting for 95% of their total egg sales. awardee_name: Tiffany Leigh Stanley (A Different Chick Farm & Orchard)
original_description: A Different Chick Farm and Orchard (ADCFO) has been growing produce since 2016 and has been certified organic since 2020. awardee_name: RKH GIN LLC, dba Woolam Gin
original_description: RKH Gin LLC, dba Woolam Gin is a primarily woman owned ginning facility that has processed organic cotton for 33 years, being the first United States to do so. It is located in a high poverty area in Lynn County, Texas and serves other high poverty areas including Dawson and Terry Counties. Woolam Gin is seeking a grant award to purchase and install equipment to expand the services and improve processing to increase production of organic cotton for farmers which will improve overall market production of the beneficial product. The overarching project purpose is to improve efficiency, therefore improving outcomes for farmers and the organic market. The equipment will increase production from 25 bales an hour to up to 40 bales an hour. The increase in processing will improve the housing time of cotton in the warehouse which will improve the grades and facilitate earlier entry into the marketplace, benefiting farm producers, processors, and consumers. The faster processing will improve turnaround for the farmer and further increase production possibilities. The primary partners and collaborators of the project will include participating organic farmers, the project manager, project supervisor, gin manager and other supporting human resources workers. This grant award will create improved markets and expand processing capacity which in turn will enrich market availability and further development of production resources and production.
updated_description: Woolam Gin is seeking a grant award to purchase and install equipment that will expand its processing capabilities, increasing production of organic cotton from 25 bales per hour to a potential 40 bales per hour. The acquisition of this new equipment will significantly reduce the housing time of cotton within the warehouse, resulting in improved grades and facilitating earlier entry into the marketplace for processors and consumers. By increasing the speed and volume of cotton processing, Woolam Gin aims to streamline operations and improve access to market opportunities for those involved in the organic cotton industry.

original_description: Steelbow Farm is seeking to broaden its delivery range and increase local food access and supply chain resilience by procuring a delivery vehicle. The overarching purpose of the proposed project is to expand access to local, organic produce by eliminating the current constraint of distance and delivery radius, while simultaneously addressing the growing demand for product in the current marketplace. Currently, Steelbow Farm has demand for their product that exceeds their capacity because they do not have a vehicle and therefore have a limited delivery range. This bottleneck is hampering Steelbow Farm’s ability to rise to the organic market demands. They believe access to this equipment would drastically improve access to organic produce, as they could radically increase their customer base and range. For context, currently, within Travis County, only .06% of food is produced locally. The Austin and Travis County areas are seeing a decline in the amount of vegetable farms and farmland, which are disappearing at an alarming 16.8 acres a day. Amidst these startling statistics, this business is thriving and demand for their produce is extremely high. Steelbow Farm wants to be able to meet the market demand and fill the gap within the local food system. As organic vegetable producers, they are striving to increase the percentage of local food consumed within their community.
updated_description: Steelbow Farm is undertaking a project to broaden its delivery range and increase local food access by procuring a delivery vehicle, with the overarching purpose of expanding access to local, organic produce and addressing the growing market demand for their products. The project will result in a vehicle being acquired, allowing Steelbow Farm to serve a significantly wider geographic area and, critically, to meet the heightened needs of consumers seeking locally sourced organic food. The anticipated outcome is a substantial increase in the volume of organic produce available within the community, directly addressing the alarming decline in local farmland within Travis County, where only a small percentage of food is currently produced locally and farmland is disappearing at a concerning rate. This project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the local food system, enabling them to connect with a larger customer base and contribute to a more resilient local food supply chain. By facilitating increased access to organic vegetables, Steelbow Farm aims to elevate the percentage of local food consumed within the community and contribute to a more robust and sustainable local agricultural economy.

awardee_name: Armagh Fine Foods LLC dba Armagh Creamery
original_description: The primary goal of this project is to enhance and expand the production capabilities of Armagh Creamery organic farming and dairy operations. By acquiring essential equipment, the project aims to achieve increased efficiency, product diversification, and expanded distribution. This equipment will enable Armagh Creamery to venture into new product lines, including heavy cream and butter, expand production of existing products, and streamline the production process, reducing the workload on current employees and enhancing overall efficiency for creating new butter product lines. The acquisition of a delivery vehicle will significantly improve distribution capabilities, allowing Armagh Creamery to reach local retailers and drop locations in Central, North, and West Texas.
