updated_description: Armagh Creamery is undertaking a significant project to enhance its production capabilities and expand its operations, focusing on increased efficiency and broadened product offerings within the organic dairy sector. original_description: Triple J Organics is a minority-owned certified organic citrus orchard in Mission, Texas established in 1995. Triple J manages 25 acres of certified organic citrus groves, primarily of Ruby Red grapefruit and early season oranges, as well as Navel Oranges, Meyer Lemons, Tangerines, and Tangelos in smaller quantities. This project will increase consumption of locally produced organic orange juice in the Rio Grande Valley and increase the profitability and long-term viability of Triple J Organics through special purpose equipment purchases that allow Triple J to process 32,000 lbs. of “waste”, or seconds, oranges into fresh juice and deliver it safely to customers in the Valley. The project will target school districts as potential customers, as well as supermarkets, restaurants, health food stores, daycare facilities, and eldercare facilities as needed. Beneficiaries include Triple J Organics, local schools and businesses who purchase the new product, as well as other organic citrus growers in the Valley who may be able to cooperate and aggregate to produce a higher margin value-added product.
updated_description: Triple J Organics, a certified organic citrus orchard established in Mission, Texas in 1995, is undertaking a project to significantly increase the consumption of locally produced organic orange juice within the Rio Grande Valley and bolster the company’s long-term viability. original_description: The Texas Department of Agriculture (TDA) will use a multi-faceted approach to promote local organic producers in the produce, grains, dairy, and fiber markets. Though these industries are each unique in their production, the issues they experience are similar. These challenges include, but are not limited to, lack of knowledge among consumers of each industry’s availability/benefits, existing gaps between producers and buyers that result in barriers for growth, and an absence of public resources that assist organic farmers from promoting themselves more efficiently. Through this project, TDA will increase local consumer knowledge, support activities to develop new markets, increase demand for domestically produced organic agricultural products, and provide additional market paths for organic farmers in Texas. Goals of this project include: 1) increase public knowledge of Texas organic agriculture industry, 2) provide opportunities to improve market share and sales of local organic producers, and 3) build new connections between Texas producers and potential buyers to accomplish these goals. TDA Marketing will produce new marketing materials targeted for the organic industry, assist organic producers with attending trade shows relevant to their respective industries, facilitate business to business interactions, and run a social media campaign that highlights each industry. These activities will strengthen the relationships between Texas organic 54 crop/product producers and buyers, as well as better inform the public on the availability and benefits of Texas organic products. These relationships would aid in ongoing efforts to strengthen the supply chain, build on current opportunities with Texas agriculture associations, assist historically underserved communities, and increase demand for locally produced organic products. To further assist the organic industries of Texas, TDA will assist in the production of the Field View Organics program. This program aims to identify organic operations across the state and mark them for aerial spraying companies to help prevent potential chemical drift or contamination of organic crops. By supporting this initiative, TDA will protect the current organic producers across the state and alleviate potential concerns for new members wanting to enter the industry.
updated_description: The Texas Department of Agriculture will implement a comprehensive project to bolster local organic producers across the produce, grains, dairy, and fiber markets, addressing shared challenges within these industries. This initiative will involve the creation of new marketing materials, support for producers attending relevant trade shows, facilitation of business-to-business interactions, and a targeted social media campaign designed to increase public awareness of the benefits and availability of Texas organic agricultural products. Anticipated outcomes include increased market share and sales for local organic producers, strengthened connections between Texas organic farmers and potential buyers, and a heightened demand for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. The primary beneficiaries of this project are Texas farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the organic agricultural sector. Specifically, the project aims to support those involved in the production of organic grains, dairy, fibers, and legumes, which are currently facing gaps in market access. A key component of the project is the Field View Organics program, which will identify organic operations and provide information to aerial spraying companies to mitigate the risk of chemical drift and contamination. This will support current organic producers and encourage new entrants to the industry. Ultimately, the Texas Department of Agriculture seeks to foster stronger supply chains and expanded opportunities within Texas agriculture, while simultaneously responding to the needs of producers and consumers interested in locally sourced organic products.

original_description: This project aims to increase the American consumer awareness of organic yaupon tea as a replacement for imported tea via the food service sector. An Organic Yaupon Marketing Plan will increase opportunities for consumer exposure to organic yaupon tea while also allowing for additional customers, buyers, and parties to participate in the domestic organic yaupon tea industry. Yaupon is a caffeinated plant native to North America and rich in polyphenols and antioxidants like imported tea. By using a hybrid of traditional tea preparation methods, organic yaupon tea has an almost indistinguishable flavor profile from imported green and black tea served in both hot and iced tea. Cat Spring Yaupon has created a cohesive marketing and outreach plan to increase the amount of organic yaupon tea served in restaurants, cafes, hotels, and spas. This plan incorporates the opportunity to promote and support additional organic yaupon producers through the American Yaupon Association while also supplying to tea companies who would otherwise be selling imported tea to their food service customers. This will also allow restaurants to substitute imported tea on their menus with organic yaupon tea thus giving their customers and guests an opportunity to sample and fall in love with the incredible domestic organic yaupon tea.
updated_description: Cat Spring Yaupon is undertaking a strategic project to elevate consumer awareness of organic yaupon tea as a viable alternative to imported tea options within the food service sector. The core objective of this initiative is to increase the availability of organic yaupon tea through partnerships with restaurants, cafes, hotels, and spas, ultimately stimulating demand for this domestically produced beverage. This project will facilitate the adoption of organic yaupon tea as a substitute for imported teas, offering consumers a familiar flavor profile comparable to green and black tea, delivered in both hot and iced formats. By engaging with food service establishments, Cat Spring Yaupon aims to establish a robust domestic market for organic yaupon tea, supporting the growth of producers and distributors within the industry. The anticipated outcome is a significant increase in the consumption of organic yaupon tea, benefiting both consumers seeking a quality tea experience and producers seeking expanded market access. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers cultivating organic yaupon, processors handling the tea, and stakeholders throughout the supply chain. The success of this project hinges on the collaboration between Cat Spring Yaupon and its partners, creating a sustainable pathway for organic yaupon tea to flourish as a recognized and valued beverage choice.

original_description: Spicy Organic LLC, a dedicated provider of premium organic spices, herbs, and grains, proposes to purchase and install machinery equipment to streamline its production processes, enhance efficiency, and expand market reach. The proposed equipment will significantly boost processing capabilities, reduce manual labor, and improve the availability of organic ingredients in both domestic and emerging markets. By introducing a semi-automatic auger filler machine, production output is projected to increase substantially from 60 pouches to 900 pouches per hour. This advancement will not only result in enhanced efficiency and productivity but also bolster the domestic market demand for the company’s organic ingredients. The Band Sealer will mark a significant leap towards improving overall efficiency and output. As pouches are sealed seamlessly and rapidly, Spicy Organic anticipates an increase in processing efficiency, enabling them to explore untapped markets and create new avenues for expanding the demand for their organic ingredients. The inclusion of a forklift machine will revolutionize this aspect of the company’s operations. With the ability to efficiently move and store organic ingredients, Spicy Organic expects a notable surge in production output. The inkjet coding machine and conveyor system are poised to streamline this process, augmenting efficiency, and output. This will ensure precise and timely labeling, bolstering the availability and marketability of their products within the domestic market. The proposed enhancements will not only elevate processing efficiency but also facilitate entry into untapped markets, increasing the demand for Spicy Organic’s premium organic ingredients.
updated_description: Spicy Organic LLC proposes a significant investment in equipment to substantially enhance its production capabilities and broaden its market reach, directly supporting the increased availability of premium organic spices, herbs, and grains. By optimizing each stage of the production process – from filling and sealing to labeling and storage – the company aims to bolster the market for its organic products and address a critical need for enhanced capacity within the organic ingredients sector. This expansion will enable Spicy Organic to better serve the needs of its customers and increase the overall supply of certified organic commodities to the marketplace.

original_description: The Organic Marketing Institute (OMI) expands the marketplace for organic agricultural products by supporting innovative certification programs that extend the third-party organic certification baseline into novel product categories. OMI promotes third-party certifications that enhance National Organic Program (NOP) standards and offer transparency and full supply chain traceability while benefiting the environment. The Organic Plus Trust (OPT) Certified Grass-Fed Organic Livestock Program has set the first national standard for grass-fed, organic ruminant livestock production for meat and dairy that builds upon USDAcertified organic dairy standards and helps differentiate farmers’ products. An end-to-end, third-party certification, it verifies all production and handling of certified products from farm through processing to sale. Grass-fed Organic Certification has seen initial producer interest and customer satisfaction due to the market stability, transparency, trust, and climate benefits of the products certified. There is demonstrated need and opportunity to scale the certification as a value add for organic producers, retailers, and customers. With funding from USDA, OMI will support farmers and brands, having the OPT Grass-Fed Organic Certification, with expanded marketing and promotional support. OMI will do this by enhancing supplier relationships, creating a marketing strategy that promotes the climate benefits, third-party integrity, full-supply chain traceability and regenerative characteristics of the products, and executing robust consumer marketing efforts. With these efforts, to grow the market for Grass-Fed, organic dairy products, supporting an additional 50 farmers per year and engaging an additional 10 brands over the course of the grant.
updated_description: The Organic Marketing Institute (OMI) is undertaking a project to expand the marketplace for organic agricultural products by supporting innovative certification programs, specifically the Organic Plus Trust (OPT) Grass-Fed Organic Certification for ruminant livestock. This project aims to establish a national standard for grass-fed, organic dairy and meat production, verifying all aspects of production and handling from farm through processing and sale. The initiative seeks to provide farmers and brands with expanded marketing and promotional support, focusing on the integrity of the third-party certification, full supply chain traceability, and the regenerative characteristics of the products. Anticipated outcomes include supporting an additional 50 farmers per year and engaging an additional 10 brands, driving market growth for grass-fed, organic dairy products. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, processors, and stakeholders within the organic food sector. By securing OPT Grass-Fed Organic Certification, producers can differentiate their products, fostering consumer confidence and driving demand. This will ultimately benefit consumers seeking high-quality, traceable organic products with recognized standards. The project’s success will be measured by the increased number of certified producers and brands actively participating in the marketplace, generating greater market stability and trust amongst stakeholders.

original_description: Grain farming is returning to the region, and the tide is rising. There are a growing number of bakeries and distilleries in Vermont and the region needs organic grain that is grown and processed locally. Many farmers cannot grow grain because they lack the capacity to clean, dry, and/or store grain. The grain drying machine and grain cleaning machine will be a great help and be used to process the grain of many farms. The purchase and installation of more efficient grain drying and cleaning equipment to replace less efficient equipment and hand labor will allow Thornhill Farm to 1) accept and purchase more organic grain from farmers on the day of harvest, and after, to dry and clean the grain, 2) to support the re-emergence of local and regional grain production in Vermont, New York, and Maine, 3) to inc usrease local organic grain market availability by making a greater amount of grain and flour available on the market for baking and spirits, and 4) to ultimately, support Northeastern grain farmers, organic agronomy and soil health, and increase regional grain markets, all of which help mitigate climate impacts through reducing climate miles, increasing organic agronomy practices, reducing exposure to flooding and drought through water-soil interactions, and sequestering carbon.
updated_description:
Here is a rewritten project description, aiming for approximately 370 words:

The Thornhill Farm project, supported by the Organic Market Development Grant (OMDG) program, addresses the resurgence of grain farming in the Northeast and aims to bolster regional organic agriculture. Recognizing a critical gap in capacity, many local farmers struggle with the essential processes of grain cleaning, drying, and storage. This project will equip Thornhill Farm with advanced grain cleaning and drying machinery, significantly increasing their ability to accept, process, and store organic grain harvested directly from local farmers across Vermont, New York, and Maine.

This initiative directly supports the OMDG program’s goals: expanding organic production capacity, developing robust market channels for domestically sourced organic commodities, and fostering sustainable agricultural practices. By enabling efficient grain processing, Thornhill Farm will dramatically increase the availability of organic grain and flour, a vital ingredient for local bakeries and distilleries.  This increased supply directly addresses a key market need identified by the OMDG program.

Beyond immediate market support, the project’s broader impact extends to regional soil health and climate resilience.  Reducing “climate miles” through localized grain production minimizes environmental impact.  Enhanced grain processing, coupled with water-soil interactions, will mitigate the effects of flooding and drought, while simultaneously sequestering carbon – a crucial component of combating climate change.  Furthermore, the project prioritizes organic agronomy, reinforcing sustainable farming methods.  

Ultimately, this investment in Thornhill Farm represents a strategic move to strengthen the entire Northeastern grain market, directly contributing to OMDG's mission of expanding organic production and building resilient agricultural systems. The implementation of this project represents an opportunity to meet increased demand for organic grain, support regional farmers, and champion environmental sustainability.

awardee_name: Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont
original_description: The Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont (NOFA-VT), in partnership with Vermont Way Foods (VWF) and Food Connects (FC), proposes to grow, and develop markets for Vermont’s organic producers in three ways 1) expanding access to promising identified markets throughout the Northeast by developing sales channels to large retailers and other wholesale buyers with consumer bases that are validated by 56 market research to value and support the qualities inherent in Vermont organic food, 2) by developing new dairy, maple, and other Vermont organic wholesale products to be branded and marketed under the VWF brand and distributed regionally by FC, and 3) increasing consumer awareness and demand for organic food through targeted marketing and promotions in Vermont and throughout the Northeast. Key outcomes include new and expanded wholesale markets for Vermont organic producers, including an overall increase in the percentage of organic products sold through the Food Connects food hub, and increased sales of VWF organic products. Additionally, the project will result in increased awareness of and preference for locally produced organic food among regional consumers. Key beneficiaries of the project include organic dairy producers, organic dairy processors, additional food hubs (certified organic handlers), and organic maple producers. As VWF scales its production and increases sales capacity, they expect these initial producers to see increased sales to VWF, and ultimately, for VWF to onboard additional producers and processors. The project will leverage support from Migrant Justice to support the coordination of Milk with Dignity certification of VWF dairy products which aim to engender consumer trust in the values-aligned brand.
updated_description: Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont (NOFA-VT), in collaboration with Vermont Way Foods (VWF) and Food Connects (FC), proposes a project designed to expand market access for Vermont’s organic producers through three key strategies. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass organic dairy producers, organic dairy processors, organic maple producers, and other stakeholders within the organic food supply chain. original_description: This project will increase the domestic and international market share for organic wines produced in Washington State and it will double the capacity of Wilridge Winery’s production facility, thereby increasing the local market for USDA certified-organic wine grapes in Washington generally, and in the Yakima area specifically. By increasing demand and, therefore, the premium paid, for USDA certified-organic wine grapes, the project will encourage other wine-grape producers in Washington to initiate the USDA organic certification process. Starting with a market study and the development of a marketing plan in year one, Wilridge Winery will identify the factors constraining the expansion of organic Washington wines into the growing organic wine market. At the same time, the project will double the capacity of Wilridge Winery’s USDA certified-organic processing facility in preparation for the implementation of the marketing plan. In year two Wilridge Winery will implement its marketing plan to persuade wine distributors (wholesalers), retailers, and consumers to purchase more organic Washington wine. The marketing plan will include intentional outreach to the highly diverse local viticulture community in the Yakima area which includes beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, limited-resource farmers, and tribal farmers. As a mentor in the Northwest Transition to Organic Partnership Program (TOPP), Wilridge Winery is committed to fostering strong connections in the local supply chain. By increasing the market share for organic Washington wines, this project serves the organic community at large by expanding the organic wine market, expanding the market for locally grown wine grapes, and encouraging partners to pursue organic certification.
updated_description: Wilridge Winery’s project aims to substantially increase the market share for organic wines produced in Washington State and to double the capacity of its processing facility, thereby boosting the local market for USDA certified-organic wine grapes within the Yakima area. This expansion will be achieved through a phased approach, beginning with a comprehensive market study and the development of a targeted marketing plan, followed by the physical construction and expansion of the winery’s production facility. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a significant increase in the demand for Washington State organic wines, leading to premium pricing for locally grown grapes and encouraging other wine-grape producers in the region to pursue USDA organic certification. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the wineries, processors, and stakeholders within the wine-grape industry, as well as consumers seeking organic wine options. Specifically, the project intends to support local farmers and ranchers by creating a larger, more robust market for their organically produced grapes. This expansion will benefit the entire supply chain, from growers to distributors and retailers, and will ultimately increase the availability of organic wine within the market. By focusing on the growth of the organic wine sector in Washington State, the project will contribute to a broader expansion of the domestic organic wine market.

original_description: The Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative (PSFHC) is a farmer owned cooperative, incorporated in 2016, with a mission to support and champion local, family scale farms by providing a direct connection with buyers in the region seeking high quality, locally produced food. PSFHC member-producers include over 80 farmers, ranchers, and value added agricultural producers providing products sourced from the Puget Sound region of Western Washington. PSFHC purchases produce from its member-producers and then markets, sells, and distributes to a diverse customer base. PSFHC is focusing on the development of a strategic financial plan for sustainable expansion. This plan includes development of processing services that will add value to member-producers products, and provide them with enhanced and competitive market access. The strategy addresses the critical need for an efficient means to prepare certified organic and conventional produce for sale as fresh cut or frozen. The 50% of produce sold through PSFHC is certified organic, the forthcoming certification of its facility will ensure organic segregation strategies comply with use of this equipment towards producing certified organic products. PSFHC will utilize funds to purchase appropriate processing equipment that will create the capacity for the organization to provide this needed service as they expand member-producers' benefit offerings.
updated_description: The Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative is undertaking a strategic project focused on sustainable expansion and enhanced market access for its member-producers, which include over 80 farmers, ranchers, and value-added agricultural producers throughout the Puget Sound region of Western Washington. This initiative will primarily involve the purchase of appropriate processing equipment, specifically designed to create the capacity for the organization to prepare certified organic and conventional produce as fresh-cut or frozen products, representing approximately 50% of the hub’s sales volume. The anticipated outcome of this project is to significantly improve the value proposition for member-producers by enabling them to meet the increasing demand for prepared organic and conventional produce, thereby expanding their sales potential and strengthening their market positions. Ultimately, this project will benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors within the Puget Sound region, providing them with a more efficient and competitive pathway to reach a wider customer base. The Food Hub’s efforts will facilitate the production and sale of prepared produce, addressing a critical need for convenient, high-quality organic and conventional options for consumers. By investing in processing capabilities, the Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative aims to strengthen the local food system and support the growth of its member-producers’ businesses, ensuring a greater volume of locally produced food reaches the market.

awardee_name: Lukens Farms, Inc. DBA Grace Harbor Farms
original_description: Grace Harbor Farms is a vertically integrated farm and food business. From the farm to the grocery store, they control their products through every stage of the supply chain. They sell wholesale and deliver directly 80% of their volume, using a distributor for the other 20% of clients that they cannot service easily themselves. Grace Harbor Farms is a trusted name in the greater Puget Sound area and have established a strong relationship with PCC Natural Foods, Whole Foods, Safeway, Albertsons, QFC, Fred Meyer, Town &Country, Haggen, and local independent Co-Ops. There is a strong demand for their conventional milk products and Grace Harbor Farms is now ready to partner with their organic dairy neighbors to bring more 58 organic dairy products to market. The addition of this equiment will allow Grace Harbor Farms to meet that demand.
updated_description: Grace Harbor Farms is undertaking a project to significantly expand its offerings of organic dairy products to meet growing market demand within the greater Puget Sound area and beyond. This project will involve the purchase of new equipment, specifically designed to support the handling and processing of organic dairy products, allowing the farm to increase its production capacity. The anticipated outcome of this investment is to substantially grow Grace Harbor Farms’ market share by providing a greater selection of organic milk and dairy products to its existing wholesale clients, including established partners such as PCC Natural Foods, Whole Foods, Safeway, Albertsons, QFC, Fred Meyer, Town & Country, Haggen, and local independent Co-Ops, as well as its distributor network. This expansion will directly benefit farmers and ranchers who supply Grace Harbor Farms with organic dairy ingredients and will provide a wider range of organic dairy options for consumers. The project is expected to bolster the farm’s ability to fulfill orders and strengthen relationships with its key distribution channels. Ultimately, Grace Harbor Farms aims to serve a broader customer base seeking high-quality organic dairy products, thereby increasing the availability of these goods to the market and supporting the farm’s continued growth and success.

original_description: Snowgrass Farm, woman-owned and located in rural Eastern Washington, seeks to purchase equipment with implements to expand processing and post-harvest activities in the winter months by providing access to their high tunnels during the winter and enabling them to grow year-round, increasing yearly production by 30%. The equipment will enable Snowgrass Farm to transport produce, planting materials, the washing, packing, processing, and storage of harvested crops. With winter access, they can grow continuously harvestable crops in their 2,760 sq ft heated tunnel, producing over 1,000lbs of produce the first winter. Improved accessibility will also increase spring production with earlier planting in both the heated and nonheated tunnels. Snowgrass Farm will sell directly to its rural community through local grocers and food banks, while also creating winter farm positions. This region does not have any organic farmers growing in winter despite the demand. Currently, Snowgrass doesn’t grow between October and April due to cold 59 temperatures and heavy snowfall. While a propane heater in a high tunnel was installed, the tunnels remain blocked by snow and inaccessible for propane refilling.
updated_description: Snowgrass Farm, a rural Eastern Washington enterprise, seeks to significantly expand its operations through the purchase of specialized equipment designed to enhance processing and post-harvest activities, ultimately aiming to increase yearly production by 30%. This project will equip the farm with the necessary tools to transport produce, plant materials, wash, pack, process, and store harvested crops, capitalizing on access to their 2,760 square foot heated high tunnel during the winter months. The anticipated outcome is the consistent production of over 1,000 pounds of produce during the initial winter season, with improved accessibility also expected to positively impact spring production through earlier planting in both the heated and nonheated tunnels. Snowgrass Farm intends to sell its products directly to the local community via partnerships with area grocers and food banks, creating employment opportunities for farmers and supporting the local economy. This project addresses a critical need within the region by enabling the farm to operate year-round, filling a gap in the market for organically grown produce. The farm’s operations will benefit farmers, consumers, and processors, providing a reliable source of fresh, organic crops. The increased production will strengthen the local food system and support the livelihoods of those involved in agricultural production and distribution. By overcoming the limitations imposed by winter weather conditions, Snowgrass Farm will contribute to a more robust and resilient agricultural supply chain.

original_description: Through this project, Mainstem Malt will launch a new certified organic malt line that coordinates an ecologically responsible grain value chain from farmer to buyer. As a unique Certified B Corp malt company sourcing exclusively from Salmon-Safe certified farmers, Mainstem came to market in 2017 to provide regional producers with a premium market for grains being grown with exceptional water quality and habitat conservation practices. Since its founding, the company has made significant purchases of domestically grown Northwest grain all while retaining elevated transparency throughout the grain valuechain and simultaneously developing the market for domestic malt. Mainstem Malt aims to build upon this successful model to develop expanded markets for certified organic grain producers in the Cascadia Region. Together with a diverse set of partners, Mainstem Malt will increase domestic organic supply chain capacity for organic barley. The project will accomplish this by expanding expert staff capacity, building, and maintaining relationships with certified organic growers and processors, establishing new markets for organic malt, and developing and executing a marketing plan that differentiates organic, regionally grown, and produced malt to both buyers and end consumers. Mainstem Malt has commitments from certified organic and transitioning-to-organic growers who recognize the value of barley within a feed grain rotation and are seeking high-end markets for their crops as well as long-standing relationships with certified organic craft beverage makers. Paired with a growing demand for organic in the craft beverage sector, Mainstem Malt is eager to build out this important regional market.
updated_description: Mainstem Malt is undertaking a project to establish a new certified organic malt line, creating an ecologically responsible grain value chain from farmer to buyer within the Cascadia Region. This initiative will focus on expanding domestic organic supply chain capacity for organic barley by purchasing and building relationships with certified organic growers and processors, establishing new markets for organic malt, and executing a targeted marketing plan. The anticipated outcome of this project is to increase the availability of domestically produced organic barley to meet growing demand from craft beverage makers and other stakeholders. Mainstem Malt’s commitment to sourcing exclusively from Salmon-Safe certified farmers and maintaining elevated transparency throughout the grain value chain will allow it to support farmers seeking high-end markets for their crops as part of a feed grain rotation. By developing this market, Mainstem Malt aims to provide a viable pathway for processors to utilize increased volumes of organic barley, ultimately benefiting farmers and contributing to the growth of the organic malt industry. The project directly supports stakeholders in the craft beverage sector who are eager to incorporate organic, regionally grown malt into their products, while also assisting farmers in establishing long-term relationships and accessing premium markets for their crops.

awardee_name: George J Otte DBA River Valley Organics
original_description: George J Otte DBA River Valley Organics is an organic family farm in rural eastern Washington. The farm grows, packs, and sells fruit. Production has expanded in response to a greater demand for quality local organic fruit from buyers, doubling the volume of fruit to process and sell. There is a need to increase packaging capacity. The project proposes to purchase a small packing line to wash and dry the fruit, rather than manually cleaning the fruit by hand. This will benefit the farm, its employees, other producers, buyers, and the local community. This will allow River Valley Organics to expand its markets to include additional 60 buyers and sell more fruit to current buyers. In addition, this will allow the business to offer packing services to other local organic growers, expanding their markets as well. Fruit availability, quality and freshness will be enhanced by packaging it in a timely manner. Employees will be able to sort and weigh the cleaned fruit instead of wiping each piece clean, which will be less physically demanding. By shifting job duties, River Valley Organics will be able to retain employees while increasing output. The estimate is that with this equipment, they can package four times as much fruit in a day as they currently do, making it more cost-effective. This will allow River Valley Organics to pack 600 boxes per day (according to manufacturer data), rather than the maximum 150 per day currently possible by hand-wiping each piece of fruit. By becoming more economically sustainable, the business will be able to continue to provide employment to local people in this impoverished rural area.
updated_description: George J Otte DBA River Valley Organics is undertaking a project to significantly enhance its fruit packing capabilities, driven by a doubling of fruit production to meet increased market demand. The core of this initiative involves the purchase of a small packing line specifically designed to wash and dry the fruit, replacing the current manual wiping process. This investment anticipates a substantial expansion of the farm’s operations, projecting the ability to package six hundred boxes of fruit daily, compared to the previous maximum of one hundred and fifty. By automating this key stage of the process, River Valley Organics intends to broaden its market reach, enabling sales to an additional sixty buyers and increased volume to its existing customer base. Furthermore, the farm intends to provide packing services to other local organic growers, thereby facilitating access to new markets for a wider range of producers and stakeholders within the agricultural sector. This upgraded capacity will improve the availability and quality of the fruit, ensuring freshness and presenting a more appealing product to consumers. The project’s anticipated outcomes include a more economically sustainable business model, allowing River Valley Organics to maintain employment opportunities for local people in this rural area. The benefits will extend to farmers, processors, and the broader agricultural community, supporting economic growth and providing viable employment within the region.

awardee_name: Bickford Farms Inc. dba Meadowlark Organics
original_description: This project’s goal is to expand the on-farm cleaning and handling capacity to facilitate market pathways for diversified organic grain growers in the Upper Midwest. Bickford Farms Inc. dba Meadowlark Organics has successfully cultivated certified organic, food-grade grains and run a wholesale and direct marketed flour business since 2016. Significant progress has been made toward addressing the need for grain cleaning and storage infrastructure in the region by constructing granary (grain cleaning facility) and on-farm flour mill, Meadowlark Community Mill. Vertical integration enables storage, cleaning, milling, packaging, and distribution from a single location. One-third of the 1,000-acre farm produces culinary grains, and an additional $150,000 of grain are sourced annually from regional farmers to meet demand. A flour mill produces and distributes approximately 13,000 pounds of flour per week. Together, they make locally grown organic grain accessible across the Upper Midwest. While the existing infrastructure has enabled growth, Meadowlark Organics’ granary needs a gravity table, optical sorter, and connecting bucket elevator to clean a wider variety of grains with improved precision, and increased capacity. These purchases will serve area farmers who are seeking markets for their diverse crops such as wheat, rye, corn, buckwheat, and dry beans. With this funding, it will enhance grain cleaning equipment, and strengthen partnerships with local organic farmers. This project will advance market paths for domestic organic agricultural producers, contribute to crop rotation diversity, and promote sustainable farming practices in this region.
updated_description: Meadowlark Organics’ project aims to expand on-farm grain cleaning and handling capabilities to facilitate market pathways for organic grain growers in the Upper Midwest. This initiative will involve the purchase of critical equipment for the Meadowlark Community Mill, including a gravity table, optical sorter, and connecting bucket elevator, to significantly enhance the precision and capacity of grain cleaning operations. The current facility, which integrates storage, cleaning, milling, packaging, and distribution, already processes approximately 13,000 pounds of flour weekly and utilizes an additional $150,000 of grain sourced annually from regional farmers, primarily to meet demand for crops such as wheat, rye, corn, buckwheat, and dry beans. The anticipated outcome is to strengthen partnerships with local organic farmers and increase the availability of domestically grown organic grains to consumers and processors throughout the Upper Midwest. This project directly benefits farmers by providing them with a dedicated space to efficiently clean and prepare their crops for sale, while also supporting the production of high-quality flour for regional markets. Ultimately, the project seeks to improve access to organic grains for a wider range of stakeholders involved in the food supply chain.

original_description: The DeLong Co., Inc. (DeLong) has spent 35 years working in the organic market, building, and maintaining relationships with producers, transportation companies, and end users. DeLong aims to revolutionize the consumption of domestically grown organic grains and livestock feed. The project provides direct access to the Union Pacific Railroad and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago, which offer seamless connectivity to all Class 1 railroads in the U.S. Through critical investments in infrastructure, equipment, and transportation capabilities, the project aims to address the barriers of limited storage capacity, inadequate quality control measures, segregation challenges, traceability, and transportation constraints while stimulating increased demand for organic products within the U.S. This project is expected to create over 36 million pounds of organic corn demand by increasing current storage capacity by 140,000 bushels, implementing proper equipment to segregate organic corn from conventional corn, and adding railcars throughout the threeyear project duration. The project seeks to create positive impacts for organic grain producers within DeLongs customer base. DeLong has purchased organic grain from 697 producers in Wisconsin and Illinois, 70 of whom are small producers with less than 300 acres of land. Providing producers with increased benefits is of the utmost importance to DeLong. Ultimately, DeLong hopes to share these project findings and successes with existing and future producers to both eliminate entry barriers and provide a net increase in domestic consumption of organic grain.
updated_description: DeLong Co., Inc. is undertaking a significant project designed to revolutionize the consumption of domestically grown organic grains and livestock feed, addressing critical barriers within the supply chain. This initiative centers around strategic investments in infrastructure, equipment, and transportation capabilities, leveraging direct access to the Union Pacific Railroad and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago to facilitate seamless connectivity to all Class 1 railroads across the U.S. Specifically, the project anticipates creating over 36 million pounds of organic corn demand through a phased approach involving a 140,000-bushel expansion of storage capacity, the implementation of specialized equipment for the precise segregation of organic corn from conventional corn, and the addition of new railcars over a three-year period. These investments are intended to benefit farmers and processors involved in the organic grain sector, ultimately stimulating increased demand among consumers for organic products within the United States. DeLong Co. has a strong existing relationship with 697 producers located in Wisconsin and Illinois, including 70 small producers with land holdings of less than 300 acres, and the project is expected to provide enhanced benefits to these stakeholders. The project’s anticipated outcomes include a measurable increase in the availability of organic corn, improved quality control measures, and streamlined traceability throughout the supply chain. The project will positively impact stakeholders by offering new market pathways for organic grain producers and fostering greater consumer access to domestically produced organic commodities.

original_description: Over the past three years, craft malt processing has grown by nearly 10 million pounds and is expected to continue increasing in the coming years. This means since 2019, craft malt production in North America has grown by 60% according to research conducted by the Craft Maltsters Guild. To date, there are no craft malt operations in Wisconsin, much less an organic craft malt operation. Currently, organic craft breweries purchase their grain and malt from out of state or even abroad. Other craft breweries are not necessarily able to trace their malt to the Midwest region. This project seeks to develop a craft malt operation in Wisconsin, the first of its kind. This operation will secure local grains from farmers in Wisconsin and process the grains into malt to be used by local craft breweries in the state. Craft malting is on the rise nationwide, and there is currently a void in Wisconsin to fill the gap between grain farmers and the abundance of craft breweries in the state. This malt operation in collaboration with a local farmer has a 500lb batch capacity to start and can directly be entirely purchased by a local craft brewer in Madison, WI. The equipment will enable Meristem Malt to take grain from surrounding farms to clean, process, and then transport the finished malt product to craft breweries and distilleries. The operation might expect to produce 8-10 tons of quality malt per week in future expansions in line with the capacity of other craft malt houses across the 62 country. The malt would go to craft breweries and distilleries, and over time could grow into a market for home brewers. The deliverable will be processed local grain as malt and delivered to a local craft brewery for testing and brewing. These brewers who value the opportunity to use local ingredients are beneficiaries, as well as the local farmers seeking to sell organic barley in the future. This creates a local value-added market for organic grain growers while allowing brewers to connect with a local product and use it to tell a value chain story.
updated_description: Meristem Malt’s project seeks to establish Wisconsin’s first craft malt operation, addressing a critical gap in the regional supply chain for craft breweries and distilleries. This venture will involve the acquisition of specialized equipment designed for cleaning, processing, and transporting grain into malt, with an initial 500-pound batch capacity, and will operate in collaboration with a local Wisconsin farmer. The anticipated outcome is the production of high-quality malt, initially targeting 8-10 tons per week, which will be directly supplied to local craft breweries for testing and brewing. This operation will benefit farmers by providing a market for their organic barley, while simultaneously offering craft breweries access to locally sourced ingredients, enabling them to develop compelling value chain stories. The project’s success will create a localized market for organic grain growers and support the production of alcoholic beverages. Stakeholders involved include the farmer, the malt operation, and the local craft breweries, representing a new economic opportunity within the state. The operation’s growth, potentially scaling to national levels, is expected to increase the availability of locally produced malt to meet the growing demand from craft beverage producers.

original_description: Jonesborough Locally Grown (JLG) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit that connects farmers, food, and the community to grow a vibrant local food system. JLG operates two markets: Boone Street Market (BSM), a year-round local foods store, and Jonesborough Farmers Market (JFM), a tailgate farmers market. Both are producer-only that source primarily within 100 miles of Jonesborough, TN. JLG keeps fees low to benefit the vendor and supports over 100 vendors, many of whom are small or beginning farmers. JLG markets operate with significant volunteer support, donations and fundraisers – somewhat unreliable labor and funding sources, as the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated. For the long-term financial stability of BSM and JFM and viability of JLG vendors, sales must increase to avoid radically changing the low vendor fee structure JLG currently employs. JLG was awarded a FMPP grant in 2018, allowing the start of an intensive marketing campaign. The previous grant was successful despite challenges presented by the pandemic, but rising inflation and overhead costs have increased the sales threshold required to sustain JLG markets. This project builds on the sampling and advertising elements of the previous project – and adds an important consumer demand: online ordering. With FMPP funds to support these initiatives, sales at BSM and JFM are projected to increase 15% by the end of the project period. Increasing sales in addition to foot traffic and retaining vendors are key to the long-term financial stability of BSM and JFM – and, therefore, the sustainability of the farmers and vendors supported by JLG markets.
updated_description: Jonesborough Locally Grown (JLG) is undertaking a project designed to bolster the financial stability of its operations, specifically the Boone Street Market (BSM) and Jonesborough Farmers Market (JFM), to ensure the continued support of its vendor network. This initiative will primarily focus on increasing sales at these two markets through the implementation of an online ordering system, supported by funds awarded through a grant program. The anticipated outcome of this project is a 15% increase in sales at BSM and JFM, driven by expanded consumer access and improved market reach. The beneficiaries of this project include the farmers, ranchers, and food processors who rely on JLG markets to sell their products, as well as the consumers seeking locally sourced goods. JLG’s current strategy of maintaining low vendor fees is projected to become unsustainable given rising operational costs and inflationary pressures, necessitating this sales growth. By adding an online ordering component, JLG aims to attract a broader customer base and facilitate greater sales volume. Ultimately, this project seeks to secure the long-term viability of JLG and the network of producers it supports, allowing them to continue providing fresh, locally grown products to the community.

original_description: Through this project, the Mother Road Farmers Market in Winslow, Arizona, will: Develop, coordinate, and expand local direct producer-to-consumer markets; Increase access to locally grown agricultural products; and Support small farms, new and beginning farmers, and/or underserved producers. The project will establish a full-time Farmers Market Coordinator to support current vendors, add additional food vendors (targeting produce), create programs, promote the market to the community, and evaluate project activities. Expected outcomes are to increase the amount of locally grown produce and food products available to residents by adding 10 produce vendors and creating a consignment program; increase income for local growers – with a focus on small, new, and/or under resourced growers; and improve access to fresh, locally grown food for low-income residents, which includes the community’s Indigenous and Hispanic populations.
updated_description: The Mother Road Farmers Market in Winslow, Arizona, will develop, coordinate, and expand local direct producer-to-consumer markets, aiming to increase access to locally grown agricultural products and provide robust support for small farms, new and beginning farmers, and regional producers. This project will establish a full-time Farmers Market Coordinator to support existing vendors, facilitate the addition of ten new produce vendors, and implement a consignment program designed to enhance sales opportunities. Anticipated outcomes include an increase in the availability of locally grown produce and food products for residents and a corresponding rise in income for participating farmers and ranchers. The project’s primary focus is to improve access to fresh, locally grown food for residents, with particular attention to the needs of the local community, including producers and consumers. The project’s success will be measured by the volume of goods sold and the number of local producers benefiting from the market’s expanded operations. Specifically, the project intends to bolster the economic viability of small farms and support regional producers in providing a consistent supply of fresh food to the community. The increased market activity is expected to strengthen local food systems and provide valuable access to nutritious food options for residents.

awardee_name: Nalwoodi Denzhone: Strength and Beauty Community, Inc.
original_description: This project will address the economic hardships facing the San Carlos Apache communities by building the Tribe’s capacity of supporting local-food enterprises with direct producer-to-consumer marketing technical assistance. Project activities include creating a marketing plan, the development of regional networks supporting local-food aggregation and distribution, establishing operation policies, food safety plans, standard operating procedures required for a successful direct producer-to-consumer marketing. Project deliverables will be utilized in the provision of targeted technical assistance and training to beginning and socially disadvantaged farmers, ranchers, and food businesses as a form of job/career training for Apache people. Project outcomes include a strengthened regional food economy on the San Carlos Apache Reservation, increased access to and consumption of local food, and job creation spurred by related economic development.
updated_description: This project aims to bolster the economic stability of the San Carlos Apache communities through the development of local-food enterprises, focusing on direct producer-to-consumer marketing initiatives. The core activities encompass the creation of a comprehensive marketing plan, the establishment of regional networks designed to facilitate the aggregation and distribution of local food products, and the implementation of operational policies, food safety plans, and standard operating procedures necessary for successful direct producer-to-consumer marketing. Anticipated outcomes include a strengthened regional food economy on the San Carlos Apache Reservation, increased access to and consumption of local food by consumers and stakeholders, and the generation of employment opportunities linked to related economic development. This project will support farmers, ranchers, and food businesses within the San Carlos Apache community, providing the tools and frameworks to build sustainable operations. The project's deliverables will be used to offer targeted technical assistance to beginning food businesses and to those facing socioeconomic challenges. The project’s ultimate goal is to support the development of a robust local food system and to create viable economic pathways for community members.

original_description: The purpose of the People’s Produce Mobile Farmers Market is to bring healthy, fairly-priced, locally-grown produce and other nutritious foods to low-income residents and food assistance beneficiaries using a refrigerated food truck operated by Project New Village, a 501(3)(c) grassroots nonprofit. The project’s service area will encompass eight weekly sites throughout Greater Southeastern San Diego, including the City of San Diego’s Promise Zone, the City of Lemon Grove, and National City. The project will provide a food retail shopping experience to consumers, meeting them at natural points of service such as libraries, YMCAs, community clinics, church parking lots, and other community-oriented gathering spaces. This project will improve equitable access to good food, which Project New Village defines as food that is: sustainable, healthy, affordable, and accessible to all residents. The project will engage new small farmers and producers, conduct culturally-competent marketing activities to market healthy food products and promote food assistance programs, reaching more than 15,000 customers.
updated_description: Project New Village’s People’s Produce Mobile Farmers Market aims to increase equitable access to good food for residents throughout Greater Southeastern San Diego. The project will operate a refrigerated food truck, establishing eight weekly sites across a defined service area, including the City of San Diego’s Promise Zone, the City of Lemon Grove, and National City. This initiative seeks to provide a food retail shopping experience for consumers, strategically positioned within community-oriented gathering spaces such as libraries, YMCAs, community clinics, and church parking lots. The project intends to improve access to sustainable and healthy food options for farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders. Anticipated outcomes include reaching more than 15,000 customers and promoting healthy food products alongside food assistance programs. The primary beneficiaries are the residents of Greater Southeastern San Diego, particularly those seeking affordable and accessible nutritious food choices. The project will focus on sourcing goods from local producers and distributing them to consumers. The initiative strives to strengthen the local food system by connecting producers with consumers directly. The project’s success will be measured by the number of transactions completed and the volume of food distributed, ultimately contributing to a more robust and reliable supply of healthy food within the community.

awardee_name: Central Coast Ag Network dba City Farm SLO
original_description: “Scaling and Expanding San Luis Obispo (SLO) County Farmer Collaborative Partnerships” will measurably address major local and regional barriers to central coast farmers as well as vulnerable/underserved/ socially disadvantaged (low income- low access) communities relating to equitable and inclusive market opportunities and consumer access. This project will build a Farmer Collaborative that offers sustained supportive services and trainings to empower, and benefit limited resource, beginning, socially disadvantaged, and veteran farmers. In addition, the project will collaborate with Harvestly to expand online sales and Slow Money SLO to integrate farmers with the SLO County Farm to School Program. This project provides capacity needed to unify small-scale, new/ beginning farmers and ranchers, as well as underserved/ socially disadvantaged and veteran producer/ consumer communities. Direct beneficiaries include current and future City Farm SLO tenants participating in the Farmer Collaborative, SLO County Farmers, consumers, school districts, and the regional economy. The project’s work plan acts as a strategic and structural backbone to growing partnerships in a way that enables farmers to share administrative, knowledge, equipment, and other resources. The project also provides farmers access to extensive trainings, toolkits, onboarding, marketing, and support services. It is intended that this project will act as a pilot demonstration that can be rapidly adopted, replicated, and scaled throughout the County.
updated_description: Scaling and Expanding San Luis Obispo (SLO) County Farmer Collaborative Partnerships aims to address significant local and regional obstacles faced by central coast farmers and the associated consumer base. This project will establish a Farmer Collaborative designed to provide sustained support and resources to limited-resource, beginning, and socially disadvantaged farmers, as well as ranchers, and to facilitate equitable market opportunities for these stakeholders. The core of this initiative involves integrating farmers with Harvestly to expand online sales channels and collaborating with Slow Money SLO to connect farmers with the SLO County Farm to School Program, thereby unifying small-scale producers and strengthening local food systems. Direct beneficiaries include current and future City Farm SLO tenants, SLO County Farmers, consumers, school districts, and the wider regional economy. The project’s work plan establishes a strategic framework for growing partnerships, enabling farmers to share administrative support, knowledge, equipment, and other resources efficiently. Anticipated outcomes include increased access to markets for farmers and enhanced consumer access to locally sourced products. The project intends to serve as a pilot demonstration, with the potential for rapid adoption and scaling throughout the County, creating a robust and interconnected system of food producers and consumers.

original_description: The project seeks to strengthen the regional food system infrastructure in Siskiyou County, CA by expanding the Mount Shasta Farmer’s Market and providing development opportunities for the area’s beginning farmers. Through collaboration with other organizations and farmers’ markets, and by supporting the business development of small-scale farmers and producers, this project seeks to strengthen the role of regional farmers’ markets in the direct-to-consumer supply chain while also supporting the development of beginning farmers. Project goals include increasing the number of customers patronizing the Mount Shasta Farmers’ Market, actively integrating beginning farmers/producers into the market, facilitating the creation of  new value-added products, providing workshops on subjects identified by project stakeholders, identifying opportunities for regional farmers’ markets to collaborate, and creating new organizations focused on outreach to new customers.
updated_description: The project seeks to strengthen the regional food system infrastructure in Siskiyou County, CA, by expanding the Mount Shasta Farmer’s Market and providing development opportunities for the area’s beginning farmers. This initiative will focus on increasing the number of customers patronizing the market and actively integrating beginning farmers and producers into its operations, supporting the creation of new value-added products, and identifying opportunities for collaboration among regional farmers’ markets. The project anticipates a strengthened direct-to-consumer supply chain, benefiting farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the local food system. Specifically, the project will support the development of beginning farmers, facilitating the expansion of the Mount Shasta Farmer’s Market and aiming to create new organizations focused on outreach to attract new customers. Ultimately, this will result in a greater volume of locally produced goods available to consumers and a more robust local food economy. The intended outcomes include a broadened range of products available at the market, increased sales for participating producers, and enhanced connections between farmers and consumers. original_description:
Community Supported Agriculture  (CSA) is a critical distribution channel for New York City’s neighborhoods and regional farmers. While the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated the critical nature of CSA to New York City residents, other non-local food distribution services have created a more competitive environment for local farmers. Coordinated marketing efforts, innovation, farmer education, and community collaborations are essential to maintaining and growing CSA in NYC.
In this project, led by the Farm Generations Cooperative, three organizations will come together to address these needs through educational opportunities and technological innovation. The organizations include: the Farm Generations Cooperative, a national cooperative of small and midscale farmers that develops technology to support farm viability; GrowNYC, an NYC-based organization that manages farmers markets and farmer education programs in the city; and Just Food, an organization with decades of experience managing CSA, food security, and equity initiatives in NYC. (Partner letters are provided.) In addition to these organizational partners, we will include both farmers and community members in this effort to enliven and grow the New York City CSA marketplace for decades to come.
Within the scope of this project our team will: assess the current state and needs of CSA programs in New York City with a survey and publicly available summary report; add two new community-facing features to GrownBy, a cooperatively-owned farm sales app, that support marketing and expansion of CSA programs in New York City; train 40 farmers on best practices for CSA; and release an updated digital toolbox and guide for managing New York City CSA programs.
updated_description: Farm Generations Cooperative recognizes the importance of Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) as a vital distribution channel for New York City neighborhoods and regional farmers, and this project aims to bolster its continued success in the face of increasing competition from other food distribution services. The project, a collaborative effort between Farm Generations Cooperative, GrowNYC, and Just Food, will focus on enhancing the New York City CSA marketplace through innovative solutions and expanded community engagement. Specifically, the team will conduct a comprehensive assessment of existing CSA programs within New York City, generating a publicly available summary report detailing current needs and opportunities. Furthermore, the project will develop and implement two new features for GrownBy, a cooperatively-owned farm sales app, designed to support marketing and expansion of CSA programs. Alongside this technical development, the initiative will provide a digital toolbox and guide for managing New York City CSA programs, furthering the capacity of stakeholders to manage these operations effectively. The anticipated outcome of this project is a strengthened and more resilient CSA system, benefiting farmers and consumers alike. The primary beneficiaries of this work include farmers who rely on CSA as a key market channel, as well as the consumers who value access to fresh, locally-sourced produce. The project seeks to improve the overall operational effectiveness and sustainability of CSA programs within the New York City area, allowing these programs to better meet the demands of the market. Ultimately, this project will contribute to a more vibrant and sustainable food system in New York City.

original_description: Since 2007, the RiseBoro Farmers Markets (RBFM) locations have connected first-generation immigrant farm owners to the predominantly Dominican, Puerto Rican, Mexican, Central American, and Ecuadorian neighborhood of Bushwick, Brooklyn. In their implementation of intergenerational farming knowledge, seed-saving, and low-impact ecological practices, the participating farmers at RBFM maintain elements of agricultural heritage while establishing themselves as business-owners. In bringing culturally familiar (yet hard-to-find in New York) products to the Bushwick community, the farmers have built a loyal following among customers who are not typical participants in local food channels. By bridging these groups of farmers and customers, RBFM demonstrates how farmers markets can encourage economic growth for small farmers while expanding affordable food access in a low-income community. This project, “Maintaining Community Traditions from the Farm to the Market” will equip us to identify and open a third farmers market location, recruit sixteen new local producers, and further establish our markets as an affordable and accessible source of heritage agricultural products. Aiming to increase farm income, we will also assist in establishing wholesale opportunities with neighborhood restaurants, markets, and non-farmer RBFM producers. In partnership with RBFM farmers, we will further evaluate the feasibility of new retail opportunities, including farm-to-institution sales and value- added product lines.

Operational efficiencies will be achieved through the purchase of food handling equipment to reduce labor in packing boxes. Marketing support, graphic design assistance, and engagement of an online marketing (e.g. Google ad-words) expert are included to engage and boost sales. All activities for CSA implementation will be complete by September 29, 2025.
updated_description: Full Farm CSA, LLC will enhance access to high-quality, organic, locally produced food for residents in Oregon’s Willamette Valley through an expansion of its full-diet CSA program. The project aims to increase the number of CSA subscriptions from a baseline of 320 to a target of 600, with an average annual subscription cost of $2,400, encompassing a wide range of products sourced from participating farms. To achieve this, Full Farm CSA will purchase food handling equipment to reduce labor associated with packing boxes, alongside utilizing marketing support, graphic design assistance, and the services of an online marketing expert to boost sales and engagement. This expansion will serve additional communities including the Portland Metro area, Salem, Corvallis, and Albany, benefiting farmers who can double their product sales through the CSA, and consumer members who will receive convenient access to fresh food. The project anticipates a target revenue increase from $768,000 to $1,440,000 by the end of the project timeline, September 29, 2025. The overall outcome will be an increased supply of locally produced food available to consumers and a strengthened position for the participating farms, creating a positive impact for ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders in the food supply chain.

awardee_name: South Central Oregon Economic Development District
original_description: Medium-scale producers in Klamath County are few in number and must persist against increasing environmental pressures, perpetual socioeconomic factors, and lack of capacity to increase production and sales. To increase the number of Klamath County (local) and regional producers (Central Oregon, Rogue Valley), we will conduct a series of feasibility studies with producers, regional supply chain networks, and customers. We will implement orientation and standards through regular communication and by farm training/networking events to increase capacity of new and existing producers. We will create a digital directory of local producers, facilitate school bulk sales, and initiate a local foods marketing campaign to increase the direct producer-to-consumer sales. A first-of-its kind Harvest Box will cap our efforts by aggregating, storing and delivering a value added product of local and regional foods for some of our most underserved residents. An estimated 50 local and regional farmers and ranchers will produce more products of greater variety and quality because of this project. A regional supply chain and local marketing campaign will increase consumer and bulk sales. Sales of Klamath Grown Online Marketplace will be sufficient to sustain the networking purpose of the nonprofit, Klamath Grown, as will the rich data gleaned from needs assessments. The successful launch of a local value added product will spawn other similar ventures. Advancements of established partnerships will ignite other food markets and opportunities that increase access to locally and regionally produced foods.
updated_description: Klamath Grown will implement a multi-faceted project to bolster the capacity of medium-scale producers in Klamath County and expand market access across Central Oregon and the Rogue Valley. This project will focus on increasing the volume and variety of products available from local farmers and ranchers, achieved through the development of a digital directory of producers, facilitating bulk sales to schools and institutions, and launching a local foods marketing campaign designed to drive direct sales. A key component will be the creation of a Harvest Box, a value-added product aggregating and distributing goods from participating farmers and ranchers, intended to directly benefit local consumers and stakeholders. The anticipated outcome is that approximately 50 farmers and ranchers will increase their production and sales, supported by the expansion of regional supply chains and enhanced marketing efforts. The success of this project is expected to generate valuable data through needs assessments, which will inform future initiatives. Ultimately, Klamath Grown seeks to strengthen the local food system by improving access to locally produced goods and increasing the volume of sales generated by participating producers. The project will support the activities of the Klamath Grown nonprofit through revenue generated by the Klamath Grown Online Marketplace, ensuring the continuation of its networking functions.

original_description: The St. Johns Farmers Market (SJFM), a program of St. Johns Center for Opportunity (SJCO), is preparing for its fourteenth season. Much of the market’s service area is within the Low Income/Low Access Census Tract where community members are impacted by rising housing costs as the populace migrates from Portland’s city center into adjacent neighborhoods. In 2020, the market was forced to relocate unexpectedly due to construction of a luxury condominium in the neighborhood’s downtown core, then Covid-19 emerged, imposing size restrictions on the market. While the market now exceeds its pre-2020 size, cash reserves were expended to prioritize food access and sta?ng needs through a period of instability. SJCO's project will invest in long neglected marketing and equipment upgrades needed to revitalize the market for its second decade of operation. In strengthening customer communications and supporting their preferences, we support vendors in achieving desired sales, allowing SJFM to grow and reinvest in our farmers for years to come. In addition to external communications, marketing funds will be used to develop and translate materials to better promote SJCO’s business development resources to our market vendors. By helping our current vendors be successful through greater sales and access to resources, SJFM will also become a more appealing marketplace for vendors, which will in turn support long term sustainability.
updated_description: The St. Johns Farmers Market, a program of St. Johns Center for Opportunity (SJCO), is undertaking a vital initiative to revitalize its operations for its second decade of service. This project focuses on strategic investments in marketing enhancements and essential equipment upgrades, directly supporting the market’s growth and long-term sustainability. Specifically, funds will be allocated to strengthen customer communications, develop and translate marketing materials, and enhance the overall marketplace appeal for vendors and consumers alike. The anticipated outcome is a more vibrant and successful market, enabling farmers and ranchers to achieve desired sales volume and fostering increased engagement with the local community. SJCO aims to bolster the market’s capacity to support its vendors, creating a stronger and more attractive environment for all stakeholders. Ultimately, this project seeks to empower the farmers and vendors participating in the St. Johns Farmers Market to thrive, enabling them to continue providing fresh produce and goods to the community. By improving communication channels and supporting vendor success, the market can reinvest in its producers and expand its reach, ensuring continued access to local food sources for the community.

original_description: The purpose of the Central Market Trust Business Development Program is to facilitate the expansion of programming outside the Market walls. The Trust will establish an online ordering platform, establish delivery mechanisms for online orders, benefitting shut ins, people earning low incomes, and people who earn low incomes and have low access to fresh and healthy foods and establish pop up markets that serve low income/low access census tract numbers. The trust will also create a marketing plan for new and existing services and product lines.
updated_description: The Central Market Trust Business Development Program aims to expand the reach of its programming beyond the Market’s immediate walls. This initiative will encompass the development of an online ordering platform, along with the establishment of efficient delivery mechanisms designed to serve individuals with limited mobility, those earning lower incomes, and farmers seeking new avenues for sales. Furthermore, the Trust will create pop-up markets strategically located within low-income census tracts, providing access to fresh food products for consumers and ranchers. The overall anticipated outcome is an increased availability of food products to a broader population of stakeholders. Specifically, the project will focus on facilitating connections between food producers and consumers, ensuring that a wider range of individuals can access quality food options. The primary beneficiaries of this program include farmers seeking to broaden their customer base, consumers desiring convenient access to fresh produce, and ranchers looking for alternative sales channels. The Central Market Trust recognizes the importance of streamlining the process of acquiring and distributing food products, enabling a more responsive and effective system for meeting the needs of the community. Through the creation of the online platform and strategic market locations, the Trust intends to enhance the accessibility of food for a diverse group of stakeholders.

original_description:
Lewisburg Farmers Market (LFM) was established in 1937 providing a venue for local farmers and producers to sell locally grown food products directly to consumers. This is the only year-round farmers market in the Central Pennsylvania region.  Changes that occurred as a result of new ownership and the Covid pandemic exposed a crucial need for marketing technical assistance to broaden the market’s appeal to the next generation of customers, re-engage shoppers lost during the Pandemic, enhance sense of community, and attract more low-income consumers. “LFM Technical and Marketing Support Project” will develop a viable business plan to assure longevity of providing healthy foods to consumers in the region, maximize the profitability of new, disadvantaged, and low income farmers and producers, increase the variety of vendors, and improve the complex relationship between vendors, customers and Market management. 
LFM will develop public and private partnerships and retain the services of a top-tier marketing and consulting firm with proven track records of providing strategy-based marketing advice and initiatives. LFM
management will monitor the data driven approach and will share the data and initiatives with Penn State Extension Farm Market Educational Program to disseminate to all Farmer Markets in Pennsylvania.
updated_description: Lewisburg Farmers Market (LFM) initiated this project to address critical needs and ensure its continued operation as the only year-round market in Central Pennsylvania, providing a venue for local farmers and producers to sell their products directly to consumers. The core of this project involves securing the services of a top-tier marketing and consulting firm to develop a comprehensive business plan, focusing on broadening the market’s appeal to attract the next generation of shoppers, re-engage those lost during the pandemic, strengthen community connections, and increase access for low-income consumers.
