Anticipated outcomes include a significantly improved market profile, increased profitability for new and existing producers, a wider range of vendors offering diverse food products, and a more robust relationship between vendors, customers, and market management. Ultimately, this project will benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the region by maximizing the potential of the market and facilitating greater sales. The LFM will leverage public and private partnerships to achieve these goals, and management will closely monitor the data-driven marketing initiatives, sharing key findings with Penn State Extension’s Farm Market Educational Program for dissemination to all Pennsylvania farmer markets. This strategic approach will foster a stronger and more sustainable marketplace, creating opportunities for growth and ensuring a continued supply of fresh, locally sourced food to the community.

original_description: Family Health Centers, Inc. (FHC) is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) that serves Orangeburg, Bamberg, Calhoun and Upper Dorchester Counties in SC. The area is rural, with high rates of poverty and numerous census tracts which have been identified as Low Income /Low Access priority areas. Many area residents find it difficult to access fresh fruits and vegetables needed for a healthy diet. FHC created Farmer’s Markets in LI/LA census tracts in Orangeburg and Denmark for the dual purpose of creating economic opportunity for local farmers by providing direct to consumer sales venues, and providing underserved residents with access to fresh produce. FHC received FMPP funding in 2017 to enhance the Orangeburg market and create the market in Denmark. That grant was closed out in good standing 02/28/2022. The farmer’s markets have been successful and vendors and consumers have requested an increase in market days and sites. Because many residents in small rural communities contend with low income and limited access, FHC seeks continuing funding to add a mobile farmers market that will bring locally grown produce to consumers in priority areas. FMPP funds will be used to retrofit a bus, purchased with health center funds, for use as the mobile market. Grant funds will be used to hire a Market Manager/Driver and a Sales Assistant to staff the mobile market. Host sites will include FHC satellite sites and Senior Centers in priority areas. SC State University’s 1890 Extension Program will assist in recruitment of additional local vendors.
updated_description: Family Health Centers, Inc. (FHC) is undertaking a project to expand access to fresh produce within Orangeburg, Bamberg, Calhoun and Upper Dorchester Counties in South Carolina, an area characterized by high poverty rates and limited access to healthy food options. The core of this initiative involves the purchase and retrofitting of a bus, funded through existing health center resources, to establish a mobile farmers market. Anticipated outcomes include increased availability of locally grown produce for farmers and consumers in priority areas, fostering direct sales opportunities for ranchers and processors. The project will directly benefit farmers by providing new avenues for selling their goods, while simultaneously offering consumers in rural communities access to fresh fruits and vegetables. Host sites for the mobile market will include FHC satellite locations and senior centers within these targeted communities. SC State University’s 1890 Extension Program will assist in recruiting additional local vendors to broaden the supply chain. To ensure the market’s operation, funds will be used to hire a Market Manager/Driver and a Sales Assistant to manage logistics and sales activities. The overall goal is to address the challenges faced by residents in these rural communities who experience difficulties obtaining necessary food items. Through this mobile market, FHC aims to support local agricultural stakeholders and improve nutritional outcomes for the population.

awardee_name: Axis 1 Center of Barnwell/ Barnwell County Commission On Alcohol & Drug Abuse
original_description:
Healthy Eating Active Living Partners (HEALing Partners) is a multi-organization regional coalition that is building community food security in rural Barnwell, SC by redeveloping and enhancing a direct-to-consumer market that makes locally produced foods more accessible and supports farmers and food entrepreneurs through a vital local farmers market. Working collaboratively with other nonprofits and the City of Barnwell, HEALing Partners will redevelop the Barnwell Farmers Market (BFM), establishing an enduring seasonal market that actively works to improve food accessibility and economic stability. The BFM will provide a reliable marketplace to local farmers and food producers, provide healthy food access within our community, educate on the connection between local food choices and quality of life, and provide the community access to resources needed to improve their health.
The BFM redevelopment project will reach its goals through development of a market manager position; recruitment, outreach, and retention of new, beginning, and underserved farmers; increased number and types of vendors; developing a viable business model that can assure profitability, accessibility, and sustainability for the market as a whole; and develop a branding and marketing strategy to increase community reach.
Expected outcomes that will result from a robust local market include: increased overall awareness of local farm products and producers, increased direct-to-consumer sales for local growers, increased ability of low-income individuals to access and purchase healthy local foods directly from farmers, increased numbers and varieties of local food producers vending at the BFM, and increased knowledge about healthy food choices and preparation.
updated_description: Healthy Eating Active Living Partners (HEALing Partners) is undertaking a vital initiative to bolster community food security in rural Barnwell, South Carolina, through the redevelopment and enhancement of the Barnwell Farmers Market (BFM). This project aims to create a sustainable, seasonal marketplace that supports local farmers and food entrepreneurs, providing a reliable venue for their products and fostering increased direct-to-consumer sales. The core of this effort involves the development of a market manager position and the implementation of a comprehensive branding and marketing strategy to broaden community reach and awareness of local farm products. Anticipated outcomes include a significant increase in the number and variety of local food producers participating in the BFM, alongside a greater ability for consumers to access and purchase healthy local foods directly from farmers. Furthermore, HEALing Partners intends to establish a viable business model that ensures profitability, accessibility, and the long-term sustainability of the market. The project will benefit a range of stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, and food processors, by providing a platform for economic activity. Ultimately, the BFM redevelopment seeks to improve food accessibility within the community, offering consumers healthier food options and promoting knowledge about preparation. The anticipated results will include a measurable increase in direct-to-consumer sales for local growers and improved access to healthy food options for the community.

original_description: Knowledge Quest (KQ) operates Green Leaf Learning Farm (GLLF) (https://www.knowledgequest.org/programs/green-leaf-learning-farm/), a three-acre USDA certified organic, urban farm where we grow affordable, fresh produce for Memphis families and provide a place for the entire community to learn about and celebrate fresh, locally grown food. The overarching goal of GLLF is to expand our impact and reach to serve the many low-income families that struggle with food insecurity and access to healthy affordable foods. Formally initiated in 2010, GLLF is located in the historically black neighborhood of South Memphis, a known food desert, where low-income residents face the combined impacts of low access to nutritious, fresh produce and limited economic opportunity. Therefore, GLLF seeks USDA FMPP funding to hire a full-time Program Manager and secure services of a PR firm who will together assess the existing consumer need for food, farmers markets, and food assistance programs. This role will expand our partnership base, develop recruitment and promotional materials, and design and deploy a cohesive advertising and promotional campaign to increase awareness of and participation in community-based fresh-food sales and events. The overall objective is that this project will ultimately lead to the development of an informed, diverse consumer base and an increase in demand for local products through marketing strategies that target our generationally, culturally, and socio-economically diverse community. This work will be accomplished through the collaboration from both the public and private sectors, all committed to the success of the farm and local producers.
updated_description: Knowledge Quest operates Green Leaf Learning Farm (GLLF) to address food insecurity in Memphis by expanding access to fresh produce for low-income families. This project seeks USDA FMPP funding to achieve this through several key actions, including the hiring of a full-time Program Manager and the engagement of a public relations firm. Specifically, the project will focus on a comprehensive assessment of the current demand for food products, farmers markets, and food assistance programs within the community, utilizing the expertise of the PR firm. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is the development of a knowledgeable consumer base, which will drive increased interest and participation in fresh-food sales and associated events. GLLF will work with local producers and consumers to increase demand for local products through the implementation of a cohesive advertising and promotional campaign. This effort will directly benefit the residents of South Memphis, a community facing challenges related to limited access to nutritious food. The project aims to support local farmers and producers while providing consumers with increased options for fresh, healthy food choices. The successful completion of this project will contribute to a stronger local food system and increased access to quality food products for the community. Ultimately, GLLF envisions a collaborative environment where stakeholders – including producers, consumers, and local organizations – work together to strengthen the local food ecosystem.

original_description: This project will develop and implement a new, bi-weekly farmers’ market in Huston, TX. The new market will increase access to healthy fresh food options to the area, especially the adjacent LI/LA census tracts. The project will encourage participation from approximately 30 climate-smart farmers/producers from within a 99-mile radius of the market site and will provide vendors with access to the local restaurants, thereby forming an additional access point for the delivery of local, climate-smart food. Project outcomes include establishment of a market for local food, provision of logistical support to vendor and promotion of local food, and increased consumer education and demand for locally grown food. Project beneficiaries include local farmers, growers, and ranchers as well as Huston area consumers.
updated_description: This project aims to establish a bi-weekly farmers’ market in Houston, Texas, to increase access to fresh food options for the local community. The initiative will facilitate participation from approximately 30 farmers and producers located within a 99-mile radius, providing them with access to local restaurants and expanding their market reach. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of a market for locally grown food, coupled with logistical support for vendors and promotional efforts designed to stimulate demand for locally sourced goods. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and food processors, alongside Houston area consumers. These stakeholders will gain access to a new distribution channel and enhanced opportunities for sales. Furthermore, the market will contribute to strengthening the local food system. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers involved, as well as the consumers who will have increased access to fresh food. The overall goal is to foster a connection between producers and consumers, promoting the sale and consumption of locally produced goods within the Houston area.

original_description: The purpose this project is to establish and implement the new and permanent “Northeast Art and Farmers Market” in El Paso, Texas. The new market will be the first of its kind to operate in Northeast El Paso and include fresh produce from area farmers and ranchers, local handmade art and artisan products and workshops for the entire family. The proposed location at the former Cohen Stadium location is part of a revitalization project to enhance a historically underserved community. A key component to the new market, will be a partnership with the 915 Pop Up Market which will operate the Farmer and Food Education Co-op which will increase the availability of fresh produce and healthy foods while supporting local food producers and makers. The introduction of this new market location, along with the implementation of a strong marketing campaign, will increase tourism and economic development in Northeast El Paso. The new venue will allow for a larger demographic of visitors and an increase in sales for local vendors. The project’s outcomes include a range of economic development activities related to and resulting from the project. Project beneficiaries include area agricultural producers, consumers (individuals, business and institutions).
updated_description: The Northeast Art and Farmers Market project aims to establish a permanent market location in El Paso, Texas, representing the first of its kind in the Northeast El Paso community. This initiative will encompass fresh produce sourced from local farmers and ranchers, alongside a selection of handmade art and artisan products, complemented by workshops designed for families. A key element of the project is a partnership with the 915 Pop Up Market, which will operate a Farmer and Food Education Co-op, supporting local food producers and makers while increasing the availability of fresh produce. The project anticipates significant economic development outcomes within Northeast El Paso, including an increase in sales for local vendors and a broadened demographic of visitors to the new market venue. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders in the region, as well as consumers seeking fresh food products. The project intends to strengthen the local economy and enhance access to goods for the community. The anticipated results of the project include a range of economic development activities directly linked to the market's operation and success. These benefits will extend to the producers and vendors participating in the market, providing them with new avenues for sales and distribution. Ultimately, the project seeks to create a vibrant marketplace that supports the local economy and serves the needs of the community.

original_description: This project will provide regionally produced Natural Beef via direct-to-consumer beef sales to Austin area consumers. The beef will be sourced from USDA Process Verified Program cattle produced a group of independent producers, and processed/packaged by a local processor, resulting in beef halves available to customers in the Austin area. Project goals include the development and promotion of a direct-to-consumer beef market for regionally raised natural beef. Project beneficiaries include actors along the value chain including the processors/packagers, independent small to medium size ranches, and area consumers.
updated_description: This project aims to establish a regionally produced natural beef supply chain, facilitating direct-to-consumer beef sales to customers within the Austin area. The initiative centers around sourcing beef halves from a group of independent producers utilizing the USDA Process Verified Program, alongside local processors who will handle the processing and packaging of the beef. Anticipated outcomes include the development of a robust market for regionally raised natural beef, fostering stronger relationships between farmers and consumers. This project will directly benefit a range of stakeholders, encompassing the ranchers involved in producing the beef, the processors and packagers who handle the product, and the consumers seeking access to this type of beef. The project’s success will depend on the efficient operation of this value chain, ensuring the availability of regionally produced natural beef to meet consumer demand within the Austin area. Ultimately, this project seeks to create a viable and sustainable market for natural beef, supporting the economic activity of ranchers and bolstering the local food system.

original_description: This project will support Utah’s farmers market sector through increased capacity, heightened visibility, increased collaboration, and improved operations. Project activities include increasing the success of new and beginning market managers through designing and distributing a market manager handbook, hosting an annual online training for new and beginning market managers, and hosting quarterly, online Ask a Manager sessions. Additional project activities include increasing support for and visibility of Utah farmers markets by creating a nonpro?t, hosting an annual forum for network members, and creating a public-facing social media page. The project will also assess the economic and community impact of Utah farmers markets partnering directly with markets to gather data with Farmers Market Coalition guidance. Through these activities, Utah farmers markets will see increased support and capacity, heightened visibility, increased collaboration, and improved operations. Consumers and market stakeholders will bene?t through improved operations, as well as heightened visibility of Utah farmers markets.
updated_description: This project will bolster Utah’s farmers market sector by significantly enhancing its capacity, increasing visibility, fostering collaboration, and improving operational efficiencies. The initiative will achieve this through several key activities, including the development and distribution of a comprehensive market manager handbook, the creation of a public-facing social media page to promote Utah farmers markets, and the establishment of an annual, non-profit forum to connect market stakeholders. Furthermore, the project will directly assess the economic and community impact of Utah farmers markets, partnering with market representatives to gather data and gain a deeper understanding of their contributions. Anticipated outcomes include increased support for market managers, a greater consumer awareness of the availability of local products, and strengthened relationships among market participants. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be Utah farmers, ranchers, and food processors, alongside the consumers who access these goods, and the various stakeholders involved in the farmers market ecosystem. The project’s success will be measured by enhanced operational practices within Utah’s farmers markets and a heightened public profile for the sector, allowing for greater access to fresh, locally produced food options for the community. Ultimately, this initiative aims to support the continued vitality and growth of Utah’s farmers market sector, strengthening local food systems and providing valuable resources to market managers and their networks.

original_description: God’s Pantry Food Bank (GPFB) serves 50 counties in Central and Eastern Kentucky, supporting more than 450 member food pantries and meal programs. Their total food distribution of 41.8 million pounds in 2021 included 13 million pounds of fresh produce. With team partners Appalachian Regional Healthcare (ARH) and Kentucky Educational Development Corporation (KEDC), GPFB is coordinating efforts to increase farm to institution distribution in southeast Kentucky, anchored by the food warehouse GPFB is developing in Hazard. GPFB’s planned facility will serve as a satellite distribution facility to improve food supply to member pantries in the distressed seven-county area. This facility will also provide supply chain infrastructure supporting farm-to-institution initiatives currently underway at ARH and KEDC. Anchoring efforts to supply more fresh fruits, vegetables, and other foods from local and regional sources, this facility will improve nutrition for patients, students, employees, and the community at large. GPFB’s food warehouse, with dry and cold storage, will fill an important gap in the regional food system, currently served by facilities located up to 230 miles away.
updated_description: God’s Pantry Food Bank is spearheading a project to bolster farm-to-institution distribution within southeast Kentucky, focusing on enhancing access to fresh food sources for a wide range of stakeholders. The core of this initiative involves the development of a new food warehouse in Hazard, Kentucky, designed to function as a crucial satellite distribution facility. This warehouse will provide essential supply chain infrastructure supporting ongoing efforts by Appalachian Regional Healthcare (ARH) and Kentucky Educational Development Corporation (KEDC) to increase the supply of fresh fruits, vegetables, and other food products directly to institutions. The anticipated outcome of this project is to significantly improve the availability of nutritious food for patients, students, employees, and the broader community. Specifically, the warehouse will offer dry and cold storage, addressing a current gap in the regional food system that is currently reliant on facilities located up to 230 miles away. This expanded distribution network aims to support local and regional producers, processors, and ranchers in supplying fresh food products to institutions. Ultimately, the project seeks to enhance nutritional intake for a substantial number of consumers and strengthen the overall food system. The facility will serve as a central hub for distributing these goods, ensuring a more reliable and efficient flow of fresh produce and other food items.

original_description: Celebrating its 30th season in 2022, the nonprofit Jefferson County Farmers Market (JCFM), operates the Port Townsend and Chimacum Farmers Markets in Jefferson County, WA. JCFM’s mission is to support local farmers and artisans with vibrant marketplaces that cultivate community and provide access to healthy food for all. The JCFM offers low-bar, low-fee sales venues that support new, emerging, and established small businesses in growing and thriving. Jefferson County is unique in many ways including its geographical isolation on the Olympic Peninsula, higher than average population living below the poverty level (13.6% compared to 10.2% in Washington State), and its large proportion of small and micro farms. These distinctive attributes present added challenges to sustaining a thriving farmers market organization. The Growing Farms, Thriving Markets project includes three core initiatives: 1) market assessment and research to identify gaps in the JCFM shopper base and strategies to reach under met populations; 2) support and professional coaching for new and growing farm vendors; 3) targeted outreach to grow and diversify JCFM’s regular shopper base supporting vendor sales growth. These initiatives are expected to help our community farmers markets thrive, improve the economic sustainability of local farmers and producers, and increase community access to nutritious, locally grown food for years to come.
updated_description: The Jefferson County Farmers Market is undertaking a vital project to bolster its operations and expand its reach within Jefferson County, Washington, as it celebrates its 30th season in 2022. This initiative focuses on three key areas: conducting a comprehensive market assessment to pinpoint gaps in the shopper base and develop strategies for reaching all segments of the community; providing specialized support and guidance for new and developing farm vendors; and executing targeted outreach efforts designed to cultivate a broader and more varied regular shopper base, thereby supporting increased sales for its vendor partners. The anticipated outcomes of this project include the enhanced economic sustainability of local farmers and producers, and improved community access to locally grown food. The primary beneficiaries of this work will be the farmers, ranchers, and processors who operate within Jefferson County, alongside the consumers who purchase their products. Recognizing the unique challenges presented by Jefferson County’s geographical isolation and its demographic characteristics – including a population experiencing economic hardship – the project specifically aims to strengthen the market’s capacity to serve all members of the community and support their agricultural ventures. Ultimately, this project seeks to ensure the continued vitality of the Jefferson County Farmers Markets and the positive impact they have on the local food system.

original_description: The intent of the project is to expand the reach of our farmers market (FM) by increasing promotion and capacity to handle an increase in the number of vendors. The project would expand the footprint of the market beyond its current boundaries, by expanding outreach activities and by hiring a market coordinator to take on the responsibility for soliciting new vendors, serving customers and general expanded activities. To increase outreach, place additional adds in the local newspapers and billboards near the FM location to attract drive by customers. The project would provide training and support services for continuing and first-time vendors. The project will also provide learning opportunities and educational/nutritional materials for FM clients to encourage their participation and consumption.
updated_description: The Farmers Market Project aims to broaden the reach and impact of the local farmers market by implementing strategic promotional activities and increasing operational capacity. This project will encompass several key elements, including expanded advertising placements in local newspapers and on billboards situated near the market location to capture the attention of passing drivers and to attract new customers. Furthermore, a market coordinator will be hired to manage vendor recruitment, ensuring a diverse selection of producers participate, and to oversee general market operations and activities, facilitating engagement with customers. A core component of this initiative involves providing support services and learning opportunities for both existing and new vendors, fostering a welcoming environment for producers and encouraging increased market participation. Alongside vendor support, the project will deliver educational materials focusing on nutritional information and consumption practices to encourage customer engagement with the market’s offerings. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, and processors who supply goods to the market, as well as the consumers who access these products. By expanding the market's visibility and capacity, the project intends to stimulate economic activity within the local community and improve access to fresh agricultural products for a wider range of individuals. The overall goal is to strengthen the connection between producers and consumers, creating a more robust and sustainable local food system.

original_description: The Platteville Farmer’s Market Revitalization project will revitalize and expand the Platteville Farmer’s Market (PFM) to benefit both producers and consumers. Producers will benefit by increased opportunities for direct producer-to-consumer sales and consumers will benefit by increased access to fresh, locally grown and produced agricultural products. The project will develop and implement a comprehensive marketing plan to promote the market and market producers; survey the community to determine consumer wants and needs; survey producers to determine educational, business development, and other support needs; work to retain and recruit market vendors; and provide start- up and continuing education to local food entrepreneurs and connect them with resources to help diversify and increase revenue streams. Expected outcomes include increased overall awareness of the PFM and local agricultural products and producers, increased direct-to-consumer sales and income for individual farmers through the market, increased knowledge for producers engaged in the PFM, and improved access to locally produced products for consumers, including the low-income population.
updated_description: The Platteville Farmer’s Market Revitalization project aims to revitalize and expand the Platteville Farmer’s Market to benefit both producers and consumers. This project will focus on increasing opportunities for direct producer-to-consumer sales for farmers and ranchers, alongside expanding access to fresh, locally grown and produced agricultural products for consumers. Key elements of this initiative include the development and implementation of a comprehensive marketing plan to promote the market and its producers, alongside conducting community surveys to determine consumer wants and needs. Furthermore, the project will survey producers to identify support needs, including educational resources and assistance in developing business strategies to increase revenue streams. A core component will be efforts to retain existing market vendors and recruit new ones, ensuring a vibrant and continuously evolving market. The anticipated outcomes of the project include increased overall awareness of the Platteville Farmer’s Market and the local agricultural products offered, along with a rise in direct-to-consumer sales and income for participating farmers and ranchers. Increased knowledge among producers regarding market operations and business development will also be realized. Ultimately, the project seeks to improve access to locally produced goods for consumers, with a particular focus on benefiting the local farming community and supporting a robust marketplace. The project anticipates benefiting all stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural goods within the Platteville area.

original_description: The goal of Greensgrow’s Community Connections Program is to build the long-term capacity and stability of Greensgrow through the development of a strategic community connections plan including development of supportive infrastructure by transitioning to a “farm without walls” and thereby addressing food insecurity and increasing connection between producers and consumers. The intended beneficiaries are residents of Kensington, Port Richmond, and Fishtown who are experiencing poverty, food insecurity, and lack of access to farm-fresh produce. Activities include 1) conducting a data-driven community needs assessment and market analysis, 2) employing a Community Connections Manager to oversee the program as well as coordinate outreach activities, participate in strategic planning process, develop and maintain connections with community partners, producers, and other urban farms, etc., 3) creation of a board to facilitate a strategic planning process, 4) development of new outreach and engagement programs to connect growers/producers to the community/consumers, 5) develop and host training opportunities for urban farms/farmers to present the new model as well as technical knowledge about producing, preparing, procuring, and/or accessing local/regional foods, and 6) develop and produce video content for social media and other outlets to connect producers with consumers.
updated_description: Greensgrow’s Community Connections Program aims to bolster the long-term stability and capacity of the organization by implementing a strategic plan centered around a “farm without walls” model, thereby addressing food insecurity and strengthening the connections between producers and consumers. This initiative will involve the creation of supportive infrastructure to facilitate the distribution of fresh produce. Anticipated outcomes include increased access to farm-fresh goods for residents of Kensington, Port Richmond, and Fishtown who experience poverty and food insecurity. The program will center on a Community Connections Manager to oversee outreach activities and strategic planning, alongside the development of a board to guide the planning process. Furthermore, Greensgrow will produce video content for social media and other outlets to connect growers/producers with consumers and stakeholders. The project will focus on expanding the network of local producers and consumers engaged in the distribution of goods. The project seeks to connect farmers with consumers, processors with retailers, and other stakeholders involved in the supply chain. Ultimately, the goal is to provide greater access to fresh produce within the targeted communities, supporting a more robust and resilient local food system.

original_description: The Refugee & Asylee Market Promotion (RAMP) project will increase refugee farmers’ integration into Sacramento’s thriving farm-to-fork market, providing community development training and technical assistance to expand financial stability and increase access to culturally relevant produce. The project aims to close the gap between Sacramento’s refugee and underserved farmers and local markets by training and assisting small-scale farmers to sell to local farmers markets, and enter mid-tier value chain suppliers, including ethnic grocery stores. RAMP’s goal is to increase supply by upskilling the farmer base and increasing demand by expanding the portfolio of buyers. By facilitating market linkages through ethnic markets and roadside stands, developing a ‘refugee grown’ label to increase demand outside of ethnic markets, and marketing a variety of culturally appropriate fruits and vegetables, the project aims to improve healthy food access and consumption for low- income immigrant communities, while developing new market opportunities for small-scale farming businesses.
updated_description: The Refugee & Asylee Market Promotion (RAMP) project seeks to strengthen the integration of refugee and asylee farmers into Sacramento’s farm-to-fork market, focusing on expanding financial stability and increasing access to a range of culturally relevant produce. This project will achieve this by facilitating connections between small-scale farming businesses and established buyers, including local farmers markets and mid-tier value chain suppliers like ethnic grocery stores, thereby increasing the supply of fresh goods. Anticipated outcomes include enhanced market opportunities for farmers and improved access to nutritious food for consumers within the local community. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers themselves, alongside the consumers who will benefit from a greater availability of diverse produce. RAMP’s strategy involves the development and promotion of a “refugee grown” label to elevate demand beyond ethnic markets and the utilization of roadside stands as sales channels. By expanding the portfolio of buyers, the project aims to establish robust market linkages, ensuring that farmers can effectively distribute their products. Ultimately, this initiative will contribute to improved food access and consumption patterns, supporting the growth and viability of small-scale farming operations within the region.

original_description: Augusta Locally Grown (ALG) plans to provide business best practices training to mostly underserved farmers of all scales and to regional farmers markets in order to increase sustainability for our regional food system. Through our years of market management and with partnering business professionals, ALG has developed an effective model for supporting both the farmer and the market that enhances product-to-consumer and mid-tier value chain opportunities, increases visibility through marketing, and leverages regional and state partnerships for scaling. Through ALG’s new position as a regional food hub at our location in The HUB for Community Innovation of Augusta, ALG will serve as the regional authority on farmers market best practices, moving to enhance our food system’s infrastructure. Partnerships with the South Carolina Food Hub Association and Georgia Organics, as well as with other markets in the region, will bring more connectivity and capacity to our regional food system and thus to local food economies. Overall, strengthening the farmers, the farmers markets, and the food systems will result in increased access and availability of local agriculture products for underserved communities.
updated_description: Augusta Locally Grown (ALG) plans to enhance the regional food system through a multifaceted approach focused on bolstering farmers and regional farmers markets. This project will establish ALG as the regional authority on farmers market best practices, supporting farmers of all scales and expanding market connectivity. Specifically, ALG will facilitate increased product-to-consumer and mid-tier value chain opportunities, promoting greater visibility through targeted marketing initiatives and leveraging strategic partnerships with organizations like the South Carolina Food Hub Association and Georgia Organics. The project anticipates improved access to local agriculture products for farmers and consumers within the region, fostering stronger relationships between producers and the individuals who purchase their goods. Through expanded market networks and enhanced infrastructure, ALG aims to increase the volume of local products available and improve the overall efficiency of the food system. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened regional food economy, greater market participation among farmers, and improved access to fresh agricultural products. Ultimately, this project will benefit farmers, processors, and consumers alike, creating a more robust and resilient local food system that better serves the needs of the community.

original_description: Ecommerce has grown in recent years, but farmers, ranchers and seafood harvesters focused on selling locally-produced meat and fish have struggled to adapt. Changing technology needs and a lack of knowledge regarding online marketing and shipping frozen meat have deterred producers who serve local markets from rapidly adopting ecommerce as a way to increase their sales of locally-produced meat and seafood. ChopLocal, an “online farmer’s market” for niche meat producers, will provide training and technical assistance to 500 livestock farmers, ranchers and seafood harvesters selling direct-to-consumer, to assist them with digital marketing and ecommerce platform establishment and maintenance. Training will include an educational blog, webinar series and online course. Technical assistance will also be provided to assist producers one-on-one in establishing an ecommerce store. This project will result in at least 150 participating producers establishing ecommerce stores.
updated_description: ChopLocal is designed to address the challenges faced by farmers, ranchers, and seafood harvesters seeking to expand their sales through direct-to-consumer channels. This project will provide comprehensive support to 500 livestock farmers, ranchers, and seafood harvesters who currently focus on selling locally-produced meat and fish. The initiative will facilitate the establishment and maintenance of ecommerce stores for these producers, offering technical assistance on an individual basis. The project anticipates that at least 150 participating producers will successfully launch and operate online storefronts, enabling them to reach a wider consumer base. This support includes the creation of resources such as an educational blog and a webinar series, alongside one-on-one assistance to ensure producers have the necessary knowledge and tools to manage their online sales operations effectively. Ultimately, ChopLocal aims to bolster the businesses of these agricultural stakeholders and to increase the availability of locally-sourced meat and seafood to consumers. The project’s success will result in increased revenue streams for the participating producers, fostering greater economic viability within the agricultural sector.

awardee_name: Greater Lafayette Commerce Community & Economic Development
original_description: This project is to help create a sustainable method for vendors of the Downtown Lafayette Farmers Market to promote and market themselves. The goal is to equip the vendors with tools they can utilize to enhance their marketing efforts, and train them to use these tools and others at their disposal. The project is broken into 3 key initiatives:  1) Development of Marketing Tools: An enhancement of the Lafayette Farmers Market website to allow vendors to create and manage their own pages on the site; 2)  Online training Library and in-person training covering a variety of marketing strategies for vendors to engage directly to consumers; and 3)  Individualized, 1-1 technical assistance and training on digital marketing initiatives, ecommerce implementation, social media, etc. to help eliminate barriers for vendors to market directly to consumers.
updated_description: The Downtown Lafayette Farmers Market project aims to establish a sustainable method for farmers and vendors to effectively promote and market their products directly to consumers. This initiative will focus on several key components, including the enhancement of the Farmers Market website to provide vendors with dedicated pages for creating and managing their own marketing materials, and the development of an online library containing a range of marketing strategies. Furthermore, the project will offer individualized technical assistance to farmers and processors regarding digital marketing initiatives, ecommerce implementation, and social media platforms, assisting them in overcoming barriers to direct consumer engagement. The anticipated outcome of this project is to empower farmers and vendors to increase their visibility and sales within the community. This will directly benefit consumers by expanding their access to fresh products and support local agricultural businesses. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, and processors who participate in the Farmers Market, as well as the consumers who purchase these goods. By facilitating direct relationships between producers and buyers, this project will strengthen the local food system and support economic activity within the community. The project intends to streamline the process of marketing and sales for all participants and improve the overall experience for those involved.

awardee_name: Central LA Economic Dev. Alliance dba Louisiana Central
original_description: The Alexandria Farmers Market’s FMPP project will reinforce and expand its current State, land-grant university, local government and community-based partnerships to catalyze better market access and farm business viability for rural small-scale agricultural producers in central Louisiana. These objectives will be achieved by: improving farmer success and vendor retention through training on food safety, cottage food laws and business financial literacy; intentionally recruiting a more diverse range of prospective market vendors for training in order to improve economic prospects for lower-income rural residents and expand the multicultural appeal of the market; and attracting record numbers of Federal nutrition benefit recipients to the market through a variety of innovative outreach and promotional strategies and family-oriented community events. The results of this project are anticipated to yield important findings and strategies that can be applied to rural farmers markets across the country.
updated_description: The Alexandria Farmers Market’s FMPP project aims to strengthen and expand existing partnerships between the market and key stakeholders, including state, land-grant university, local government, and community organizations, to improve market access and farm business viability for small-scale agricultural producers throughout central Louisiana. This initiative will focus on recruiting a broader range of prospective vendors and attracting a significant number of individuals receiving federal nutrition benefits to the market, supporting economic opportunities for rural residents and enhancing the market’s appeal. The anticipated outcomes of this project include increased sales for farmers and ranchers, and a greater volume of transactions at the market. Specifically, the project will focus on supporting the operational success of market vendors, and fostering a robust consumer base. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers participating in the market, as well as the consumers who purchase products from the market. Furthermore, this project seeks to provide support for those involved in food processing activities. The project anticipates generating valuable insights and strategies that can be applied to rural farmers markets nationwide.

original_description: Through this project, farmers and community members will create safe, on-farm festivals that generate local sales, build customer loyalty, and strengthen rural communities. Project partners will bring together an experienced event and community organizing team to identify and train eight community-based teams, made up of farmers and food advocates, to produce a series of unique, on-farm festivals. Project activities include: Development of trainings, website, and a toolkit of best practices; Employ peer-based learning to train cohorts across Minnesota; Create an asset maps to identify community resources; Incorporation of a input from a range of local food producers and businesses to build capacity for entire communities; Creation of fun, interactive educational materials about the value of local food; Conducting communications campaigns to promote events; and Evaluation to assess the economic impact and sustainability of the on-farm festival model. As a result of this project, it is anticipated that 2,600 local farmers and consumers/community members will engage with local food.
updated_description: Through this project, farmers and community members will create safe, on-farm festivals designed to generate local sales, build customer loyalty, and strengthen rural communities. The project will involve the establishment of eight community-based teams, comprised of farmers and food advocates, who will produce a series of unique festivals. These festivals will incorporate input from a range of local food producers and businesses, fostering capacity building across entire communities and featuring fun, interactive educational materials about the value of local food. The anticipated outcome is the engagement of 2,600 local farmers and consumers/community members in these events. The project will create a website and toolkit of best practices to support these activities. Furthermore, teams will develop asset maps to identify community resources and conduct communications campaigns to promote the festivals. The project aims to increase local sales and strengthen community bonds. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within rural communities. These individuals will participate in and benefit from the increased economic activity generated by the on-farm festivals, contributing to a strengthened local food system. The project will support the creation of a vibrant and resilient local food network, focused on direct-to-consumer marketing opportunities.

original_description: This project addresses those needs by offering key tangible infrastructure and technical assistance services, including: processing capacity, sales point access, and expanded consumer marketing to increase accessibility of regionally produced food for both direct to consumers and public institutions. This project represents a transformative investment in regional agriculture, rural development, food access, and equity, to build a strong localized food economy. LFPP funding will support the staffing expansion necessary to accommodate any and all farmers and food businesses throughout Greater Washington County, Maine that could benefit from Minke Food Hub.
updated_description: The Minke Food Hub project addresses critical needs within Greater Washington County, Maine, by providing tangible infrastructure and technical assistance services to support regional agriculture and food businesses. This initiative will offer increased processing capacity, access to sales points, and expanded consumer marketing efforts, ultimately boosting the accessibility of locally produced food for both direct-to-consumers and public institutions. The project represents a transformative investment focused on building a strong, localized food economy, and will be supported by staffing expansion to accommodate all farmers and food businesses within the region. The anticipated outcome is a significant increase in the volume of regionally produced food reaching markets, benefiting farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders. Specifically, the project aims to improve access to markets for these producers, thereby strengthening the overall food system. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers and food businesses of Greater Washington County, Maine, as well as the consumers who will have greater access to fresh, locally sourced food. This initiative is designed to foster a more resilient and robust local food system, providing increased market opportunities for producers and enhancing food security within the region.

awardee_name: Board of Regents, NSHE, obo University of Nevada, Reno / Nevada System of Higher Education
original_description:
Nevada is one of the fastest-growing states in the US. Farmers markets can be part of the solution to feeding the expanding population while addressing climate concerns and access to fresh produce.
Farmers markets also support the local agricultural economy, serve as community spaces for newcomers, and ameliorate food insecurity in rural and poor urban neighborhoods. Throughout the state of Nevada, farmers markets have been operating with some success. However, they urgently need help with consumer marketing. The vast majority of farm vendors are small operations with limited marketing resources. According to NevadaGrown, a quasi-association of Nevada farmers markets, typical farmers markets are also small operations not equipped to engage in comprehensive consumer marketing. To address these challenges, we will conduct a community development training and technical assistance project. The first year will be devoted to a comprehensive needs assessment and a marketing plan development. In the second year, we will implement the marketing plan by providing training and technical assistance to farmers market managers and farm vendors during the off-season and orchestrating a community-based integrated marketing campaign during the peak season. In the third year, we will repeat the training/technical assistance and campaign cycle to enhance retention and fluency of the knowledge and skills gained. In every stage of this project, the needs of farmers, farmers market managers, and consumers—especially those in underserved communities—will be prioritized and the project team composition and structure will reflect the community orientation.
updated_description: Nevada’s rapidly growing population presents significant challenges in meeting food demands while supporting a robust local agricultural economy. This project aims to bolster farmers markets throughout Nevada by providing comprehensive marketing assistance to farmers and market managers. The core activity involves developing a detailed marketing plan, followed by its implementation through targeted technical support delivered during the off-season and a community-based marketing campaign during peak market periods. This initiative seeks to enhance the visibility and appeal of Nevada’s farmers markets to a wider range of consumers, thereby increasing sales for participating farmers and ranchers. The anticipated outcomes include increased market attendance, enhanced sales volume for vendors, and strengthened connections within the local agricultural sector. Key beneficiaries include farmers, market managers, and consumers seeking access to fresh produce. The project will focus on providing resources to these stakeholders to improve their operational effectiveness and market reach. Specifically, the project will support farmers in attracting new customers and consumers in connecting with local food sources. The project team will prioritize the needs of all involved parties, ensuring the project’s structure reflects a strong community focus. The success of this initiative relies on the effective promotion of Nevada’s farmers markets and the support they provide to the state’s agricultural producers and the communities they serve.

original_description: The purpose of “Harnessing technology to enhance the expertise of Oklahoma agricultural producers while partnering with community organizations for long-term sustainability of the Scissortail Park’s Farmers Market” is to simultaneously improve producer sustainability and consumer access to local foods.  The project will expand the skills of local producers harnessing technology, training, community building, implementing a secondary mid-week market, and marketing to increase sales and attendance. Project beneficiaries include local producers as well as the Oklahoma City community more broadly. Project outcomes are anticipated to include increased producer sales, increased vendor recruitment, and increased participation in the market from consumers in the surrounding neighborhoods.
updated_description: The Scissortail Park’s Farmers Market project aims to simultaneously improve the sustainability of local agricultural producers and expand consumer access to fresh, locally sourced foods. This project will focus on enhancing producer capabilities through strategic technological implementation, fostering community building initiatives, and establishing a secondary mid-week market to bolster sales and increase attendance. Anticipated outcomes include a rise in sales figures for participating farmers and ranchers, increased recruitment of vendors to the market, and greater consumer participation from the surrounding neighborhoods. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass local farmers, ranchers, and food processors, alongside the broader Oklahoma City community. Specifically, the project seeks to strengthen the market’s position as a key destination for consumers seeking high-quality agricultural products. The increased market activity is expected to positively impact the economic viability of the involved producers, contributing to the long-term sustainability of the Scissortail Park’s Farmers Market. By facilitating greater access to local food sources, the project intends to support a robust local food system and enhance the overall experience for market stakeholders.

original_description: Lane County Farmers Market (LCFM) is our region’s oldest and largest farmers market and an integral part of Lane County’s economic and cultural infrastructure.  LCFM requests financial support through the Farmers Market Promotion Program to enable us to fulfill our potential to support the viability of our producers, create a more inclusive marketplace, and better engage our community.  The City of Eugene has constructed a new pavilion and plaza area for the purpose of housing LCFM and creating a more active civic center downtown.  This new market space allows LCFM to provide vending space to more producers.  We plan to recruit and mentor new and socially disadvantaged farmers to become long-term market members.  LCFM seeks to create new marketing options for farmers and to develop a value-added products training program.  The program will allow farmers to enjoy greater revenues through expanded product offerings and the ability to sell year-round.  LCFM will also develop a mid-tier value chain by creating new pathways for farmers to vend with local restaurants, grocery stores, and co-ops; developing relationships that serve buyers and sellers.  Local chefs who are proponents of using locally grown foods have expressed interest in giving cooking demonstrations at the market.  Demonstrations will serve three purposes: creating alliances between restaurants/chefs and our market, disseminating recipes on how to use seasonal produce, and showcasing farmers’ value-added products.   LCFM plans to share materials developed and findings from these new programs with other farmers markets that are interested in developing similar programs.
updated_description: Lane County Farmers Market (LCFM) is seeking financial support to enhance its role as a vital component of Lane County’s economic and cultural landscape. This project will leverage the recently constructed pavilion and plaza in Eugene to expand market capacity and foster a more active civic center, providing increased vending opportunities for farmers. Anticipated outcomes include strengthened relationships between producers and consumers, facilitated access to new markets through connections with local restaurants, grocery stores, and cooperatives, and the development of value-added product streams to generate greater revenues for participating farmers. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the Lane County agricultural sector, who will gain access to expanded sales channels and opportunities to diversify their product offerings. Specifically, LCFM intends to create new pathways for farmers to engage with the local food system and enhance their economic viability. Furthermore, LCFM plans to develop materials and share findings regarding these programs with other farmers markets interested in similar initiatives, contributing to broader improvements across the region’s agricultural landscape. The project aims to support the growth and sustainability of the market and contribute to the overall economic health of the community.

original_description: The Chatham University program supports farmers and other food business owners in implementing better business practices and developing new products, consumer experiences, and other revenue streams. It does so at a critical time in Pennsylvania agriculture where an aging farmer population is under increasing market pressure to transition farmland out of production. The program will support farmers in developing viable value- added products, provide specialized courses in business model diversification, offer individual consulting services, conduct hands-on consumer workshops, and enhance a network of retail and promotional partners. The program is anticipated to increase the longevity of regional farmers, ranchers, and food businesses, sustain vibrant communities of informed consumers, and ultimately foster a stronger regional food system.
updated_description: Chatham University’s program supports farmers and other food business owners in implementing better business practices and developing new products, consumer experiences, and other revenue streams, addressing a critical need within Pennsylvania agriculture. This initiative aims to bolster regional farmers, ranchers, and processors by supporting the development of viable value-added products, facilitating specialized consultations, and enhancing a network of retail and promotional partners. The program anticipates increasing the longevity of these regional food businesses while fostering vibrant communities of informed consumers who engage directly with the food system. Specifically, Chatham University will provide resources and support to help farmers expand their operations, explore new markets, and strengthen their relationships with retail outlets and consumers. The overall project seeks to contribute to a stronger regional food system. By facilitating direct producer-to-retail and producer-to-restaurant activities, the program intends to improve the viability of farms and food businesses. These efforts will contribute to sustained regional food production and strengthen the connections between producers and the communities that consume their products.

original_description: The Food Trust’s 2022–27 three-year project, “Stronger Together: Growing Philadelphia Farmers Markets and Agricultural Businesses Through Citywide Partnerships, Promotion and Technology” (Stronger Together), The Food Trust (TFT) will strengthen our partnerships with the Philadelphia Department of Public Health (PDPH) and Philadelphia Parks & Recreation (PPR) to create a city-wide promotional campaign for all Philadelphia farmers market and farm stands; support the City of Philadelphia’s coordination of farmers market operator resources; and identify and further develop an online platform that will support the creation of a regional network of local agricultural businesses and a variety of purchasers. The goals of this project are to support new and existing market operators' processes and market growth, increase revenue streams for market vendors through online marketing and direct producer-to-consumer opportunities, and strengthen nutrition security and healthy food access throughout the city of Philadelphia. In addition, TFT plans to reconvene its Farmers Market Advisory Group (FMAG), which includes urban and rural farmers, community members, and other local food stakeholders, in order to guide capacity building and market planning. FMAG will provide continuous peer-to-peer technical assistance and support on skills and strategies for farmers in Pennsylvania (PA) to increase sales in the communities they serve through workshops, webinars and the creation of a community of learning for farmers.
updated_description: The Food Trust’s “Stronger Together” project aims to bolster Philadelphia’s farmers markets and agricultural businesses through strategic partnerships and technological advancement. This initiative will create a city-wide promotional campaign encompassing all Philadelphia farmers markets and farm stands, coordinated in conjunction with the City of Philadelphia’s efforts to manage resources for market operators. Furthermore, The Food Trust will develop an online platform designed to foster a regional network connecting local agricultural businesses with potential purchasers – farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders – facilitating direct-to-consumer sales and market growth. The anticipated outcomes include increased revenue streams for market vendors through enhanced online marketing opportunities and direct producer-to-consumer interactions, and the strengthening of nutrition security and healthy food access throughout Philadelphia. The project will also revitalize the Farmers Market Advisory Group (FMAG), comprised of local farmers, community members, and stakeholders, to provide continuous peer-to-peer technical assistance and support. This support will focus on strategies to improve sales within their communities through workshops and webinars, creating a collaborative learning environment. Ultimately, the project seeks to benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors by expanding their market reach and bolstering their business operations, while simultaneously improving access to fresh food for consumers throughout the city.

original_description:
This project will support and promote direct-to-consumer (D2C) marketing of locally processed food products that are primarily made by a diverse and inclusive community of members at Hope & Main, Rhode Island’s premier food business incubator. 

We expect that 150 new food producers, 40% of whom are expected to be minority-owned businesses, will participate along with 100+ current members and other local food processors, growers, and  producers in the State. 

The project will support four main D2C channels including Hope & Main’s onsite markets and other famers markets throughout Rhode Island e-commerce, two mid-tier value chain partners—the Farm Fresh RI Market Mobile program and Coastal Food Shed’s Virtual Market and the annual RI Tabletop Show.  Hope & Main is able to provide training and technical assistance that is targeted toward proven pathways to safely launch, scale, and de-risk small food businesses on their journey toward sustainability.
updated_description: Hope & Main’s project aims to bolster and expand direct-to-consumer marketing efforts for locally processed food products originating from a network of producers at Hope & Main, Rhode Island’s food business incubator. The project anticipates the participation of approximately 150 new food producers, with 40% expected to be involved in the food processing sector, alongside 100+ existing members and other local food processors, growers, and producers throughout the State. This initiative will strategically leverage four distinct direct-to-consumer channels, including Hope & Main’s onsite markets and engagement with other farmers markets across Rhode Island, a virtual market through Coastal Food Shed, and participation in the annual RI Tabletop Show. Furthermore, the project will utilize the Farm Fresh RI Market Mobile program as one of two mid-tier value chain partners. The anticipated outcome is the increased visibility and sales for these food products, supporting the growth of these businesses and the communities that produce them. Stakeholders, including farmers and consumers, will benefit from access to fresh, locally processed food. The project seeks to strengthen the local food system by connecting producers directly with consumers, ensuring the viability of these small businesses and promoting a robust marketplace for their products. The initiative supports the economic development of the region by facilitating direct sales and expanding market opportunities for these producers.

original_description:
Though the COVID-19 pandemic was highly challenging for small farmers and ranchers and our food systems overall, consumers found new reasons to see these producers as reliable sources of fresh foods. FRESHFARM is poised to innovate to meet the needs and opportunities of this post-pandemic food and economic landscape by: supporting increased economic sustainability for our more than 250 producers through farmers markets and farm stands; growing the customer base and loyalty for local food with promotion and education through at-market signage, video, our website, and loyalty programs; mobilizing new frontiers for market data with a sophisticated platform benefitting all producers in our network; and creating and sustaining vibrant direct producer-to-consumer outlets for
low-income/low-access communities.
updated_description: FRESHFARM is undertaking a project to bolster economic sustainability for a network of over 250 farmers and ranchers through established channels such as farmers markets and farm stands, while simultaneously cultivating increased customer bases and loyalty among consumers through targeted promotional and educational initiatives encompassing at-market signage, video content, the organization’s website, and loyalty programs. A key element of this project involves the development of a sophisticated data platform designed to benefit all producers within the FRESHFARM network, providing valuable market insights. The anticipated outcome of this work is the creation and maintenance of vibrant, direct producer-to-consumer outlets, with a specific focus on serving low-income/low-access communities. This initiative will directly support farmers and ranchers, and enable them to expand their reach and strengthen their businesses. Furthermore, FRESHFARM aims to foster stronger relationships between producers and consumers, building a loyal customer base. The project will also contribute to the expansion of market opportunities for producers, and the establishment of reliable supply chains. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers and ranchers themselves, as well as the consumers who will gain access to fresh, locally sourced food. The project is expected to strengthen the overall food system by providing a stable and accessible channel for producers to connect with their customers, and to build a more resilient and localized food supply.

original_description:
Butte County is burdened by some of the highest food insecurity rates in the state and nation, with nearly 31,300 residents in the rural Northern California county struggling with basic access to healthy food. At the same time, 98% of the food produced in the agriculturally‐rich county is sold out of the area, according to a 2022 assessment conducted by the Butte County Local Food Network. Though local need is strong, there are significant gaps constricting access to locally‐produced food.  The purpose is to increase access and availability of local fruits and vegetables to food insecure Butte County residents, Jesus Provides Our Daily Bread  seeks to develop and expand the capacity of its successful Harvesting Hope Community‐Supported Agriculture Program aka Harvesting Hope. The program currently serves Butte County residents with bi‐weekly local produce boxes, with much of the produce cultivated by individuals experiencing homelessness, through a holistic vocational training program
offered by the Jesus Center. Through this new effort, Harvesting Hope will expand infrastructure to launch a new retail access point for direct‐to consumer‐sales in a disadvantaged community, expand experiential vocational training serving beginning, underserved, and small farmers and drive increased consumption of local produce through new educational marketing efforts targeting food‐insecure consumers. Expected outcomes are 30 trained in small farm production practices and total annual sales beginning in Year 2 of $90,000, with intended beneficiaries the 1,000 individual consumers and 10 farms served by the new retail market access point and the 30 trained through experiential vocational training.
updated_description: Jesus Provides Our Daily Bread seeks to address significant food insecurity challenges within Butte County, California, a region experiencing some of the highest rates of food insecurity nationally. The project focuses on increasing access to locally produced fruits and vegetables by expanding the capacity of its successful Harvesting Hope Community-Supported Agriculture Program. Specifically, the project will establish a new retail access point for direct-to-consumer sales within a disadvantaged community, alongside efforts to increase the volume of local produce consumed. Anticipated outcomes include the training of 30 farmers in small farm production practices and the generation of approximately $90,000 in annual sales, commencing in Year 2. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative will be the 1,000 individual consumers and 10 farms served through the new retail market access point, alongside ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the local agricultural sector. Furthermore, the project will support the expansion of local food systems by connecting consumers directly with producers. The overall goal is to improve the availability of fresh produce for residents and bolster the viability of local agricultural operations within Butte County.

awardee_name: County of Riverside Office of Economic Development
original_description: This grant award is being requested by Riverside County Office of Economic Development in partnership with the Blythe Chamber of Commerce to improve the economic conditions of the agricultural producers in the underserved communities of Blythe and the Palo Verde Valley and their residents by developing, operating and expanding a direct producer to consumer Farmers’ Market, to improve access to and consumption of locally and regionally produced agricultural goods, provide critical business and marketing training programs to increase sales, retain existing jobs and create new jobs, respond to the climate crisis and water allocation cuts. A subaward will be granted to the Blythe Chamber of Commerce for outreach, recruitment and retention of producers, outreach, recruitment and retention of Farmers’ Market vendors, outreach, recruitment and retention of customers, management of Farmers’ Market administrative staff, weekly operations oversight of markets, electronic marketing and social media marketing, data collection and sharing with Project Director and local stakeholders and direct community engagement. The intended beneficiaries are the agricultural producers and residents of Blythe and the Palo Verde Valley areas. This grant award is critical to improving the economic outlook for the local economy.
updated_description: The Riverside County Office of Economic Development, in partnership with the Blythe Chamber of Commerce, is seeking a grant to improve the economic conditions for agricultural producers and residents within the Blythe and Palo Verde Valley areas. This project will establish and operate a direct producer-to-consumer Farmers’ Market, facilitating increased access to locally and regionally produced agricultural goods for farmers, ranchers, and processors. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened local economy through improved sales and retention of existing jobs, with the potential for creating new employment opportunities. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative are the farmers and ranchers of the Blythe and Palo Verde Valley regions, as well as the consumers who will have greater access to fresh agricultural products. The Riverside County Office of Economic Development will oversee the project, with the Blythe Chamber of Commerce handling outreach, recruitment and retention of producers, farmers’ market vendors, and customers, and managing administrative staff. This includes weekly market operations oversight, electronic marketing, and social media marketing efforts, alongside data collection and sharing with relevant stakeholders. Ultimately, the project aims to bolster the local economy by connecting agricultural producers directly with consumers seeking fresh goods.

awardee_name: San Luis Obispo County Community College District dba Cuesta
original_description:
Cuesta College will collaborate with local economic and food production stakeholders to provide a new direct-to-consumer market that supports underserved farmers and ranchers and provides expanded food access to residents. This project’s purpose is to address accessibility to local food and direct-to-consumer food systems and cultivate regional food economies through collaborative partnerships. Activities include a feasibility study, business development plan, and initial implementation for a new farmers' market in San Luis Obispo County. 
Cuesta College will initiate a sustainable, community-based enterprise with a triple bottom line – benefit to local producers (with additional support for underrepresented producers), local consumers with limited access to local food infrastructure, and community college students. The project’s projected impacts include expanded direct-to-consumer market opportunities for local farm and ranch operations, increased participation from underrepresented producers, and increased access to local food for community residents, particularly those living within or adjacent to the designated low-income/low-access area. Intended outcomes include one new direct producer-to-consumer market access point established, at least 50 producers reporting increased engagement with the new market, and a minimum of 100 new local agricultural product customers. 
Income from the market will help fund student employment at the market, introducing them to higher education and opportunities to study and pursue careers in agriculture that require training beyond high school.
updated_description: Cuesta College will establish a new direct-to-consumer market in San Luis Obispo County with the purpose of supporting local producers and expanding access to local food for community residents. This project will involve the creation of a sustainable enterprise focused on a triple bottom line – benefiting local farmers and ranchers, providing increased access to local food for consumers, and supporting student employment opportunities at the market. The anticipated outcomes include the establishment of one new market access point, with a minimum of 50 producers reporting increased engagement through the market, and a minimum of 100 new local agricultural product customers. This initiative will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors within the region, as well as community residents seeking access to fresh, local food. The project’s overall impact will be to strengthen regional food economies and provide a viable market channel for agricultural products. Cuesta College will operate this market to generate income to fund student employment positions, offering these students exposure to higher education and potential career paths within the agricultural sector. This market will serve as a crucial connection point for agricultural products and will contribute to the viability of local food businesses.

original_description: The purpose of the Greater Reedley Farm-To-Table Farmer's Market is to bring consumers face-to-face with farmers to increase consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables while also providing a low-barrier entry point for local farmers to sell produce. Market activities and deliverables are two 10-week markets annually (fall and spring) that will include 1) fresh fruit and/or vegetable vendors (local producers/vendors preferred); 2) food preparation demonstrations, allowing participants to observe the preparation of fresh fruit and vegetables and taste testing; 3) a demonstration and participation in a physical activity such as Zumba, yoga, pickle ball, etc. To increase Market attraction, vendors selling processed foods such as local honey, almonds, olive oil, roasted coffee, crafts booths, and local entertainment will also be included. Market activities are uniquely designed to increase the consumption of fresh produce as a strategy to address the high occurrence of obesity/diabetes in this geographically isolated area where rates are roughly 35%, which is significantly higher than California rates of only 25%.
updated_description: The Greater Reedley Farm-To-Table Farmer’s Market project aims to connect consumers directly with local farmers, thereby increasing the consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables within the community.
