updated_description: This project assesses the current state of our local food and farm network [LFFN] in four counties of Wisconsin’s Upper Fox River watershed – Marquette, Fond du Lac, Green Lake, and Winnebago – with the primary purpose of developing opportunities to improve farm-consumer relations and increase sales and consumption of local products. Recognizing significant challenges faced by producers, including a historically low return of just 14.5 cents per food dollar and a substantial agricultural carbon footprint, alongside consumer expectations for inexpensive, readily available food, this initiative seeks to strengthen the LFFN and make direct-to-consumer farms more economically sustainable. The anticipated outcomes include increased sales and consumption of local products, bolstered by improved connections between farmers and consumers. This will benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors within the network, allowing them to maintain operations and continue providing essential food and fiber. Ultimately, the project aims to support the viability of local food systems. The beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, and processors within the network, as well as consumers seeking locally sourced products. By addressing the current imbalances in the market and fostering stronger relationships, this project strives to ensure a more resilient and productive local food system.

original_description: Leprendo is dedicated to empowering small and mid-size farmers, particularly those in traditionally underserved communities throughout Southern California. Our mission is to overcome traditional economic barriers by directly connecting these farmers with consumers through the innovative use of the Leprendo online marketplace. This approach takes on a popular media format consumed by customers through short-form video formats (Tiktok, YouTube shorts, Instagram Reels). Initially focusing on Southern California, from the Central Valley to San Diego, we are set to enhance our platform's functionality and engage farmers through comprehensive digital marketing training. Collaborations with local micro-influencers will play a pivotal role, as they produce compelling short- form videos that showcase the unique stories and high-quality products of our farmers. This strategy is designed to drive consumer interest and sales, significantly boosting farmer visibility and market access. The project goals are: (1) develop online marketplace integrated w/ short-form video, (2) increased sales for farmers through online direct-to-consumer, (3) educating our farmers on short-form video marketplaces and online direct-to-consumer success, and (4) developing and implementing a logistical support system.
updated_description: Leprendo is dedicated to empowering small and mid-size farmers, particularly those in Southern California, by directly connecting them with consumers through an innovative online marketplace utilizing short-form video content on platforms such as TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels. The project’s purpose is to overcome traditional economic barriers faced by these farmers and to significantly increase their market access. Specifically, Leprendo will develop and implement an integrated online marketplace specifically designed to showcase farmer products through compelling video content. This initiative anticipates increased sales for farmers through direct-to-consumer channels and will establish a logistical support system to facilitate efficient operations. The anticipated outcomes include improved market visibility for farmers and a strengthened connection between producers and consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers throughout Southern California, alongside the consumers who will have access to high-quality agricultural products. Leprendo will also support processors and other key stakeholders within the agricultural supply chain. Through this approach, Leprendo aims to create a more accessible and robust market for agricultural goods, stimulating economic activity and providing opportunities for producers to thrive. The project’s ultimate goal is to bolster the agricultural sector by providing a dynamic platform for direct sales and fostering stronger relationships between producers and their customer base.

original_description:
Moon Valley Farm's (MVF) Year-Round Online Farmers Market (OFM) Expansion project will 
strategically grow our partnerships by 75+ regional producers, market them through storytelling and 
expand our delivery routes by thousands of new customers. The mission is to increase the capacity 
of our farm hub to collaborate with more farmers, sell to more local customers and to reach 
communities in low-income and low-access areas. To accomplish growing our farmer partnerships, we 
will collaborate with the Department of Agriculture of Frederick County and Beginner Farmer 
Training Programs run by two regional non-profits: Future Harvest and ECO City Farms to link with 
specialty crop growers who will benefit from additional sales outlets. Through investing in 
videography, photography, advertising and marketing funnels and by launching a new delivery route 
to 4 Mid-Atlantic cities: Baltimore, Maryland, Washington, DC, Frederick, Maryland and Northern 
Virginia, the OFM will provide a robust sales channel for producers and healthy local food to over 
5000 new customers.
The first objective of this project is to form partnerships with 75 or more new producers with a 
commitment that over half are socially-disadvantaged. To accomplish this, MVF will hire an 
Aggregation Manager to strategically form and cultivate new farm producer relationships by 
collaborating with the Office of Agriculture and non-profit organizations Future Harvest and ECO 
City Farms. Outside of this, the Aggregation Manager will onboard the new farmers by showcasing 
this opportunity to a wide pool of regional growers, field their questions and cultivate mutually 
beneficial partnerships. For long term proficiency and resilience, the Aggregation Manager will 
ensure the new farmers' logistics are streamlined and attended to, their products are food safe, in 
attractive packaging and that their farm operations and products are highlighted in our marketing. 
The second objective is to generate professional, evergreen marketing materials for the growers by 
contracting with graphic design, photography and videography professionals to capture their 
stories. Our marketing team will employ the collaborative strategies outlined in our marketing plan 
to engage our robust network of email subscribers and social media followers to expand this retail 
channel. We'll profile the new producers on our website, which boasted an impressive SEO score of 
97/100 in a 2023 digital audit to reach our 5000 unique visitors every month. The first 2 years of 
the project will capture the lives and stories of our network of farmers so that we can utilize 
these materials in targeted, optimized marketing campaigns and these will be utilized in a 
strategic advertising campaign to generate thousands of new leads across four cities.
updated_description: Moon Valley Farm’s Year-Round Online Farmers Market (OFM) Expansion project aims to significantly grow our producer network by over 75 regional farmers, expanding sales channels and reaching new customers through a robust online retail platform and expanded delivery routes. This project involves strategic partnerships with regional growers, including specialty crop producers, and the acquisition of professional marketing services such as graphic design, photography, and videography to create compelling narratives about these producers and their products. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is to serve over 5,000 new customers across four Mid-Atlantic cities – Baltimore, Maryland; Washington, DC; Frederick, Maryland; and Northern Virginia – while simultaneously bolstering the operations of these farmers. This project will benefit a wide range of stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, and food processors, by providing them with increased access to markets and supporting their ability to deliver high-quality products to consumers. Moon Valley Farm will develop targeted marketing campaigns to engage its established network of email subscribers and social media followers, leveraging a website with a high SEO score of 97/100, to drive traffic and generate leads for these producers. The initiative’s success will be measured by the increased volume of sales and the expansion of Moon Valley Farm’s reach within the selected geographic areas, supporting the livelihoods of participating farms and providing consumers with greater access to locally sourced food options.

original_description:
Locally Grown is an Uber Eats-style marketplace for small farms selling direct to consumers. Our mission is to simplify
marketing and operations for local producers by connecting them directly to their target market and providing a simple way to
manage orders and inventory. We currently support 50 farms in North Carolina and over 4,500 consumers.
This initiative is designed to generate $750,000 in total farmer revenue by expanding our capacity to onboard additional farms
up to our goal of 1,000 local U.S producers, and to attract 100,000 app downloads from consumers eager to support our farm
partners. This will be accomplished by adding marketplace features requested by many of our farm partners and applying
targeted marketing strategies to boost consumer engagement and subsequently farm revenues.
Key activities funded by this grant include enhancing technical resources, deploying new marketplace features like notifications
for past customers and localized promotions to help farmers reach their audience, and developing marketing materials to
promote our farm partners and attract new customers. These enhancements will increase the visibility of local farms and make
the buying process more accessible and efficient for consumers, contributing to a more connected local food system.
updated_description: Locally Grown’s purpose is to establish a streamlined marketplace connecting small farms directly with consumers, aiming to simplify operations for producers and facilitate a more efficient local food system. This initiative will involve the enhancement of technical resources, the deployment of new marketplace features such as notifications for past customers and localized promotions, and the development of targeted marketing materials to promote the participating farm partners and attract new customers. The anticipated outcomes include generating $750,000 in total farmer revenue by expanding the platform to accommodate up to 1,000 local U.S. producers, alongside attracting 100,000 app downloads from consumers eager to support these farm partners. These improvements will increase the visibility of local farms and make the buying process more accessible and efficient for consumers, benefiting farmers, ranchers, and other food producers. Specifically, the project seeks to bolster the capacity of the marketplace to support a broader network of local food businesses. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers who will gain access to a larger customer base and improved operational efficiencies, as well as the consumers who will have increased access to fresh, locally sourced products. Ultimately, this will strengthen the local food ecosystem and provide a valuable channel for producers to connect with their target markets, contributing to a more robust and connected food system for all stakeholders.

original_description:
This project will equip local producers with the knowledge, practical experience, and continued guidance needed to successfully market, sell, and scale their agricultural products at Farmers Markets. This four-month program will be offered twice a year, with each session enrolling a cohort of 10 producers, four of whom will be producers with 0-1 years of experience in markets. The program will be delivered through online gatherings, in-person workshops, mentoring, and peer-to-peer support offered in three phases: Farmers Market Foundations, Farmers Market Success, and Farmers Market Longevity. In addition, a Farmers Market 101 workshop will be offered monthly and open to the public.During the pilot of the program we will focus on beneficiaries associated with the Moreno Valley Market, Rancho Cucamonga Market, or Chino Hills Market, 67% of whom are POC. The ongoing evaluation of this program will measure business and profit growth for producers, increases in the quality and customer engagement of markets supporting the local community, and decreases in retail- level and consumer-level food waste. At the conclusion of this project, each participant will have:
-Certifications, equipment, and permits for operating as a vendor -An identifiable brand, marketing strategy, and social media content calendar -In-person marketing strategies for increasing customer engagement -business evaluation systems, and -A step-by-step plan to expand their business to additional markets
updated_description: This project aims to empower local producers to successfully operate and expand their agricultural businesses through participation in Farmers Markets. The program, delivered twice annually with each session enrolling ten producers, will consist of three phases – Farmers Market Foundations, Farmers Market Success, and Farmers Market Longevity – incorporating online gatherings, in-person workshops, and peer-to-peer support. Each participant will receive certifications, equipment, and necessary permits to operate as a vendor, alongside the development of an identifiable brand, a targeted marketing strategy, and a social media content calendar. Furthermore, producers will gain access to in-person marketing strategies designed to increase customer engagement and will establish business evaluation systems, alongside a step-by-step plan for expanding their business to additional markets. The program will focus on supporting a group of farmers, ranchers, and processors who will benefit from increased sales and improved market access. Specifically, the project will support the growth of producers participating in the Moreno Valley Market, Rancho Cucamonga Market, and Chino Hills Market. The anticipated outcomes include measurable business and profit growth for these producers, and a heightened quality and customer engagement within the markets themselves. The project will ultimately contribute to reduced levels of food waste at the retail and consumer levels. The goal is to equip these stakeholders with the tools and knowledge needed to strengthen their market presence and enhance their overall business operations.

original_description: The City of Torrance, California requests $157,628.35 to implement the Torrance Farmers' Market - Service for Seniors project. The project will improve the Market's accessibility and reach through a distribution program targeted at senior citizens, residents with disabilities, and all others facing mobility obstacles which prevent them from navigating the busy Marketplace. Participating residents will receive pre-boxed, assorted fresh produce packages at public distribution sites strategically located throughout the City, allowing them ease of access to local grown food while still engaging with their local community on a frequent basis. Produce packages will include carefully chosen, diverse products along with recipe cards including ingredients from the package, promoting culinary education and widening participants' food experiences. The program is expected to increase Market usage and sales by 6%. This project will additionally benefit Torrance's local farmers and ranchers who utilize the Market, providing them with wider distribution opportunities to their customer base and allowing them to strategize on food products to include in the boxes, in order to minimize produce waste and promote new, unique, or surplus produce. Market staff will work closely with supplying producers and program recipients to improve producer-to-consumer operations, ensuring that Torrance's senior community has access to healthy, fresh, locally grown produce.
updated_description: The City of Torrance requests $157,628.35 to implement the Torrance Farmers’ Market – Service for Seniors project, a comprehensive initiative designed to enhance access to fresh, locally grown produce for a key segment of the community. This project will establish a distribution program specifically targeting senior citizens, residents with mobility challenges, and individuals facing obstacles preventing them from easily navigating the Torrance Farmers’ Market. Through strategically located public distribution sites, participants will receive pre-boxed packages of assorted fresh produce, allowing for convenient access to locally sourced food and continued engagement within their community. These carefully curated packages will include a selection of produce chosen in collaboration with supplying producers, alongside recipe cards that utilize ingredients from the boxes, promoting culinary exploration and broadening consumer food experiences. The anticipated outcome of this project is an increase of 6% in Market usage and sales, benefiting Torrance’s local farmers and ranchers by expanding their distribution networks and allowing for strategic planning regarding product offerings to minimize waste. The project will facilitate improved producer-to-consumer operations, ensuring that stakeholders have access to healthy, fresh produce. Ultimately, this initiative will provide a valuable service to the Torrance community, supporting local agricultural businesses and expanding access to nutritious food options for a significant population group.

original_description: The Tukwila Village Farmers Market (Tukwila Village) provides important food access to Low Income/Low Food Access (LI/LA) communities in Tukwila, Washington. The market was founded in 2017 to specifically support entry-level immigrant, refugee, and BIPOC vendors, support customers to use food benefits, and to create a unique and welcoming market space for the diverse community. Tukwila Village was co-founded by Global to Local's Food Innovation Network and International Rescue Committee's New Roots Program, with ongoing technical assistance provided by Public Health - Seattle & King County. This project will support Tukwila Village in strategically increasing their customers, vendors, and operational capacity. To accomplish this, they will conduct community outreach to assess needs and desires, revamp their promotional activity, restructure their market's incentive program (Heart Bucks), conduct targeted recruitment to diversify the vendors, develop a volunteer program, and complete a strategic plan. Through this project, Tukwila Village will be able to grow to a new level to support more vendors and customers in accessing fresh, local, cultural produce.
updated_description: Tukwila Village Farmers Market is undertaking a strategic project to expand its reach and impact within the Tukwila community. This initiative will focus on increasing customer numbers, attracting a broader range of vendors, and enhancing the market’s operational capacity, aiming to bolster access to fresh, local produce. The core of this project involves several key activities, including conducting community outreach to understand customer and stakeholder needs, redesigning promotional efforts, and restructuring the Heart Bucks incentive program to encourage market participation. Furthermore, the market will implement targeted recruitment strategies to broaden the selection of vendors and establish a volunteer program to support daily operations. Through these efforts, Tukwila Village anticipates a measurable increase in the number of individuals benefiting from the market, including farmers, ranchers, and processors who supply goods, alongside a corresponding growth in the number of consumers accessing fresh produce. The overall outcome will be a strengthened market that effectively serves the community, providing a central location for purchasing local food products. This expansion is intended to directly support those seeking access to a variety of food options, and the market’s growth will contribute to a more robust local food system within the Tukwila area.

original_description:
The Jacksonville Farmers Market (JFM), North Florida's oldest and largest operating farmers market, is
grappling with a significant decline in vendors, customers, and overall vibrancy. Despite being situated
in a USDA Priority Area, the market has lost its prominence as a primary food source for the
community.
The current landowner approached Feeding Northeast Florida (FNEFL) to assume management of the
Jacksonville Market. With prompting and support from the City, we are exploring how best to revitalize
the market that benefits both consumers and local food producers. FNEFL's objective is to boost the
involvement of local food producers and restore the market's prominence as a leading sales venue in
the region. By collaborating strategically with community partners, the JFM can expand market access,
aggregation, and distribution channels for small and medium-sized producers.
FNEFL is seeking a grant to develop a comprehensive business and management plan in preparation
for assuming operational control. FNEFL will enlist the expertise of a consultant to devise a phased
implementation process to reestablish the market as a primary sales outlet. We recognize that our
plans remain contingent on input from our neighbors, farmers, food producers, and regional
stakeholders, and we stand to listen and learn from people and families who will frequent this space to
ensure the market reflects their preferences and requirements.
updated_description: The Jacksonville Farmers Market, North Florida’s oldest and largest operating market, is undertaking a project to address a significant decline in vendors, customers, and overall vibrancy despite its location in a USDA Priority Area. Feeding Northeast Florida (FNEFL) is seeking a grant to develop a comprehensive business and management plan in preparation for assuming operational control of the market, with the intent of boosting the involvement of local food producers and restoring the market’s prominence as a leading sales venue in the region. This initiative will focus on expanding market access, aggregation, and distribution channels for small and medium-sized producers, including farmers, ranchers, and processors, ultimately benefiting the community by providing a central location for these entities to sell their goods. The anticipated outcome is a revitalized market capable of supporting increased sales volume and strengthening connections between producers and consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the local food producers and the consumers who rely on access to fresh, locally sourced products. FNEFL intends to implement a phased approach, utilizing a consultant’s expertise, to ensure the market’s successful reestablishment as a key sales outlet. This will involve closely listening to and incorporating feedback from stakeholders to tailor the market’s offerings and operations to meet the preferences and requirements of the community, fostering a thriving environment for local food production and consumption.

original_description:
Schenectady Greenmarket's project aims to foster diversity among market vendors and customers through recruitment,
outreach, and retention strategies, with a focus on historically underserved populations. It seeks to support historically
underserved producers by providing resources such as a Vendor Success Toolkit and small business trainings, facilitated
by the Community Loan Fund. Additionally, mentorship opportunities will be offered by senior vendors to new vendors to
refine their marketing strategies. The project also intends to create an inclusive environment by expanding the market’s
Food Box Program and increasing marketing and outreach efforts to low-income and socially disadvantaged community
members. Expansion of the Food Box Program will provide additional revenue streams for local producers and increased
access to fresh, affordable foods for low-income Schenectady residents. Collaboration with community partners like Soul
Fire Farm will enhance awareness and accessibility of the Food Box Program and other market services among low-income
communities, while also supporting the market in increasing customer diversity through educational food demonstrations
and workshops highlighting culturally significant foods. Overall, these efforts aim to support the success and sustainability of
historically underserved producers, increase vendor and customer diversity within the market space, and improve access to
local foods for low-income residents._x000D_
updated_description: Schenectady Greenmarket’s project is designed to strengthen the market’s producer network and expand access to local food sources within the Schenectady community. The core of this initiative involves providing resources to support local producers, including a Vendor Success Toolkit, and fostering connections through mentorship opportunities facilitated by experienced vendors. A key component is the expansion of the Food Box Program, intended to create additional revenue streams for participating farmers and ranchers, while simultaneously increasing the availability of fresh produce for low-income consumers. Collaboration with organizations like Soul Fire Farm will bolster awareness and accessibility of these services among targeted stakeholders. Furthermore, Schenectady Greenmarket will focus on enhancing the market environment to promote greater participation from a wide range of consumers, and to ensure the long-term viability of local agricultural businesses. The anticipated outcomes include a more robust producer base and expanded access to fresh foods for residents. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass local producers, consumers, and related stakeholders within the Schenectady area. Ultimately, this effort seeks to support the continued operation of the market and to provide essential resources to those involved in the local food system.

original_description:
This project will improve food access for refugees and low-income residents in the Mountain View and Muldoon neighborhoods of East Anchorage by supporting multiple food access channels through Catholic Social Services' Refugee Assistance and Immigration Services (RAIS) program, aligning with the Farmers Market Promotion Program's "Capacity Building" focus.
Our objectives for this project include 1) To create a food access hub at Grow North Farm through the coordination of a CSA, roadside stand, and farmers market. Our current program conducts limited outreach to nearby residents despite our ability to provide discounts for nutritional assistance recipients, which is something that we plan to expand.2)  We will assist beginner refugee farmers with selling their produce through various sales channels - CSA, farmers markets, wholesale, etc.  3)  We will expand our value-added goods program to promote increased earning potential for refugee farmers. Our current value-added goods program needs strategic business planning to ensure long-term sustainability. We will equip refugees with skills to create value-added products and foster entrepreneurship. Refugee entrepreneurs face significant barriers in starting businesses and accessing markets such as language barriers and unfamiliar regulations. 4) We will develop a strategic plan to expand and operate the Muldoon Farmers Market. This long-standing community farmers market in a low-income area of Anchorage is at risk of closing.
updated_description: Catholic Social Services’ Refugee Assistance and Immigration Services (RAIS) is undertaking a project to enhance food access for farmers, consumers, and stakeholders within the Mountain View and Muldoon neighborhoods of East Anchorage. This initiative will establish a multi-channel food access hub centered at Grow North Farm, integrating a Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program, a roadside stand, and a farmers market to directly connect producers with buyers. Simultaneously, the project will support beginning refugee farmers in selling their produce through various sales channels, including direct sales and wholesale opportunities, and expand a value-added goods program designed to increase earning potential for these producers. A key component of the project is the development of a strategic plan to ensure the continued operation of the Muldoon Farmers Market, a vital resource for the community. By facilitating the sale of fresh produce and the creation of processed food items, the project anticipates increased availability of food options for residents in the targeted neighborhoods. The project’s success hinges on supporting these farmers as they navigate the process of bringing their products to market, with an emphasis on building sustainable business practices and expanding market reach. Ultimately, this work will contribute to improved food security for the community members who rely on these direct-to-consumer food systems.

original_description: Northwest Agriculture Business Center seeks to contribute towards breaking down barriers to economic success, and meet USDA objectives to develop, coordinate, and expand direct producer-to-consumer marketing and strategies for local producers to enhance existing market channels and develop new revenue opportunities. Through this project, our organization will facilitate expansion of existing markets via the Genuine Skagit Valley program’s Farmstand Fresh and other promotional campaigns. Consumers will be drawn to Skagit County and surrounding communities through promotion of agritourism activities and farm stand products through paid advertising, social media, website links, and cross-promotion partnerships and collaborations.  Consumers will be encouraged to favor Skagit farm products in buying choices, as identified by the Genuine Skagit Valley certification mark.  Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) transaction education will introduce the opportunity of new markets and consumer segments to farm stand operators, with access to governmental entity resources and enrollment technical assistance. Program participation will be improved through farmer outreach. Barriers to program benefits for non-English speaking Latinx producers will be lowered through translation and interpretation of promotional toolkit and other materials into Spanish, and by working with producers to improve culturally relevant pathways to participation.
updated_description: Northwest Agriculture Business Center seeks to advance economic opportunities for farmers and stimulate consumer interest in local agricultural products. This project focuses on expanding existing market channels and creating new revenue streams for producers within Skagit County and surrounding communities through initiatives like the Genuine Skagit Valley program’s Farmstand Fresh campaign and associated promotional activities. The project will utilize paid advertising, social media engagement, website links, and strategic collaborations to draw consumers to the region, encouraging a preference for Skagit farm products identified by the Genuine Skagit Valley certification mark. A key component involves educating farm stand operators about Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) transactions, providing them with access to relevant governmental resources and enrollment technical assistance. To maximize participation, the organization will conduct targeted outreach to farmers, and crucially, will address language barriers for Latinx producers by translating promotional materials and providing interpretation services. This will facilitate culturally relevant pathways to program benefits. The anticipated outcome is an increase in sales for participating producers and a broadened consumer base for Skagit County agricultural goods. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the agricultural sector, as well as consumers who will have increased access to locally produced food items. Ultimately, the project aims to strengthen the local food system and promote economic viability for agricultural businesses within the region.

original_description: To meet the surging demand for affordable and accessible food during the pandemic, CJ formed the Produce Buyers Club by building a coalition of Atlanta nonprofits serving low-income, low-access (LILA) communities to purchase and distribute Georgia farmers' surplus produce. With our ongoing efforts, a significant portion of this market remains untapped.
updated_description: CJ’s Produce Buyers Club is designed to address the demand for accessible food sources within Atlanta’s low-income, low-access communities. The project focuses on building a coalition of Atlanta nonprofits to purchase surplus produce from Georgia farmers and ranchers. This initiative anticipates a significant expansion of the market for agricultural products, connecting these producers directly with consumers seeking fresh food options. The core of the project involves facilitating the efficient distribution of agricultural goods, with the goal of reducing waste and ensuring a reliable supply of produce to communities facing limited access. Ultimately, the Produce Buyers Club will benefit farmers by providing a channel to sell their excess inventory, and consumers will gain access to a consistent supply of fresh food. The project aims to strengthen the relationships between agricultural stakeholders and the communities they serve, creating a more robust and resilient food system.

original_description:
The proposed initiative aims to provide new markets for local produce farms and wider access to their produce for residents
of at least three underserved neighborhoods in South Jersey by operating weekly farmers markets in areas that have not
been able to sustain commercial farmers markets in the past. The core objective is to connect more local and hyper-local
growers with more underserved consumers, to the benefit of both. Our premise is that nonprofits can facilitate markets that
are financially worthwhile for growers while providing access to produce at prices low-income residents can afford.
The collaborating farms and nonprofits will work with additional local growers to aggregate and transport produce from rural
and urban growers and sell the produce through at least three farmers market stands at prices each neighborhood can
support, including but not limited to consumers using SNAP and other benefit programs. Through experience and customer
surveys, we will learn about the produce varieties, pricing, presentation and food education services that can sustain each
market into the future. By serving as anchor stands and demonstrating the methods that make each location economically
successful, the initiative aims to recruit additional farmers (in addition to Rancocas Creek Farm) and individual retailers to
join each site. The proposed grant will enable the collaborating farms and nonprofits to work with at least nine additional
growers and create at least three markets. Over the two-year grant period, we will develop business plans based on local
experience to sustain each market into the future.
updated_description: The Rancocas Creek Farm initiative aims to establish weekly farmers markets in three specific areas of South Jersey, fostering connections between local growers and consumers. This project will purchase necessary supplies and equipment to operate these markets, focusing on aggregating produce from multiple growers, including Rancocas Creek Farm and nine additional farmers and retailers, and transporting it to the market stands. The anticipated outcome is the creation of sustainable markets that provide access to fresh produce for residents, with the goal of supporting the economic viability of the participating growers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include local farmers, ranchers, and processors, as well as the consumers in these communities. The project will develop business plans based on local experience, ensuring the long-term success of each market and encouraging further participation from additional stakeholders. By creating these markets, the project intends to provide access to a variety of produce at prices suitable for the target consumers, facilitating transactions utilizing benefit programs. The project seeks to demonstrate successful market operations, with the goal of attracting additional growers and retailers to join each site, further expanding the supply of produce available to the communities. Through careful planning and operation, the initiative strives to build a dependable source of fresh food for residents of these areas, promoting a direct link between producers and consumers.

original_description:
This project will leverage community resources for enhancing the grower-consumer relationship at the Main Street Market of Tyndall. The project will support a local market for growers and consumers. Project work includes regular food demonstration
meals held at area venues to promote local products.  The market will serve a a venue for a Community Supported Agriculture 'food box subscription' program that establishes season-long sales demand for growers. The project will also work with the local school system to create age-appropriate programs that explain all aspects of the local food market.
updated_description: The Main Street Market project aims to strengthen the connection between growers and consumers at the Tyndall market by fostering a local market environment. This project will support the sale of local products through regular food demonstration meals held at various locations, designed to promote the offerings of area farmers and ranchers. A key component of the project will be the implementation of a Community Supported Agriculture ‘food box subscription’ program, establishing consistent seasonal sales demand for participating growers. Furthermore, the project will collaborate with the local school system to develop educational programs about the local food market, tailored for different age groups. The anticipated outcome is a thriving market with increased sales volume for growers and enhanced consumer awareness of locally produced goods. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of local food. By creating a more direct channel between producers and consumers, the project seeks to build a robust and sustainable market system within the Tyndall area, ultimately resulting in increased access to fresh, locally-sourced food options.

original_description: The intent of this FMPP proposal is to connect, coordinate and cultivate our local food economy through public-private partnerships to create a new International Farmers Market in West Boise. This new direct producer-to-consumer market will increase the capacity of our local food system and expand mid-tier value chains. It will create a new fresh food resource in an economically diverse LI-LA neighborhood and expand economic opportunities for small acreage producers of ethnic produce.  Global Lounge, a multi-cultural enterprise, will add coordination, volunteers, entertainment, and food vendors. Activities include planning, supporting partnerships, marketing, and adding structure including vendor agreements, staffing, operations, and technology. Effectively incorporating technology for sales will be supported by a consultant from the Boise Farmers Market. The farmers will have an active role in shaping a culturally rich marketplace and new access point for sales.  Global Gardens refugee farmers will gain an alternative to large up-scale markets where their profits are lower than their investment. The LI-LA community will have a new opportunity to access fresh, local, and ethnic varieties, and increase fresh food consumption. Strong community participation, and increased sales for farmers will result. It will allow farmers to pilot new value-added products. Deliverables will record farmer adaptation to technology, marketing materials, data on sales and customer traffic.
updated_description: Global Lounge proposes the creation of a new International Farmers Market in West Boise to connect and strengthen the local food economy through public-private partnerships. This initiative will establish a direct producer-to-consumer market, significantly increasing the capacity of the regional food system and fostering the development of mid-tier value chains. The project encompasses planning, partnership support, marketing activities, and the implementation of operational structures, including vendor agreements and technology integration, with guidance from a consultant specializing in market sales. Anticipated outcomes include increased sales for farmers, allowing them to pilot new value-added products, and providing consumers with access to a fresh food resource within the LI-LA community. Key beneficiaries of this market will be farmers, ranchers, and processors who will benefit from expanded sales opportunities. The market will also serve a broader consumer base seeking access to fresh produce, and will enhance the availability of ethnic varieties. Specifically, Global Lounge aims to support the Global Gardens refugee farmers by offering an alternative to larger markets where their profits are often lower than their initial investment. The project will track farmer adaptation to technology and capture data on sales and customer traffic as key deliverables. Furthermore, the market will contribute to a stronger local food economy and support the growth of the regional food system.

original_description:
Since 2008, Catholic Charities of Northeast Kansas, in partnership with Cultivate KC, has managed the New Roots program, a 4-year farmer training program and incubator farm for refugees and immigrants with agricultural backgrounds who wish to launch their own small farm businesses. Forty six families have graduated from the program (32 of which are still actively farming in the area), and approximately 12 families are in the 4-year training program each year. Both organizations are committed to growing the program. Through many years of experience and with the input of program participants, we have built a strong program emphasizing participatory education, language access, equity, self- sufficiency, and graduate success. Though participants have a wealth of agricultural experience, marketing and expanding sales continue to be a challenge due to language and cultural barriers, amongst other factors.
Additionally, the local community lacks consistent and convenient access to fresh produce. “New Roots Marketing and Sales Expansion to Support Farmers with Language Barriers in Kansas City” aims to address these challenges by increasing opportunities for the community to access fresh, local produce while expanding farmers' sales through a variety of avenues and increasing the number of new farmers in Kansas City.
updated_description: Catholic Charities of Northeast Kansas, in partnership with Cultivate KC, is undertaking a project to increase access to fresh produce within the Kansas City community while simultaneously expanding sales opportunities for farmers. This initiative will focus on establishing various avenues for farmers to connect with consumers, including direct producer-to-retail channels, and direct producer-to-restaurant connections, aiming to improve the flow of goods from agricultural producers to the public. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened local food system, providing greater access to fresh produce for consumers and increased revenue streams for farmers. Specifically, the project will support farmers in their efforts to market and sell their products, addressing challenges related to language and cultural factors that have historically limited their reach. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers participating in the New Roots program, as well as the local consumers seeking fresh, locally sourced food. Furthermore, the project intends to strengthen the overall food system by connecting agricultural producers with potential buyers, supporting a broader range of stakeholders involved in the food supply chain. The project will ultimately contribute to a more robust local food network, creating new opportunities for farmers to sustain their businesses and for the community to benefit from locally grown agricultural products.

original_description: The Ivanhoe Farmers Market, in partnership with Kansas City Black Urban Growers, will utilize USDA Farmers Market Promotion Program funds to strengthen the capacity of a crucial direct-to-consumer farmers market operation within the local food system, support food producers in the development of marketing strategies that are culturally and technologically relevant, and drive access and consumption of locally produced agriculture products. In alignment with key project goals and identified objectives of the FMPP, the collaborative partnership and probetween the two community-based organizations will drive the following outcomes: an increase in community engagement in the local food economy, an increase of upward mobility opportunity for local producers, and an increase in the local food consumption. The successful expansion of market operations, awareness of fresh, locally grown foods producers, and the training and development of minority, urban farmers will create significantly more direct to-consumer sales that benefit both the small, historically underserved producers and an urban community facing food insecurity.
updated_description: The Ivanhoe Farmers Market, in partnership with Kansas City Black Urban Growers, will implement a project utilizing funds to strengthen a direct-to-consumer farmers market operation within the local food system, focusing on supporting producers in the development of marketing strategies relevant to their operations. This initiative will drive increased access and consumption of locally produced agricultural products, aiming to enhance the overall local food economy. The project anticipates several key outcomes, including heightened community engagement with the local food system, and increased economic opportunities for agricultural producers. Specifically, the project will facilitate greater direct sales between producers and consumers, supporting the growth of agricultural businesses. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the local agricultural sector, as well as consumers seeking access to fresh food. The project’s success will be measured by an increase in sales volume and a broader reach of locally sourced agricultural goods. Ultimately, the project intends to stimulate greater economic activity within the local food system, benefiting those involved in its production and distribution, and supporting those seeking access to a variety of fresh food options.

original_description: This project will develop and expand the capacity of a successful Farmers Market and Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program to operate year-round. The result will be increased revenue for local farmers and improved access and availability of healthy foods for an underserved community. St. Luke's Episcopal Church, located in the heart of downtown Jamestown, NY, oversees the Jamestown Public Market, a vibrant program that has operated in the area for over 100 years. Currently running from June-October, the initiative includes a weekly outdoor farmers market and the Eat Fresh, Do Good CSA. In response to a growing push from farmers and consumers, this project will launch an extended direct-to-consumer-sales schedule by adding winter and spring CSAs as well as an indoor farmers market in the offseason. Like the current programming, SNAP and the Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program will be accepted. This project will help develop new product offerings, and retain customers and farmer vendors, including at least two historically underserved producers. Free training for farmers will be offered in partnership with Cornell Cooperative Extension in Chautauqua County and will include education on business, marketing, and the development of value-added agricultural products. Targeted outreach to people in Jamestown's low-income households and food desert neighborhoods will help ensure that the expanded programming is accessed by the community members who need it most.
updated_description: St. Luke’s Episcopal Church is undertaking a project to expand the Jamestown Public Market, a successful farmers market and Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program, to operate year-round, aiming to increase revenue for local farmers and improve access to healthy foods for the community. This initiative will encompass the development of new product offerings, including expanded seasonal CSAs for spring and winter, alongside an indoor farmers market during the off-season, ensuring a continuous supply of fresh produce and other agricultural products. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened market presence for local farmers and increased food availability for consumers, with a particular focus on retaining existing vendors and attracting at least two historically limited-access producers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers participating in the market and the consumers seeking locally-sourced food options. The project will concentrate on reaching individuals within Jamestown, particularly those in lower-income households and areas with limited access to fresh food. This expansion will support a broader range of agricultural stakeholders by providing them with new sales channels and market opportunities. The goal is to create a more robust and reliable market system that can meet the demands of the community throughout the year, bolstering the economic viability of local farms and ensuring a consistent supply of fresh, locally-grown food for residents.

original_description: The purpose of the project is to collect key indoor farmers market facility and stall design needs and specifications from 20 interested Fulton Stall Market farmers and producers. After design needs and specifications are identified, a farmer- focused architectural design plan will be created, and a financial proforma and business plan developed for the Seaport Public Market, a multi-vendor indoor farmers market in Lower Manhattan. The intended beneficiaries are participating New York and regional farmers, consumers, low-income residents of adjacent Lower East Side and Chinatown neighborhoods served by Fulton Stall Market. Also, this project will benefit the economy and social vitality of Lower Manhattan harmed by 9/11, Hurricane Sandy, and COVID-19 pandemic
updated_description: The purpose of this project is to gather essential indoor farmers market facility and stall design needs and specifications from twenty interested Fulton Stall Market farmers and producers. Following this initial data collection, a farmer-focused architectural design plan will be created, alongside the development of a comprehensive financial proforma and business plan specifically tailored for the Seaport Public Market, a multi-vendor indoor farmers market situated in Lower Manhattan. Anticipated outcomes include a detailed design plan that directly addresses the operational requirements of participating farmers and producers, coupled with a robust financial roadmap for the market’s establishment and sustained operation. The project will benefit farmers, producers, consumers, and other stakeholders within the Lower Manhattan region, contributing to the economic and social vitality of the area, which has been impacted by various events including 9/11, Hurricane Sandy, and the COVID-19 pandemic. original_description: Nourish Knoxville’s (NK) Digging Deeper project will help bridge the gap between producers’ need for more direct-to-consumer market opportunities and buyers’ increasing interest in local food. The project will enlist marketing professionals, producers, buyers, and seven partnering organizations to develop and promote a marketing campaign with impactful, user-friendly, accessible resources to connect the East Tennessee local food system. NK will overhaul their printed local food directory into an agritourism-focused local food guide that will expand to cover 36 counties with a combined population of 2.5 million. Concurrently, NK will launch the online East Tennessee Local Food Guide, offering user-specific gateways to find agritourist experiences with maps and farm trails, wholesale providers, CSAs, restaurants and stores featuring local foods, local artisanal food producers, and farmers markets. NK and its partners across the region will actively promote registrations into and use of both guides to their networks and the public; partners will receive subawards for their efforts. By 2027, the project will provide 30,000 print copies to 190 locations, inform 1,300 producer beneficiaries about new market opportunities, promote over 300 producer beneficiaries, and provide local food information to 58,000 East Tennesseans. Digging Deeper will increase producers’ economic opportunities, increase access to local food, and strengthen the capacity of our regional local food network.

original_description:
The "CSA for All: Strategic Marketing for Equitable CSA Expansion" project is set to redefine Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) by enhancing its inclusivity and accessibility. Historically, CSA programs have predominantly attracted white, English-speaking, middle-class participants. This initiative seeks to broaden the CSA landscape, offering more opportunities for both farmers and consumers from diverse backgrounds to engage with CSA. Utilizing the national CSA Innovation Network (CSA-IN), the project will employ equity-focused strategies in CSA marketing and technical assistance.

Key steps include assessing innovative CSA models that prioritize equity and food access, conducting a national survey to gauge the values and preferences of CSA members from various demographics, and emphasizing farmer input through a Farmer Advisory Committee and listening sessions. This research will guide the creation of national marketing campaigns and multilingual materials, designed to highlight CSA benefits to a diverse audience, thereby boosting support for local farms and promoting a more inclusive CSA community.

Finally, the CSA-IN will leverage its robust platform of ideas sharing both internally and externally to share outcomes and resources from this proposal. Through its national scope and emphasis on inclusion, the project aims to transform the CSA model into a cornerstone of local food systems that truly serves all members of the community.
updated_description: The “CSA for All: Strategic Marketing for Equitable CSA Expansion” project seeks to transform Community Supported Agriculture by expanding its reach and accessibility to a broader range of participants. This initiative, utilizing the national CSA Innovation Network (CSA-IN), will focus on developing and implementing equity-focused marketing strategies and technical assistance to address the historically limited demographic engagement within CSA programs. Specifically, the project will assess innovative CSA models that prioritize food access and conduct a national survey to understand the values and preferences of farmers and consumers. The research findings will guide the creation of national marketing campaigns and multilingual materials, designed to highlight the benefits of CSA to a wider audience, thereby increasing support for local farms. A Farmer Advisory Committee and listening sessions will ensure farmer input is central to the development process. The anticipated outcome is a more inclusive CSA community, supported by increased participation from various stakeholders. This project will benefit farmers by expanding market opportunities and promoting local food systems. It will also provide consumers with increased access to fresh, local produce. The CSA-IN will share project outcomes and resources internally and externally. The project’s success will be measured by increased participation rates across various demographic groups, and by the wider adoption of inclusive CSA models.

original_description: Western Kentucky University, Need More Acres Farm, Foundation for Connecting Communities, Community Farmers Market, SoKY Farmers Market, with other three participating farmers markets have established a MORE Partnership with a primary purpose to increase Market Opportunities, Reinforce and Expand (MORE) regional farmers markets and other direct and indirect producer-to-consumer market outlets. Specific objectives are to (a) leverage partnership's previous field-based expertise, resources, and network capital for local growers to access more market opportunities for locally-produced agricultural products, (b) augment sales of locally grown agricultural products particularly among socially disadvantaged local growers, (c) reinforce previously supported farmers markets and extend outreach efforts to "more" markets in the region, (d) expand awareness, access, and consumption of locally grown agricultural products among communities of color, seniors, pregnant women and nursing moms, including vulnerable minor parents. With these objectives, MORE Partnership aligns with the 2024 FMPP's purpose of funding projects that develop, coordinate, and expand direct producer-to-consumer markets to help increase access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. Major expected outcomes include increased local farm revenues by at least 25 percent and expanded awareness, access, and consumption of local agricultural products by at least 35 percent.
updated_description: Western Kentucky University, in partnership with Need More Acres Farm, the Foundation for Connecting Communities, the Community Farmers Market, SoKY Farmers Market, and other participating farmers markets, has established a MORE Partnership with the primary purpose of increasing Market Opportunities for local producers. The core beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers involved in producing these goods, alongside the consumers who will have increased access to fresh, locally sourced food. Specifically, the MORE Partnership aims to connect these stakeholders with greater market reach and facilitate the distribution of agricultural products to a wider customer base. The project seeks to support the growth of the local agricultural sector by ensuring that producers have the resources and connections needed to successfully sell their products, ultimately leading to enhanced economic opportunities for those involved in food production.

original_description:
The Food Finance Institute (FFI) is proposing a four-part program that will train and support 100 DTC farmers to understand key sales, business, and financial management systems that will result in increased sales and profitability. In addition, 20 farm finance consultants will be trained to better support their network of DTC farmers within their communities. The program targets both early career and growth stage DTC farmers through four core objectives:

Improve fundamental financial management skills and costs of sales through Farm Finance Foundations training
Advance financial acumen to access capital to diversify and expand sales through Farm Finance Intensive training
Connect DTC farmer peers to improve financial and sales management confidence through peer-to-peer learning circles
Support DTC farmers throughout business stages with Farm Consultant Training, Monthly Meet Ups and Office Hours
As a result 100 DTC farmers will have improved financial skills, carefully priced products in targeted DTC channels that ensure profitability, and increased access to capital to implement DTC growth strategies. 20 consultants will have increase financial and sales management skills to support DTC farmers in their network and three Business Model Optimization Reports will be published to showcase DTC local farmer financial and sales benchmarks and business model successes.
updated_description: The Food Finance Institute is proposing a comprehensive program designed to bolster the financial capabilities of direct-to-consumer farmers and their supporting consultants. This initiative will directly support 100 farmers engaged in direct producer-to-retail activities, alongside 20 farm finance consultants, equipping them with the necessary skills to improve sales and profitability. The core of the program involves enhancing fundamental financial management practices and costs of sales, alongside advancing financial acumen to facilitate access to capital for strategic growth within DTC channels. Specifically, the project will foster peer-to-peer learning circles among farmers, and provide ongoing support through monthly meetings and dedicated office hours. As a result, farmers will be able to carefully price their products to ensure profitability and secure capital for implementing DTC expansion strategies. Furthermore, the 20 farm finance consultants will gain strengthened financial and sales management expertise, enabling them to better support their network of farmers. The culmination of this program will yield three Business Model Optimization Reports, presenting key benchmarks and successes related to DTC local farmer financial and sales performance. These reports will be valuable resources for stakeholders within the farming community. Ultimately, this initiative will positively impact farmers, consumers, and other related businesses involved in the direct-to-consumer market.

original_description: “Cutting the Learning Curve: Targeted Trainings for New Managers, Board Members, and Market Producers” builds on the Washington State Farmers Market Association's popular “Farmers Market Boot Camp” to provide basic tools, resources, and connections and set 440 people on a positive professional path in their first farmers market season. This two-year project achieves three outcomes: 1) Work with State Partners in Alaska, Oregon, Idaho, and Ohio, to improve the pedagogical effectiveness and inclusivity of the WSFMA's Farmers Market Boot Camp for new market managers and board members; 2) Create a Boot Camp “add-on” specifically for new board members; and 3) Pilot a Boot Camp for new producers informed by findings from a survey of specialty crop growers who sell at farmers markets.
updated_description: Washington State Farmers Market Association’s “Cutting the Learning Curve” project aims to support new market managers, board members, and producers entering the farmers market sector, establishing a positive professional path for these individuals during their initial season. This two-year initiative will focus on enhancing the effectiveness of the Farmers Market Boot Camp, initially developed by the WSFMA, and expanding it with a specialized “add-on” specifically designed for new board members, informed by feedback from a survey of specialty crop growers. Furthermore, the project will pilot a new Boot Camp format tailored for new producers, reflecting the specific needs identified through the survey data. These efforts will collectively provide resources and connections to approximately 440 farmers, ranchers, processors, and market stakeholders, enabling them to successfully operate within the farmers market system. The project seeks to improve operational practices and contribute to the overall success of participants involved in direct-to-consumer activities. Ultimately, the project intends to bolster the capacity of market producers to engage with consumers and expand market access for fresh, locally produced goods.

original_description: In order to address inequities and barriers in the farmers market sector, MIFMA intends to strengthen community between Michigan farmers market managers and empower them as leaders in their communities to create anti-racist initiatives to improve their markets. The goal of the Market Manager Racial Equity Cohort is to empower market managers to foster greater understanding with the communities they serve by dismantling systems of oppression and implementing the tenets of the Farmers Market Coalition’s Anti-Racist Farmers Market Toolkit. Grant funds will be used to provide stipends to market managers for participating in the cohort and implementing an anti-racist initiative at their markets. Additionally, MIFMA intends to create and publish a curriculum for the cohort program and share outcomes from the project with MIFMA members and the broader national farmers market sector. The overall goals of this project are to support meaningful impacts in the participating market's communities and create a program model that can be replicated in other regions and other sectors of the food system.

original_description: Future Harvest, a nonprofit serving sustainable farmers in the mid-Atlantic region, proposes a regional marketing initiative focused around cooking culturally appropriate food and designed to assist farmers in accessing direct-to-consumer market channels. Future Harvest serves over 1000 members. Of those who are farming, 67% sell their produce directly to consumers. 75% of these farmers are beginning farmers, in their first ten years on the farm. This is a vulnerable time for farmers, and they need support through education and technical assistance. Farmers market managers also need training in how to best support farmers. Future Harvest proposes to provide 24 on-location field days to teach farmers how to market products to a direct audience and to ground market managers in best practices. These field days will be complemented by one-on-one technical assistance and coordinated in cooperation with the Mid-Atlantic Black Farmers Caucus. Future Harvest will help build consumer demand by facilitating demonstrations by chefs. Chef John Shields will produce twelve short online cooking shows. Three chefs who emphasize local food and its role in communities will provide demonstrations at local markets. Future Harvest will also provide consumer education materials that farmers will be able to access and share. Future Harvest anticipates that 480 farmers and market managers will make changes as a result of these programs, and 30,000 consumers will access resources.

original_description: Future Proofing Farm Shares will amplify and prevent disruptions to direct-to-consumer marketing efforts in Kentucky through outreach, training, and technical assistance, with an emphasis on operations using community supported agriculture (CSA) marketing models. Farm share programs continue to increase yet, based on stakeholder feedback, many consumers are still unfamiliar with purchasing from and directly supporting local farms. Strong state-wide partnerships will: increase capacity of existing and prospective farms offering farm shares; recruit institutional buyers, employer-partners, and farmers creating robust Farm-to-Workplace/ Producer-to-Institution models; develop a multi-farm CSA model for urban farmers; and educate wellness program participants and the general public. Specifically, the project is expected to: provide technical assistance and training to more than 100 CSA operations, including development of at least 37 business plans; generate at least 3 market assessments, with 1 focused on growers in historically underserved areas; result in more than 125 collaborations within the local supply network; train 500 stakeholders on direct-to-consumer market channels; improve food safety knowledge of at least 100 farmers; and reach more than 400,000 consumers, educating them on purchasing local products. The project will increase competitiveness and resiliency of prospective, new, and experienced producers and improve access to locally-produced agricultural products.
updated_description: Future Proofing Farm Shares aims to amplify and prevent disruptions to direct-to-consumer marketing efforts across Kentucky, focusing on operations utilizing community supported agriculture (CSA) models. original_description: Northeast Oklahoma City is known widely for negative statistics relating to health, food access and economic outcomes. A recent feasibility study conducted by OSU Extension was implemented to better understand the needs of this community. The Eastside Fresh Market concluded its second year in 2023 and is an established food access point for Northeast Oklahoma City residents, creating opportunities for area food producers. Also, existing and beginning farmers alike need support navigating the technical hurdles of sustaining their direct-to-consumer enterprises. Furthermore, there is a need to increase the capacity of the Eastside Fresh Market itself by expanding the customer base. This project addresses key producer needs through technical training and marketing support, and community needs by scaling up targeted marketing campaigns.

Investment will focus on stabilizing and expanding the local food economy, anticipated to yield a 100% increase in sales among the participating farmers and a 10% increase in sales revenue for producers and value-added vendors at Market Central.
