The International Rescue Committee will utilize community outreach strategies to improve the utilization of public benefits by approximately 1,200 Low-Income/Low-Access consumers. The overall impact of this initiative will be a strengthened local food system, increased economic opportunity for refugee and immigrant farmers and producers, and enhanced access to food resources for the target consumer group.

awardee_name: Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont
original_description: This project is to enhance our statewide online producer directory; To provide training and professional development for farmers market leaders, focusing on market viability and inclusion; And to provide customized marketing technical assistance and professional development to strengthen direct marketing farms and promote climate resilience.
updated_description: This project aims to enhance our statewide online producer directory to facilitate connections between farmers and consumers. The core objective is to provide specialized assistance to strengthen direct marketing operations for farmers and ranchers, focusing on market viability and promotional strategies. Specifically, this project will deliver customized marketing technical assistance to farmers and processors, bolstering their ability to reach consumers directly. Anticipated outcomes include increased sales volume for participating farms and a strengthened network of producers engaged in direct-to-retail activities. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the agricultural sector. This initiative seeks to improve the operational effectiveness of direct marketing businesses and enhance access to markets for producers. Ultimately, the goal is to support a robust and resilient local food system.

awardee_name: West Virginia National Guard Foundation, Inc.
original_description:
The West Virginia National Guard Foundation and Patriot Guardens will focus project efforts on reaching veteran farmers
with the intention of reaching new markets for their whole farm products, value-added products or through the addition of
agritourism/ecotourism operations on the property. During the project, educational programming will be developed and
delivered at three primary locations: Base Innovations Small Business Center in Charleston, WV, Patriot Apple Project in
Summersville, WV and the Patriot Guardens Urban Farm in Dunbar, WV. Each of these locations represent areas which
have been deemed food insecure, but also offer opportunities to reach direct-to-consumer markets in the local areas. Patriot
Guardens staff will reach well over 150 individuals through education and on-farm technical assistance, the vast majority of
which will seek to find new market opportunities such as farmers markets, restaurants and Community Support Agriculture
to sell their products.
Patriot Guardens will seek to work primarily with military veterans, actively serving military and military family members such
as spouses and children as they look to start or expand agricultural operations in the state. Most of these military connected
individuals will be members of the West Virginia National Guard, however service members from all branches and
affiliations are welcome to participate.
updated_description: The West Virginia National Guard Foundation and Patriot Guardens are undertaking a project focused on assisting veteran farmers in West Virginia with expanding market access for their agricultural products. This initiative aims to connect these farmers – including ranchers and processors – with direct-to-consumer sales channels such as farmers markets, local restaurants, and Community Supported Agriculture programs. The project will deliver educational programming at three key locations: the Base Innovations Small Business Center in Charleston, the Patriot Apple Project in Summersville, and the Patriot Guardens Urban Farm in Dunbar. Through these locations, the project anticipates reaching over 150 individuals, primarily military veterans and their families, seeking to develop or grow agricultural operations. The West Virginia National Guard Foundation and Patriot Guardens will provide technical assistance to these stakeholders, supporting them in identifying new markets for their farm products, value-added products, or the potential for agritourism or ecotourism operations. Ultimately, this project seeks to empower these farmers to increase sales and create sustainable economic opportunities within their communities. The intended outcome is a strengthened local food system and increased economic viability for veteran-led agricultural businesses across West Virginia.

original_description:
Small and beginning farmers in West Virginia face significant challenges in achieving profitability due to small-scale
operations, limited market access, and the rural nature of many communities. This project aims to address these challenges
by piloting a marketing and education initiative across three West Virginia counties (Pocahontas, Nicholas, and Fayette).
The project will focus on developing a living-wage pricing list and marketing toolkit for fresh produce, educating farmers on
fair pricing strategies, launching branding and marketing campaigns to educate consumers, and increasing access to local
foods, especially for vulnerable populations like seniors and participants in nutrition assistance programs.
Led by High Rocks Educational Corporation, an award-winning leader in transforming the lives of young people in West
Virginia, the project leverages the organization's mission to educate, empower, and inspire. High Rocks Educational
Corporation operates the second-largest AmeriCorps program in the state and three youth social enterprises, providing
young people with opportunities to earn while learning key personal and professional development skills and industry best
practices. The organization’s impact on local communities is profound, making it an ideal leader for this initiative.
In partnership with Five Rivers Farmer Cooperative, Coalfield Development’s Refresh Appalachia, WV Food and Farm
Coalition, and Fayette County Schools, the project will collect data, provide training, pilot new food access markets, and
engage with industry stakeholders. Key activities include creating a cost-tracking tool, developing a "Living Wage for
Appalachian Farmers" brand and certification, training farmers, and conducting consumer education campaigns.
By promoting fair pricing and increasing market opportunities, the project aims to create a sustainable and equitable local
food system that ensures living wages for Appalachian farmers and enhances food security for local communities. The
project will leverage data collection, stakeholder engagement, and targeted marketing to achieve its objectives and set the
stage for broader implementation across the state.
updated_description: High Rocks Educational Corporation is undertaking a vital project to address the challenges faced by small and beginning farmers in West Virginia, specifically within Pocahontas, Nicholas, and Fayette counties. The initiative aims to establish a sustainable and equitable local food system by developing a “Living Wage for Appalachian Farmers” brand and certification, creating a cost-tracking tool, and launching targeted marketing campaigns to increase market access for these farmers and educate consumers about the value of locally sourced produce. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of a viable pricing strategy, enhanced opportunities for farmers to sell their goods, and an increase in the availability of fresh food within the communities, particularly benefiting ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the agricultural sector. The project will directly assist farmers by establishing a living-wage pricing list and marketing toolkit, while simultaneously improving food security for vulnerable populations such as seniors and participants in nutrition assistance programs. High Rocks Educational Corporation, leveraging its experience operating the second-largest AmeriCorps program in the state and three youth social enterprises, is uniquely positioned to lead this effort and foster economic growth within the agricultural landscape of West Virginia. By promoting fair pricing and increasing market opportunities, the project seeks to ensure a sustainable and equitable local food system, ultimately benefiting farmers and consumers alike.

original_description:
This project seeks to increase market opportunities and sales for direct-market farmers by providing training and technical
assistance in marketing and business planning; boosting customer demand through consumer-facing events and strategic
social media campaigns; and increasing farmers’ direct sales to independent grocers by conducting outreach to grocers and
farmers, offering marketing incentives to the grocers and facilitating connections. This work will be carried out in western
Virginia and central Arkansas, two regions where there is a young but growing local food movement and CNG has robust
collaborators. In Virginia, the Virginia Association for Biological Farming will carry out much of the project work, including
organizing consumer-facing events featuring the importance of local food and ecological farming practices. The project
aims to bolster consumers' appreciation for ecological certifications used by direct-market farmers, to help shore up the
value of this marketing tool. As a result of this project, 480 farmers will receive marketing and business development training
through online courses and conference workshops, and 66 farmers will increase sales by the end of the project period. At
least ten farmers markets will receive marketing support via our social media campaigns carried out with collaborators local
to these markets. At least 22 independent grocers will meaningfully increase the share of fresh produce sold that comes
from local farms.
updated_description: This project seeks to significantly expand market opportunities and sales for direct-market farmers through a multi-faceted approach encompassing marketing and business planning support, strategic consumer-facing events, and targeted outreach to independent grocers. The project’s primary goal is to bolster the burgeoning local food movement in western Virginia and central Arkansas by connecting farmers directly with consumers and retailers. Specifically, 480 farmers will receive marketing and business development assistance via online courses and conference workshops, and an additional 66 farmers are anticipated to increase their sales figures by the project’s conclusion. Furthermore, at least ten farmers markets will receive marketing support through collaborative social media campaigns, and a minimum of 22 independent grocers are expected to increase the proportion of fresh produce they source from local farms. This initiative will also focus on elevating the recognition and value of ecological certifications utilized by direct-market farmers, promoting a deeper appreciation among consumers for these standards. The overall anticipated outcome is a strengthened local food system, benefitting farmers, consumers, and processors alike, with a projected increase in the volume of fresh produce sales originating from local sources. Ultimately, the project intends to foster mutually beneficial relationships between these stakeholders, creating a more robust and sustainable local food supply chain within the designated regions.

original_description: The project aims to empower UConn Extension's regional marketing campaign in Northeastern Connecticut (NECT), with a focus on increasing access to farms and farmers markets among SNAP participants. Through strategic media efforts and collaboration with an emerging regional food hub, the project will also help farms reach new customers via an online marketplace.
updated_description: UConn Extension’s regional marketing campaign in Northeastern Connecticut aims to increase access to farms and farmers markets among SNAP participants, ultimately supporting a strengthened local food system. This project will achieve this through strategic media efforts and collaboration with an emerging regional food hub, facilitating new customer acquisition for participating farms. The anticipated outcomes include a greater volume of sales for farmers and increased market access for consumers seeking fresh agricultural products. Specifically, the project will enhance the visibility of local farms and farmers markets within the Northeastern Connecticut region. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative are farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the agricultural sector, alongside the consumers who will gain improved access to a variety of food products. This project seeks to improve the reach of local food producers and to expand the market for their goods. It is expected that this increased market access will contribute to the economic viability of farms in the region. The project will provide a channel for farmers to connect directly with their customers, furthering the availability of fresh food.

original_description: Cornell's Agriculture Marketing Research Program will increase sales of local foods at farmers markets (FMs) with an approach using analysis of FM vendors' customer spending data obtained from Point-of-Sale (POS) software. POS data are paired with Rapid Market Assessment (RMA) consumer surveys in 3 focus regions of New York and Pennsylvania. We utilize vendor and local demographics to understand shopper and vendor diversity dynamics, vendor sales performance, and identify opportunities for vendors and FM Managers (FMMs) to make FMs a more inclusive environment. We compare individual (vendor and FM) and aggregate results to identify practical marketing practices to increase access to and sales of locally grown foods. In addition to marketing techniques informed by participant data, we incorporate recommendations from the Farmers Market Coalition's Anti-Racist Toolkit; thus addressing implicit bias commonly found in FM culture and communications and working to remove barriers that discourage a broad diversity of consumers and vendors. These efforts result in data-informed recommendations to farmer vendors and FMMs working together to create a welcoming shopping environment. Capitalizing on our team of experts from Penn State, Cornell, and the farmer and FMM communities, we extend the benefits of the project to additional audiences through presentations and publications, including a 6-week Direct Marketing Farmer Training Course and a 1-day NY-PA Direct Marketing Conference.
updated_description: Cornell’s Agriculture Marketing Research Program aims to enhance sales of locally grown foods at farmers markets through a data-driven approach. The project utilizes Point-of-Sale (POS) data collected from farmers market vendors alongside Rapid Market Assessment (RMA) consumer surveys in designated regions of New York and Pennsylvania. This analysis examines vendor and local demographic information to understand shopper and vendor characteristics, assess sales performance, and identify opportunities for improvement within the farmers market environment. By comparing individual and aggregate results, the program will develop practical marketing recommendations for farmer vendors and farmers market managers to increase access to and sales of locally produced goods. The research focuses on creating a welcoming shopping environment for all stakeholders, including farmers and consumers. The project anticipates outcomes such as increased sales volume for local producers and enhanced market access for those participating in farmers markets. Ultimately, the project seeks to support farmers and consumers involved in the local food system, with the goal of strengthening market connections and promoting the sale of locally grown products. The research will culminate in actionable insights designed to be implemented collaboratively by farmer vendors and farmers market managers.

original_description: The Central Wisconsin Farmers Market Collaborative (CWFMC) is a community-led initiative that has been assessing needs & building partnerships to address food equity & improve low income  access at Farmers Markets (FM).Central Wisconsin is predominantly rural; there are just over a dozen markets serving about 350,000 people in the five counties in our project area; spanning close to 5 thousand total square miles. These markets have some limits that this project will help address: few have a paid market manager; less than half redeem food assistance benefits; none offer consistent double-your-dollar incentives for benefit use. FM also lack the capacity to engage the community, grow their customer base, & support new or marginalized farmers. With many barriers to technology, including limited broadband internet access, only a small fraction of our market vendors utilize electronic/mobile payment services, especially among Amish/Mennonite, non-English speaking vendors, & farmers with limited income. Research clearly shows that Central Wisconsin farmers & FM need technical & educational support to: expand & diversify their customers & vendors; adopt emerging electronic & mobile sales technologies; improve outreach to & accessibility for food assistance recipients; develop business plans that leverage local partnerships; & implement strategic communication plans. The CWFMC, formed during the LFPP planning grant, is now poised to implement change
updated_description: The Central Wisconsin Farmers Market Collaborative is undertaking a project to address critical needs at Central Wisconsin farmers markets to improve food equity and increase access to fresh food for low-income consumers. The project seeks to expand and enhance the operations of Central Wisconsin farmers markets, recognizing that there are currently limited capacity within the markets to engage the community, grow their customer base, and support new or marginalized farmers. Specifically, the project aims to address the current limitations within the markets by increasing the use of food assistance benefits, expanding access to electronic/mobile sales technologies, and establishing strategic communication plans. The CWFMC will support farmers and market stakeholders by seeking to increase vendor participation, recognizing the constraints related to technology access, particularly among Amish/Mennonite vendors and those with limited income, and encouraging the use of electronic payment services. Ultimately, the project will improve access for consumers, and support farmers and ranchers, with the goal of enriching the markets’ ability to engage customers and provide a greater selection of goods. This work will support an increase in the use of food assistance benefits at the markets.

original_description: Farm Generations Cooperative will collaborate with each of our thirteen farmer member-owners to create a promotional plan for their farm's direct-to-consumer sales in the 2025 season, to be implemented in our cooperatively owned marketing platform, GrownBy. We will measure the effectiveness of each farm's promotional campaign using GrownBy sales and customer data, focusing on the return-on-investment realized from each distinct promotional campaign.
updated_description: Farm Generations Cooperative will develop targeted promotional plans for its thirteen farmer member-owners to enhance direct-to-consumer sales within the 2025 growing season, utilizing the cooperative’s GrownBy marketing platform. The core of this project involves creating individualized marketing strategies for each farm, designed to maximize sales through direct channels. Through the implementation of these plans, Farm Generations Cooperative anticipates a measurable increase in sales volume reported within the GrownBy system, allowing for a detailed assessment of the return on investment associated with each promotional campaign. This initiative will directly benefit the farmers who are members of the cooperative, as well as the consumers who purchase products from these farms. The project’s outcomes will be tracked through sales data and customer information collected within GrownBy. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate the value of focused promotional efforts and to contribute to the success of the participating farms. This will allow the cooperative to determine which approaches are most effective in reaching the target consumer base and to optimize marketing investments accordingly. By supporting these farms, Farm Generations Cooperative strengthens the local food system and provides consumers with access to fresh, locally produced goods.

original_description: Good Food Farmers Network (GFFN) is an online sales platform established to expand market access for small-scale and beginning farmers. GFFN collaborates with 25 producers and serves 275 households. This project will support a Member Engagement Campaign to increase annual revenue by 30%. This campaign will increase direct payments to participating producers by $115,000 annually and increase GFFN net revenue by $45,000 annually of which approximately $35,000 per year will be allocated for ongoing support of the part- time Member Engagement Coordinator position (initially established through this grant and matching funds) and $10,000 per year towards ongoing generation of print materials and other collateral. To achieve this 30% increase in annual revenue, this project has two key objectives: (1) to increase average transaction value by 15% or $12 per order, and (2) to increase average weekly member order rate by 15%, from 52% to 60% participation. To achieve these objectives, this grant will support developing and disseminating weekly online and social media content promoting available products and educating members on how to use available foods emphasizing quick and convenient meals; print materials reinforcing the online messaging; promotional merchandise; and events that increase member connection to GFFN farms and regional agriculture.
updated_description: Good Food Farmers Network (GFFN) is undertaking a Member Engagement Campaign with the primary purpose of expanding market access for small-scale and beginning farmers, currently collaborating with 25 producers and serving 275 households. This project will focus on increasing annual revenue by 30%, which includes a targeted increase of $115,000 in direct payments to participating producers and an additional $45,000 in GFFN net revenue. To achieve this ambitious goal, the project will implement two key strategies: firstly, boosting the average transaction value by 15%—approximately $12 per order—and secondly, raising the average weekly order rate among members from 52% to 60%. The campaign will utilize a multi-faceted approach incorporating the development and distribution of weekly online and social media content showcasing available products and providing information on convenient meal preparation; the creation of accompanying print materials to reinforce these online messages; the procurement of promotional merchandise; and the hosting of events designed to strengthen connections between members and regional agriculture. These efforts are expected to benefit farmers by maximizing their sales potential and improving their financial stability, while simultaneously providing consumers with increased access to fresh, locally sourced goods. Furthermore, the project will allocate approximately $35,000 annually to support the ongoing operation of a part-time Member Engagement Coordinator position and $10,000 annually for generating print materials and other collateral, ensuring the sustainability of the campaign’s activities and the continued success of the network. The overall impact will be realized through enhanced sales for participating farmers and increased consumer engagement with local food systems, solidifying GFFN’s role as a key facilitator within the regional food landscape.

original_description:
The City of South Bend's Engagement and Economic Empowerment team hosts the Linden Avenue Farmers Market (LAFM), a seasonal farmers market and family-friendly entertainment venue that runs once per month from June through October. Now in its fourth year, LAFM continues to partner with local and regional small- to medium-scale agricultural producers, prepared food artisans, and food security partners to improve food systems in low-income/low-access neighborhoods that have been dis-invested throughout their history. In this proposal, the City will expand its support to activate local farmers by providing market access opportunities through the LAFM and its wraparound supports: vendors will have access to market equipment such as tents, tables, and electrical accessories. In addition, LAFM offers staff and volunteer assistance with pre-market engagement, and volunteer assistance with day-of logistics.

Promoting small-scale farmers markets while simultaneously addressing food security requires a comprehensive approach with innovative mechanisms for vendor recruitment, community outreach, and mission-driven programming; expanding vendor incentives and offerings will bolster the quality and quantity of regional farming and improve consumer access to healthy food systems.
updated_description: The City of South Bend’s Engagement and Economic Empowerment team is undertaking a project to expand the Linden Avenue Farmers Market (LAFM), a seasonal market operating monthly from June through October, designed to enhance regional food systems and bolster local agricultural producers. This initiative will provide vendors, including farmers, ranchers, and food processors, with access to essential market equipment, such as tents, tables, and electrical accessories, alongside staff and volunteer assistance for pre-market engagement and day-of logistics support. The anticipated outcome of this project is an increased quantity and quality of regional farming products available at the LAFM, directly benefiting consumers and strengthening local food systems. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers participating in the market, as well as the consumers seeking access to fresh, locally sourced food. The City of South Bend aims to create more opportunities for these stakeholders to connect and contribute to a robust food network within the community. Ultimately, the expansion of the LAFM seeks to improve access to healthy food options for the community, with a focus on increasing the selection and availability of products from regional agricultural sources.

original_description:
The Healthy By Design (HBD) coalition is dedicated to fostering resilient local food systems that promote community health and well-being. Through the USDA FMPP Turnkey Marketing and Promotion grant, we aim to increase vendor recruitment and expand customer reach using a targeted marketing campaign. The proposal aims to strengthen vendor capacity and participation through innovative retention-focused marketing tools that correct market attendance misconceptions and increase market visibility beyond the immediate neighborhood. The marketing campaign will involve identifying strategic marketing opportunities. Proposed partners will include a TBD-determined sub-awardee to support community-wide marketing efforts. This project supports the Healthy People 2030 objective to improve health by promoting healthy eating and making nutritious foods readily available.

The weekly market is held at South Park located in the South Side of Billings; a neighborhood that is a USDA defined food desert having lost its only grocery store in 2013. Potential, and existing, market vendors have expressed several barriers to regular participation, including limited customer base beyond the neighborhood, and lack of multiple anchor vendors to attract customers. Previous FMPP grants underscore a track record of impactful initiatives. By expanding market attendance and vendor participation, the project aims to enhance the economic and health outcomes of the broader community.
updated_description: The Healthy By Design (HBD) coalition is undertaking a project to bolster resilient local food systems, directly supporting community health and well-being within the South Side of Billings. This initiative, funded through a USDA FMPP Turnkey Marketing and Promotion grant, focuses on increasing vendor recruitment and expanding customer reach through a targeted marketing campaign designed to address key barriers faced by market participants. Specifically, the project will concentrate on enhancing vendor capacity and participation by utilizing innovative retention-focused marketing tools, aiming to correct market attendance misconceptions and elevate market visibility beyond the immediate neighborhood. Recognizing the challenges faced by farmers and ranchers supplying the market, along with the consumers who frequent it, the project seeks to attract a broader customer base, thereby improving economic outcomes for these stakeholders. The anticipated outcome is increased market attendance and vendor participation, leading to a stronger local food system. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers and ranchers providing goods to the weekly market at South Park, as well as the consumers who access fresh food options. Ultimately, this project seeks to improve the overall health and well-being of the Billings community by making nutritious foods readily available and strengthening connections between food producers and consumers.

original_description: Despite an increase in population and a need for easy access to fresh produce, Nevada remains far behind other regions of the United States in the production, adoption, and development of a local food industry. The City of Henderson is committed to creating a healthy, livable, and sustainable community as identified in the City's Henderson Strong Comprehensive Plan and 2024-2027 Strategic Plan. The City of Henderson's Premier Harvest Farmers Market Program aims to support the growth, coordination, and expansion of the City's existing Farmers Market Program. The purpose of this project is to increase access to healthy foods to populations in low income/low access census tracts, especially seniors, low income, and SNAP eligible populations. This project will seek out the development, implementation, and evaluation of a Farmers Market Feasibility Study to identify ways to promote and market existing and new farmers markets. Through a public-private partnership, the city will work with contracted farmers market operator(s) to enhance existing markets, increase the frequency the markets are offered, and expand to new locations. Along with these efforts, marketing materials and supplies will be purchased with the goal to boost foot traffic and awareness of the various markets, and healthy foods will be more accessible to a wider population of the city.
updated_description: The City of Henderson is undertaking a project to increase access to fresh produce within the city, aligning with its commitment to creating a healthy, livable, and sustainable community as outlined in the Henderson Strong Comprehensive Plan and 2024-2027 Strategic Plan. This project aims to support the expansion of the City’s existing Farmers Market Program, focusing on promoting and marketing existing and new markets to encourage greater participation from farmers and consumers. Specifically, the City of Henderson will partner with contracted farmers market operators to enhance current market operations, potentially increasing the frequency of market offerings and exploring new locations to serve a broader population. As part of this effort, the City will purchase marketing materials and supplies with the goal of boosting foot traffic and increasing awareness of the various markets and the available fresh foods. The anticipated outcome of this project is to improve access to healthy foods for a wider range of stakeholders, with a particular focus on supporting local farmers and providing consumers with more options. This initiative will benefit populations in low-income/low-access census tracts, including seniors, those eligible for SNAP benefits, and other consumers seeking fresh produce. By facilitating direct-to-consumer activities, the City of Henderson intends to strengthen the local food system and improve access to nutritious foods for its residents.

original_description: Through the following initiatives, Portland Farmers Market aims to: 1) Increase accessibility and awareness of farmers markets as direct-to-consumer sales opportunities for historically under-served farmers and ranchers, 2) Provide trainings to enhance vendors’ success in diverse marketplaces, and 3) Increase the number of vendors at Lents International and King Farmers Markets.  Vendor Recruitment: We will implement a new digital recruitment strategy, host prospective vendor info sessions, simplify and translate application & informational materials to improve access for vendors with limited English proficiency, and collaborate with organizations serving new farmers/ ranchers to present workshops on developing a farmers market enterprise.  Vendor Trainings & Peer-to-Peer Workshops: Partnering with OFMA and expert instructors, we will present a training series on enhancing vendor success and customer service in diverse marketplaces.  We will also convene Peer-to-Peer Workshops where vendors share knowledge and discuss common challenges in a panel-style format.  New Vendor Incubation: Incubator booths at Lents International and King Farmers Markets will enable new farmers to experience selling at market and learn from experts, in collaboration with Outgrowing Hunger and Headwaters Incubator Farm.  These initiatives will engage 248 current and 80 prospective vendors (duplicated) in trainings & workshops, and 24 unique vendors in new direct-to-consumer sales at farmers markets.
updated_description: Portland Farmers Market aims to expand direct-to-consumer sales opportunities for farmers and ranchers by increasing market access and fostering successful business ventures. This project will facilitate the growth of the Portland Farmers Market system through a comprehensive strategy, including the implementation of a new digital recruitment approach, the hosting of vendor information sessions, and the simplification of application materials to enhance accessibility for all vendors. Specifically, Portland Farmers Market will establish incubator booths at the Lents International and King Farmers Markets, providing new farmers with the opportunity to directly engage with consumers and learn from experienced professionals in collaboration with Outgrowing Hunger and Headwaters Incubator Farm. The project anticipates the engagement of 248 current vendors and 80 prospective vendors, resulting in the activation of 24 unique vendors and the support of a broader network of producers. These initiatives are designed to strengthen the Portland Farmers Market system by attracting new participants and empowering existing vendors to thrive, ultimately benefiting farmers, ranchers, and the consumers who purchase their goods. The anticipated outcome is a more robust and accessible market environment, driving economic activity and providing access to fresh, locally produced products.

original_description:
Food For All! increases locally grown produce sales at two existing
farmers markets, and tests two new markets for economic sustainability,
by using digital and print media. “Farmers Forks” hires farmers to give
cooking demonstrations and teach dishes to make with their crops. Twice
annual focus groups gather input on materials, strategies and
programming.
Deliverables include quarterly print campaigns in Edible South Florida
Magazine, ongoing banners and social media posts by Edible, monthly
print ads in The Biscayne Times, ongoing promotion on Yelp, a weekly
produced e-newsletter to over 3500 people, 3 social media posts and
stories weekly to over 10,000 people, 3 mailings of postcards to 10,000
people in market vicinity and targeted neighborhoods, and 2 annual
Freebee vehicle wraps running for 2 months, including postcard delivery to
all riders.
Outcomes expected: 10% increase in sales of produce by farms at existing
markets. At two new markets, at least four farms will find new
opportunities, with 25% sales growth in year two. 30 consumers will
engage per “Farmers Forks” event, 75% reporting learning new recipes
and 50% will try a local ingredient.
Collaborators include media Edible South Florida Magazine, Freebee, and
Biscayne Times. Site locations are Legion Park, Vizcaya Museum &
Gardens Trust, and Tropical Audubon Society. Beneficiaries are farms
with an increase in direct sales: Tiny, French, Paradise, Regener8,
Samsara, Under the Vine, Intergro, LNB and others.
updated_description: Food For All! aims to increase locally grown produce sales at two existing farmers markets and test two new markets for economic sustainability through a comprehensive marketing strategy. This project involves the creation and execution of a multi-faceted campaign utilizing digital and print media, including quarterly print campaigns in Edible South Florida Magazine, ongoing banners and social media posts managed by Edible, monthly print ads in The Biscayne Times, continuous promotion on Yelp, a weekly produced e-newsletter distributed to over 3500 recipients, and three social media posts and stories weekly reaching over 10,000 people. Furthermore, the project includes three mailings of postcards to 10,000 individuals residing in market vicinity and targeted neighborhoods, as well as two annual Freebee vehicle wraps running for two months, encompassing postcard delivery to all riders. Anticipated outcomes include a 10% increase in sales of produce by participating farms at existing markets, with at least four farms securing new opportunities at the two new markets, projecting a 25% sales growth in year two. The project expects to engage approximately 30 consumers per “Farmers Forks” event, with 75% reporting learning new recipes and 50% indicating a willingness to try a local ingredient. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers – Tiny, French, Paradise, Regener8, Samsara, Under the Vine, Intergro, and LNB – as well as the consumers who will have access to fresh, locally sourced produce. The farms involved represent a range of producers, while the consumers represent a broad group of individuals seeking to purchase agricultural products. This project intends to stimulate economic activity among farmers and provide consumers with new food options.

original_description:
Farm to School Frederick is dedicated to enhancing marketing and promotional endeavors for five Farmers Markets situated in low-income and low-access areas across Frederick County. Despite these markets having a strong foundation, there's a pressing need to increase access to and availability of locally produced agricultural products to families of color and those facing challenges in accessing nutritious foods, especially fresh fruits and vegetables.

The project includes a comprehensive needs assessment, the development of a dynamic marketing strategy and the creation of diverse promotional materials to attract a wide-ranging customer base. Collaboration plays a central role, with Farm to School Frederick already fostering robust partnerships with farmers, the Office of Agriculture, community organizations, and Frederick County Public Schools. Leveraging its established position as a trusted community partner, the impact of the initiatives will be amplified.

Farmer Market Managers and a marketing firm will provide guidance and produce professional content. The project will actively engage communities through interviews, focus groups, and surveys to gather insights for improving market accessibility and increasing farmer sales. Data collection and analysis will evaluate the campaign's impact on attendance, revenue, and sales, ultimately aiming to enhance the visibility and prosperity of Farmers Markets while fostering a more inclusive local food system.
updated_description: Farm to School Frederick is undertaking a vital project to enhance marketing and promotional efforts for five Farmers Markets located within low-income and low-access areas of Frederick County. The primary purpose of this initiative is to increase access to locally produced agricultural products for farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders, specifically targeting families and those experiencing challenges in obtaining nutritious foods, particularly fresh fruits and vegetables.
