updated_description: The San Diego Policy & Innovation Center, in partnership with the San Diego Fishermen’s Working Group and a network of collaborators, is undertaking a project to strengthen and shorten the local supply chain for commercial fish within San Diego. This initiative aims to increase local fish purchasing, elevate the percentage of profits retained by fishermen, and enhance the visibility of this community. The core of this effort involves the revival of the Fishermen’s Marketing Association, a dormant non-profit, to facilitate coordinated outreach to restaurants and engagement with consumers. Specifically, the project will establish a web-based sales platform accessible to all fishing vessels, alongside collaborative events and direct engagement with chefs. Furthermore, the project will launch an annual “Local Fish, Global Flavor” festival, anticipated to attract at least 1000 attendees, showcasing local fish integrated into global and fusion dishes prepared by local chefs. The anticipated outcome is a more robust and visible local fish market, benefiting fishermen and consumers alike. The primary beneficiaries of this project include local fish processors, farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders within the San Diego food economy. By streamlining the flow of fish from the source to the consumer, this project intends to create a stronger, more resilient, and more profitable market for San Diego’s fishing industry, supporting the livelihoods of those involved and providing consumers with access to fresh, locally sourced seafood.

original_description: ALBA will strengthen training capacity, improving BOLD farms’ readiness to enter markets. ALBA will partner with Kitchen Table Consultants to revise ALBA’s marketing training program, create new case studies, IT training, mentoring, and creating a buffer in between farms and the reality of market conditions.  ALBA will expand partnership with a for-profit food hub (Coke Farm) to strengthen coordination of product mix, and forecasting, streamline transport logistics, and establish profitable local marketing channels. ALBA will diversify marketing channels by identifying and onboarding alternative clients (other than Coke) on the Central Coast and San Francisco Bay Area, to which BOLD farms can supply directly. ALBA will leverage the networks of prominent community partners, the Blue Zones Project and Slow Money Monterey Bay which share common values and have extensive regional food system contacts. In addition, Taste for Profit Marketing will help develop a promotional campaign to attract buyers. The project builds on ALBA’s 21 years of providing incubation and marketing assistance to underserved producers, and Coke Farm’s 41 years of experience marketing organic produce
updated_description: ALBA will strengthen its capacity to improve the readiness of BOLD farms to enter markets through a comprehensive initiative focused on enhancing coordination and market access. This project will establish a strategic partnership with Coke Farm to streamline product mix, forecasting, and transport logistics, as well as develop profitable local marketing channels for BOLD farms. ALBA will also diversify its client base by onboarding new buyers within the Central Coast and San Francisco Bay Area, expanding the range of markets available to its farmer partners. To achieve these goals, ALBA will collaborate with Kitchen Table Consultants to develop case studies and establish IT support, bolstering operational efficiency. Furthermore, ALBA will leverage the networks of prominent regional partners, including the Blue Zones Project and Slow Money Monterey Bay, to facilitate connections and opportunities for BOLD farms. The initiative anticipates a measurable increase in the volume of agricultural products reaching consumers and stakeholders, ultimately benefiting farmers and ranchers by providing greater access to established markets. This project is designed to improve the overall effectiveness of the agricultural system by creating a more integrated and robust local food network, supporting the producers and increasing the availability of regionally produced products to the public.

original_description: The Center for Land-Based Learning will improve and expand its Mobile Farmers Market operations in West Sacramento and into Woodland CA. Having completed a resoundingly successful pilot season in 2021 serving 300 unique customers in low-income areas and making 80% of all sales through SNAP, the Mobile Market has proven to be an effective tool in reaching low-income residents living in low-access neighborhoods. All produce sold on the Mobile Market comes from local growers. The Mobile Market supports 31 local, small-scale, producers, 30% of which are disadvantaged, by developing new markets in low-income, low-access neighborhoods. To efficiently operate the mobile market, additional food hub facility infrastructure to support processing, aggregation, and storage of local produce is now needed. The food hub will provide a place for farmers to deliver produce, access cold storage, and perform light processing including peeling, chopping, and packing to create value-added products in the form of ready-to-use produce. By offering light processing capacity, produce that would otherwise not be accepted at market due to imperfections can be sold at added value and convenience to low-income customers strapped for time and culinary knowledge on produce preparation. Providing pre-peeled and chopped produce vastly increases the ability of our target demographic to consume them. Low-income seniors and residents affected by diet-related illness often experience physical challenges wielding knives to perform tasks such as cubing winter squash. Offering ready-to-use fresh produce via Mobile Markets opens market opportunities in targeted low-income low-access communities that were otherwise unavailable.
updated_description: The Center for Land-Based Learning is undertaking a project to enhance and expand its Mobile Farmers Market operations in West Sacramento and Woodland, California. This initiative involves the purchase and construction of a food hub facility designed to support local growers and processors, providing essential infrastructure for processing, aggregation, and storage of fresh produce. The anticipated outcome of this project is to increase access to locally produced agricultural products within targeted low-income communities. Specifically, the food hub will offer capabilities including peeling, chopping, and packing to transform produce, allowing for the creation of ready-to-use items. This expands market opportunities for farmers and processors, enabling them to sell products that might otherwise be unsuitable due to minor imperfections. The Mobile Farmers Markets will serve low-income residents, representing a significant consumer base. These markets will positively impact the communities they serve by offering convenient access to fresh produce, addressing potential challenges experienced by consumers regarding food preparation. The project seeks to improve the ability of these communities to consume fresh produce, supporting local farmers and increasing the volume of goods available to the target population. Ultimately, this project aims to strengthen the local food system by providing crucial support to producers and broadening the reach of locally sourced agricultural products to those in need.

original_description: In Southwest Colorado, snowmelt and precious rivers are the lifeblood of rural mountain and high desert communities. Entrepreneurs and nonprofit partners are working to build equitable food systems with shorter, value-based supply chains that provide living wages to growers and healthy food access to communities. The project’s 18-month planning process involved 300 stakeholders, piloted likely solutions, and identified 8 critical factors for success in the “Roadmap for Regional Connectivity.” The Southwest Colorado Food Hub-to-Hub Connectivity Project is a collaboration of five nonprofits and five food hubs covering one-quarter of the state that will increase access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. The project will: 1) expand and connect the infrastructure of five mid-tier value chain enterprises (food hubs) by (a) establishing a new food hub facility in Gunnison, and (b) expanding four hub-to-hub distribution routes to meet increased demand with greater efficiency, frequency, consistency, and reliability; and 2) developing the wholesale market for local/regional specialty crops through a 3-year regional marketing, education, and outreach campaign; an annual series of agritourism (farm tours) events; and five speed-dating events between chefs/buyers and producers in the region. These integrated activities address supply-side and demand-side issues simultaneously. Producers across the region who want to scale up their businesses gain reliable pathways to new, wider markets. New and existing markets gain access to a wider number of producers and products, along with reliable, frequent, and consistent deliveries. The project will increase local food purchases from 344 producers by $3.8M over three years.
updated_description: The Southwest Colorado Food Hub-to-Hub Connectivity Project aims to bolster regional food systems in Southwest Colorado, focusing on increasing access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. This project, encompassing five nonprofits and five food hubs across one-quarter of the state, will achieve this through a multi-faceted approach including the establishment of a new food hub facility in Gunnison and the expansion of four existing hub-to-hub distribution routes, designed to meet heightened demand with improved efficiency and reliability. Anticipated outcomes of this project include a significant increase in local food purchases, projected to rise by $3.8 million over three years, driven by expanded market access for farmers and ranchers within the region. The project’s beneficiaries include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders who seek to scale their businesses and connect to wider markets, as well as consumers who will benefit from a greater variety of locally sourced products. To achieve this, the project will implement a three-year regional marketing, education, and outreach campaign, alongside annual agritourism events featuring farm tours and five speed-dating events between chefs and producers. These integrated activities are designed to address supply-side and demand-side challenges simultaneously, ensuring a more robust and connected food network throughout Southwest Colorado.

original_description: Increase the availability, consumption and sale of local foods throughout Florida by identifying key local food system actors to connect and build stronger relationships in our food system by gathering key information such as needs and barriers to develop tools and support, network opportunities and trainings. Our expectation is that our efforts will serve as a model for other communities to replicate not only in Florida, but around the country.
updated_description: Increase the availability, consumption and sale of local foods throughout Florida by identifying key local food system actors to connect and build stronger relationships in our food system. This project aims to facilitate the development of stronger local food systems by gathering critical information regarding the needs and barriers faced by farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders. The project will support the establishment of food hubs, shared-use kitchens, and similar initiatives designed to improve access to locally produced agricultural products. The anticipated outcomes include increased volumes of locally grown products reaching consumers and bolstering the operations of food businesses within the state. Ultimately, this project seeks to create a model replicable across Florida and potentially other communities, contributing to a more robust and interconnected food system. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers who produce agricultural goods, as well as the consumers seeking access to fresh, locally sourced food. The project will support the growth of food businesses that act as intermediaries, connecting producers directly with markets, thereby increasing the volume of locally grown products available to the public. The project’s success will be measured by the demonstrable increase in the availability of local foods throughout Florida, strengthening the connections between producers and consumers.

original_description: Consumers have questions about how wild seafood is harvested from the oceans, but find farmed seafood even more mysterious. This project aims help demystify these processes, enhancing interest in and sales of locally produced Florida seafood. Videos address the need for increased consumer awareness of sustainable, local seafood, including Florida’s diverse aquaculture products. We will create four, 15-minute long videos showcasing Florida seafood producers, stimulating market development for these local foods to be showcased at local screenings and be freely available online.  We want consumers to value their local seafood.
updated_description: Consumers are seeking greater understanding of how wild seafood is harvested and are interested in the processes behind farmed seafood production. This project aims to demystify these processes, ultimately enhancing interest in and sales of locally produced Florida seafood. The project will create four videos, each approximately 15 minutes in length, which showcase Florida seafood producers and their operations. These videos will be used to stimulate market development for these local foods, with the intention of showcasing them at local screenings. The anticipated outcome is that consumers will value the seafood produced within Florida. The project focuses on increasing awareness of Florida’s aquaculture products and the value of supporting local seafood businesses. The stakeholders involved – including farmers, processors, and producers – will benefit from increased visibility and potential sales growth. The project’s success will be measured by the increased demand for locally sourced Florida seafood. The goal is to establish a stronger market for Florida seafood products within the region. By providing clear information about production methods, the project seeks to build consumer confidence and support for local seafood businesses, contributing to the economic viability of these operations.

original_description: West Georgia Farmers Cooperative’s project purpose is to expand its food hub/distribution services in a local income/low access area serving rural west Georgia and Atlanta. Our primary objective is to expand the current food hub’s customers and revenue.  Planned activities include attracting new business and clients, creating value-added products from current fresh products (fruits, vegetables, seafood) and attaining GAP certification for food hub and the cooperative’s farmer members.
updated_description: West Georgia Farmers Cooperative’s project aims to expand its food hub and distribution services within a local income and low access area, serving rural west Georgia and Atlanta. The primary objective is to increase the current food hub’s customer base and revenue stream through targeted business development efforts. This expansion will involve attracting new business and client relationships, alongside the creation of value-added products derived from existing fresh agricultural commodities such as fruits, vegetables, and seafood. Furthermore, West Georgia Farmers Cooperative intends to achieve Global Agricultural Practices (GAP) certification for both the food hub and its cooperative member farmers, ensuring quality standards and facilitating market access. The anticipated outcome of this project is a significant increase in the availability of locally produced agricultural products within the target region, directly benefiting farmers and consumers. This initiative will support regional food businesses and provide expanded market opportunities for agricultural producers. The project will positively impact the communities of west Georgia, supporting local food systems and strengthening the connection between producers and those seeking fresh food options. The cooperative seeks to bolster the agricultural economy and promote the efficient distribution of regional food resources.

original_description: The need for a sustainable food system infrastructure is critical to the successful future of Hawaii. Despite the unique challenges that this region faces, Common Ground Collective (CGC) and its partners are working to create food security and economic opportunity on Maui. Through field work and research, CGC has discovered that Maui has a significant amount of agricultural-zoned lands that are vastly underutilized, allowing for the creation of a new backyard-to-market supply chain that could drastically increase the amount of food provided to Maui residents. CGC recognizes the benefits and necessity of building strong network connections to support positive market growth in the agricultural sector and strengthen the community. With this project, CGC and partnering organizations will decrease Maui’s reliance on imported goods by enhancing the local food system, supporting local agricultural producers by providing distribution assistance and financial opportunities to new local growers, and expanding the capacity of local food businesses to contribute to the regional food system and those in need. A working model of the project will be shared with other rural communities as this project paves the way for a more sustainable food system and thriving global economy.
updated_description: Common Ground Collective (CGC) is undertaking a vital project to establish a sustainable food system infrastructure on Maui, recognizing the significant potential within the region’s agricultural-zoned lands. This project aims to dramatically increase the availability of food for Maui residents by creating a new backyard-to-market supply chain, utilizing existing farmland to reduce reliance on imported goods. The core of this initiative involves supporting local producers – including farmers and ranchers – by providing distribution assistance and fostering financial opportunities for new growers, while simultaneously expanding the capacity of local food businesses to contribute to the regional food system. Ultimately, this project seeks to improve access to agricultural products for consumers and other stakeholders. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened local food system capable of supporting a greater volume of food production and distribution across the island. CGC’s efforts will focus on establishing connections and streamlining processes to facilitate the growth of the agricultural sector. The project will support the advancement of food businesses, allowing them to play a key role in supplying food to the broader community and, consequently, generating economic opportunities for those involved in the production and distribution of food. The success of this project will serve as a working model, demonstrating a pathway toward a more sustainable food system and potentially replicable across other rural communities.

original_description: The Hawaiian islands lack adequate food processing infrastructure for increased food self-sufficiency and food security for residents and visitors alike. Meanwhile, Hawa'ii’s small farmers (66% of farms are under 9 acres in size) struggle to make a profit, facing the highest production costs in the US. The purpose of this project is to address these twin challenges of lack of food processing capacity for local crops, and increasing profits for small farmers through adding value to local crops. The Olohana Foundation recently acquired legacy industrial juicing equipment which we wish to put into operation once again, providing a valuable option to local farmers for adding value to their tropical fruit crops and reducing on-farm food waste. In collaboration with local fruit producers, we will pilot the production of two new local fruit products utilizing this food processing equipment. These final food products will be routed directly into the local food system via the Food Basket: Hawai’i Island’s food bank, and Hawai’i Farm to Car farmers market. By developing these two new fruit products, we will be directly growing the mid-tier value chain infrastructure for Hawai’i Island (the Big Island) and beyond, increasing local capacity for aggregation, processing and distribution. An estimated 33 local fruit producers will benefit from this new market for their crops, including B grade crops, which will help to reduce on-farm food waste. Additionally, we will reach an estimated 452 local consumers, providing an affordable, local and healthy food option.
updated_description: Olohana Foundation’s project addresses the critical need for enhanced food processing capabilities on Hawai’i Island, aiming to increase profits for local farmers and reduce on-farm food waste. The foundation will revitalize legacy industrial juicing equipment to facilitate the production of two new fruit products utilizing locally grown tropical crops. This initiative anticipates significant positive outcomes, including the creation of a new mid-tier value chain infrastructure, directly supporting farmers in aggregating, processing, and distributing their goods. A total of approximately 33 local farmers, including those producing crops graded as “B,” will benefit from this expanded market opportunity, contributing to a reduction in food discarded on farms. Furthermore, the project will reach an estimated 452 local consumers through direct distribution to the Food Basket, a local food bank, and the Hawai’i Farm to Car farmers market, providing them with accessible, locally sourced food options. The project’s anticipated impact extends beyond simple food distribution; it represents a tangible step toward strengthening the agricultural economy of Hawai’i Island by adding value to agricultural products and creating a more robust local food system. This approach supports the livelihoods of farmers and provides consumers with access to fresh, locally grown fruit, furthering the capacity for the island’s agricultural stakeholders to thrive.

original_description: When COVID-19 hit, Hawaiian supply chains were severely disrupted, resulting in empty store shelves. Residents became acutely aware of the need to re-establish resilient and secure local food systems across the Hawaiian Islands. In response to this disruption, momentum has developed with key players to rebuild the state’s food system, including farmers/producers, customers, institutions, policy makers, and a diverse funder group. During the pandemic, food hubs stepped in to flexibly fill voids in each locality and demonstrated competence and value to the community and members of the food value chain. Thus, the Hawaii Food Hub Hui, in partnership with the Hawaii Good Food Alliance, is building individual and collective capacity in Hawaii’s food hubs to ensure maximum sales for Hawaii’s numerous small and mid-size farmers and producers, and equitable access to fresh, healthy, local food for all. The primary project goal is to increase local food sales via Hawaii’s food hubs. This project aims to maximize the replicability of the proposed project in other regions, communities, and agricultural systems by 1) improving individual food hubs’ economic viability by supporting processing, aggregation, and distribution of local food products that are marketed throughout Hawaii; 2) strengthening relationships and cooperation within the Hawaii Food Hub Hui by facilitating regional value chain coordination; and 3) promoting new business opportunities and marketing strategies to increase public awareness of Hawaii’s food hubs.
updated_description: The Hawaii Food Hub Hui, in partnership with the Hawaii Good Food Alliance, is undertaking a project focused on increasing local food sales through Hawaii’s food hubs, aiming to rebuild resilient food systems across the Hawaiian Islands. This project will support the development and expansion of food hubs, which will involve the procurement of equipment and resources necessary for processing, aggregation, and distribution of local food products. Anticipated outcomes include increased sales for farmers and producers throughout the state, coupled with enhanced access to fresh, healthy, local food for all consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass a wide range of stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, processors, and distributors, as they seek to improve their market reach and operational efficiencies. Specifically, the project will facilitate regional value chain coordination within the Hawaii Food Hub Hui, creating stronger connections between producers and markets. Furthermore, the initiative will promote new business opportunities and marketing strategies, ultimately aiming to raise public awareness of the vital role played by Hawaii’s food hubs in supporting local agriculture and ensuring a reliable supply of food. The project's success relies on effectively connecting producers with consumers, creating a more robust and sustainable food system within the Hawaiian Islands.

awardee_name: Kokua Kalihi Valley Comprehensive Family Services
original_description: The Roots Food Hub Online project will create an online sales and marketing application to expand the Hub’s customer base, increase marketing through photographs and stories, and create new sales opportunities that will support local farmers to build sustainable businesses. Roots will use social media with links to the online platform to expand marketing. The project coincides with the re-launch of the Roots Food Hub mobile market, which will provide additional in-person sales venues and provide pick-up locations for online buyers.  Project activities include the following, 1) design and develop a web application for customers to purchase locally grown farm products through the Roots Food Hub, 2) build out the Roots website to include stories and photographs of local farms who sell their goods through the Food Hub, 3) integrate the web portal with the Food Hub POS to ensure accurate inventory and tracking of sales, 4) expand Instagram and other social media posting to link to the new web application, and 5) launch Mobile Market with designated pick-up areas and times for online orders. Deliverables include an online sales portal, social media marketing plan, and physical marketing with signage and flyers. Outcomes include increase in sales revenue for local farm products by 10% a year, increase in EBT sales revenue by 5% a year, and retention of 60% of farm suppliers each year. Intended beneficiaries include Food Hub local farm suppliers (25 in 2022) and customers in Kalihi and surrounding neighborhoods on Island of Oahu.
updated_description: Roots Food Hub will develop an online sales and marketing application designed to expand its customer base and increase marketing efforts through engaging photographs and compelling stories about local farms. The project encompasses the purchase and development of a web application for consumers to directly purchase locally grown farm products, alongside a revamped Roots website featuring these farm narratives and photographs. Anticipated outcomes of this initiative include a 10% annual increase in sales revenue for local farm products and a 5% annual increase in Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) sales revenue, alongside a retention rate of 60% for its farm suppliers each year. This project will benefit farmers and ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders participating through the Roots Food Hub, as well as consumers residing in Kalihi and surrounding neighborhoods on the Island of Oahu. The online platform will streamline the purchasing process for these consumers, facilitating access to fresh, locally sourced agricultural products. Furthermore, Roots Food Hub will expand its social media posting to drive traffic to the new web application. Finally, the project includes the launch of a mobile market with designated pick-up areas and times to support online orders, contributing to a more efficient supply chain. The primary beneficiaries of this work are the participating farmers and the consumers in the targeted communities, ultimately strengthening the local food system and bolstering economic opportunities for producers.

original_description: This project takes a multi-dimensional approach to building capacity in the Chicago local food system through business support for urban and rural farmers, earned income opportunities and access to a variety of sales channels including wholesale purchasing, direct to consumer sales, institutional purchasing, and optimizing the visibility and distribution of local produce by building upon Star Farm’s existing community relationships and institutional partnerships.  This project will forge new pathways for purchasing, troubleshooting and streamlining the farmer and institutional partner relations, and creatively promoting the consumption of local produce through existing programs such as the Star Farm Mobile Market, the Star Farm Fresh Market and Shared Kitchen. Making local produce accessible and culturally relevant to influence the long-term shopping patterns of individual consumers and institutional purchasers will be Star Farm’s position as the liaison between making sure farmers have support to build capacity and deliver high-quality, food-safe products and ensuring that partners and their clients are having their produce needs met and are incorporating the value of local produce into their programs and delivery of services.
updated_description: Star Farm’s project aims to bolster the capacity of the Chicago local food system through strategic business support for farmers, encompassing a range of sales channels including wholesale purchasing, direct to consumer sales, institutional purchasing, and the optimization of local produce distribution. This initiative will focus on establishing new pathways for purchasing, troubleshooting relationships with farmers and institutional partners, and creatively promoting the consumption of local produce utilizing existing programs such as the Star Farm Mobile Market and the Star Farm Fresh Market, alongside the Shared Kitchen. The core goal is to enhance access to local produce for consumers and institutional purchasers, solidifying Star Farm’s role as a key liaison. Specifically, the project will support farmers in delivering high-quality, food-safe products and ensure that partners and their clients are receiving the produce they need while incorporating local produce into their programs and services. The anticipated outcome is to strengthen the overall local food system by increasing the availability of locally produced agricultural products to a broader range of stakeholders. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other food system stakeholders, who will gain enhanced operational capabilities and expanded market reach. By streamlining purchasing processes and facilitating distribution networks, this project seeks to positively impact the supply chain and ultimately improve access to locally sourced agricultural products for a wider audience.

awardee_name: Board of Trustees of Western Illinois University
original_description:
The purpose of this project is to establish a department at Western Illinois University that will assist farmers and ranchers in Illinois with technical assistance in the form of business planning, local food webinars on best business practices , and local food stakeholder networking in Illinois.  This project will subcontract with FoodWorks in Southern Illinois to help create a curriculum, and provide small business technical assistance to FarmWorks clients as needed. The project  anticipates the creation of 80 jobs, 64 new farmer operations, 2 new meat processing facilities, 1 food hub business, and 12 locally owned grocery stores expanding local food purchases in the state of Illinois over the 3-year funding period. At least 3 case studies will be created to share information with other TA providers.

This project will also focus on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion of minority rural groups, in particular the large African American population in Southern Illinois. For example, the population in Alexander County Illinois is 31.8% African American (1,599 individuals). We will also focus on the Hispanic and West African communities that have developed in Western Illinois as a result of the meat packing employers, from Beardstown Illinois up to and including some communities in Iowa. Beardstown, Illinois is currently 38.0% Hispanic (2,261 individuals). 

This grant will focus solely on the business aspects of local food farming and the techniques of selling to intermediaries such as food hubs, institutions, and retail outlets.
updated_description: Western Illinois University will establish a department dedicated to providing technical assistance to farmers and ranchers throughout Illinois, focusing on business planning, and facilitating local food stakeholder networking. This project anticipates the creation of 80 jobs, 64 new farmer operations, two new meat processing facilities, one food hub business, and twelve locally owned grocery stores, all aimed at expanding local food purchases within the state over the three-year funding period. The project will subcontract with FoodWorks in Southern Illinois to assist with curriculum development and provide small business technical assistance to FarmWorks clients as needed. The anticipated outcomes include increased market access for local food producers and greater availability of regionally produced agricultural products for consumers. Specifically, the department will support farmers and ranchers in developing robust business strategies and connecting with intermediaries such as food hubs, institutions, and retail outlets. The project’s beneficiaries include farmers, ranchers, meat processors, and food stakeholders across Illinois. The department will focus on the operational aspects of establishing and growing these food businesses, contributing to a more connected local food system. The overall goal is to bolster the economic viability of regional food production and distribution networks.

original_description: Kansas Rural Center’s “Building the Central Kansas Food Corridor” project will connect farmers and food distribution partners in a twelve-county corridor in Kansas defined by Interstate 135, anchored by the population centers of Wichita in the south and Salina in the north. This project will achieve three objectives. First, creating a farmer led food hub in the region and providing technical assistance to farmers looking to move into wholesale markets. Second, Kansas Rural Center’s value chain coordinator will work to connect the food hub and other farmers in the region to mid-tier market channels including restaurants, grocery stores, schools and other institutions. Third, project partners, Common Ground Producers and Growers, St. John’s Missionary Baptist Church and Kansas Wesleyan University will work to develop mobile markets to improve access to local foods in communities with low access to fresh, nutritious food. This project pursues a holistic approach to developing the food system. It will simultaneously help farmers in the region who have production geared towards local markets access new market channels and increase access to fresh, local food for consumers across the region, with a special attention towards areas that currently have limited access.
updated_description: Kansas Rural Center’s “Building the Central Kansas Food Corridor” project aims to develop a robust regional food system within a twelve-county area defined by Interstate 135, centered around Wichita and Salina. This project will achieve this by establishing a farmer-led food hub, providing technical assistance to farmers interested in accessing wholesale markets, and facilitating connections between this hub and other regional producers with mid-tier market channels including restaurants, grocery stores, and institutions. The project will also involve Common Ground Producers and Growers, St. John’s Missionary Baptist Church, and Kansas Wesleyan University in the development of mobile markets. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is to increase access to locally produced agricultural products for consumers and farmers alike, with a particular focus on communities with limited access to fresh food. The beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, and food processors within the corridor, as well as consumers seeking local food options. The project seeks to strengthen the entire food system by creating pathways for regional producers to reach new markets and for consumers to obtain fresh, local products. Ultimately, this project intends to improve food access for all stakeholders within the Central Kansas region.

original_description: The mission of Locals Food Hub and Pizza Pub is to provide fresh, locally produced, nutrient rich foods to those that have been traditionally underserved, while increasing the economic health and long-term viability of small, often family-owned Kentucky producers. The food hub, which is in a Low Income/Low Access area, offers eggs, cheeses, fresh breads, meat, dairy, greens, veggies, local fruits, staples, artisan foods and more. Our program will support the aggregation, processing, packaging, storage, and distribution of local and regional food products, including value-added agricultural products, that are marketed locally to low- income low access neighborhoods through creation and implementation of the Locals Box program; developing marketing strategies for products from local and regional food producers to increase awareness and sales at our food hub location; and to facilitate regional food chain coordination and mid-tier value chain development through the lease of a refrigerated truck to deliver the Local Boxes and to improve transportation from producers to the food hub location.
updated_description: Locals Food Hub and Pizza Pub’s mission is to provide fresh, locally produced, nutrient-rich foods to farmers, ranchers, and processors within a Low Income/Low Access area, while simultaneously strengthening the economic health and long-term viability of small, often family-owned Kentucky producers. The project will focus on the aggregation, processing, packaging, storage, and distribution of local and regional food products, including value-added agricultural items, and will be implemented through the creation and operation of the Locals Box program, which delivers these goods to consumers in the designated neighborhood. A key component of this effort involves the acquisition of a refrigerated truck to facilitate efficient transportation of products from producers to the food hub location and to streamline the delivery of Locals Boxes to consumers. Anticipated outcomes include increased awareness and sales of locally produced goods at the food hub location, alongside the strengthening of regional food chain coordination and the development of mid-tier value chains. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers, ranchers, and processors who supply the food hub, as well as the consumers residing in the Low Income/Low Access area who will gain access to a wider variety of locally sourced food products. This initiative aims to establish a more robust and sustainable food system, supporting economic growth for regional producers and improving access to wholesome food for the local community.

original_description: Iverstine Farms Butcher’s (IFB) LFPP project will expand the availability of local meat subscriptions, creating more direct to consumer opportunities in Louisiana. IFB will partner with Coastal Plains Meat Company, a veteran-owned, USDA inspected, processor to allow for customer purchasing of whole animals. The project will enable participating producers to diversify product lines, adding value to harder to market cuts. The project will also enable diversification of market channels, targeting larger entities with the capacity for consistent purchasing, increasing delivery operations reach and scale. Through the creation of media assets and a promotional campaign centered on farmer’s stories, consumers will have a greater understanding of the region’s farm community and be empowered to connect with and support local ranching operations.
updated_description: Iverstine Farms Butcher’s (IFB) LFPP project aims to expand the availability of local meat subscriptions, creating more direct-to-consumer opportunities in Louisiana by partnering with Coastal Plains Meat Company, a veteran-owned, USDA inspected processor. This initiative will facilitate the purchase of whole animals by participating producers, allowing them to broaden their product lines and add value to cuts that are typically more difficult to market. The project anticipates increasing market channels for ranchers and farmers, specifically targeting larger entities capable of consistent purchasing and expanding the reach and scale of delivery operations. Through the creation of media assets and a promotional campaign centered on farmer stories, IFB intends to provide consumers with a greater understanding of the region’s farm community, empowering them to connect with and support local operations. The overall outcome is a strengthened local food system where producers can access expanded markets and consumers gain access to fresh, locally sourced meat. The primary beneficiaries of this project include ranchers, farmers, and processors within the Louisiana region, alongside consumers seeking access to locally produced goods. By streamlining purchasing processes and expanding market access, IFB seeks to positively impact the broader food system and support economic activity within the agricultural sector.

original_description: The Western MA Food Processing Center (WMFPC), a program of The Franklin County Community Development Corporation (FCCDC), supports food and farm businesses as they launch value-added products into the marketplace.  The FCCDC team provides technical support to businesses to start and grow.  The FCCDC will expand its impact and deepen connections among food producers by launching a Food Business Incubator Program that will provide businesses with the tools, information, and resources needed to scale production and make positive impacts in the local food system. The FCCDC team will partner with the Sustainable Business Network of Massachusetts to formalize an incubator model that FCCDC has piloted during the first part of 2022. The 6-month incubator program will serve farms and local food businesses as they develop marketing strategies, explore distribution opportunities, and improve food safety practices.   Graduates of the program will have more distribution opportunities, will implement food safety strategies and understand relevant federal regulations, and will enter new markets by implementing new marketing plans. Additionally, the FCCDC will support growing businesses by providing ongoing technical support and by fostering connections between producers and essential resources; including wholesale buyers, investors, and potential customers; at an annual New Venture Pitch event.
updated_description: The Western MA Food Processing Center, a program of The Franklin County Community Development Corporation (FCCDC), is undertaking a Food Business Incubator Program to support farmers and local food businesses in launching value-added products and expanding their market reach. This project will provide critical resources, including tools and information, to businesses seeking to scale production and positively impact the local food system. The FCCDC will formalize an incubator model in partnership with the Sustainable Business Network of Massachusetts, building upon a pilot program initiated in early 2022. The 6-month incubator program will serve a cohort of farms and food businesses as they develop comprehensive marketing strategies, explore viable distribution channels, and implement robust food safety practices. Graduates of the program will have increased access to distribution opportunities, will effectively implement food safety strategies, and will understand relevant federal regulations. Furthermore, participants will be equipped to enter new markets through the development and implementation of innovative marketing plans. The FCCDC will continue to support growing businesses by offering ongoing technical support and fostering connections between producers and key stakeholders, including wholesale buyers, investors, and potential customers, through an annual New Venture Pitch event. This project aims to strengthen the local food system by increasing the capacity of food businesses to operate efficiently and sustainably, ultimately benefiting farmers, ranchers, processors, and consumers. The anticipated outcome is a greater availability of locally produced agricultural products and a more resilient and connected food supply chain.

original_description: Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) have historically experienced significant barriers to entrepreneurship and the COVID-19 pandemic significantly widened those barriers. With the support of the Local Food Promotion Program (LFPP), Flavors LLC., will support 150 BIPOC local growers, farmers, and food business enterprises in the greater Prince George’s County region by launching a hybrid 12-week culinary micro-enterprise program. This program will, 1) improve business development knowledge and growth strategies to help grow and scale a profitable agriculture and culinary business through weekly workshops led by field experts, 2) provide equitable access to local growers, farmers, and culinary business advisors and funding opportunities through collaborative community partnerships, and 3) develop and launch the Flavors web and app-based virtual education platform for program delivery to local growers, farmers , and BIPOC food business enterprises to connect, network, and expand their business opportunities with food and beverage entrepreneurs, industry leaders, capital and investment resources, and service providers nationwide.
updated_description: Flavors LLC. will launch a 12-week culinary micro-enterprise program designed to support 150 BIPOC local growers, farmers, and food business enterprises within the greater Prince George’s County region, funded through the Local Food Promotion Program. The program will deliver a hybrid approach, combining weekly workshops led by field experts with the development and launch of a web and app-based virtual education platform. This platform will connect, network, and expand business opportunities for local growers, farmers, and food business enterprises, connecting them with industry leaders, capital and investment resources, and service providers nationwide. The anticipated outcome is to increase the operational capacity of these food businesses, leading to greater access to markets for agricultural products. The beneficiaries of this project include local food producers, such as ranchers, farmers, and processors, as well as the consumers who rely on these products. Flavors LLC. aims to streamline the application process for applicants conducting activities from a prescribed list, ultimately supporting the growth of regional food systems.

original_description: Smithereen Farm, a certified organic farm located in Pembroke, Maine, in collaboration with the nonprofit organization Greenhorns and other key community partners in the Downeast Maine region are proposing to create a comprehensive local food hub, culminating in the Minke Kitchen site. This project also honors the historical agricultural products and character of our region with specific infrastructure to process the Maine blueberries and seafood products that have defined Downeast Maine for generations.
updated_description: Smithereen Farm, in collaboration with Greenhorns and key community partners in the Downeast Maine region, is proposing a comprehensive local food hub culminating in the Minke Kitchen site, designed to stimulate economic growth within the agricultural sector. original_description: The need for a sustainable food system infrastructure is critical to the successful future of Hawaii. Despite the unique challenges that this region faces, Common Ground Collective (CGC) and its partners are working to create food security and economic opportunity on Maui. Through field work and research, CGC has discovered that Maui has a significant amount of agricultural-zoned lands that are vastly underutilized, allowing for the creation of a new backyard-to-market supply chain that could drastically increase the amount of food provided to Maui residents. CGC recognizes the benefits and necessity of building strong network connections to support positive market growth in the agricultural sector and strengthen the community. With this project, CGC and partnering organizations will decrease Maui’s reliance on imported goods by enhancing the local food system, supporting local agricultural producers by providing distribution assistance and financial opportunities to new local growers, and expanding the capacity of local food businesses to contribute to the regional food system and those in need. A working model of the project will be shared with other rural communities as this project paves the way for a more sustainable food system and thriving global economy.
updated_description: Common Ground Collective (CGC) is undertaking a vital project to establish a sustainable food system infrastructure on Maui, recognizing the critical need for food security and economic opportunity within the region. This initiative focuses on maximizing the utilization of Maui’s significant agricultural-zoned lands to create a new, direct-to-market supply chain, significantly increasing the availability of food for Maui residents. The project involves the development of a robust system to connect farmers and ranchers with consumers, and will support the growth of local food businesses, including processors and distributors, through targeted assistance. The anticipated outcomes include a reduction in Maui’s reliance on imported goods, increased economic activity among local producers, and enhanced capacity within the regional food system to serve those in need. This project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and food businesses, as well as consumers seeking locally sourced products. Ultimately, CGC aims to foster a thriving local food system that contributes to the well-being of the entire community. The project’s success will provide a working model for other rural communities seeking to build similar sustainable food systems and contribute to a more robust global economy.

original_description: This project will create a mid-tier Regional Food System that provides farmers access to critical aggregation and distribution infrastructure. This will enable Direct to Consumer farmers to significantly increase per-customer revenue through collaboration with other farms and value-add producers. An initial group of ten beginning farmers who are BIPOC or women-owned will be provided the benefits of a traditional food hub, aggregation and delivery services while allowing the farmer to maintain ownership of their customers. Each farm will be provided a branded ecommerce website, marketing support, training, order picking and delivery services. Subsequently, services will be expanded, with the project anticipating providing support to 130 farms. In addition, training will be provided to three traditional food hubs to incorporate project best practices.
updated_description: This project will create a mid-tier Regional Food System designed to provide farmers with access to critical aggregation and distribution infrastructure, ultimately enabling direct-to-consumer farmers to significantly increase per-customer revenue through collaboration with other farms and value-add producers. The initiative will initially support a group of ten beginning farmers who are BIPOC or women-led, providing them with the benefits of a traditional food hub, along with aggregation and delivery services while allowing them to retain ownership of their customer base. Each participating farm will receive a branded e-commerce website and marketing support to facilitate sales and outreach. Furthermore, the project anticipates expanding services to support 130 farms across the region, establishing a robust network for the distribution of agricultural products. This expanded system will connect farmers directly with consumers, creating new revenue streams and bolstering the local food economy. The project’s anticipated outcomes include increased access to locally produced food for consumers and strengthened economic viability for participating farms. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers involved, as well as the consumers who will gain access to a wider variety of regional food products. The project seeks to establish a more efficient and integrated food system, benefiting all stakeholders.

original_description: Small, limited resource, and historically underserved farmers are well behind the adoption curve for quality management systems (QMS) and technologies that improve production planning, monitoring, food safety, and marketing. Quality systems and technology currently available target high volume production, focusing on users with high-end computing hardware and peripherals. This is where the ag technology money is. Up In Farms, focused on the Mississippi Delta, is fielding an alternative QMS, deployed on smart phones and tablets, that farmers can implement at minimal up-front and operating cost: Farm QMS. With a light, responsive front end and intuitive user interface, Farm QMS is a digital gateway for capturing harvest and food safety data at the point of production. Once this information is entered, Farm QMS supports “digital twin” food tracking as products moves from harvest through the mid-tier value chain and on to end points such as grocers, institutions, food service, and consumers. Up In Farms’ deployment strategy is to establish core functions that serve farmers’ immediate needs, getting them started as users. Funds from this LFPP grant will add features that facilitate regional food chain coordination, mid-tier value chain development, tracking and marketing to reduce on-farm food waste, and indirect producer-to-consumer marketing, meeting several LFPP objectives.
updated_description: Up In Farms is developing Farm QMS, a mobile-based quality management system designed to address the specific needs of small farmers in the Mississippi Delta, who have historically lagged in adopting advanced production management technologies. This project will deliver a digital gateway for capturing harvest and food safety data directly at the point of production, utilizing smartphones and tablets to facilitate seamless data collection. Farm QMS supports “digital twin” food tracking as products move from harvest through the mid-tier value chain, encompassing connections to grocers, institutions, food service operations, and ultimately, consumers. The anticipated outcome is to reduce on-farm food waste through improved tracking and increased efficiency within the regional food chain. This initiative will benefit farmers by providing a tool to manage their operations more effectively, and consumers by ensuring traceability and transparency in the origin of their food products. The project will focus on streamlining connections between producers and buyers, offering support to processors, and facilitating direct producer-to-consumer marketing activities. Ultimately, the project aims to enhance the competitiveness of agricultural businesses in the region and improve access to locally produced goods for consumers. This system will support increased operational efficiency and product visibility across the entire food chain, representing a significant advancement for stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural goods.

original_description: Local Food for Local Families, an innovative network organized by Hopa Mountain, Mission West Community Development Partners, Local Food Marketplace, Livingston Food Resource Center, Community Food and Agriculture Coalition (CFAC), Western Montana Growers Cooperative, Great Northern Development Corporation (GNDC), and the Montana Food Bank Network, will support the development, coordination, and expansion of rural and tribal food hubs to increase access to Montana produced agricultural products. Project partners will provide training and support to producers, cooperatives, and food hubs to utilize a new business-to-business interconnected Local Food Marketplace software, offering these local food businesses expanded real-time options to sell food to one another and to grocers, food pantries, and institutions. This initiative builds upon lessons learned from our individual organizations’ COVID-19 response efforts as each entity worked to meet the needs of Montana producers, processors, and food pantries. Partners will focus on increasing the marketing capacity of rural farmers and ranchers along with the development of food hubs with shared-use kitchens in underserved communities. Hopa Mountain, Mission West, GNDC and CFAC will coordinate peer-to-peer producer and cooperative training to share successful local marketing efforts. Existing food hubs and cooperatives, such as the Livingston Food Resource Center and the Western Montana Growers Cooperative, will provide technical assistance to support the expansion of new food hubs and cooperatives. By working together, the Local Food for Local Families initiative will invest in food businesses and local economies while realizing a distributed food system that benefits local producers, businesses, food hubs and families.
updated_description: Hopa Mountain, in partnership with Mission West Community Development Partners, Local Food Marketplace, Livingston Food Resource Center, Community Food and Agriculture Coalition (CFAC), Western Montana Growers Cooperative, Great Northern Development Corporation (GNDC), and the Montana Food Bank Network, is undertaking a vital initiative to bolster Montana’s local food system. The purpose of this project is to develop, coordinate, and expand rural and tribal food hubs, ultimately increasing access to agricultural products produced within Montana. This project will leverage a new business-to-business interconnected Local Food Marketplace software, facilitating direct sales opportunities for farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders to connect with grocers, food pantries, and institutions. Livingston Food Resource Center and the Western Montana Growers Cooperative will provide technical assistance to support the expansion of new food hubs and cooperatives. By establishing these hubs, the project anticipates a strengthened local economy, increased market access for Montana producers, and improved distribution of food to families and communities. The anticipated outcome is a distributed food system that benefits all stakeholders involved – from the farmers and ranchers who produce the goods to the consumers who purchase them, and the food hubs that connect these groups. The primary beneficiaries of this project are Montana’s agricultural producers, food businesses, and the families who rely on access to locally produced food.

original_description:
Old Salt Co-op provides meat with integrity sourced from Montana landscapes its customers care about. Owned directly by the ranchers that supply it and by butchers, chefs, and creatives who run it, Old Salt is fueled by customers who return value back to the source. Old Salt launched based on what ranchers have known for too long. The current industrial system isn’t working for them. As processing has been consolidated, the independent ranch has been squeezed to the point where breaking even is the goal. With limited capacity, independent ranchers are lining up for years to get finished livestock custom processes or are sacrificing significant revenue by sending juvenile calves and other animals out of state to larger wholesalers. The meat ends up an anonymous commodity, purchased someplace by someone unknown.

We are working to change that by creating a culture and a market channel for local meat in Montana. With funding from LFPP, Old Salt will launch a meat share program that includes evaluation of the ecological outcomes and ranch traceability. We will grow this program to directly work with 10 ranchers in the first two years and service no less than 4,000 subscribers. We will couple that with a robust marketing effort that will grow interest in local meat that is from animals raised “with integrity.” It is our hope that through the collaborative work of Old Salt, independent ranchers in our state can thrive and connect with their local market.
updated_description: Old Salt Co-op is undertaking a project to address the challenges faced by independent ranchers in Montana, aiming to establish a direct market channel for locally produced meat. The core of this initiative involves collaborating with ten ranchers over the first two years, with the goal of servicing at least four thousand subscribers through a meat share program. This program will incorporate an evaluation of ecological outcomes and robust ranch traceability, ensuring transparency and accountability throughout the supply chain. The anticipated outcome is a thriving market for Montana-raised meat, where ranchers receive fair compensation for their products and consumers gain access to high-quality meat sourced with integrity. Ultimately, Old Salt Co-op seeks to strengthen the connection between farmers and consumers, creating a sustainable system that supports the livelihood of ranchers and provides a valuable food source for the community. The beneficiaries of this project include the ranchers themselves, who will benefit from increased market access and financial stability, as well as the consumers who will have access to meat produced with a commitment to quality and responsible farming practices. The project focuses on creating a stronger local food system, promoting direct relationships between producers and the people who purchase their goods, thereby strengthening the overall Montana agricultural economy.

original_description: The Yellowstone Valley Food Hub’s Expanding Mid-Tier Distribution Networks to Benefit Montana farmers and wholesale buyers project seeks to expand the Yellowstone Valley Food Hub's wholesale market capabilities through the purchase of supplies and software, hiring of an additional staff person, and rental of a warehouse space. The Yellowstone Valley Food Hub (YVFH) is a cooperatively owned food hub in Billings, MT whose mission is to connect local farmers and ranchers to local consumers. The cooperative owners are the farmers, ranchers, bakers, and makers themselves. These cooperative owners will also be the primary beneficiaries of this project. Currently the YVFH serves consumers of central and eastern Montana through a direct-to-consumer online ordering platform. While this direct-to-consumer market has helped the YVFH grow to where it is today, there is incredible benefit and potential growth if it were to expand the wholesale arm of its business. Through this project the YVFH would be able to begin cultivating relationships with grocery stores, restaurants, caterers, and other wholesale buyers. This expansion would strengthen our regional food system, provide direct economic benefit to farmers and ranchers, increase our community's access to local food, streamline chef and grocery store manager's ability to access local food, and bolster Central and Eastern Montana's rural agriculture economy.
updated_description: The Yellowstone Valley Food Hub’s project aims to significantly expand its wholesale market capabilities to better serve Montana farmers and wholesale buyers. This expansion will be achieved through strategic investments, including the purchase of necessary supplies and software, the rental of a warehouse space, and the hiring of an additional staff person. The Yellowstone Valley Food Hub, a cooperatively owned food hub based in Billings, MT, is focused on connecting local producers—farmers, ranchers, bakers, and makers—with consumers in central and eastern Montana through its existing online ordering platform. The project’s anticipated outcomes include the establishment of direct relationships with a wider range of wholesale buyers, such as grocery stores, restaurants, and caterers, thereby strengthening the regional food system and providing direct economic benefit to Montana producers. These investments are expected to increase access to local food for consumers and streamline the procurement process for chefs and grocery store managers. Ultimately, this project will bolster the rural agriculture economy of Central and Eastern Montana by facilitating increased sales and market opportunities for farmers and ranchers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the Montana producers, processors, and stakeholders involved in the local food supply chain, alongside the consumers who will gain improved access to fresh, regionally sourced products.

In partnership with Ellison Farms,
updated_description: Watauga Meats and Butchery’s project aims to expand value-added agricultural product availability, facilitate producer-to-consumer marketing programs, and reduce food waste through a new Food Market and Meat Hub located within a repurposed facility. original_description: Currently, high quality aseptic food processing is only available to large companies who have the finances and resources available to develop and launch products with high minimum order quantities with significant financial risk. SinnovaTek has right-sized its thermal processing systems in order to construct a pathway for entrepreneurs and small companies to have access to advanced aseptic processing technologies as a pathway to creating value-added food products. Its subsidiary, FirstWave, exists as a small scale aseptic copacker to enable product launches with no minimum order quantities. Even in this scenario, many small brands do not have the expertise or resources to properly move through the commercialization process. They are often limited in knowledge of the commercialization steps including product definition, formulation, and testing and often do not have the finances available to handle these costs. With this grant opportunity, SinnovaTek will create a commercialization and training accelerator for these small, local brands to move through this process. The outcome will be a product commercialization for 12 small companies, split into 4 cohorts, that will utilize local food ingredients. Through this accelerator, these companies will be trained in thermal processing, food safety, and the entrepreneurial path to store shelves. They’ll develop products alongside industry proven resources to prepare their products for commercial launch with sales samples in hand. The selected participants will come out of this program with a product ready for commercial success and the knowledge to repeat the process and sustainably grow their business.
updated_description: SinnovaTek has developed a project to facilitate the commercialization of value-added food products for small companies and local brands. This initiative will provide access to advanced aseptic processing technologies, utilizing its subsidiary, FirstWave, as a small-scale aseptic copacker. The project will result in the creation of 12 distinct products, developed by small companies, organized into four cohorts and utilizing local food ingredients. These products will be prepared for commercial launch, including the production of sales samples. The intended beneficiaries of this project are local farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the regional food system. SinnovaTek’s goal is to support these stakeholders by streamlining the commercialization process, encompassing product definition, formulation, and testing, ultimately leading to a viable product ready for market introduction. The project anticipates the successful launch of twelve products, generating opportunities for local food businesses to expand their operations and increase access to markets for their goods. The project will support local food systems by allowing for the creation of new products and increasing the availability of regionally produced agricultural products to consumers.

original_description:

Rolling Grocer 19 (RG19) will achieve this goal through four main objectives. Expanding and promoting offerings of local foods in a unique discount grocery store which offers subsidized pricing tiers and market match incentives.  Expanding a newly-established Rural Access Delivery Program which brings healthy local foods to low-income, low- access seniors and others in rural areas.  Increasing exposure to and purchases of locally-produced products through the development of a new value-added offering of prepared foods, providing a healthy convenience food option. Creating new and expanded market opportunities for local farmers and ranchers to sell their products to the Hudson community through the above initiatives.

updated_description: Rolling Grocer 19 aims to enhance access to high-quality, locally-produced products for low-income residents of Hudson, New York, and surrounding rural areas of Columbia County, while simultaneously expanding market opportunities for local farmers and ranchers.
