The primary beneficiaries of Rolling Grocer 19 will be local farmers and ranchers, who will gain increased sales channels and access to a broader customer base, as well as consumers seeking affordable and nutritious food options. The project’s success will be measured by the volume of locally produced goods sold, the number of individuals accessing these goods, and the overall impact on the local food system.

original_description:
The Hub is a farmer owned Local Food aggregation site with a market and eatery in Tupper Lake, NY selling product from over 39 area farms, marketing both raw and processed farm products directly to consumers since 2017.  The focus will be on utilizing key farm products that are economically viable to produce in the region, bringing product from low-income farmers to low access areas.  
The goal is to support and expand the local food economy by providing institutions with analytical assistance and logistical support, increasing aggregation and distribution efficiencies, supporting market venues, enabling microprocessor startups through our incubator kitchen and support team, preserving product value from excess harvest during glut, bringing new value-added products to market and educating consumers.
The goal is to handle $100,000 worth of produce in year one, performing value-added processing on 35%, increasing by 25% each year, serving institutions, retail, wholesale, food service and individuals.  
By year two the goal is to operate a full-scale kitchen facility enabling co-packing in a business incubator environment.
In three years, the project plans to handle over $400,000 in local produce from over 80 small family farms existing largely in very low-income areas, and incubate a minimum of ten new value-added food processing businesses.
The applicant and collaborators’ expertise in cost accounting, retail and wholesale marketing, farming and food production will enable us to efficiently achieve these goals.
The funding will allow purchase of specialty processing equipment and labor for analysis, coordination, and support.
updated_description: The Hub’s purpose is to establish a robust local food aggregation site in Tupper Lake, NY, facilitating the sale of products from over 39 area farms to consumers since 2017, with a focus on economically viable regional agricultural production and bringing products from low-income farmers to low-access areas. The project will involve the purchase of specialty processing equipment, alongside the development of a full-scale kitchen facility enabling co-packing within a business incubator environment, to achieve anticipated outcomes including handling over $400,000 in local produce from over 80 small family farms, and incubating a minimum of ten new value-added food processing businesses by year three. This initiative will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and food processors within the region, as well as consumers seeking access to fresh, locally sourced goods. The Hub will serve institutions, retail outlets, wholesale buyers, food service providers, and individual consumers. The anticipated results are a significant expansion of the local food economy, with the project aiming to increase aggregation and distribution efficiencies, support market venues, and preserve product value through glut management. By year two, the organization will operate a fully functional kitchen facility, supporting a business incubator environment, and by year three, the Hub will have expanded its reach to effectively serve a broadened network of stakeholders. This project’s success relies on the applicant’s and collaborators’ combined expertise in cost accounting, retail and wholesale marketing, and food production, and the funding will allow for the necessary resources to execute these goals.

original_description: Ocean farmers currently lack expertise in kelp farming and e?cient pathways to market. This project will improve economic outcomes for ocean-based farmers in New England by creating e?cient pathways to scale and facilitating the market for kelp-based value-added products. To accomplish this goal, this project will recruit and train new kelp farmers, increase the e?ciency of processing the raw material into a high-quality, shelf-stable dry powder, and promote the use of kelp in a diverse set of end products. The project will be assisted by GreenWave, a non-pro?t with the goal of increasing regenerative coastal farming, leading processor Inland Seafood, R&D and supply chain experts JPG Resources, , and a number of early-adopting kelp farmers. This project will improve the kelp drying e?ciency for preservation and processing for customers, and the project will seek new customers for kelp products. The project will test products from two new species of kelp, Rockweed and Dulse with the goal of understanding the most valuable uses. As part of this work, a market analysis will help guide future product development and chart a path for broader kelp uptake. Our project will develop the necessary infrastructure to support a sustainable market for kelp products, thus incentivizing coastal harvesters to begin farming to increase and diversify revenues.
updated_description: GreenWave will initiate a project focused on enhancing economic opportunities for ocean-based farmers in New England by establishing efficient pathways to scale and promoting the market for kelp-based value-added products. This project will involve the recruitment of new kelp farmers and the improvement of processing techniques for raw kelp material, specifically aiming to produce a high-quality, shelf-stable dry powder. Furthermore, the project will explore the utilization of two new kelp species – Rockweed and Dulse – to determine the most valuable applications for these materials. A market analysis will be conducted to guide future product development and facilitate broader adoption of kelp products. The project anticipates increasing the efficiency of kelp drying for preservation and processing, ultimately creating new customer bases for kelp products. The intended outcomes include the development of a sustainable market for kelp products, which will incentivize coastal harvesters to begin farming and diversify their revenues. This project will benefit farmers, processors, and other stakeholders within the New England coastal region. The anticipated results will improve access to locally produced agricultural products for consumers and contribute to the growth of regional food businesses. The project’s success is predicated on the development of appropriate infrastructure to support these activities.

original_description: Healthy Oklahoma Nutrition Alliance’s (HONA) project will stand up an online market pilot that will serve as the starting point for the incubation of central Oklahoma’s first local food hub. The project aims to simplify the procurement process on behalf of local farmers and retailers, and to increase access to wholesale and non-profit markets. The project’s coordinated systems-approach will provide a much-needed quantitative understanding of supply and demand trends for Oklahoma’s local foods, which will be used to incubate and continue to refine a new mid-tier local food distribution center. The project will be guided by a diverse advisory board of partners across farmers, extension agents, business development professionals, local food purchasers and other support organizations, who will work together to improve access to and procurement of local food by streamlining product through one centralized ordering platform.
updated_description: Healthy Oklahoma Nutrition Alliance’s project will establish an online market pilot designed to initiate the development of central Oklahoma’s first local food hub. This project aims to streamline the procurement process for local farmers and retailers, ultimately increasing access to wholesale and non-profit markets. The core of this initiative involves the creation of a centralized ordering platform intended to facilitate the movement of agricultural products. Anticipated outcomes include a greater volume of local food sales and a strengthened market for Oklahoma’s producers. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the agricultural supply chain, as well as consumers seeking locally sourced goods. The project’s coordinated systems-approach will provide a much-needed quantitative understanding of supply and demand trends for Oklahoma’s local foods, which will be used to incubate and continue to refine a new mid-tier local food distribution center. The project will support a stronger market for agricultural products and further development of the local food system. The centralized ordering platform will serve as a key tool for connecting producers with buyers, and fostering greater economic activity within the agricultural sector.

original_description:
This project will increase access to local food in workplaces and neighborhoods, build equitable access and distribution infrastructure, and support food sovereignty and economic development for underserved communities in three different geographies in the United States.  Social barriers, wealth disparity, knowledge gaps, and lack of coordination in the regional value chain can result in limited access to local food markets for members of disadvantaged communities and for the employees of workplaces and institutions in the same city or geography.  Our approach is to facilitate a shared online market model serving both workplaces and surrounding communities, built on the unique strengths and interdependencies of each community’s local food system and using a powerful, proven, purpose-built open-source platform solution.  

In this project, Open Food Network USA will partner with organizations from three historically excluded or underserved communities who will receive subawards to implement online food hubs that support food access and food businesses, center culture and relationships in supply chain operations and wealth creation, include institutions and nearby workplaces in supporting community food infrastructure, and improve health outcomes for everyone while capturing knowledge and best practices for the benefit of other communities doing similar work.  Project beneficiaries include small scale producers and local aggregators, community members, workplace employees in or near subject communities, and community-based organizations who will participate in the accomplishment of the project’s four goals: expanded local market participation; new businesses; technology support; and evaluation, learning, and reproducibility.
updated_description: Open Food Network USA’s purpose is to increase access to local food within workplaces and neighborhoods, building equitable access and distribution infrastructure while supporting food sovereignty and economic development across three distinct geographies in the United States. This project will develop a shared online market model, leveraging a powerful, proven, open-source platform solution, to connect farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders directly with consumers and workplace employees. Anticipated outcomes include the establishment of robust local food systems that improve access to regionally produced agricultural products, fostering new businesses and supporting economic growth within the targeted communities. The project will directly benefit small-scale producers, local aggregators, community members, and workplace employees in or near the project areas, ultimately aiming to improve access to food for all. These stakeholders will participate in the operation of the shared online market, focusing on establishing relationships and streamlining supply chain operations. The project’s successful completion will lead to increased participation in local food markets, the launch of new food-related businesses, and the generation of valuable knowledge to be replicated in other communities. Through this initiative, Open Food Network USA intends to facilitate the operation of efficient and effective food systems, providing greater economic opportunities for food producers and enhancing access to fresh, regional food for consumers.

original_description:
On the north coast of Oregon, local producers continue to seek new ways to sustain and grow their operations, while consumers are increasingly looking to connect and interact with their food system. Over 100 small-scale farmers, ranchers, foragers, and fishers provide food for rural North Coast Oregon and Southwest Washington. The demand for local food exceeds supply, and the region's producers struggle to access resources needed to scale their businesses.

The North Coast Food Web and our partners' LFPP proposal focuses on developing the infrastructure for small farms and food businesses to service customers within 100 miles of Astoria, OR. We will ensure that farmers and food businesses have the comprehensive support they need to serve their communities. We will formalize our comprehensive food business support services to provide training, technical assistance, and one-on-one support for these emerging operations. We will grow our kitchen incubator helping those interested in value-added production, upgrade and expand our offerings, and restart a delivery program via our online farmers market to draw in new customers. We are supported by a strong network of partners who are deeply invested in our coastal community and have served as informal leaders, advisors, and partners for the last decade. As we formalize and expand the programs of the North Coast Food Web, we will create a more resilient food system increasing profitability and reducing risk for local farm and food businesses.
updated_description: North Coast Food Web is undertaking a vital project to bolster the local food system on Oregon’s north coast, addressing the existing imbalance between supply and demand for locally produced food. This initiative centers around developing essential infrastructure to support small farms and food businesses within a 100-mile radius of Astoria, Oregon, including the upgrade and expansion of a kitchen incubator and the reinstatement of a delivery program through an online farmers market. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened local food network, increasing profitability and reducing risk for farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of food. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the numerous small-scale producers who operate within the region, as well as the consumers who seek access to fresh, local food options. By facilitating direct connections between producers and their communities, the North Coast Food Web aims to create a more resilient and economically viable food system, strengthening the position of these businesses and ensuring their continued operation. The project will provide support to these businesses, helping them to attract new customers and enhance their market reach. This comprehensive support will contribute to a more sustainable and robust local food economy on the north coast.

awardee_name: The Meetinghouse on Atherton- DBA Taproot Community Kitchen
original_description: Taproot Kitchen has an established culinary venture that provides adults with autism and intellectual disabilities critical job training while also utilizing fresh food gleaned from local farms. This Taproot project is ready to increase its capacity to partner with other organizations and regions and further support local farmers, food-focused entrepreneurs, and marginalized community members. The proposed project will formally partner with local/regional agriculture producers, small businesses, entrepreneurs, and human services agencies to implement a Community Kitchen and Seconds Market. At the center of the project are the local farmers and producers, who will be providing the community with access to fresh, locally grown fruits, vegetables, and meats. The Taproot Community Kitchen will provide access to an equipped commercial kitchen that will support the creation of value-added products, the preservation, and storage of agricultural products. The Seconds Market (less than perfect and surplus goods) will provide producers with access to new partnership markets for sell of their “seconds” and surplus produce. Funds received through the Local Food Promotion Program will be used to hire an Operations Manager and Kitchen Manager, who will establish a Seconds Market by May 2023 and develop a fully equipped, managed and operational shared Taproot Community Kitchen by Oct 2023. The overarching goal is to create a sustainable food system in this rural, agriculturally rich region. The objectives outlined will focus on the development of a shared responsibility for the production, supply, and consumption of safe and nutritious food grown locally.
updated_description: Taproot Kitchen is undertaking a project to establish a Community Kitchen and Seconds Market, designed to bolster local food systems within a rural, agriculturally rich region. This initiative will involve the acquisition of resources to construct a fully equipped commercial kitchen and the development of a market for selling surplus agricultural products. The anticipated outcomes of this project include increased access to fresh, locally grown fruits, vegetables, and meats for consumers and stakeholders, alongside new market opportunities for farmers, ranchers, and food processors. The core of the project centers on collaborating with local producers to facilitate the creation of value-added products, the preservation, and storage of agricultural goods, ultimately strengthening the supply chain. Specifically, Taproot Kitchen aims to establish a shared facility where stakeholders can manage and distribute these resources. The Seconds Market will provide a channel for producers to sell their “seconds” and surplus produce, increasing their market reach. By May 2023, the project will achieve the establishment of the Seconds Market, and by October 2023, a fully equipped, managed, and operational shared Taproot Community Kitchen will be realized, representing a significant step towards a sustainable local food system. This project will benefit a wide range of stakeholders, including those involved in the production and distribution of agricultural goods, and will contribute to a more robust and resilient regional food economy.

Farm Fresh RI is undertaking a project to significantly expand market opportunities for local producers within the state’s emergency food system. This initiative aims to implement a Sustainability Advisory Group to identify pathways to financial viability for over 80 farmers and fishermen, enhance and grow the wholesale market for 50+ locally-grown agricultural products, and expand the wholesale market for 30+ locally-harvested, wild-caught seafood. The core of this project involves establishing robust connections between these producers and state’s emergency food buyers, anticipating increased sales volume for farmers and fishermen. The anticipated outcome is a more resilient and reliable wholesale market for local producers and harvesters, capable of meeting the needs of the emergency food system while mitigating supply chain vulnerabilities. Ultimately, the project will benefit farmers, fishermen, and the broader network of stakeholders involved in the emergency food system, facilitating greater access to markets and strengthening the overall system’s capacity. The project will focus on expanding wholesale sales to emergency food customers and strengthening the state’s emergency food system.

original_description:
Town Made serves as a food processing, aggregation, and marketing hub, serving Washington County Rhode Island and beyond.
Town Made seeks USDA LFPP funding to implement a scholarship fund to foster access to its commercial kitchen facilities to under-served communities, expand its food production operational capabilities, and provide business and marketing support to assist local food entrepreneurs in bringing their products to market.
updated_description: Town Made seeks USDA LFPP funding to establish a scholarship fund, thereby fostering access to its commercial kitchen facilities for farmers, ranchers, and other food production stakeholders within Washington County Rhode Island and beyond. This project will enable the expansion of Town Made’s operational capabilities through the acquisition of resources to support increased food production volumes. Specifically, Town Made aims to enhance its capacity for aggregating and processing agricultural products, facilitating a more robust supply chain for regional markets. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is to increase the availability of locally and regionally produced food items for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include local food entrepreneurs, small-scale producers, and the broader food system within Washington County Rhode Island, who will gain access to essential infrastructure and marketing support. By providing a centralized hub, Town Made intends to streamline the process of bringing food products to market, ultimately supporting the growth of regional food businesses and improving access to fresh, locally sourced food for consumers. This initiative will strengthen the connections between food producers and consumers, creating a more efficient and resilient local food system.

original_description:
Red Tomato, other food hubs, and local food advocates must become more effective intermediaries beyond physically bringing local product to market for small- and mid-sized farms to stay viable. This project seeks to add value through co-branding and co-marketing of Eco-certified fruit, a collaborative program among growers, agricultural scientists and extension, and mission driven marketers, to differentiate local and sustainably grown fruit in the Northeast region by building trust in the environmental, economic, and cultural care of regional growers.
Obj. 1: Investigate, identify, and leverage the co-branding/co-marketing opportunities held by small and midsized fruit growers in the Northeast that will reach and connect with eaters.

Objective 2: Develop & deploy marketing tools, resources, and opportunities in partnership with growers, processors, and other institutional partners as a part of a larger strategy that allows Red Tomato to reach beyond retailers and connect with eaters and consumers, building a connected and engaged community that supports and purchases local and regional products.
Objective 3: Grow and measure the impact of the Eco Program and co-branding strategy on the eating community through sales and social media metrics.
updated_description: Red Tomato seeks to enhance the viability of small and mid-sized fruit growers in the Northeast region by establishing a robust co-branding and co-marketing program focused on Eco-certified fruit. This project will develop a collaborative strategy involving growers, agricultural scientists, and mission-driven marketers to differentiate regional fruit products through trusted messaging regarding their environmental, economic, and cultural care. Specifically, Red Tomato will investigate and identify co-branding/co-marketing opportunities held by these fruit growers, ultimately building a connected and engaged community of consumers who are willing to purchase local and regional products. The anticipated outcome is to increase sales and brand recognition of these growers’ products within the Northeast market. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers who produce the fruit, as well as the processors and other stakeholders involved in the supply chain. By streamlining the marketing efforts, Red Tomato aims to connect growers directly with consumers, building a more resilient and sustainable food system. The project’s success will be measured through sales figures and social media engagement, providing key data to demonstrate the impact of the Eco Program and the overall co-branding strategy.

original_description: The Catawba Farm and Food Coalition’s funding will support the expansion of opportunities for local farmers in rural areas and create more local, healthy food access for consumers located in food deserts. This project will connect local farmers to an already developed and implemented online farmers market and year-round brick-and-mortar farmers market store, both of which are designed and working to increase product sales for local South Carolina farmers. It will also create access to a new mobile fresh food market utilizing the refrigerated van owned by the coalition. Through working in rural areas with our partners, this project will also allow greater access to local food in food deserts throughout the Upstate and Piedmont Regions of South Carolina. Funding will allow the Catawba Farm and Food Coalition to expand on current delivery routes and product pick up routes through the counties of Chester, Fairfield, Lancaster, Union, York and the Catawba Indian Nation. The expected outcome of this project is to increase product sales for local South Carolina farmers through multiple market avenues and to increase access to local healthy food products through direct producer-to-consumer sales and producer-to-retail connections.
updated_description: The Catawba Farm and Food Coalition’s project aims to expand opportunities for local farmers in rural areas and create more local, healthy food access for consumers. This initiative will leverage an already developed online farmers market and a year-round brick-and-mortar farmers market store to increase product sales for South Carolina farmers, while also deploying a mobile fresh food market utilizing a refrigerated van. Through collaboration with partners in counties including Chester, Fairfield, Lancaster, Union, York, and the Catawba Indian Nation, the project will facilitate greater access to local food in areas designated as food deserts throughout the Upstate and Piedmont Regions of South Carolina. The project’s anticipated outcomes include increased product sales for local farmers via multiple market avenues, coupled with enhanced direct producer-to-consumer and producer-to-retail connections. The primary beneficiaries of this work will be local farmers, ranchers, and food processors, alongside consumers seeking access to fresh, local food. The project will support increased sales for those stakeholders and expand the availability of locally produced agricultural products. The Catawba Farm and Food Coalition intends to achieve this by strategically expanding existing delivery routes and product pick-up routes to reach a wider range of consumers and strengthen connections within the regional food system.

original_description:
Our goal is to do our part to balance the scales of economic opportunity for those have not enjoyed the same opportunities as others. To do so, the aim of the store is to provide a needed channel to the market for local growers and producers while at the same time providing an opportunity for our team members to utilize their talents in a positive environment and bring the benefits of locally grown product to our community. If successful, the store can tangibly and sustainably benefit these three constituencies while at the same time serve as an example for others of like minds. Since our inception, we have operated at a significant cash deficit. We have funded this deficit out of our own retirement savings.
While we can do so for a time, there is a limit to our ability to continue to do so.
This deficit is a largely a result of inadequate customer traffic. We will use the funds provided from this grant to address this shortcoming by raising awareness in our nearby communities of our product offerings and making them more accessible in the store. By elevating customer traffic, we will reach a breakeven sales point and become a self-sustained enterprise. This grant can be a crucial lynchpin in our ability to do so.
updated_description: Our store’s purpose is to create a market channel for local growers and producers while simultaneously providing a positive environment for team members to utilize their talents and bring locally grown products to the community. This project will focus on elevating customer traffic to reach a sales point that allows the store to become self-sustaining. Specifically, the grant funds will be used to enhance the store’s accessibility and visibility within nearby communities, thereby increasing the flow of customers. The anticipated outcome is a sustainable business model benefiting farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the local food system. This initiative seeks to improve access to locally produced agricultural products for consumers and create a viable business that can operate independently. The project will directly benefit those involved in producing agricultural goods, ensuring a market for their products and a continued opportunity to contribute to the community’s food supply. By attracting more customers, the store will achieve a point where it can cover its operating costs and maintain its operations without relying on personal funds. Ultimately, this project aims to establish a robust and resilient local food business, strengthening the connections within the community and supporting the producers who supply it.

original_description:
The Swamp Rabbit Café and Grocery (SRCG) was founded ten years ago with the mission to support a just and sustainable food system that allows local farmers to thrive. Currently purchasing local and regional products from over 300 producers, the SRCG stands by this mission in every transaction and decision it makes, and has purchased more than $8.5 million from local farmers since its founding ten years ago. SRCG is the premium buyer in our region of foods from local farmers. SRCG also has a strong social media presence and a strategic physical location on the busy Swamp Rabbit Trail, creating a reach of tens of thousands of consumers online, and up to 4,000 in-person consumers on a busy day.
Using this leverage, existing network, and reputation, SRCG will reach, support, and promote local farmers, particularly new, small, and disadvantaged farmers.
Despite the rise in interest in local foods and the work we've done and continue to do to support local farms, the challenges to succeed are numerous for small, new, and disadvantaged farmers. Through this project, SRCG will provide intentional support to new, beginning, small, and disadvantaged farmers, including guidance on packaging, food safety, and marketing. With additional staffing and a promotion plan that highlights local farmers, SRCG will promote local farmers and food to consumers.
By the end of the 3-year project period, the SRCG will increase the number of local producers from whom it purchases from 300 to 390, and increase the amount of local produce purchased from local producers by 60%. This represents an increase of $1.05M annually in purchases from local farmers by the end of 3 years. SRCG will also increase its base of customers buying local food by 25%.
Our existing and future network of farmers will benefit from increased purchases of their products from SRCG. Small, beginning and disadvantaged farmers who need additional support to bring their products to market will benefit from the services provided by SRCG and partner organizations. All producers selling products to the SRCG will benefit from the increased marketing, advertising, and promotion by the SRCG, enabling them to increase sales and their customer base. In addition to benefiting producers, this project will increase consumers’ ability to purchase local food from local and regional producers.
updated_description: Swamp Rabbit Café and Grocery (SRCG) is undertaking a three-year project focused on significantly expanding its role as a key purchaser of goods from local farmers, aiming to increase the number of producers from whom it purchases by 90, reaching 390, and boosting the volume of local produce purchased by 60%, representing a $1.05 million annual increase in local farmer sales. This initiative will primarily involve strengthening existing relationships and establishing new connections with farmers, ranchers, and food processors within the region, supporting their ability to bring products to market. The anticipated outcomes include a 25% increase in the base of customers buying local food, alongside a substantial growth in the overall supply of local agricultural products available to consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the local farmers and ranchers who will receive increased purchases of their products from SRCG, as well as the consumers who will benefit from greater access to regionally produced food. Furthermore, the project will aim to support food processors and other stakeholders involved in the agricultural supply chain. By expanding its purchasing network and actively promoting local food options, SRCG intends to create a more robust and sustainable local food system, bolstering economic opportunities for regional producers and providing consumers with a wider selection of high-quality, locally sourced goods. Ultimately, this project seeks to elevate the position of SRCG as a central facilitator, contributing to the expansion and success of numerous agricultural businesses within the region.

original_description:
The Appalachian Region Winery Incubator, a value chain facility, will create and expand businesses and provide education and training for those wishing to enter the Wine and Grape Industry. The Facility will provide co-working space, in-demand skills training, entrepreneurship and business support growing the regional Industry. In the target region, the Nine Lakes of Eastern Tennessee American Viticultural Area (AVA), there are currently 232 acres of vineyards and 29 wineries. There are vineyards in every county and wineries in all but two of the fourteen counties. According to the Tennessee Farm Winegrowers Alliance, with moderate industry growth an anticipated 1,000 acres of vineyards could be needed in the next 5 – 8 years supporting an estimated 50 wineries and satellite facilities. According to the Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics, University of Tennessee, the total variable cost for a winery producing 10,000 gallons on an annual basis was estimated at $911,895.00, annual fixed cost was estimated at $178,260.00 and annual debt service payment was estimated to be
$80,928.00. These are insurmountable costs for many who wish to enter the industry. A value chain incubator facility is a critical resource for equitable growth. The grant funds will be used to equip and operate a newly constructed complex to serve as a winery incubator.
updated_description: The Appalachian Region Winery Incubator is designed to create and expand businesses within the wine and grape industry, offering a critical resource for equitable growth in the Nine Lakes of Eastern Tennessee American Viticultural Area. This project will establish a newly constructed complex to serve as a winery incubator, utilizing grant funds to equip and operate this facility. The anticipated outcome is the development of increased vineyard acreage and a greater number of wineries, potentially expanding to approximately 1,000 acres of vineyards and 50 wineries within the next 5-8 years, supported by satellite facilities. This initiative directly benefits farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the regional grape and wine industry, aiming to reduce financial barriers for entry, particularly considering the significant costs associated with winery operations – approximately $911,895 in variable costs, $178,260 in fixed costs, and $80,928 in annual debt service for a winery producing 10,000 gallons annually. Ultimately, the incubator will assist in fostering a more robust and accessible wine industry within the Nine Lakes region, providing a supportive environment for businesses to flourish and increase the availability of locally produced wines for consumers.

original_description:
HOPE for Small Farm Sustainability is seeking funding to establish a regional food system that connects nonprofit organizations and small-scale farmers and ranchers for the success of wholesale purchase via transportation between food hubs. By joining the Texas Rio Grande Valley, Central Texas, the Upper Gulf Coast of Texas, and North Texas, we will create a food network that bridges the gap between small farmers that lack access to markets and organizations or markets in urban areas that lack locally produced farm products.

HOPE proposes to establish a logistics, storage, and transportation system. HOPE will establish and manage a logistics system to safely transport products to storage HUBS in Harlingen, TX, Central Texas, Houston, TX, in order to connect with the Dallas Farmers’ Market for wholesale. Nonprofit community food suppliers in Central Texas and the Houston-area will also purchase available wholesale products.
Our project includes various forms of technical assistance to support the growers: wholesale sales training, product tracing practices, safe handling, labeling, packing, and transporting value-added product development and financial management. A proposed online sales portal featuring product content will enable the project to market products to wholesale buyers. We will connect small-scale, disadvantaged producers, nonprofit organizations, and the community for year-round production availability of vegetable, meat, and value-added farm products.
updated_description: HOPE for Small Farm Sustainability is seeking funding to establish a regional food system connecting nonprofit organizations and small-scale farmers and ranchers, facilitating wholesale purchases through a transportation network spanning the Texas Rio Grande Valley, Central Texas, the Upper Gulf Coast of Texas, and North Texas. This project will create a food network to bridge the gap between producers lacking access to markets and organizations or markets in central areas that require locally produced agricultural products. The core of this initiative involves the establishment of a logistics, storage, and transportation system, with designated storage hubs in Harlingen, TX, Central Texas, and Houston, TX, intended for connection with the Dallas Farmers’ Market to facilitate wholesale sales. HOPE will support farmers and ranchers by providing resources for safe handling, labeling, and packing of products, as well as assistance with value-added product development and financial management. The project anticipates increased availability of vegetable and meat products for distribution to wholesale buyers and nonprofit community food suppliers. The anticipated outcomes include expanded market access for small-scale producers and greater product availability for consumers and stakeholders throughout the targeted region. The beneficiaries of this project encompass farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the regional food supply chain. This initiative aims to strengthen the local food system and ensure a reliable source of agricultural products for the communities involved.

original_description:
Culinary Entrepreneurs Cultivating Local Value-Chains in Utah” project will increase revenues and market options for local farmers and value-added and culinary (VA&C) businesses and increase access to locally-grown food in Salt Lake County, Utah. This three-year project will provide training and capacity building for refugee farmers in IRC SLC’s farm incubator and food-access program, New Roots (NR SLC) and entrepreneurs in its Spice Kitchen Incubator (SKI) culinary entrepreneurship program. The project will support other local farmers and VA&C businesses with the desire to utilize local produce.

Refugee farmers and VA&C producers face barriers to value-chain entry and business expansion, including limited formal education, literacy, and English language skills. IRC SLC will use its extensive experience working with these populations to develop culturally relevant, linguistically-accessible curricula and materials in the areas of food safety, certifications, marketing, and business strategies to navigate the value chain and reach a broader customer base. IRC SLC has been supporting beginning farmers and VA&C entrepreneurs for over 15 years, including extensive work in developing new markets and market linkages in both high-value markets and within low income/low access (LI/LA)  neighborhoods throughout Salt Lake County. This project will leverage these relationships support network development towards increasing farmer revenue by 150% and VA&C producer revenue by 300% over 3 years, while 6 LI/LA neighborhoods will see an increase in the variety and year-round availability  of affordable products made with locally grown food.
updated_description: IRC SLC’s “Culinary Entrepreneurs Cultivating Local Value-Chains in Utah” project aims to increase revenues and market options for local farmers and value-added and culinary (VA&C) businesses, while simultaneously enhancing access to locally-grown food in Salt Lake County, Utah. This three-year project will support refugee farmers and VA&C producers within the IRC SLC’s farm incubator and food-access program, New Roots (NR SLC) and its Spice Kitchen Incubator (SKI) culinary entrepreneurship program, alongside other local farmers and VA&C businesses seeking to utilize local produce. The project anticipates significant outcomes, including a 150% increase in farmer revenue and a 300% increase in VA&C producer revenue over the three-year period, alongside an increase in the variety and year-round availability of affordable products made with locally grown food in six low-income/low-access (LI/LA) neighborhoods. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the local food system. This initiative will directly benefit consumers by expanding access to locally sourced food products. The project will focus on strengthening the value chains of local food producers and improving their ability to reach a broader customer base, with a specific focus on supporting producers in low-income/low-access neighborhoods. Through strategic network development, IRC SLC intends to create a more robust and resilient local food system within Salt Lake County.

original_description: This project will initiate the aggregation and distribution of meat products via Appalachian Sustainable Development’s (ASD) Appalachian Harvest Food Hub, expanding existing markets in collaboration with current producers, existing facilities, and established collaborators. The market demand already exists through school systems and local retailers and is expected to grow as regenerative agriculture, animal welfare, healthier meats, and local/regional food system resilience become increasingly important to consumers. Project activities include expanding ASD training to include support for meat producers, including production practices, food safety, and meeting brand, product, packaging, and certification standards; building and managing markets for meat; and coordinating delivery logistics. This project will increase markets for regional beef producers, including those utilizing environmentally sustainable production practices such as grass-finishing and silvopasture. Expected project outcomes include increased regional food security and increased food hub sales volume, profit, and the number of year- round offerings, benefiting consumers, farmers, and the local economy. This project will also play a critical role in making deliveries to small rural purchasers (e.g., school systems and small retailers) financially viable, as it will increase the value and volume of each delivery, ensuring these mid-tier markets are serviceable over the long term. Another outcome of this project will be to lay the foundation for substantial expansion of regenerative agriculture practices and the premium pricing connected to them by end-use customers and major retailers. Documentation of this project will provide a template for other organizations to replicate and will include operational procedures and a Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) plan.
updated_description: Appalachian Sustainable Development will initiate a project to expand the Appalachian Harvest Food Hub, leveraging existing markets and collaborations with producers, processors, and established partners to increase access to regionally produced meat products. This project will focus on establishing and managing markets for meat, coordinating delivery logistics, and building infrastructure to support the distribution of products, with the goal of increasing sales volume and the number of year-round offerings. Anticipated outcomes include enhanced regional food security, increased profitability for the food hub, and the potential for substantial expansion of regenerative agriculture practices, driving premium pricing for these products. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass farmers, ranchers, and meat processors operating within the region, alongside consumers seeking locally sourced protein. Specifically, this project aims to make deliveries to small rural purchasers—such as school systems and small retailers—financially viable, ensuring these mid-tier markets are consistently serviced. Furthermore, this project will lay the foundation for broader adoption of regenerative agriculture by showcasing the value of these practices to end-use customers and major retailers. The project’s final deliverable will be a documented operational template for replication by other organizations, including a Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) plan, to ensure safe and reliable meat distribution.

original_description: In Phase 1, this project will create a website to promote resources related to value-added seafood products, partner with a local university to support and train entrepreneurs and work with an established network of influential chefs and food producers to develop at least 15 new value-added seafood products with a focus on byproducts. In Phase 2, Conservation International Hawaii (CI Hawaii) will host 3 events during its statewide direct-to-consumer seafood marketing campaign to promote and enhance the value-chain links for the value-added products created in Phase 1 and will host a zero-waste fish workshop to strengthen knowledge around a diversity of value-added seafood products. This project will build on CI’s successful market-based model which will improve local and regional food systems to increase food security, create local food products, increase revenue streams for seafood producers and processors, reduce seafood waste, and create local economic opportunities.
updated_description: Conservation International Hawaii will develop a comprehensive project focused on enhancing the value-added seafood sector within local and regional food systems. This project’s primary purpose is to create a website to promote value-added seafood products, collaborate with a local university to support seafood producers, and work with a network of established chefs and food producers to generate at least fifteen new value-added seafood products utilizing byproducts. The anticipated outcomes of this initiative include the expansion of local food businesses, increased revenue streams for seafood processors and producers, and a reduction in seafood waste. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and seafood processors, as well as consumers seeking access to locally produced goods. By fostering new product development and market channels, this project aims to strengthen regional food systems and create economic opportunities for those involved in seafood production. The project intends to improve access to locally produced seafood products and build stronger relationships between seafood producers and consumers. Ultimately, this work will support the creation of more robust and resilient food systems, benefiting all stakeholders involved in the seafood industry and contributing to a more secure local food supply.

awardee_name: SOUTHSIDE VIRGINIA FRUIT AND VEGETABLE PRODUCERS ASSOCIATION
original_description:
Southside Virginia Fruit and Vegetable Producers Association is a grassroots, farmer founded and operated growers association born out of the need of Southside Virginia farmers to have access to institutional buyers and shared equipment and facilities. The project has numerous benefits to our member farms and local community that highlight the need for an economic opportunity such as the one envisioned by our organization. The association is composed of producers from the following counties in Southside Virginia, which represent the project area: Appomattox, Brunswick, Buckingham, Campbell, Charlotte, Cumberland, Halifax, Lunenburg, and Prince Edward.
The goal for this project is to aggregate and transport fruit and produce from local farmers to wholesale buyers across the Virginia. Expected benefits for the proposed project will be: increased sales for local farm businesses, expanded market opportunities, increased employment opportunities in economically distressed areas, and increased operational capacity, advancing farmer and community sustainability.
updated_description: The Southside Virginia Fruit and Vegetable Producers Association is undertaking a project designed to aggregate and transport fresh fruit and produce from local farmers across nine Southside Virginia counties – Appomattox, Brunswick, Buckingham, Campbell, Charlotte, Cumberland, Halifax, Lunenburg, and Prince Edward – to wholesale buyers throughout the state. This initiative aims to increase sales for participating farm businesses and expand market opportunities for these producers. The project’s anticipated outcomes include enhanced operational capacity for the farmers involved and increased access to broader markets for their goods. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the local farmers themselves, alongside consumers seeking locally sourced agricultural products. Furthermore, the project seeks to stimulate economic activity within these economically distressed areas, contributing to overall community sustainability. The Southside Virginia Fruit and Vegetable Producers Association envisions a future where these agricultural businesses can effectively connect with buyers, ultimately bolstering the region’s economy and providing increased access to fresh, regional food supplies. This project intends to facilitate the movement of agricultural products from the source to the point of sale, optimizing the supply chain and supporting the viability of agricultural operations within the designated area.

awardee_name: Mad Local Food Group, LLC dba Pasture and Plenty

Expand capacity to aggregate, develop and manufacture local food products and innovate to grow wholesale and direct-to-customer markets, with a focus on purchase commitments to Black, Indigenous and Persons of Color (BIPOC) and beginning farmers. awardee_name: West Virginia Food and Farm Coalition, Inc.
original_description: This project will create a comprehensive, value-added, regional Appalachian branding and marketing strategy allowing the state’s valued-added product makers to access additional markets in 10 Mid-Atlantic and southern metropolitan areas. The project will identify 50 locations for value-added product sales outside of West Virginia while utilizing the Coalition’s WV Rural Grocer Network for sales within the state. Mamaw’s Molasses will provide support for both new and existing value-added makers with the creation of two shared use curriculums, build and market a value-added product line, provide technical and marketing assistance to identified markets, and deliver West Virginia value-added products to regional markets in the MidAtlantic region. This project is expected to reach 30 value-added makers, 60 farmers, 30 retail outlets, 20 restaurants, and 10 in-state independently-owned grocery stores.  The WV Harvest Farm to Institution application will connect producers and growers with state institutions through collaborative partnerships that result in stronger local food system in WV. WV Harvest will engage with the current growers, producers, and processors in the state of WV to begin the strategic aggregation of locally grown/raised/produced food products under the WV Harvest Brand. This includes creating an institution focused coordinated food chain and mid-tier value chain, purchasing locally grown/raised/processed products, and aggregating/storing locally grown/produced products in a central location. In addition, WV Harvest will expand on current work by informing the nutritional directors in K-12 and purchasing managers at WV State Institutions about the large selection of fresh and value-added food products available for purchase. This includes informational displays and marketing installations in schools and institutions of higher education.
updated_description: Mamaw’s Molasses is undertaking a comprehensive regional branding and marketing strategy designed to expand market access for value-added product makers within West Virginia and ten Mid-Atlantic and southern metropolitan areas. This project will involve the identification of fifty strategic locations outside of West Virginia for sales, utilizing the Coalition’s WV Rural Grocer Network for sales within the state, and the construction of two shared-use curriculums for value-added product creation. Specifically, the project will focus on establishing a coordinated food chain and mid-tier value chain, purchasing locally grown/raised/processed products, and aggregating/storing these products in a central location. The initiative seeks to connect producers and growers with state institutions through collaborative partnerships, informing nutritional directors in K-12 schools and purchasing managers at WV State Institutions about the available selection of fresh and value-added products. This will be achieved through informational displays and marketing installations in schools and institutions of higher education. The project’s beneficiaries will include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of locally sourced food products. Ultimately, the project aims to improve market access for these producers and provide consumers with a greater selection of locally produced goods.

original_description: This planning project produces a feasibility study for a fair food pricing and local food distribution initiative in the tri-corner region of New York, Connecticut and Massachusetts. The plan would outline the feasibility of a community-based initiative to increase local food purchasing by households meeting the United Way ALICE (Asset Limited Income Constrained Employed) criteria and to in turn expand the market for regional growers practicing sustainable farming methods. The study includes assessment of the marketplace, technology and infrastructure needs and limitations, marketing strategies, farmer recruitment, staffing requirements, partnership potential and financial projections. Output will include a financial model assessing the overall earnings gap to afford local food and a proposed sliding scale program with recommendations for how the program can be funded, implemented and administered. The project is led by the North East Community Center (NECC), a regional resource with a history of local food system work. NECC will partner with Q Farms, a local agricultural producer focused on sustainable livestock production and regional agricultural development. The Glynwood Center for Regional Food and Farming will provide consultation support. At the end of the 18-month program period, NECC Food Program staff will present the feasibility study at a meeting of the Hudson Valley Food System Coalition. If the feasibility study yields positive results, it will be used to develop a business plan and to apply for program funding.
updated_description: North East Community Center (NECC) is undertaking a 18-month planning project to assess the feasibility of a community-based initiative focused on increasing local food purchasing by households meeting the United Way ALICE criteria and expanding the market for regional growers practicing sustainable farming methods within the tri-corner region of New York, Connecticut, and Massachusetts. This project will encompass a comprehensive marketplace assessment, an evaluation of technology and infrastructure needs and limitations, the development of targeted marketing strategies, and the recruitment of regional farmers and ranchers involved in livestock production. The initiative will also establish a financial model to analyze the earnings gap associated with affording local food and propose a sliding scale program, alongside recommendations for its funding, implementation, and administration. Stakeholders involved include NECC, Q Farms, a local agricultural producer, and Glynwood Center for Regional Food and Farming, who will provide consultation support. The anticipated outcome of this project is the creation of a detailed feasibility study, which will be presented to the Hudson Valley Food System Coalition. Ultimately, this study will serve as the foundation for developing a business plan and pursuing program funding opportunities. The primary beneficiaries of this project include regional farmers and ranchers, as well as the consumers who will gain access to locally produced food options, and the overall goal is to strengthen the regional food system.

original_description: Regional food enterprises can help increase food system resilience, yet for success must build effective community partnerships and marketing campaigns; promote inclusive access; facilitate producer agency; and ensure efficient operations and logistical management. This project will advance the Southwest Washington Food Hub in these five capacity areas and expand as a regional mid-tier value chain. To implement its hybrid growth strategy in intermediated and consumer direct markets, it will 1) cultivate drop site collaboration with area businesses, partner with local employers to deliver a workplace wellness “farmshare”, and build sales relationships with school and institutional buyers, and 2) hire operations, sales and administrative managers to do so. It will promote equity, working with BIPOC leaders and farmers, and include Spanish-language materials for producers and buyers. As membership expands, it will 4) train and build connectivity among food hub membership through peer mentoring and training that supports onboarding, operational efficiency, and safety. Finally, it will 5) transfer administrative agency to the food hub and complete a strategic plan through administrative funding, organizational development facilitation, and grower engagement. As a cooperative, the hub exists to put profits in the hands of producers, and provides a democratically controlled and member-focused alternative to traditional distributor models. Through grant activities, food hub producer participation will increase from 26 to 4 farmer members by 225 and producer payments are also estimated to grow. Barriers to market access will be lowered for BIPOC and Spanish-speaking producers growing culturally-relevant crops
updated_description: The Southwest Washington Food Hub’s purpose is to advance a regional mid-tier value chain by bolstering its capacity in five key areas: community partnerships, marketing campaigns, inclusive access, producer agency, and efficient operations and logistical management. This project will expand the food hub’s reach by cultivating collaboration with drop-site businesses, establishing sales relationships with school and institutional buyers, and partnering with local employers to implement a workplace wellness “farmshare” program. Furthermore, the project will facilitate increased producer participation from 26 to 4 farmer members, resulting in anticipated growth in producer payments and strengthening the cooperative’s model of democratic control and member-focused operations. The Food Hub will support stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural products, aiming to lower barriers to market access for producers cultivating a variety of crops. The project will support consumers accessing locally-sourced goods and foster a robust regional food system. This expansion will be achieved through strategic investments in operational infrastructure and systems, ensuring efficient processing, storage, and distribution capabilities. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened and more resilient regional food network, benefitting farmers, processors, and ultimately, consumers.

original_description: Despite growth and interest in farming in Alaska, the state still imports over 95% of its food - there is simply not enough production, nor accessible and affordable regional distribution systems. With the rising popularity of local food, as well as an increased interest in connecting existing food hubs and creating new ones, the Alaska Food Policy Council (AFPC) will facilitate food system research and educational opportunities, to increase viable and sustainable local food production and distribution through a network for Alaskan Food Hubs. AFPC will convene a Food Working Group with a focus of improving, supporting, and connecting food hub operations statewide and within regions. Through a comprehensive assessment and review of food hub best practices, the working group will inform the production of a Food Hub Working Group and Recommendations Report and Operations Manual. We will provide professional development opportunities to build new skills and facilitate additional information sharing between food hub operators and producers at the Fall 2023 Alaska Food Festival & Conference.
updated_description: The Alaska Food Policy Council will undertake a project focused on bolstering local food production and distribution within the state, addressing the critical need for increased regional food supply. This project will involve the establishment of a Food Working Group dedicated to improving and connecting food hub operations across Alaska, with the goal of producing a comprehensive Food Hub Working Group and Recommendations Report and Operations Manual. The Working Group’s assessment of best practices will directly inform the development of strategies to strengthen the capacity of food hubs, thereby supporting farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in local food systems. The anticipated outcome is a more robust and interconnected network of food hubs, which will facilitate the movement of agricultural products from producers to consumers throughout Alaska. This increased production and distribution will ultimately benefit the entire food system by providing greater access to locally sourced goods. The Alaska Food Policy Council will contribute to enhancing the overall viability of local food businesses, and improve the supply chain. The project’s beneficiaries include those involved in the production of agricultural products, as well as the consumers who have access to a wider range of locally available food.

original_description:
The Co-op members and community partners have identified a need for expanded collaborative activities to keep smaller-scale agriculture alive, and to get more healthy local food to communities around the state. 

The purpose of this planning grant is to advance public awareness of and viability for Arizona’s smaller-acreage local food producers and distributors, through a two-pronged approach: 

1.	Developing a feasibility study and business plan for an Arizona Food and Farm Sustainability Center that provides a shared facility and resources where small-acreage farms can leverage infrastructure and economies of scale, offers technical and business assistance to new and continuing agricultural producers, strengthens partnerships among organizations from all aspects of the state’s food system and creates a community gathering place in which to celebrate local food and farms; 

2.	Developing a marketing strategy and brand for the Co-op that elevates local farms, coordinates outreach efforts to producers and customers alike, and promotes community wellness.

original_description:
Rural Arizona livestock producers face tremendous local supply chain challenges, crippling their ability to meet market demand for value-added meat products. There is simply not enough capacity to process, package, and store meat, causing deep losses in revenue opportunities for producers who then are forced to sell to wholesale markets. In 2021,  a USDA-inspected processing facility in rural Arizona was purchased because it was one of the last facilities for small family farms to have cattle processed for direct to customer sales in the region. Currently, the facility, Cattlemen’s Processing slaughters 20 heads of beef per week in an aging and space-constrained facility. However, the need is much greater in the community for animal processing. With the support of USDA funds, Cattlemen’s Processing seeks to create more opportunities for local ranchers by expanding their local processing capacity.

The purpose of this planning project is to: conduct a feasibility study to determine best practices for direct-to-customer processing in highly rural settings and the subsequent expanded business plan based upon feasibility study findings in order to process on behalf of additional ranches in the community. 

The feasibility study will identify needed facility upgrades, direct-to-consumer strategies, and financial requirements. The study will help Cattlemen’s Processing meet the local ranching community’s needs, ensuring that more ranchers are able to sell directly to customers.
updated_description: Cattlemen’s Processing seeks to expand its local processing capacity to address significant supply chain challenges faced by rural Arizona livestock producers. The primary purpose of this planning project is to conduct a feasibility study and subsequently develop an expanded business plan, focusing on best practices for direct-to-customer processing within highly rural settings. This study will identify necessary facility upgrades, including improvements to the existing aging and space-constrained facility, and will explore direct-to-consumer strategies to efficiently handle increased demand. Anticipated outcomes include the ability for Cattlemen’s Processing to process on behalf of additional ranchers in the community, significantly increasing the volume of animals processed each week. The beneficiaries of this project are the local farmers and ranchers who currently face limitations in accessing processing services, as well as the consumers who desire access to locally sourced meat products. The project aims to strengthen the local economy by supporting these stakeholders and ensuring that ranchers can effectively meet market demand. Ultimately, this project will allow Cattlemen’s Processing to play a vital role in connecting producers directly with consumers, improving the financial viability of local livestock operations, and bolstering the regional meat supply chain.

awardee_name: AZ Board of Regents on behalf of Arizona State University
original_description:
The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated existing vulnerabilities in Hawai‘i’s food system, evidenced by increased reliance on public food assistance. 

Our market analysis and feasibility study of aquaculture in the islands aims to improve income and economic opportunities for both traditional and contemporary aquaculture producers through a) conducting market research on species that have market potential, b) identifying gaps and solutions for needed aquaculture supply-chain infrastructure, and c) developing a brand / trademark with production standards attached to it to promote seafood grown in traditional native Hawaiian aquaculture systems. We will assess current production levels, research how consumer preferences might be shifted towards farmed fish including tilapia and traditional fishpond-raised species and identify how aquaculture producers can be supported through supply chain development.
updated_description: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted vulnerabilities in Hawai‘i’s food system, and this project aims to improve income and economic opportunities for farmers and aquaculture producers across the islands. This initiative will focus on conducting comprehensive market research to identify species with commercial potential, coupled with a detailed assessment of gaps and solutions for aquaculture supply-chain infrastructure. Specifically, the project will develop a recognized brand and associated production standards designed to promote seafood cultivated through traditional native Hawaiian aquaculture systems. Furthermore, the project will evaluate current production levels and investigate potential shifts in consumer preferences towards farmed fish, including tilapia and species raised in traditional fishponds. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened local aquaculture sector capable of meeting market demands and a reliable source of seafood for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are aquaculture producers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of seafood. Ultimately, the project seeks to establish a robust and recognized brand, fostering confidence among consumers and supporting sustainable aquaculture practices within Hawai‘i’s unique environment.

original_description: Most American farmers struggle to generate enough revenue to turn a profit, let alone make a living. Meanwhile, more than 1 million people in San Diego County are nutrition insecure and don’t have enough food to meet their basic needs. Almost 250,000 of them are children. To address these challenges, Equation Collaborative will assess the feasibility of strengthening secondary market opportunities for local farmers by integrating local produce into the existing nutrition security program, called +BOX, in a way that creates value for all stakeholders, including local farmers, nutrition insecure families, and school district distribution partners. This grant will partner with the Community Health Improvement Partners’ Farm to Institution Center to develop a network of local farmers to participate in the feasibility study by providing expertise and feedback on proposed market opportunities. This grant will then partner with Dualboot Partners, a software development company, to assess the feasibility of expanding the market opportunity for local farmers by expanding the +BOX program to additional households through +BOX Connect, a software application that will piggyback existing technology systems in partner school districts to increase participation among low-income families and connect them to nutrition resources, including increased access to local produce. This grant will pilot test +BOX Connect with Bella Mente Academy, a K-8 charter school, to determine the likelihood that +BOX Connect will increase participation in nutrition security programs, like +BOX, among low-income households, while simultaneously creating a vibrant market for local farmers that increases revenue and the opportunity to reach profitability.
updated_description: Equation Collaborative will undertake a project to assess the feasibility of strengthening secondary market opportunities for local farmers by integrating local produce into the existing nutrition security program, +BOX. This initiative will involve partnering with the Community Health Improvement Partners’ Farm to Institution Center to develop a network of local farmers to provide expertise and feedback on proposed market opportunities, while simultaneously collaborating with Dualboot Partners, a software development company, to evaluate the potential expansion of the +BOX program through +BOX Connect. +BOX Connect is a software application designed to piggyback on existing technology systems within partner school districts, with the goal of increasing participation among low-income families and connecting them to nutrition resources, including access to local produce. The project will pilot test +BOX Connect with Bella Mente Academy, a K-8 charter school, to determine the likelihood of increased participation in nutrition security programs among low-income households. The anticipated outcome is the creation of a vibrant market for local farmers, resulting in increased revenue and opportunities for profitability. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the local food system. Furthermore, the project will directly benefit consumers, particularly low-income families seeking access to nutritious food options. This initiative seeks to enhance the availability of local agricultural products and strengthen the connections between food producers and those who rely on them for sustenance.

original_description: Veggielution will research and create a Santa Clara County (California) Food Hub Feasibility Plan (the Plan) that will discuss and address county-wide food insecurity; food swamps, where low-income residents lack access to culturally relevant healthy, organic food; opportunities for food entrepreneurs and employment; and limited channels for smaller and/or BIPOC regional organic growers to market products. The Plan will ultimately recommend a best practice model for a San Jose Food Hub by investigating potential solutions and how Veggielution and local stakeholders can play a part in actualizing those solutions. For this project, and once approved for funding, Veggielution will contract with New Venture Advisors, an independent business consultant versed in the food systems landscape in San Jose, California and regionally. Working closely with Veggielution’s Executive Director, New Venture Advisors will develop the Plan. During an assessment and discovery phase, New Venture Advisors will conduct exhaustive literature reviews; interviews with and surveys of food systems stakeholders, partners, growers, farmers, grocers, leaders, residents, and others; and a business analysis of Veggielution to determine the benefit of Veggielution serving as San Jose’s Food Hub.Veggielution anticipates the Plan will suggest strategic recommendations for a San Jose / Santa Clara County Food Hub model, including whether or not Veggielution can best operate the Food Hub. Veggielution also expects the Plan will highlight solutions to apparent and discovered food system problems, issues, and barriers. These recommendations will benefit low-income residents, food entrepreneurs and workers, and smaller, disadvantaged farmers.
updated_description: Veggielution will undertake a comprehensive feasibility study to develop a plan for a San Jose Food Hub within Santa Clara County, California, addressing critical food system challenges. This project will involve extensive research, including exhaustive literature reviews, interviews, and surveys of a wide range of stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, processors, and consumers, to assess the viability of establishing a centralized food distribution network. The anticipated outcome is a detailed plan that recommends a best-practice model for a San Jose Food Hub, specifically evaluating the potential role of Veggielution in its operation. The plan will meticulously analyze existing market conditions, identify barriers to accessing regional agricultural products for consumers, and explore solutions for smaller producers and regional growers. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be the local food system, encompassing farmers and ranchers seeking improved market access, and consumers seeking reliable sources of fresh, regional agricultural products. Furthermore, the study will investigate ways to enhance the flow of goods from agricultural producers to those who need them most. The resulting plan will offer strategic recommendations designed to increase the availability of locally produced goods and address existing obstacles within the food supply chain.

original_description:
Early Care and Education (ECE) providers operate child care programs that serve children ages zero to five years old, and often older children through afterschool programs. ECE providers have consistent food needs throughout the year and can be a good customer for smaller local farms who can prepare smaller order quantities, compared to larger institutional purchasers. Currently, Quality Care for Children (QCC) connects ECE providers with local farmers through one-to-one match making which is time consuming and not scalable. 
QCC, in partnership with an experienced consultant, the Georgia Farm to ECE Coalition, local farmers, ECE providers, the GA Department of Early Care and Learning (DECAL) and other stakeholders will research and develop a value chain coordination model that enables locally grown foods to be easily purchased by ECE programs. The model report will include an analysis of existing value chain coordination models, identification of a feasible model for Georgia, and recommendations for management, financing, and utilization of USDA CACFP funding for local purchases. QCC will also host farmer and ECE provider networking events to facilitate relationship building and identify potential pilot sites for the model.
updated_description: Quality Care for Children is undertaking a project to develop a value chain coordination model that will enable locally grown foods to be easily purchased by early care and education programs. This initiative will focus on connecting farmers with ECE providers, facilitating smaller order quantities suitable for these smaller purchasers. The anticipated outcome of this project is the establishment of a streamlined system for procuring agricultural products, directly benefiting farmers and ECE providers. Specifically, Quality Care for Children, in collaboration with a consultant and various stakeholders including local farmers, ECE providers, and the Georgia Farm to ECE Coalition, will conduct research, identify a feasible model for Georgia, and provide recommendations for management and utilizing USDA CACFP funding. The project seeks to improve access to locally produced agricultural products for early care and education facilities, which will ultimately support the procurement activities of ECE providers. The project will involve the identification of potential pilot sites and the fostering of relationships between farmers and ECE providers. The primary beneficiaries of this work will be farmers seeking to expand their customer base, and ECE providers seeking to incorporate locally sourced food into their programs. The successful completion of this project will improve the availability of agricultural products for the early care and education sector, creating new market opportunities for farmers and supporting the nutritional needs of children in early learning environments.

original_description: Concrete Jungle, Inc. is seeking funds for business planning and a feasibility study to increase purchases of surplus produce from Georgia farmers and diversify the markets we sell to.
