CJ will complete a feasibility study to determine how to increase sales and support distribution to small hunger relief agencies that have limited resources to distribute fresh produce.   We will evaluate key last-mile food safety, packaging and logistics challenges, use iterative business planning to find new farmers with surplus produce, and to expand our markets to commercial and institutional buyers
updated_description: Concrete Jungle, Inc. is seeking funding to support a business planning initiative and a feasibility study focused on expanding the purchase of surplus produce from Georgia farmers and broadening the markets to which they sell their goods. This project will involve the completion of a feasibility study designed to determine methods for increasing sales volume and establishing distribution channels to small hunger relief agencies that possess limited resources for distributing fresh produce. The core activities will center around evaluating key last-mile food safety considerations, developing appropriate packaging solutions, and streamlining logistics processes. Concrete Jungle, Inc. intends to utilize an iterative approach to business planning, actively seeking out new farmers with available surplus produce while simultaneously expanding market reach to include commercial and institutional buyers. The anticipated outcome of this project is to significantly increase the volume of produce handled by the organization and establish reliable distribution networks for this surplus. The primary beneficiaries of this project include Georgia farmers, processors, and other stakeholders in the agricultural supply chain, as well as hunger relief agencies and the communities they serve. Ultimately, this project aims to enhance access to locally sourced produce, contributing to the availability of fresh food for those seeking to purchase it, and supporting the operational capacity of organizations dedicated to distributing it.

original_description: The Hawaiian islands lack adequate food processing infrastructure for increased food self-sufficiency and food security for residents and visitors alike. Meanwhile, Hawa'ii’s small farmers (66% of farms are under 9 acres in size) struggle to make a profit, facing the highest production costs in the US. The purpose of this project is to address these twin challenges of lack of food processing capacity for local crops, and increasing profits for small farmers through adding value to local crops. The Olohana Foundation recently acquired legacy industrial juicing equipment which we wish to put into operation once again, providing a valuable option to local farmers for adding value to their tropical fruit crops and reducing on-farm food waste. In collaboration with local fruit producers, we will pilot the production of two new local fruit products utilizing this food processing equipment. These final food products will be routed directly into the local food system via the Food Basket: Hawai’i Island’s food bank, and Hawai’i Farm to Car farmers market. By developing these two new fruit products, we will be directly growing the mid-tier value chain infrastructure for Hawai’i Island (the Big Island) and beyond, increasing local capacity for aggregation, processing and distribution. An estimated 33 local fruit producers will benefit from this new market for their crops, including B grade crops, which will help to reduce on-farm food waste. Additionally, we will reach an estimated 452 local consumers, providing an affordable, local and healthy food option.
updated_description: Olohana Foundation’s project aims to address the challenges faced by local farmers and expand access to fresh produce on Hawai‘i Island. The Foundation is reactivating legacy industrial juicing equipment to enable farmers to add value to their tropical fruit crops, effectively reducing on-farm food waste. This initiative anticipates the production of two new local fruit products, which will then be distributed directly through the Food Basket, a local food bank, and the Hawai‘i Farm to Car farmers market. The project will directly benefit approximately 33 farmers, particularly those producing crops graded as “B,” and will reach an estimated 452 local consumers, offering them an affordable, locally sourced food option. By developing this mid-tier value chain infrastructure, the project intends to increase local capacity for aggregation, processing, and distribution of agricultural goods. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened local food system and improved access to fresh produce for the island’s residents. Ultimately, this project seeks to bolster the economic viability of local producers and provide a greater selection of fresh fruits to the community.

original_description: In partnership with the Franklin County Farmers Market and Franklin Center for Innovation, Frankfort will conduct a feasibility study for a community kitchen, potentially co-located with a farmers’ market. Project partners will engage in a site selection, design, and business planning process to develop the community kitchen. This kitchen will support the local farm to institution supply chains, activate the City Strategic Plan for Economic Development through providing food entrepreneurs a food processing facility to rent at affordable rates, and preserve abundant harvests for later use by restaurants, institutions, food access organizations, and individual households. Through on-site programming and educational classes, the community kitchen will build skills and enthusiasm for processing, preparing, and consuming healthy foods. There will be a particular focus on meeting the needs of community members with limited income and access to fresh foods and entrepreneurial opportunities. Frankfort has made a commitment to mitigate climate change through clean energy/renewable electricity resolution, and this project will incorporate green design, renewable energy, and reduction of food waste into community kitchen design to reduce its climate footprint.
updated_description: Frankfort will conduct a feasibility study for a community kitchen, in partnership with the Franklin County Farmers Market and Franklin Center for Innovation, to support the City Strategic Plan for Economic Development and address the needs of local food systems. This project will involve a comprehensive site selection process, followed by the design and development of a detailed business plan for a shared-use kitchen facility. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is to establish a kitchen that will facilitate the connection between farmers and institutions, enabling the processing and preservation of harvests for use by restaurants, food access organizations, and individual households. Specifically, the project will focus on supporting farmers, ranchers, and food processors by providing a facility to rent at affordable rates, thereby increasing access to locally produced agricultural products. The community kitchen will contribute to the preservation of abundant harvests for later use by restaurants, institutions, food access organizations, and individual households. This facility will benefit stakeholders by offering a location to process and prepare food, reducing waste, and expanding options for consumers. Ultimately, Frankfort aims to enhance the efficiency of local food systems and strengthen the connection between producers and consumers. The project will incorporate green design principles and renewable energy solutions to minimize its operational footprint and reduce food waste, contributing to a more sustainable approach to food processing and distribution.

original_description: Local Food Connection--founded as an independent food hub but now housed as a department within the multi-state distributor Creation Gardens--will study feasibility of “farm to corporate” as a new market category for regional food by utilizing “third-party produce management companies” within the traditional food system. These companies exist to ease the processes and manage costs for produce and other food categories for multi-unit, multi-geographic (“corporate”) restaurants and foodservice. “Third parties” therefore create both access points and barriers for regional food producers and hubs who seek to scale. Curiosity about sourcing regional foods is growing across “third parties.” Yet, accessing corporate markets is complex, and any steps to create a new market here require great care for the farms and small businesses who are the core of local food systems. In partnership with Food Works Group, a women-owned strategic advisory firm, Local Food Connection will collaboratively size the supply of and demand for regional food for a potential farm-to-corporate program. Hand-in-hand with additional advisors, we will inventory key stakeholders, from “third parties” to local producers, creating access points for producers of diverse types and backgrounds. We will rely on stakeholder interviews, qualitative data, and information about existing resources and gaps. We will create a roadmap to implement and scale this new market category plus develop key metrics to use for future decision- making. Our outcomes will detail how to assist foods systems in moving the needle toward more corporate, multi-unit buyers conducting regional food purchasing programs.
updated_description: Local Food Connection will conduct a feasibility study to establish “farm to corporate” as a new market category for regional food systems, leveraging the services of “third-party produce management companies” within the existing food distribution landscape. This project aims to facilitate access for regional food producers, including farmers and ranchers, to engage with multi-unit, multi-geographic “corporate” restaurants and foodservice operations. The core work involves a collaborative effort with Food Works Group to assess the supply and demand for regional food products, identifying key stakeholders along the supply chain – from producers to these “third parties”. Through stakeholder interviews and a thorough review of existing resources, the project will map access points for regional food producers, creating a detailed roadmap for implementation and scaling this new market category. The anticipated outcomes will encompass a strategic plan with key metrics designed to support decision-making regarding corporate food purchasing programs. Ultimately, this project seeks to improve the ability of regional food systems to serve larger buyers, contributing to increased volume and market reach for producers. The project will focus on establishing streamlined pathways for regional food to reach these consumers and businesses, supporting a more robust and interconnected food system.

original_description: Under the project, “Building Community for Local Food System Resiliency,” Land Stewardship Project will bring together a diverse set of stakeholders to coordinate the expansion of the regional food system. The project will analyze existing commercial networks operating in the region, identify gaps, and explore new opportunities for connection. The project will convene specialized working groups around increasing sales of local food and build new partnerships to facilitate stronger regional food chain coordination. A diverse team of stakeholders including farmers, consumers, food businesses, food banks, Economic Development Authority staff, and food system researchers are committed to collaborating to achieve the project goals. The project will generate data that stakeholders can use to strengthen local food value chains and increase sales of local foods.
updated_description: Land Stewardship Project is undertaking a project to build community for local food system resiliency, focusing on the coordination of expansion within the region’s commercial networks. The project will analyze existing systems, pinpoint gaps, and identify new opportunities for connection among farmers, processors, and other stakeholders. This initiative will support the development of specialized working groups dedicated to increasing the sales of local foods and fostering stronger regional food chain coordination. The project anticipates generating data that stakeholders can utilize to enhance local food value chains and increase the volume of locally produced goods reaching consumers. The anticipated outcomes include strengthened relationships amongst food businesses and a more efficient movement of agricultural products through the regional system. Ultimately, this project aims to benefit farmers and ranchers by providing access to new markets and consumers by offering a wider selection of locally sourced food options. The project will support the overall growth of the local food system and contribute to a more robust and connected food supply chain, benefiting all stakeholders involved.

The Local Food Promotion Program seeks to create a comprehensive business development plan to process, add value, market, and sell meat from local producers facilitated by an eCommerce platform. This plan will encompass key elements including thorough market research, which will involve detailed analysis of market segmentation, market trends, SWOT and PEST analyses, and the establishment of food safety protocols. Specifically, the project will investigate packaging insulation capabilities, comparing fully recyclable and non-recyclable components, and assessing varying temperature conditions to ensure products can withstand up to three days of transportation between cold storage and customer possession. Furthermore, the plan will develop an eCommerce platform and establish a logistical pathway to deliver locally sourced products to consumers, with an emphasis on creating an easy-to-use interface for ordering. The anticipated outcome is a business development plan outlining steps to implement and sustain local meat products for up to 36 months, with a budget of $500,000 or less. This project intends to benefit local ranchers and their surrounding customer base who may have limited access to direct procurement of locally sourced meat products, supporting the growth of regional food businesses. The project anticipates increased access to locally produced meats for farmers and consumers alike, improving supply chain efficiencies. The successful execution of this plan will require careful attention to packaging solutions and logistical considerations to maintain product quality and freshness throughout the distribution process, ultimately strengthening relationships between producers and the individuals purchasing their products.

original_description: To address the need for food security, employment and business opportunities in a low income, low access region of Omaha Nebraska Omaha Permaculture proposes in this application to develop a comprehensive plan for the Omaha Community Urban Farm Hub (OCUFH). To be located on a newly acquired 8 acre site in a densely populated region of north east Omaha, this site will provide an opportunity for community farmers to grow, process and market their products in their own neighborhood. The plan has 4 objectives 1) to determine project feasibility using a survey instrument to understand community food needs, gauge interest of local urban farmers and through this effort to raise awareness of the OCUFH; 2) to hire an expert in the field of commercial food processing to develop a plan to convert a 3500 sq ft building located on-site into a USDA certified  food handling facility; 3) to hire a food safety expert to develop a comprehensive food handling and processing safety plan from field to shelf; and 4) to hire a food marketing expert to develop a marketing template that the OCUFH farmers can use to market their products to the community. The OCUFH will provide local farmers with expert assistance, materials and infrastructure to facilitate quality and safe production and processing of their products. The Omaha community will benefit from this food hub by having locally produced, healthy products available for consumption.
updated_description: Omaha Permaculture proposes a project to address food security and employment opportunities in a low-income area of Omaha, Nebraska, by developing the Omaha Community Urban Farm Hub (OCUFH). This project will be implemented on a newly acquired 8-acre site in a densely populated region of northeast Omaha, providing a space for local farmers to grow, process, and market their products within their neighborhood. The core of this initiative involves several key elements, including the purchase of a 3,500 square foot building on-site to convert into a USDA-certified food handling facility, and the engagement of expert consultants to develop a comprehensive plan. Specifically, the project will hire a specialist in food processing, a food safety expert, and a food marketing consultant. The consultants will each develop plans for the facility, a food handling and processing safety plan, and a marketing template, respectively. These resources will equip local farmers with the necessary support and infrastructure to produce and process high-quality products safely. The anticipated outcome is the creation of a functional food hub that increases access to locally produced goods for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are local farmers and the community as a whole, who will gain access to fresh, healthy food options. The project intends to support processors and other stakeholders within the food system, ultimately strengthening the local economy and providing increased food availability for the community.

original_description: This project will support the aggregation and distribution of locally produced oysters; develop new marketing strategies for producers; facilitate regional food chain coordination; and respond to changing needs in producer-to-consumer marketing. This model has a high degree of replicability and external benefits to the local community and estuary, its success will invigorate oyster fisheries and the overall ocean environment throughout the Gulf Coast
updated_description: This project will support the aggregation and distribution of locally produced oysters, aiming to develop new marketing strategies for oyster producers and facilitate regional food chain coordination. The core of this initiative involves establishing a system to connect farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in oyster production with consumers, streamlining the flow of goods from the source to the market. Anticipated outcomes include a strengthened local food system, with increased access to regionally produced oysters for consumers and a positive impact on the overall oyster fisheries throughout the Gulf Coast. The project will contribute to reinvigorating the local oyster production, ultimately benefiting the entire ocean environment within the region. This model’s replicability suggests potential for expansion and positive effects on numerous communities. Successfully implementing this system will enhance the viability of oyster fisheries and provide a significant boost to the local economy. Stakeholders involved in the oyster industry will see improved market access and a greater ability to sell their products. Furthermore, this project intends to contribute to a more efficient and robust food chain, connecting producers directly with the end consumer, ensuring greater value for the oyster producers, and providing consumers with a reliable source of locally sourced seafood.

original_description:
Norwich Meadows Farm LLC will lead a planning process for the establishment of a unique specialty food hub, with both brick-and-mortar and virtual components, centered in Chenango County in Central New York. The hub will build on Norwich Meadows Farm’s uniquely successful history, its expertise, and its unequaled partner relationships, including collaborations with aspiring and successful food hubs across the region. The proposed hub will be distinguished by its strategic location and its emphasis on sustainability, diversity, flavor, and accessibility for both smaller producers and underserved consumers. 

This project brings together partners including Farm Credit East, the premier agricultural lender in the region, and Baldor Specialty Foods, a renowned distributor of specialty foods across the region, to conduct a feasibility study and to plan for the launch of a successful new enterprise. 

The hub’s strategic location will connect producers in upstate New York to major metropolitan markets with significant unmet demand for local food. The hub will be designed to efficiently address the unique needs of small-scale, organic and sustainable farms and to reach consumers in underserved communities.  

Accessibility will be a guiding principle of the hub, with a participatory organizational structure ensuring that it meets the needs of farmers, and efficient handling and distribution processes keeping costs down. The hub will commit to waste minimization, energy efficiency and climate-friendly practices across the supply chain as well as charitable actions built on a long history of such work by Norwich Meadows Farm and its partners.
updated_description: Norwich Meadows Farm LLC is undertaking a planning process to establish a unique specialty food hub centered in Chenango County in Central New York, building upon its established history, expertise, and strong partnerships within the region. This project will involve the creation of a strategic food hub designed to connect upstate New York producers – including farmers and ranchers – with major metropolitan markets experiencing significant demand for local food products. The hub’s development will encompass a feasibility study and planning for launch, supported by key partners such as Farm Credit East and Baldor Specialty Foods. The anticipated outcomes include the establishment of an efficient supply chain and distribution network, specifically designed to address the needs of small-scale producers. The hub will facilitate access to markets for these producers, benefiting from the logistical capabilities of Baldor Specialty Foods. This venture aims to support the growth of regional food businesses and increase the availability of locally produced goods. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers and ranchers supplying the hub, as well as the consumers who will have greater access to fresh, regional food. Furthermore, the project expects to support food processors and other stakeholders within the food system. The anticipated results will be a robust, interconnected system for distributing regional food products, resulting in increased sales opportunities for producers and improved access to quality food for consumers.

original_description: This planning project produces a feasibility study for a fair food pricing and local food distribution initiative in the tri-corner region of New York, Connecticut and Massachusetts. The plan would outline the feasibility of a community-based initiative to increase local food purchasing by households meeting the United Way ALICE (Asset Limited Income Constrained Employed) criteria and to in turn expand the market for regional growers practicing sustainable farming methods. The study includes assessment of the marketplace, technology and infrastructure needs and limitations, marketing strategies, farmer recruitment, staffing requirements, partnership potential and financial projections. Output will include a financial model assessing the overall earnings gap to afford local food and a proposed sliding scale program with recommendations for how the program can be funded, implemented and administered. The project is led by the North East Community Center (NECC), a regional resource with a history of local food system work. NECC will partner with Q Farms, a local agricultural producer focused on sustainable livestock production and regional agricultural development. The Glynwood Center for Regional Food and Farming will provide consultation support. At the end of the 18-month program period, NECC Food Program staff will present the feasibility study at a meeting of the Hudson Valley Food System Coalition. If the feasibility study yields positive results, it will be used to develop a business plan and to apply for program funding.
updated_description: North East Community Center (NECC) is undertaking a 18-month planning project to assess the feasibility of a community-based initiative focused on increasing local food purchasing by households meeting the United Way ALICE criteria and expanding the market for regional growers practicing sustainable farming methods within the tri-corner region of New York, Connecticut, and Massachusetts. This project will encompass a comprehensive evaluation of the marketplace, including technology and infrastructure needs and limitations, alongside the development of marketing strategies and a plan for farmer recruitment. The initiative aims to bridge the earnings gap to afford local food, resulting in a proposed sliding scale program designed for implementation and administration. NECC will collaborate with Q Farms, a local agricultural producer focused on sustainable livestock production and regional agricultural development, and will receive consultation support from the Glynwood Center for Regional Food and Farming. The anticipated outcome of this study is a detailed financial model and a robust operational framework. The primary beneficiaries of this project include regional farmers, ranchers, and processors who will gain access to expanded markets, and consumers who will have greater access to locally produced food. The North East Community Center will present the feasibility study at a meeting of the Hudson Valley Food System Coalition at the conclusion of the program period. If the study demonstrates positive results, it will serve as the foundation for developing a business plan and securing program funding to further advance this initiative.

original_description:
Refugee and Immigrant Self Empowerment (RISE) proposes this Local Food Promotion Planning Grant project to create intentional procedures that support the socially disadvantaged farmers currently in the farming program to increase the scope of their farm businesses and access previously untapped and inaccessible market outlets. This three-phase project will  assess the feasibility of RISE creating a local food hub to promote the farm businesses of the participating refugee and immigrant farmers.  Create business plans for the current farmers and for farmers recruited in the future. Create a hub logistical plan. All three phases will be completed in partnership with Food Works Group, a professional food systems consultancy.
Assuming feasibility, a food hub will be created to aggregate, store, market, and distribute produce grown locally by the refugee and immigrant community. The resulting model would allow farmers to sell directly to the food hub, not only providing a new source of local food to the greater Syracuse area, but also providing farmers with the stability necessary for utilizing their time and resources to sustainably increase income and production. Farmers will be extensively trained to scale production appropriately and follow careful guidelines to meet mandatory safety standards.
The project outcomes will be  agricultural product diversification, farmer empowerment, and revenue generation for the 15 farmers in the program and refugee and immigrant farmers recruited to join the program in the future.
updated_description: Refugee and Immigrant Self Empowerment (RISE) proposes this Local Food Promotion Planning Grant project to develop intentional procedures that support participating farmers within its existing program, aiming to broaden the scope of their farm businesses and access previously inaccessible market outlets. This three-phase project will assess the feasibility of RISE creating a local food hub, encompassing the creation of business plans for current and future farmers, and a comprehensive hub logistical plan. Assuming feasibility, the project will establish a food hub to aggregate, store, market, and distribute produce grown locally by the refugee and immigrant community, offering farmers a new channel for sales and providing a stable foundation for increased production. The anticipated outcome is agricultural product diversification and revenue generation for the 15 farmers currently involved in the program, as well as for farmers recruited to join the program. This initiative will benefit stakeholders within the greater Syracuse area by providing access to fresh, locally sourced food. The project focuses on empowering farmers and creating a sustainable model for local food production. Ultimately, the project intends to create a robust local food system and support the economic growth of the participating farmers.

awardee_name: Economic and Community Development Institute, Inc.
original_description: When COVID-19 hit, Hawaiian supply chains were severely disrupted, resulting in empty store shelves. Residents became acutely aware of the need to re-establish resilient and secure local food systems across the Hawaiian Islands. In response to this disruption, momentum has developed with key players to rebuild the state’s food system, including farmers/producers, customers, institutions, policy makers, and a diverse funder group. During the pandemic, food hubs stepped in to flexibly fill voids in each locality and demonstrated competence and value to the community and members of the food value chain. Thus, the Hawaii Food Hub Hui, in partnership with the Hawaii Good Food Alliance, is building individual and collective capacity in Hawaii’s food hubs to ensure maximum sales for Hawaii’s numerous small and mid-size farmers and producers, and equitable access to fresh, healthy, local food for all. The primary project goal is to increase local food sales via Hawaii’s food hubs. This project aims to maximize the replicability of the proposed project in other regions, communities, and agricultural systems by 1) improving individual food hubs’ economic viability by supporting processing, aggregation, and distribution of local food products that are marketed throughout Hawaii; 2) strengthening relationships and cooperation within the Hawaii Food Hub Hui by facilitating regional value chain coordination; and 3) promoting new business opportunities and marketing strategies to increase public awareness of Hawaii’s food hubs.
updated_description: The Hawaii Food Hub Hui, in partnership with the Hawaii Good Food Alliance, is undertaking a vital project to bolster Hawaii’s food system following significant disruptions experienced during the COVID-19 pandemic. The primary purpose of this project is to increase local food sales through the enhancement and expansion of Hawaii’s food hubs, supporting farmers and producers across the islands. This initiative involves the development of infrastructure and resources designed to maximize the operational capacity of these hubs, focusing on processing, aggregation, and distribution activities for a broad range of local agricultural products. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in the volume of food sales generated by participating food hubs, contributing to greater access to fresh, healthy food for consumers and bolstering the economic viability of Hawaii’s agricultural sector, particularly benefiting farmers and ranchers. The project aims to strengthen regional value chain coordination within the Hawaii Food Hub Hui, facilitating improved relationships among stakeholders involved in the movement of food products. Ultimately, the project seeks to increase public awareness of Hawaii’s food hubs and the positive impact they have on the local food system, benefiting all involved in the production and distribution of food across the state.

original_description: Though the “Exploring Local Farm and Food Product Delivery in Southeastern PA” project, Chester County Economic Development Foundation and ACDS LLC, a regional agriculture-focused consulting firm, will conduct a feasibility study in late 2022 to determine cost-effective and timely delivery routes of farm and food products from Berks and Chester Counties to Greater Philadelphia area grocers and restaurants. At least one new distribution model will be recommended that not only meets the delivery needs of at least 15 producers, but also ensures profitability of the farmers and artisans is preserved. The model will increase the market opportunities, sales, and profitability of farmers and food artisans in the region, and serve as a blueprint for a future project that builds the business plan for the delivery network. Partners, the Chester County Ag Development Council and the Berks County Department of Agriculture, will assist in marketing the network and recruiting farmers and artisans to the project
updated_description: Chester County Economic Development Foundation, in collaboration with ACDS LLC, will conduct a feasibility study targeting the development of a new distribution model for farm and food products originating from Berks and Chester Counties to serve the Greater Philadelphia area’s grocers and restaurants. The primary goal of this project is to determine cost-effective and timely delivery routes, ultimately supporting at least fifteen producers, including farmers and food artisans, and ensuring the preservation of profitability for these stakeholders. This study will assess various logistical options and recommend a model that expands market opportunities and sales potential for these producers. The anticipated outcome is a robust distribution network that efficiently connects agricultural products with consumers in the Philadelphia region, thereby increasing the volume of sales and enhancing the economic viability of participating farms and food processing operations. The beneficiaries of this project include the farmers and ranchers who produce these goods, as well as the retailers and restaurants that utilize these products. Furthermore, the project seeks to strengthen the overall local food system by creating a streamlined pathway for distributing goods from the agricultural sector to the market. This distribution network is expected to improve access to fresh, locally sourced food products for a broader consumer base. The project will analyze operational efficiencies to minimize costs and optimize delivery routes, with the aim of creating a sustainable and scalable model for future expansion.

original_description: Our project purpose is to establish data that will provide a greater understanding of the current health and food access needs specific to the Indigenous communities in South Central Texas. Reports from this feasibility study will inform future programming and services provided by the Texas Tribal Buffalo Project to develop innovative approaches to combating food insecurity and improving the overall health and wellbeing across the region within the Indigenous communities.
updated_description: The Texas Tribal Buffalo Project’s purpose is to establish data that will provide a greater understanding of the current health and food access needs specific to the Indigenous communities in South Central Texas. This project will generate reports detailing these needs, which will subsequently inform the development of innovative approaches to combating food insecurity and improving the overall health and wellbeing across the region within the Indigenous communities. The project anticipates a detailed assessment of existing resources and challenges related to food availability for farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders. The anticipated outcome is the creation of actionable insights to guide the Texas Tribal Buffalo Project’s programming and services. Ultimately, this work will benefit the Indigenous communities by supporting efforts to enhance access to locally produced agricultural products, contributing to improved nutrition and overall wellness for those reliant on regional food systems. The project will support the development of strategies for optimizing food distribution networks and improving the availability of agricultural products for consumers within these communities, supporting the vital role of local food producers. This focused data collection will empower the Texas Tribal Buffalo Project to design solutions tailored to the specific requirements of the Indigenous communities in South Central Texas.

awardee_name: Midwest Organic and Sustainable Education Service, Inc. aka Marbleseed
original_description: The project will convene all the stakeholders to identify and develop a comprehensive, holistic framework for solving the problem of insufficient meat processing options on a regional scale. The study will focus on solutions that emphasize collective ownership, equitable access, and widely shared benefit for farmers, processors, and workers. It will connect small meat processors and farmers to ensure access to processing facilities and financial sustainability for the meat supply chain in the region. It will explore alternative ownership structures for processors that are looking to retire including employee-owned structures and cooperatives, to preserve and expand current small meat processing infrastructure and jobs in rural communities. The outcomes will include designing a viable, detailed business model and necessary legal structure, determining the capital necessary to actualize the plan, and working with state agencies to address any regulatory barriers to implementation as a replicable model. It is the collaborators’ intent to make this feasibility study and resulting business plan and model widely available and adaptable beyond Northwest Wisconsin, as it addresses an urgent need for small, grass-based livestock producers nationally.
updated_description: The project will address the critical need for enhanced meat processing options on a regional scale, focusing on the development of a comprehensive and holistic framework that prioritizes collective ownership, equitable access, and shared benefit for farmers, processors, and workers involved in the meat supply chain. This initiative seeks to connect small meat processors and farmers, ensuring access to processing facilities and fostering financial sustainability across the region’s meat supply network. Specifically, the project will explore alternative ownership structures for processors approaching retirement, including employee-owned structures and cooperatives, with the goal of preserving and expanding existing small meat processing infrastructure and the associated jobs within rural communities. The anticipated outcomes include the design of a viable and detailed business model, coupled with the determination of the necessary capital to implement the plan and collaboration with state agencies to mitigate any regulatory barriers to its successful execution. Ultimately, this project intends to create a replicable model that benefits farmers, ranchers, and processors nationally, supporting local food systems. The project will contribute to strengthening the regional economy by enabling the continued operation of small meat processing businesses and supporting the livelihoods of those who depend on them. The project aims to ensure that the necessary resources and infrastructure are in place to meet the demands of local markets and consumers, facilitating the efficient distribution of locally produced meat products.

original_description: This project will build upon several years of experience in researching local agricultural communities with a new planning project to determine the feasibility of a fulfillment platform that enables local/regional producers to promote and sell their products to consumers directly in a scalable, cost-efficient manner. The applicant will test business models based on proprietary technology to include utilization of value-added approaches to data and actionable datasets to support the platform commercially. The goal of this planning project is to build a case to develop a modern marketing, promotional, and fulfillment hub, supported through a scalable technology platform that curates local small and mid-size farm products in front of the modern consumer. We expect to see an increase in demand for local and regional food products, increase in opportunities to support future local food business development, and reduction in labor and costs associated with marketing.
updated_description: This project will develop a modern marketing, promotional, and fulfillment hub designed to connect local small and mid-size farm products with consumers in a scalable and cost-efficient manner. The core of this initiative involves the creation of a proprietary technology platform alongside value-added approaches to data and actionable datasets, intended to support the commercial viability of the platform. Anticipated outcomes include an increase in demand for locally and regionally produced agricultural products, alongside the generation of opportunities to support future local food business development among farmers and ranchers. The project’s primary beneficiaries will be the local agricultural community, encompassing farmers, ranchers, and food processors who will gain access to expanded market channels. This hub will streamline the process of promoting and distributing their goods, reducing the labor and costs associated with traditional marketing methods. The goal is to establish a system that effectively curates these products, presenting them to modern consumers seeking fresh, regional food sources. Ultimately, this project aims to enhance market access and overall economic activity within the local agricultural sector, facilitating the efficient movement of goods from production to point of sale.

original_description: California produces nearly half of the nation’s fruits and vegetables and is the top dairy state, yet 1 in 5 Californians — about 8 million — struggle with food insecurity. According to the California Department of Education, in the 2022‐2023 school year, 3,075,721 K‐12 students qualified for free lunch, relying on school districts for at least one meal a day. California is also the first state to mandate schools provide a nutritiously adequate breakfast and lunch to every student, regardless of income; this current school year is the first for implementation. This increased demand for school‐provided meals creates a strong need for California school districts to source nutritious food, creating an opportunity for local producers, processors, and intermediaries to meet this demand. However, barriers to serving these institutional buyers exist – especially for small farms – and must be remedied. As such Rumiano Cheese Company, an agricultural business that aggregates, processes, and markets value‐added organic dairy products made from milk produced by 27 Northern California dairy producers, seeks to boost Farm to Institution sales of locally‐produced organic dairy products through activities that will expand the local food system’s capacity to produce, process, and distribute value‐added organic dairy products into Northern California schools. Activities will also include creating and delivering engaging educational content for school foodservice staff and students to support long‐term increased consumption. Intended beneficiaries include 49,460 school‐aged children and 27 Northern California dairy producers; this project’s primary expected outcome is increased farm to institution sales of locally‐produced organic value‐added dairy products
updated_description: Rumiano Cheese Company is undertaking a project to increase farm to institution sales of locally-produced organic dairy products within Northern California schools. This initiative focuses on sourcing nutritious food for 49,460 school-aged children and 27 Northern California dairy producers, aiming to address food insecurity within the state’s educational system. The project involves the aggregation, processing, and marketing of value-added organic dairy products produced by these regional dairy producers, with the goal of expanding the local food system’s capacity to meet the increased demand created by the state’s mandate for breakfast and lunch provision in all schools.  Specifically, Rumiano Cheese Company will support the producers in supplying these institutions with their organic dairy products. The anticipated outcome is a measurable rise in farm to institution sales, contributing to a more robust local food supply chain and improving access to wholesome foods for students.  This project directly supports the producers by connecting them to a key market channel, promoting the consumption of locally produced organic dairy items, and strengthening the overall agricultural economy of Northern California.

original_description: Pivot Produce’s proposed project, Arizona Planned Production and Logistics Expansion, or APPLE, will utilize the successful southern Arizona F2I model to increase local foods sales to Maricopa County-based institutions. The proven "F2I" model to be replicated uses a value chain approach to coordinate farmers’ crop planning with institutional purchasing demand. APPLE will 1) Provide in‐person training on crop planning, food safety, and value‐added products for 15 small farmers; 2) Provide transportation of produce from farms to markets; and 3) Expand and create connections to institutional markets including hospitals, schools, and food banks, and implement purchasing commitments. The project will reduce on‐farm food waste by 20%; expand and create 10 institutional markets, increasing access to locally grown produce by 30%, and increase sales by 30% for a total of 35 small farmers in six counties in southern and central Arizona.
updated_description: Pivot Produce’s proposed Arizona Planned Production and Logistics Expansion, or APPLE, aims to significantly increase sales of locally grown produce to institutions within Maricopa County by replicating the successful southern Arizona F2I model. This project will establish connections between 35 small farmers across six counties – southern and central Arizona – and 10 new institutional markets, including hospitals, schools, and food banks. The core of the APPLE project involves a value chain approach, coordinating farmers’ crop planning directly with the purchasing demands of these institutions. Specifically, Pivot Produce will provide transportation services, ensuring the efficient movement of produce from farms to these markets, and will implement purchasing commitments to guarantee a stable supply. Anticipated outcomes include a reduction of on-farm food waste by 20% and a 30% increase in sales for participating farmers. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative include the farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of locally grown agricultural products. The project seeks to expand access to locally produced goods for consumers within the Maricopa County region, achieving a 30% expansion of available produce supply. By streamlining logistics and building direct market relationships, APPLE intends to strengthen the local food system and support the viability of small agricultural businesses.

original_description:
Local farmers are vital to the health of their communities by growing healthy local produce, employing community members, and building community resilience. Despite these contributions, they face challenges securing institutional contracts due to preference for large national firms presenting lowestcost
bids. Foodshed, a farmer-owned aggregation and distribution cooperative in San Diego, works at
the intersection of farm viability and climate-smart practices to promote local food equity. Foodshed
supports 60 small farms—68% are socially disadvantaged and BIPOC producers—and distributes 80% of their produce to historically underserved communities. Despite these strides, their efforts are exclusively grant-funded.
To ensure financial viability, commercial and institutional contracts must be established. This backdrop
comes as the “food as medicine” movement is gaining traction within healthcare and local government,
providing new funding opportunities, including Medi-Cal’s CalAIM Medically Supportive Food & Nutrition initiatives. The food as medicine movement also presents a promising opportunity for
promoting health equity by addressing food and nutrition insecurities, which are root causes of chronic
diseases that contribute to 50% of deaths in San Diego County. The Public Health Alliance of Southern California (Alliance) will cultivate partnerships and help establish contracts between farms and
institutions to support local farmers. The Alliance is a coalition of 11 local health jurisdictions with deep expertise in health, food systems, equitable contracting processes, and transforming data into action. The Alliance is expertly positioned to transform the connections between farmers and healthcare institutions to support a resilient local food system and enhance community health equity.
updated_description: Foodshed is undertaking a critical project to ensure the long-term viability of its operations and expand its impact within San Diego County. The project focuses on establishing commercial and institutional contracts with local farms, leveraging the growing “food as medicine” movement and related funding opportunities, including those presented by Medi-Cal’s CalAIM Medically Supportive Food & Nutrition initiatives. This initiative will support the procurement of goods and services, specifically fostering connections between local farms – representing 60 small farms, 68% of which are operated by socially disadvantaged producers – and healthcare institutions, as well as other key stakeholders. The anticipated outcome is the expansion of produce distribution to historically underserved communities, with Foodshed currently distributing 80% of the farms’ produce to these communities. This project directly benefits farmers, consumers, ranchers, and processors within the region, aiming to increase access to locally produced agricultural products and address food and nutrition insecurities that contribute to significant health challenges. By securing these contracts, Foodshed intends to bolster the resilience of the local food system and, ultimately, enhance community health outcomes, particularly given that 50% of deaths in San Diego County are attributed to chronic diseases. The Alliance, a coalition of 11 local health jurisdictions, will be instrumental in navigating equitable contracting processes and transforming data into actionable insights, solidifying Foodshed’s role as a central component of a resilient local food system and a driver of improved community well-being.

original_description: The purpose of the project is to develop, coordinate, and expand local and regional food business enterprises to help increase access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. This project addresses the needs of small scale, under-resourced and socially disadvantaged farmers in the region who often struggle to compete with large scale producers by providing direct lines and networks to commercial and institutional sale opportunities. The program focuses on supporting the processing, aggregation, distribution, and storage of local and regional food products by providing refrigerated transportation, assisting farms to meet institutional buying standards and providing indirect producer to consumer marketing. SCG will serve as the lead agency for the project and as an intermediary organization to benefit small farm operations serving local markets. SCG is already aggregating from farmers and this project will build upon this established foundation. The project will impact an anticipated new and existing 25 SCG network participating farmers/producers, 18 institutional/network buyers (including one new anticipated local/regional distributor), 300 additional local/regional farmers who will have access to institutional food safety workshops, and 130,000 consumers reached within the community at large through an advertising campaign designed to promote local food. These figures, after initial project pilot funding, are anticipated to grow continually and produce a project that is self-sustainin g. The benefits to farm and ranch operations serving local markets include an increase in sales, in kind marketing provided by the project, food safety training, and a reduction in transport costs.
updated_description: SCG will lead a project focused on developing and expanding local and regional food business enterprises to increase access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. This project will achieve this by supporting the processing, aggregation, distribution, and storage of local and regional food products, including procuring refrigerated transportation and assisting farmers to meet institutional buying standards, alongside providing indirect producer to consumer marketing. The anticipated outcomes include a positive impact on approximately 25 SCG network participating farmers/producers, 18 institutional/network buyers including one new anticipated local/regional distributor, and reaching 130,000 consumers within the community through a targeted advertising campaign. The project specifically intends to benefit farmers and ranchers serving local markets through increased sales, in-kind marketing support, and reduced transport costs. Furthermore, this project will provide access to food safety workshops for 300 additional local/regional farmers. The overall goal is to foster a sustainable system supporting these stakeholders and their production. SCG’s existing aggregation activities will serve as the foundation for this expansion, creating a network designed to maximize the reach of local food producers. The anticipated growth of the project, following initial pilot funding, demonstrates a commitment to a self-sustaining model.

awardee_name: North Dakota Rural Electric Cooperative Foundation
original_description:
North Dakota’s food supply chain capacity is shrinking as established suppliers reduce their territories and close distribution facilities. This has significant adverse impacts on the state’s school districts and other institutional buyers, especially in rural counties. The North Dakota Rural Electric Cooperative Foundation (NDRECF), working with community partners, is addressing this problem by anchoring local producers and processors in regional food hubs, and connecting those hubs in the near term to institutional buyers such as school districts.
For a decade, NDRECF has engaged producers, intermediaries, buyers, government entities, and economic development agencies to develop solutions and test innovative approaches to improving food access across the state. In 2022, NDRECF convened stakeholders in meetings to consider developing a statewide network of food warehouses serving both first mile (aggregation, value added processing) and last mile (distribution, farm-to-school, and pantry support) needs. The strategy that emerged includes establishing a pilot facility in Minot as the first step toward a network of food hubs across North Dakota.
The project has significant community support, including collaborations with Strengthen ND, Community Crossroads Advisors, Great Plains Food Bank, Foundation for Agricultural and Rural Resources Management and Sustainability (FARRMS), and the Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation (MHA).
Project deliverables include quantifying demand, matching demand to local producers and processors, establishing the facility operating entity, creating the initial design and layout, and selecting a site for construction or renovation.
updated_description: North Dakota’s Rural Electric Cooperative Foundation is undertaking a critical project to address shrinking food supply chain capacity across the state, significantly impacting farmers, ranchers, processors, and stakeholders reliant on institutional buyers, particularly school districts in rural counties. The project’s core objective is to establish a pilot facility in Minot, marking the first step towards a statewide network of food hubs designed to fulfill both first mile (aggregation and value-added processing) and last mile (distribution, farm-to-school, and pantry support) needs. This initiative will involve the purchase and development of a facility, including the creation of an initial design and layout, and the selection of a suitable site for construction or renovation. Anticipated outcomes include quantifying demand for locally produced goods and effectively matching that demand with regional producers and processors. The project’s ultimate goal is to strengthen access to food for communities throughout North Dakota. The primary beneficiaries of this work include those involved in food production and processing, as well as the school districts and other institutional buyers who currently rely on these local resources. North Dakota’s Rural Electric Cooperative Foundation is working in collaboration with key partners such as Strengthen ND, Community Crossroads Advisors, Great Plains Food Bank, Foundation for Agricultural and Rural Resources Management and Sustainability (FARRMS), and the Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation (MHA) to achieve these outcomes.

original_description:
Our project -- Advancing Agricultural Markets for Provider Prescribed Produce (AAMPPP) -- purpose is to strengthen market ties between local producers in New Mexico and large health care institutions. Key short‐term outcomes include doubling local purchasing and increasing market stability for producers. In the long‐term, project success will include identifying local food investments as meaningful preventative healthcare strategies and cost‐saving measures for institutions and insurance providers.
AAMPPP is a partnership between MoGro Mobile Grocery, sub‐awardee Presbyterian Healthcare Services (PHS), and eight local producer participants.  MoGro provides crucial supply chain interventions with cold storage, product pickup, delivery to new rural access points, and coordination and relationship building between producers and HCPs. PHS provides an extensive patient network, (serving 1 in 2 New Mexicans), an advanced patient referral system (EPIC) that integrates referrals for local food, and a wide and relevant audience for data dissemination. Eight producers provide multi‐ generation expertise in growing nutritious food and strong dedication to feed community members who most in need.
Major activities include purchase agreements, improved food safety plans, and coordination activities to create bonds between producers and institutions, and data dissemination to other major healthcare institutions and insurance providers. The primary beneficiaries are 20 New Mexico producers who farm an average of 5‐10 acres, and 5,000 New Mexico families, 90 percent of whom currently face food insecurity. Secondary beneficiaries are 20 additional producers, 51 New Mexico health clinics, and more than 500 healthcare professionals who will be able to provide more comprehensive care to their patients.
updated_description: Advancing Agricultural Markets for Provider Prescribed Produce (AAMPPP) is a project designed to strengthen market connections between local producers in New Mexico and large healthcare institutions. This initiative will focus on purchasing fresh produce from eight local producers, averaging 5-10 acres in size, utilizing interventions such as cold storage, product pickup, delivery to new rural access points, and coordination activities to foster relationships between these farmers and healthcare providers. Anticipated outcomes include doubling local purchasing volume and establishing greater market stability for the producers involved, ultimately leading to the identification of local food investments as meaningful preventative healthcare strategies and cost-saving measures for institutions and insurance providers. The primary beneficiaries of the project are 20 New Mexico producers and 5,000 New Mexico families who currently face food insecurity, with these consumers receiving access to fresh, nutritious produce. Secondary beneficiaries include 20 additional producers, 51 New Mexico health clinics, and over 500 healthcare professionals who will be able to provide more comprehensive care to their patients. This project aims to directly support the livelihoods of these farmers while simultaneously improving access to healthy food options for a significant portion of the New Mexico population. The project seeks to create a robust supply chain that benefits both producers and the healthcare system, facilitating a collaborative approach to improving community health outcomes.

original_description:
Connecting Hudson Valley Farmers to the Culinary Institute of America (CIA) with an Online Wholesale Marketplace, will bring together agricultural producers, the world’s premier culinary college, and the Farm Generations Cooperative to dramatically increase the amount of local food purchased by the CIA and other regional institutions. 

This project accomplish this goal with 1) research and a local procurement pilot at the CIA, and 2) a new online marketplace to facilitate the sourcing logistics, billing, supply-demand planning, and inventory challenges faced by producers and the CIA. 

Agricultural producers, CIA faculty, administrators, and procurement staff will be involved in every stage of the project: from identifying challenges, to clarifying technical specifications, and ultimately using the new online wholesale marketplace to significantly increase the amount of local food purchased by the CIA. The deliverables include 1) a public summary of a needs assessment focused on increasing local food procurement at CIA; 2) a collaboratively-written product specification for an online wholesale marketplace; 3) a marketplace application that will be tested by CIA and producer collaborators; 3) a public report on the impact of CIA’s local food procurement pilot on the regional food economy; 4) release of the online wholesale marketplace for public use nationwide.

This project will result in an appropriate, innovative, affordable, and cooperatively-owned technical solution to the nationwide challenge of facilitating farm-to-institution sales. The projects team of engineers, producers, and chefs is uniquely suited to deliver technology that will benefit the Hudson Valley region and institutions nationwide.
updated_description: Hudson Valley Farmers to the Culinary Institute of America (CIA) with an Online Wholesale Marketplace will dramatically increase the amount of local food purchased by the CIA and other regional institutions, addressing a critical need for direct producer-to-institution sales. This project will accomplish this goal through a phased approach, beginning with research and a local procurement pilot at the CIA, followed by the development and implementation of a new online marketplace specifically designed to facilitate sourcing logistics, billing, supply-demand planning, and inventory challenges faced by farmers and the CIA. The marketplace will support a collaborative network of producers, CIA faculty, administrators, and procurement staff, allowing for optimized sourcing of agricultural products. Anticipated outcomes include a significant increase in the volume of locally sourced food utilized by the CIA and a streamlined operational process for participating farmers. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the Hudson Valley region and beyond, creating greater market access for their goods. Ultimately, this initiative aims to establish a robust, nationwide platform that connects producers with institutions, promoting a more efficient and sustainable food system. The successful completion of this project will result in a fully functional and publicly available online marketplace, offering a technologically-driven solution to a widespread challenge in the food industry.

original_description: The Global Growers Local Markets Project will expand its sales program to connect farmers and buyers through a variety of distribution channels. Key activities include: developing marketing plans, hosting agritourism events, creating on-farm market access points, facilitating aggregation and distribution, making improvements to aggregation and distribution infrastructure, introducing farmers to a variety of record-keeping technologies, connecting farmers with food safety and market readiness resources, and achieving Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) certification. Deliverables and expected outcomes include: a refreshed marketing plan based on LFPP Planning Grant recommendations, improved aggregation and storage systems at two locations, reductions in on-farm food waste, improved use of technology, improved food safety practices, facilitation of sales between farmers and local/regional buyers at a variety of scales and market access points, strengthened markets for local produce, and increased viability of small-scale farms. The primary beneficiaries are beginning, small-scale, and historically underserved farmers (refugees, immigrants, and farmers of color). The project also benefits local buyers and distributors, who will be connected with farmers prepared to access larger markets. Ultimately, local communities will have increased access to healthy and culturally diverse foods produced within their region. As a result of this project, farmers will increase knowledge of local value chains and market access points, increase connections with buyers, improve record-keeping, improve market readiness, and improve operational efficiencies through aggregation and distribution.
updated_description: The Global Growers Local Markets Project aims to expand its sales program by connecting farmers and buyers through a variety of distribution channels, focusing on the development of marketing plans and the facilitation of sales between farmers and local/regional buyers at various scales. This project will result in improvements to aggregation and storage systems at two locations, alongside a refreshed marketing plan based on LFPP Planning Grant recommendations, and the creation of on-farm market access points. Anticipated outcomes include reductions in on-farm food waste, improved use of technology, enhanced food safety practices, and increased viability for small-scale farms. The primary beneficiaries of this project are beginning, small-scale, and historically involved farmers, along with local buyers and distributors who will be connected with producers prepared to access larger markets. The project seeks to strengthen local markets for produce and optimize operational efficiencies through aggregation and distribution. Ultimately, local communities will have increased access to agricultural products produced within their region. By addressing key elements of the supply chain, this initiative seeks to support farmers in expanding their reach and improving their ability to meet market demands.

original_description:
Led by Growing Places, the Local Food Works in North Central MA Local Food Promotion Program project builds on five years of planning and assessment to create an equitable, sustainable, and accessible North Central MA (NCMA) food system that can support the region’s 200 small and medium sized farms, address high rates of food insecurity and nutrition related chronic diseases, and strengthen the local economy via a regional food value chain.
    The project is founded on a NCMA food system feasibility study, Regional Food Center operating model and business plan, and strategic plan that were developed with input from 130 diverse community partners that comprise the Local Food Works-NCMA Coalition. Key project activities seek to 1) build a robust mid-tier value chain through a new regional food processing center; 2) support local farmers and small food businesses to expand to new market channels; and 3) develop a coordinated and accessible marketing and promotion system with supportive purchasing technology.
     As a result of project activities, primary project deliverables and outcomes during the grant period include:
•	10 new market channels/65 market access points participating in Local Food Works Regional Food Center’s (LFW-RFC) distribution system
•	45 NCMA farmers reach new market channels through the LFW-RFC
•	15 small food business microenterprises reach new market channels through the LFW-RFC and support the Center’s growth via kitchen rentals for product production
•	2,370 consumers purchase/receive locally produced agricultural products from the LFW-RFC generating an additional $753,131 in sales
•	71 food and agriculture jobs created or maintained because of the LFW-RFC       
     In addition to short- and medium-term outcomes, the project will bolster the NCMA food system to strengthen the local food economy, increase equitable healthy food access for households that suffer from disproportionate rates of nutrition related chronic diseases, and improve the quality of life of NCMA farmers and small food businesses.
   The three main primary beneficiaries of this project other that Growing Places who serves as the mid-tier enterprise are NCMA farmers focusing on those who are small and historically underserved; small food businesses; and consumers focusing on those who are food insecure although all will benefit. Each will achieve short term benefits related to knowledge, awareness, skills, and access as well as long-term benefits related to financial gains/savings and improvements in health and quality of life.
    To achieve project objectives, Local Food Works in North Central MA is centered on community collaboration and collective impact through the Local Food Works Steering Committee and broader Coalition. Towards this end, the project engages farmer-based organizations (Central Mass Grown and the Montachusett Agricultural Alliance) to recruit and embed a strong farmers voice within all project activities; HEAL, a youth and resident driven coalition focused on economic empowerment and healthy food access that will support consumer and small food business engagement; the North Central MA Health Equity Partnership (CHNA9) to engage NCMA’s anchor institutions to ‘buy local’ via its anchor collaborative; the United Way of North Central MA to recruit local food pantries to increase local purchasing from the LFW-RFC; the North Central MA Chamber of Commerce to promote the project to local food buyers and entrepreneurs; local schools, colleges and healthcare systems to support local purchasing at the institutional and consumer levels; and NCMA municipalities and the Community Foundation to promote the project and leverage resources for the Regional Food Center’s continued growth and expansion. Also supporting the project are consultants with expertise in food safety, product development, business development, and communication who will build capacity of partners to create a sustainable NCMA food value chain.
updated_description: Growing Places’ Local Food Works in North Central MA Local Food Promotion Program project aims to develop a sustainable regional food system within the North Central Massachusetts (NCMA) area, supporting approximately 200 small to medium-sized farms and addressing food insecurity while strengthening the local economy. This project will establish a new regional food processing center, a key component of the initiative, alongside the expansion of market channels, ultimately resulting in an anticipated 2,370 consumers purchasing products from the Local Food Works Regional Food Center (LFW-RFC), generating an additional $753,131 in sales and creating 71 food and agriculture jobs. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the NCMA region, with a focus on expanding access to local agricultural products for consumers, particularly those experiencing food insecurity. The LFW-RFC is projected to establish 10 new market channels, connecting approximately 45 NCMA farmers to expanded market opportunities and supporting the growth of 15 small food business microenterprises through kitchen rentals.  Furthermore, the project will engage anchor institutions, such as hospitals and schools, to prioritize purchasing local food products, bolstering the regional food value chain.  Through partnerships with the United Way of North Central MA and the Community Foundation, the LFW-RFC will increase local purchasing from food pantries and leverage resources for the Regional Food Center’s continued growth and expansion, facilitating a more robust and resilient food system for the North Central Massachusetts region.

original_description: First Nations Development Institute (First Nations), a national, nonprofit Native American organization, will support 13 grassroots Native food sovereignty Collaborators in growing their farming and ranching operations to increase Native food security in their Tribal communities and expand local and regional access to traditional foods. Two virtual convenings and an in-person convening will build a peer support network among participants, while financial support totaling $24,000 per group and capacity building consultant expertise will help them to develop and expand marketing networks, improve food safety / handling / transportation. The in-person convening will occur at First Nations’ 2024 Native Food Sovereignty Summit which trains Native food systems groups to increase access to healthy foods, promote nutrition, and create food systems-based jobs and income opportunities. The 13 producer Collaborators are located in rural, low income Native communities in Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, New Mexico, North Dakota, South Dakota, Texas, and Wisconsin, with operations that include meat, eggs, honey, maple products, wild rice, juneberries, and produce. Ultimately, community and regional accessibility to traditional Native foods will increase, revitalizing cultural foodways, overcoming inequity, and improving the health and well-being of Native people and communities. Research documents the positive effects on health and well-being that happens when Native communities move away from Western foods to a diet that emphasizes traditional foods. A final evaluation report on the project’s processes, outputs, outcomes, and lessons learned will encourage wider adaptation of project learning.
updated_description: First Nations Development Institute will support thirteen grassroots Native food sovereignty Collaborators located in rural, low-income Native communities across Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, New Mexico, North Dakota, South Dakota, Texas, and Wisconsin. These farmers and ranchers will increase their farming and ranching operations, focusing on the production of meat, eggs, honey, maple products, wild rice, juneberries, and produce, to enhance Native food security within their Tribal communities and broaden local and regional access to traditional foods. The project will provide each group with $24,000 in financial support, alongside capacity building consultant expertise, to facilitate the development and expansion of marketing networks, improve food safety handling, and transportation systems. The anticipated outcomes include increased community and regional accessibility to traditional Native foods, contributing to the revitalization of cultural foodways and the promotion of healthier dietary patterns. The beneficiaries of this project are the farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in producing and distributing these goods, as well as the consumers who will gain access to locally sourced traditional foods. A final evaluation report will detail the project’s processes, outputs, outcomes, and lessons learned, aiming to encourage broader adaptation of these findings.

original_description: With robust demand driven by the pandemic,  CitySeed proposes to enhance the capacity of CitySeed Incubates, a comprehensive package of programming and shared-use kitchen access in downtown New Haven, Connecticut. As New Haven’s first shared-use commercial kitchen incubator, our program will attract people of color, women, and immigrants from a 45-minute radius. As a result of this LFPP investment, CitySeed will scale the internal capacity of our staff and systems to serve the business, marketing, and sourcing needs of farms and ventures in our growing network. Other services and program offerings include entrepreneurial training, mid-tier value chain development, and supply chain coordination.
updated_description: CitySeed proposes to enhance the capacity of CitySeed Incubates, a comprehensive package of programming and shared-use kitchen access in downtown New Haven, Connecticut, to support the growth of local food businesses. This project will focus on scaling internal systems and staff to meet the evolving needs of a growing network of farms and ventures, aiming to facilitate the movement of agricultural products from producers to consumers. The core of this initiative involves expanding the shared-use kitchen facilities, bolstering the organization’s ability to manage business, marketing, and sourcing activities for its associated stakeholders. CitySeed anticipates that this enhanced capacity will significantly improve the operational efficiency of participating farms, ranchers, and food processors, contributing to increased access for consumers to locally produced goods. Ultimately, the project intends to strengthen the local food supply chain, promoting the development of agricultural enterprises and ensuring a more robust marketplace for regional food products. The project’s anticipated outcomes include improved logistics and coordination within the food system, leading to greater volume and availability of locally grown food.

original_description: One of the most remote islands in the world, Kauaʻi imports over 85% of its food despite year-round production capabilities, has one of the highest costs of living in the U.S., and has the lowest per-farm revenue average in Hawaiʻi. To make progress on these issues, longstanding community-based nonprofit, Mālama Kauaʻi (MK), will launch their new Moloaʻa ʻĀINA Center food hub. The facility is opening by Fall 2023, and this project will help to staff the facility's launch, food safety compliance, program expansions, and farm value-product development services. MK has been the leading food hub on Kauaʻi since 2020 and has been working on increasing food production and access for the island since 2006. The project will fund key staff positions critical to expanding programs and services to utilize the new facility fully. It is expected to increase average YoY producer sales by 10%, for 175+ local farmers and food producers - 60% of which will be small, BIPOC-owned businesses. A minimum of 25 Moloaʻa Irrigation Cooperative Members will utilize the facility for value-added product production, storage, and business assistance. Outcomes of this work will bolster Kauaʻi’s local agriculture industry, allow MK to meet the scale needed by large buyers, and fill gaps in the current food system.
